"""Conditional on being liquid enough to trade, an unusually large daily displacement achieved on below-normal participation is consistent with a temporary liquidity imbalance or incomplete price discovery rather than broad, persistent demand. The signal deliberately does not claim to identify signed order flow or dealer inventory; it tests the narrower prediction that extreme low-participation dislocations have weaker six-session continuation and, on average, partial reversal. Screening out sparse and very low-volume names makes the hypothesis about tradable dislocations rather than mechanical stale-price or bid-ask-bounce effects."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _lagged_positive_volume_baseline(volume: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute a causal 20-session positive-volume baseline ending at t-1."""
    lagged_volume = volume.shift(1)
    positive_lagged_volume = lagged_volume.where(lagged_volume > 0.0)
    positive_count = positive_lagged_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=1).count()
    baseline = positive_lagged_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
    return baseline, positive_count


@register_factor
class ParticipationNormalizedImpactRecoil(BaseFactor):
    """Liquidity-screened low-participation price-impact dislocation rank."""

    factor_id = "participation_normalized_impact_recoil"
    name = "Liquidity-Screened Low-Participation Recoil"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of directional close-to-close impact scaled by "
        "intraday range and inverse current participation, restricted to names "
        "with adequate recent trading activity. Positive values identify upward "
        "low-participation dislocations expected to have weaker continuation or "
        "partial reversal over the next six sessions."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_previous_close = previous_close > 0.0
        valid_range = high.notna() & low.notna() & (high >= low)

        close_return = close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        range_fraction = (high - low) / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        valid_displacement = (
            valid_previous_close
            & valid_range
            & close_return.notna()
            & range_fraction.notna()
            & (range_fraction > 0.0)
        )

        volume_baseline, positive_history_count = _lagged_positive_volume_baseline(volume)
        valid_history = (positive_history_count >= 15.0) & (volume_baseline > 0.0)
        participation = volume / volume_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact = close_return * range_fraction / participation.clip(lower=0.10)

        baseline_cutoff = volume_baseline.where(valid_history).quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        sufficiently_liquid = volume_baseline.ge(baseline_cutoff, axis=0)
        eligible = (
            valid_displacement
            & valid_history
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & (volume >= 0.25 * volume_baseline)
            & sufficiently_liquid
            & impact.notna()
        )

        eligible_impact = impact.where(eligible)
        lower = eligible_impact.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = eligible_impact.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized_impact = eligible_impact.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)

        return rank(winsorized_impact) - 0.5

The signal deliberately does not claim to identify signed order flow or dealer inventory; it tests the narrower prediction that extreme low-participation dislocations have weaker six-session continuation and, on average, partial reversal. programs.description: At the close of completed session t, use corporate-action-adjusted OHLC prices as supplied by the feed and define close-to-close return r_t = close_t / close_{t-1} - 1. Define the intraday range fraction q_t = (high_t - low_t) / close_{t-1}, requiring close_{t-1} > 0, high_t >= low_t, and q_t > 0. Define Vbar20_t as the arithmetic mean of volume over sessions t-20 through t-1, requiring at least 15 positive-volume observations; define participation p_t = volume_t / Vbar20_t, requiring volume_t > 0 and Vbar20_t > 0. Define impact I_t = r_t * q_t / max(p_t, 0.10), so a given directional close-to-close displacement receives greater magnitude only when contemporaneous volume is low relative to the stock's own recent participation. Before cross-sectional ranking, winsorize I_t each day at the 1st and 99th percentiles among eligible names. Eligibility requires valid I_t, at least 15 valid trailing-volume observations, current volume at least 25% of Vbar20_t, and Vbar20_t at or above the cross-sectional 30th percentile among names with valid histories; these conditions exclude zero-volume and persistently sparse names while retaining temporary below-normal participation. The factor value is the daily cross-sectional percentile rank of winsorized I_t, mapped to [-0.5, 0.5]; positive values denote positive low-participation dislocations and are expected to predict lower subsequent returns, while negative values denote negative dislocations and are expected to predict higher subsequent returns. The signal is formed only after the completed t daily bar and may be traded no earlier than the next executable bar.

"""The sounder neighboring mechanism is post-report information diffusion rather than an EPS-consensus-revision residual. Earnings news is more likely to have persistent six-bar effects when the bottom-line surprise, top-line surprise, and contemporaneously reported operating-cash-flow growth all point in the same direction: this combination is harder to attribute to accounting noise, one-off expense items, or an isolated analyst-model assumption. The delayed counterparty is investors who initially process headline EPS but require revenue and cash-flow confirmation before revising valuations and portfolio weights."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(group_panel: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Extract ticker labels from a static classification panel."""
    if group_panel.empty:
        return pd.Series(dtype=object)
    return group_panel.iloc[0].copy()


def _group_event_percentiles(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    event: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    minimum_count: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causally rank event values within same-date classification groups.

    The group count is based on the fresh-report event universe, rather than
    metric availability, as specified by the reporting-event construction.
    """
    percentiles = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    usable = pd.DataFrame(False, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    valid_labels = labels.reindex(values.columns).dropna()
    for group in pd.unique(valid_labels):
        columns = valid_labels.index[valid_labels == group]
        if len(columns) == 0:
            continue

        group_event = event.loc[:, columns]
        qualified = group_event.sum(axis=1) >= minimum_count
        group_values = values.loc[:, columns].where(group_event)
        group_rank = group_values.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        percentiles.loc[:, columns] = group_rank.where(qualified, np.nan)
        usable.loc[:, columns] = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(qualified.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
            index=values.index,
            columns=columns,
        )

    return percentiles, usable


def _hierarchical_event_percentile(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    event: pd.DataFrame,
    industry_labels: pd.Series,
    sector_labels: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Use qualified industry ranks, otherwise qualified sector ranks."""
    industry_rank, industry_usable = _group_event_percentiles(
        values, event, industry_labels, 5
    )
    sector_rank, sector_usable = _group_event_percentiles(
        values, event, sector_labels, 10
    )

    fallback = sector_rank.where((~industry_usable) & sector_usable, np.nan)
    return industry_rank.where(industry_usable, fallback)


@register_factor
class CashConfirmedDualSurpriseDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Directional EPS, revenue, and cash-flow confirmation after fresh reports."""

    factor_id = "cash_confirmed_dual_surprise_drift"
    name = "Cash-Confirmed Dual Surprise Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "On fresh reporting dates, ranks normalized EPS and revenue surprises "
        "plus operating-cash-flow growth within qualified industry or sector "
        "event universes; scores only directionally unanimous, nonzero signals."
    )
    window_length = 2
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "industry",
        "sector",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].reindex_like(close)

        eps_changed = eps_actual.notna() & eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
        revenue_changed = revenue_actual.notna() & revenue_actual.ne(
            revenue_actual.shift(1)
        )
        event = eps_changed | revenue_changed

        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        cash_flow_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(close)

        normalized_eps = eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.05)
        normalized_revenue = revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().clip(
            lower=1000000.0
        )

        industry_labels = _static_labels(data["industry"].reindex_like(close))
        sector_labels = _static_labels(data["sector"].reindex_like(close))

        eps_rank = _hierarchical_event_percentile(
            normalized_eps, event, industry_labels, sector_labels
        )
        revenue_rank = _hierarchical_event_percentile(
            normalized_revenue, event, industry_labels, sector_labels
        )
        cash_rank = _hierarchical_event_percentile(
            cash_flow_growth, event, industry_labels, sector_labels
        )

        eps_score = 2.0 * eps_rank - 1.0
        revenue_score = 2.0 * revenue_rank - 1.0
        cash_score = 2.0 * cash_rank - 1.0

        jointly_positive = (
            (eps_score > 0.0) & (revenue_score > 0.0) & (cash_score > 0.0)
        )
        jointly_negative = (
            (eps_score < 0.0) & (revenue_score < 0.0) & (cash_score < 0.0)
        )
        common_sign = jointly_positive.astype(float) - jointly_negative.astype(float)
        conviction = pd.concat(
            [eps_score.abs(), revenue_score.abs(), cash_score.abs()],
            axis=0,
        ).groupby(level=0).min()

        # concat/groupby preserves alignment but can reorder duplicate timestamp
        # labels; restore the original panel layout explicitly.
        conviction = conviction.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        signal = common_sign * conviction
        return signal.where(event & (common_sign != 0.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

Earnings news is more likely to have persistent six-bar effects when the bottom-line surprise, top-line surprise, and contemporaneously reported operating-cash-flow growth all point in the same direction: this combination is harder to attribute to accounting noise, one-off expense items, or an isolated analyst-model assumption. programs.description: Define a fresh reporting event on date t when either epsActual or revenueActual is non-null and differs from its value at t-1. For event names, compute normalized EPS surprise = epsSurprise / max(abs(epsEstimate), 0.05), normalized revenue surprise = revenueSurprise / max(abs(revenueEstimate), 1000000), and operating-cash-flow growth = operatingCashFlowGrowth. On each event date, rank each of these three quantities cross-sectionally within industry when that industry's fresh-event universe has at least 5 names; otherwise use sector when its fresh-event universe has at least 10 names; otherwise assign no signal. Convert each percentile rank to a centered score in [-1, 1]. The stock is eligible only if all three centered scores have the same nonzero sign. Its factor score is that common sign times the minimum absolute centered score across the three measures, so a large score requires jointly extreme and directionally consistent EPS, revenue, and cash-flow information. The signal is zero outside fresh reporting events and has no contemporaneous-price-response, EPS-versus-revenue estimate-residual, stability-window, or revision-elasticity gate.

"""Operating-backed earnings delivery that resolves distributed headline disbelief.

Mechanism: a tax-clean operating surprise can reprice rapidly when investors have
already sold a recently upgraded but unconfirmed narrative.  The factor requires a
completed high-turnover downside episode whose range is cooling, separating an
exhausted sceptical distribution from an ongoing deterioration."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank excluding non-finite observations."""
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _distribution_release(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal score for a past turnover-backed selloff now losing range intensity."""
    prior_close = close.shift(1)
    valid = (prior_close > 0.0) & (close > 0.0) & (high >= low) & (volume >= 0.0)
    ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).where(valid)
    bar_range = ((high - low) / prior_close).where(valid)

    completed_loss = (-ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().shift(3)).clip(lower=0.0)
    shock_range = bar_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().shift(3)
    base_range = bar_range.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(6)
    current_range = bar_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()

    shock_volume = volume.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().shift(3)
    base_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(6)
    turnover_excess = (
        shock_volume / base_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).clip(lower=0.0)

    range_excess = (
        shock_range / base_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).clip(lower=0.0)
    cooling = (
        1.0 - current_range / base_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(lower=0.0)

    return completed_loss * turnover_excess * range_excess * cooling


@register_factor
class OperatingDeliveryDisbeliefRelease(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "operating_delivery_disbelief_release"
    name = "Operating Delivery Disbelief Release"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks operating-backed and tax-clean EPS surprises when they resolve a "
        "recent unconfirmed upgrade narrative after turnover-backed downside "
        "pressure has cooled."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "epsActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "marketCap",
        "debtToEquity",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        pretax_income = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax_expense = data["incomeTaxExpense"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(21)
        eps_revision = (eps_estimate - eps_lag) / eps_lag.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        revenue_revision = (
            (revenue_estimate - revenue_lag)
            / revenue_lag.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        operating_margin = operating_income / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        margin_change = operating_margin - operating_margin.shift(63)

        estimate_updated = eps_estimate.notna() & eps_estimate.shift(1).notna() & eps_estimate.ne(eps_estimate.shift(1))
        positive_upgrade = estimate_updated & (eps_revision > 0.0)

        financing_deterioration = (
            _cs_rank(data["debtToEquity"] - data["debtToEquity"].shift(63)).fillna(0.5)
            + _cs_rank(-(data["currentRatio"] - data["currentRatio"].shift(63))).fillna(0.5)
            + _cs_rank(-(data["interestCoverage"] - data["interestCoverage"].shift(63))).fillna(0.5)
        ) / 3.0
        confirmation = (
            _cs_rank(revenue_revision.where(positive_upgrade)).fillna(0.5)
            + _cs_rank(margin_change.where(positive_upgrade)).fillna(0.5)
        ) / 2.0
        headline_fragility = (
            _cs_rank(eps_revision.where(positive_upgrade)).fillna(0.0)
            * (1.0 - confirmation).clip(0.0, 1.0)
            * financing_deterioration
        ).where(positive_upgrade)
        active_disbelief = headline_fragility.ffill(limit=15)

        prior_actual = eps_actual.shift(1)
        report_event = eps_actual.notna() & (prior_actual.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_actual))
        annual_operating_income = operating_income.shift(252)
        annual_pretax_income = pretax_income.shift(252)
        annual_tax_expense = tax_expense.shift(252)
        safe_cap = market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)

        current_etr = (tax_expense / pretax_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)
        annual_etr = (
            annual_tax_expense / annual_pretax_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(0.0, 0.50)
        eps_surprise = (eps_actual - eps_estimate) / (eps_estimate.abs() + 0.01)
        operating_support = (operating_income - annual_operating_income) / safe_cap
        tax_support = (
            -pretax_income * (current_etr - annual_etr) / safe_cap
        )

        eligible = (
            report_event
            & (pretax_income > 0.0)
            & (annual_pretax_income > 0.0)
            & eps_estimate.notna()
            & operating_support.notna()
            & tax_support.notna()
            & active_disbelief.notna()
        )
        credible_delivery = (
            _cs_rank(eps_surprise.where(eligible))
            + _cs_rank(operating_support.where(eligible))
            - _cs_rank(tax_support.where(eligible))
            - 0.5
        )

        release = _distribution_release(close, data["high"], data["low"], data["volume"])
        release_gate = _cs_rank(release.where(release > 0.0))
        disbelief_gate = _cs_rank(active_disbelief.where(active_disbelief > 0.0))
        active = eligible & release_gate.notna() & disbelief_gate.notna()

        signal = credible_delivery * disbelief_gate * release_gate
        return (
            signal.where(active, 0.0)
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0)
            .reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
            .fillna(0.0)
            .astype(float)
        )

programs.trading_idea: A positive reported EPS surprise has greater six-bar upside when operating-income growth, rather than tax-rate relief, validates it after the market has become sceptical of a recent estimate-only upgrade. The scepticism state is identified by an EPS revision lacking revenue or margin corroboration and accompanied by deteriorating financing capacity; a completed high-turnover selloff whose range is now cooling indicates that this disbelief has already been distributed into price. Neither parent mechanism alone distinguishes a genuinely operating-backed report from a fragile headline narrative that is being incorrectly unwound just before confirmation arrives.

"""Operating-confirmed, unassimilated dual-consensus revision bridge.

Mechanism: a revision becomes actionable when it was not already incorporated in
industry-relative price and is subsequently validated by a same-direction EPS and
operating-margin delivery.  This separates realized information transmission from
late consensus chasing or isolated accounting headlines.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_mapped_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional rank mapped to [-1, 1], excluding invalid values."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return 2.0 * clean.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0


def _industry_relative_return(
    pre_return: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_names: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal same-row industry-relative return using valid contemporaneous names."""
    values = pre_return.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    labels = industry.to_numpy(dtype=object)
    output = np.full(values.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for row in range(values.shape[0]):
        row_labels = labels[row]
        codes, _ = pd.factorize(row_labels, sort=False)
        valid = np.isfinite(values[row]) & (codes >= 0)
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        for code in np.unique(codes[valid]):
            members = valid & (codes == code)
            if int(members.sum()) >= minimum_names:
                output[row, members] = values[row, members] - values[row, members].mean()

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=pre_return.index, columns=pre_return.columns)


def _event_memory(event_score: pd.DataFrame, max_age: int, decay: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Carry the latest revision event forward with causal exponential decay."""
    values = event_score.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    output = np.zeros(values.shape, dtype=float)
    last_value = np.full(values.shape[1], np.nan, dtype=float)
    last_bar = np.full(values.shape[1], -1, dtype=int)

    for bar in range(values.shape[0]):
        age = bar - last_bar
        active = (last_bar >= 0) & (age <= max_age) & np.isfinite(last_value)
        output[bar, active] = last_value[active] * np.exp(-age[active] / decay)

        arrived = np.isfinite(values[bar])
        last_value[arrived] = values[bar, arrived]
        last_bar[arrived] = bar

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=event_score.index, columns=event_score.columns)


@register_factor
class OperatingRevisionNoveltyDeliveryBridge(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "operating_revision_novelty_delivery_bridge"
    name = "Operating Revision Novelty Bridge"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Uses a decayed state of concordant EPS and revenue revisions that were "
        "underreacted to in industry-relative prices, then scores only report "
        "events whose EPS surprise and operating-margin change validate that state."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsActual",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        revenue = data["revenue"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex_like(close)

        eps_prior = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_prior = revenue_estimate.shift(21)
        eps_revision = (
            (eps_estimate - eps_prior) / eps_prior.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        revenue_revision = (
            (revenue_estimate - revenue_prior)
            / revenue_prior.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        eps_update = eps_estimate.notna() & eps_estimate.shift(1).notna() & eps_estimate.ne(eps_estimate.shift(1))
        revenue_update = (
            revenue_estimate.notna()
            & revenue_estimate.shift(1).notna()
            & revenue_estimate.ne(revenue_estimate.shift(1))
        )
        revision_event = eps_update | revenue_update

        eps_direction = _cs_mapped_rank(eps_revision)
        revenue_direction = _cs_mapped_rank(revenue_revision)
        joint_direction = (eps_direction + revenue_direction) / 2.0
        concordant = (
            eps_revision.notna()
            & revenue_revision.notna()
            & eps_revision.mul(revenue_revision).gt(0.0)
            & revision_event
        )

        pre_return = close.shift(1) / close.shift(7).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        relative_return = _industry_relative_return(pre_return, industry, 5)
        price_direction = _cs_mapped_rank(relative_return)
        underreaction = (1.0 - joint_direction * price_direction).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
        revision_state_event = (joint_direction * underreaction).where(concordant)
        revision_state = _event_memory(revision_state_event, 42, 14.0)

        report_event = eps_actual.notna() & (
            eps_actual.shift(1).isna() | eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
        )
        eps_surprise = (
            (eps_actual - eps_estimate) / (eps_estimate.abs() + 0.01)
        )
        operating_margin = operating_income / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        margin_change = operating_margin - operating_margin.shift(63)

        surprise_direction = _cs_mapped_rank(eps_surprise.where(report_event))
        margin_direction = _cs_mapped_rank(margin_change.where(report_event))
        delivery_direction = (surprise_direction + margin_direction) / 2.0
        aligned_delivery = (
            report_event
            & revision_state.ne(0.0)
            & delivery_direction.notna()
            & revision_state.mul(delivery_direction).gt(0.0)
        )

        delivery_strength = delivery_direction.abs().clip(upper=1.0)
        signal = (revision_state * delivery_strength).where(aligned_delivery, 0.0)
        return (
            signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0)
            .reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
            .fillna(0.0)
            .astype(float)
        )

The interaction identifies a bridge from unassimilated expectations to realized operating evidence: the revision supplies the prior belief change, the muted relative price response identifies incomplete incorporation, and the operating report resolves the uncertainty quickly enough to matter over six sessions.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _event_change(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify newly available quarterly observations without using future data."""
    prior = frame.ffill().shift(1)
    return frame.notna() & prior.notna() & frame.ne(prior)


def _pressure_release_state(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Completed downside/range shock followed by a causal volatility cooling phase."""
    previous_close = close.shift(1)
    valid = (close > 0.0) & (previous_close > 0.0) & high.notna() & low.notna()
    ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).where(valid)
    bar_range = ((high - low) / previous_close).where(valid)

    completed_downside = (-ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().shift(3)).clip(lower=0.0)
    shock_range = bar_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().shift(3)
    baseline_range = bar_range.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(6)
    current_range = bar_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()

    valid_baseline = baseline_range > 0.0
    range_excess = (shock_range / baseline_range - 1.0).where(valid_baseline).clip(lower=0.0)
    cooling = (1.0 - current_range / baseline_range).where(valid_baseline).clip(lower=0.0)
    return completed_downside * range_excess * cooling


@register_factor
class OperatingCashReactionDeficitPressureRelease(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "operating_cash_reaction_deficit_pressure_release"
    name = "Cash-Credible Pressure-Release Deficit"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Fresh tax-clean, operating- and cash-confirmed positive earnings surprises "
        "whose idiosyncratic first reaction is muted, conditioned on a completed "
        "downside shock with cooling realized range."
    )
    window_length = 258
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "epsActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "operatingMargin",
        "revenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "marketCap",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        low = data["low"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        revenue = data["revenue"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        pretax_income = data["incomeBeforeTax"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        tax_expense = data["incomeTaxExpense"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex_like(close).astype(float)

        report_event = _event_change(eps_actual) | _event_change(eps_estimate)
        safe_cap = market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)
        cash_margin = operating_cash_flow / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        annual_operating_income = operating_income.shift(252)
        annual_pretax_income = pretax_income.shift(252)
        annual_tax_expense = tax_expense.shift(252)
        annual_etr = (
            annual_tax_expense / annual_pretax_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(0.0, 0.50)
        current_etr = (tax_expense / pretax_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)

        eps_surprise = (eps_actual - eps_estimate) / (eps_estimate.abs() + 0.01)
        operating_support = (operating_income - annual_operating_income) / safe_cap
        tax_support = (-pretax_income * (current_etr - annual_etr)) / safe_cap
        cash_step = cash_margin - cash_margin.shift(63)
        margin_step = operating_margin - operating_margin.shift(63)

        eligible = (
            report_event
            & (eps_surprise > 0.0)
            & (pretax_income > 0.0)
            & (annual_pretax_income > 0.0)
            & (operating_support > 0.0)
            & (cash_step > 0.0)
            & (margin_step > 0.0)
            & eps_estimate.notna()
            & tax_support.notna()
        )

        credibility = (
            rank(eps_surprise.where(eligible))
            + rank(operating_support.where(eligible))
            + rank(cash_step.where(eligible))
            + rank(margin_step.where(eligible))
            - rank(tax_support.where(eligible))
            - 1.5
        )

        stock_return = close.pct_change()
        cross_sectional_return = stock_return.sub(stock_return.median(axis=1), axis=0)
        pre_event_volatility = stock_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std().shift(1)
        reaction_z = cross_sectional_return / pre_event_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        muted_reaction = (1.0 - reaction_z).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        pressure_release = _pressure_release_state(close, high, low)
        release_weight = 0.25 + rank(pressure_release)
        event_score = (
            credibility * muted_reaction * release_weight
        ).where(eligible & release_weight.notna())

        carried_score = event_score.shift(1).ffill(limit=5)
        return carried_score.reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

"""Common-shock-masked analyst revision assimilation drift.

Mechanism: firm-specific analyst revisions can be under-incorporated when a
large opposing industry shock monopolises attention and sparse participation
limits arbitrage. A weak but directionally consistent beta-adjusted residual
response identifies credible information that has not yet fully repriced.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    """Construct static industry memberships from point-in-time labels."""
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    if industry.empty:
        return groups
    labels = industry.iloc[0]
    for column in industry.columns:
        label = labels[column]
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column)
    return groups


def _excluded_peer_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    lagged_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Lag-cap-weighted same-industry return excluding the focal stock."""
    peer_ret = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for columns in groups.values():
        r = ret[columns]
        cap = lagged_cap[columns]
        valid = r.notna() & cap.notna() & cap.gt(0.0)
        used_cap = cap.where(valid, 0.0)
        used_ret = (r * cap).where(valid, 0.0)
        total_cap = used_cap.sum(axis=1)
        total_ret = used_ret.sum(axis=1)
        total_n = valid.astype(float).sum(axis=1)

        excl_cap = total_cap.to_numpy()[:, None] - used_cap.to_numpy()
        excl_ret = total_ret.to_numpy()[:, None] - used_ret.to_numpy()
        excl_n = total_n.to_numpy()[:, None] - valid.astype(float).to_numpy()
        values = excl_ret / np.where(excl_cap > 0.0, excl_cap, np.nan)

        peer_ret.loc[:, columns] = pd.DataFrame(values, index=ret.index, columns=columns).where(excl_n >= 8.0)
        peer_count.loc[:, columns] = pd.DataFrame(excl_n, index=ret.index, columns=columns)
    return peer_ret, peer_count


def _lagged_beta(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS beta estimated exclusively from observations through t-1."""
    yy = y.shift(1)
    xx = x.shift(1)
    paired = yy.notna() & xx.notna()
    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    x0 = xx.where(paired, 0.0)
    y0 = yy.where(paired, 0.0)
    sx = x0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sy = y0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sxx = (x0 * x0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sxy = (x0 * y0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    safe_n = count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    denominator = sxx - sx * sx / safe_n
    numerator = sxy - sx * sy / safe_n
    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count >= 40.0)


@register_factor
class RevisionMaskedCommonShockAssimilation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "revision_masked_common_shock_assimilation"
    name = "Common-Shock-Masked Revision Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Fresh EPS revisions whose weak but confirming beta-adjusted response is "
        "masked by an unusually large opposing industry shock under low participation."
    )
    window_length = 62
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "industry", "epsEstimate"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        previous_estimate = estimate.shift(1)
        revision = (estimate - previous_estimate) / previous_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        fresh_revision = (
            estimate.notna()
            & previous_estimate.notna()
            & estimate.ne(previous_estimate)
            & np.isfinite(revision)
        )

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        stock_ret = (close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).where(
            close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0)
        )
        groups = _industry_groups(data["industry"])
        peer_ret, peer_count = _excluded_peer_return(
            stock_ret,
            market_cap.shift(1).where(market_cap.shift(1).gt(0.0)),
            groups,
        )
        beta = _lagged_beta(stock_ret, peer_ret, 60)

        prior_abs_peer = peer_ret.abs().shift(1)
        shock_cutoff = prior_abs_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=48).quantile(0.80)
        large_peer_shock = peer_ret.abs().gt(shock_cutoff) & shock_cutoff.notna()
        opposing_shock = np.sign(peer_ret).ne(np.sign(revision)) & peer_ret.ne(0.0)

        residual_response = stock_ret - beta * peer_ret
        residual_confirmation = np.sign(residual_response).eq(np.sign(revision)) & residual_response.ne(0.0)

        prior_median_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        low_participation = (
            volume.gt(0.0)
            & prior_median_volume.gt(0.0)
            & volume.div(prior_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).le(0.80)
        )
        prior_dollar_volume = (close.shift(1) * volume.shift(1)).where(
            close.shift(1).gt(0.0) & volume.shift(1).gt(0.0)
        )
        liquid = prior_dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median().ge(5_000_000.0)

        eligible = (
            fresh_revision
            & large_peer_shock
            & opposing_shock
            & low_participation
            & liquid
            & residual_response.notna()
            & beta.notna()
            & peer_count.ge(8.0)
        )
        muted_cutoff = residual_response.abs().where(eligible).median(axis=1)
        muted_residual = residual_response.abs().le(muted_cutoff, axis=0) & muted_cutoff.notna().to_numpy()[:, None]
        retained = eligible & residual_confirmation & muted_residual

        magnitude_rank = revision.abs().where(retained).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        sufficient = retained.sum(axis=1).ge(5).to_numpy()[:, None]
        score = np.sign(revision) * magnitude_rank
        return score.where(retained & sufficient, 0.0).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

"""Fresh analyst-consensus EPS revisions can diffuse gradually when the initial market reaction confirms the news direction but remains muted and participation is below the stock's own normal level. Requiring directional confirmation avoids interpreting an opposite price move as mere investor inattention when it may instead reflect more timely contradictory information. The strategy targets revisions that appear credible enough to move price in the expected direction, but insufficiently broadly incorporated to complete repricing over the next six sessions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _average_percentile_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise average rank divided by eligible count, retaining only eligible cells."""
    masked = values.where(eligible)
    ranks = masked.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=False)
    counts = eligible.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan)
    return ranks.div(counts, axis=0).where(eligible)


@register_factor
class FreshEstimateResponseDeficitDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks fresh, credible EPS revisions with muted confirming price response."""

    factor_id = "fresh_estimate_response_deficit_drift"
    name = "Muted-Confirmation Revision Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Fresh EPS-consensus revisions whose same-day intrabar response confirms "
        "the revision but remains cross-sectionally muted, with below-normal "
        "participation and a precommitted dollar-volume liquidity screen."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "open", "volume", "marketCap", "epsEstimate"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"]

        previous_estimate = estimate.shift(1)
        prior_scale = previous_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revision = (estimate - previous_estimate) / prior_scale
        fresh_event = (
            estimate.notna()
            & previous_estimate.notna()
            & estimate.ne(previous_estimate)
            & np.isfinite(revision)
        )

        intrabar_return = close.div(open_.replace(0.0, np.nan)) - 1.0
        prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        participation = volume.div(prior_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        low_participation = (
            volume.gt(0.0)
            & prior_volume_median.gt(0.0)
            & participation.le(0.80)
        )

        prior_dollar_volume = (close * volume).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        base_valid = (
            fresh_event
            & market_cap.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(market_cap)
            & prior_dollar_volume.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(prior_dollar_volume)
            & intrabar_return.notna()
            & low_participation
        )

        liquidity_cutoff = prior_dollar_volume.where(base_valid).quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        liquid = prior_dollar_volume.ge(liquidity_cutoff, axis=0) & liquidity_cutoff.notna().to_numpy()[:, None]
        eligible = base_valid & liquid

        event_count = eligible.sum(axis=1)
        abs_response = intrabar_return.abs()
        muted_cutoff = abs_response.where(eligible).median(axis=1)
        directionally_confirming = np.sign(intrabar_return).eq(np.sign(revision))
        muted_confirmation = (
            directionally_confirming
            & abs_response.le(muted_cutoff, axis=0)
            & muted_cutoff.notna().to_numpy()[:, None]
        )

        magnitude_rank = _average_percentile_rank(revision.abs(), eligible)
        score = np.sign(revision) * magnitude_rank
        retained = eligible & muted_confirmation & event_count.ge(10).to_numpy()[:, None]
        return score.where(retained, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Muted-Confirmation Revision Drift
programs.trading_idea: Fresh analyst-consensus EPS revisions can diffuse gradually when the initial market reaction confirms the news direction but remains muted and participation is below the stock's own normal level. Requiring directional confirmation avoids interpreting an opposite price move as mere investor inattention when it may instead reflect more timely contradictory information. The strategy targets revisions that appear credible enough to move price in the expected direction, but insufficiently broadly incorporated to complete repricing over the next six sessions.
programs.description: At decision date t, define a fresh EPS-estimate event only when epsEstimate[t] and epsEstimate[t-1] are both finite and epsEstimate[t] != epsEstimate[t-1]. Define the revision innovation as z[t] = (epsEstimate[t] - epsEstimate[t-1]) / max(abs(epsEstimate[t-1]), 0.01). The contemporaneous response is the same-day intrabar return r[t] = close[t] / open[t] - 1, which ends at the decision bar. The volume-participation ratio is q[t] = volume[t] / median(volume[t-20:t-1]); observations require positive current volume and a positive 20-prior-bar median, and qualify as below-normal participation only if q[t] <= 0.80. To avoid selecting structurally illiquid names, eligible stocks must additionally have a finite positive marketCap and have their prior-20-bar average dollar volume, mean(close*volume over t-20 through t-1), at or above the cross-sectional 30th percentile among otherwise valid stocks on t. Among eligible fresh events, retain only directionally confirming observations where sign(r[t]) = sign(z[t]) and abs(r[t]) is no greater than the cross-sectional median abs(r[t]) among eligible fresh events; this is an explicit muted-confirmation condition, not a price-revision anti-alignment trade. For retained names, score equals sign(z[t]) times the cross-sectional percentile rank of abs(z[t]) among eligible fresh events. If fewer than 10 eligible fresh events exist on a date, or if a name fails any event, liquidity, participation, or muted-confirmation condition, its score is set to exactly 0. Cross-sectional ranks use average ranks divided by the number of eligible fresh events. This differs from revision_response_elasticity_calibration and turnover_validated_revision_anti_alignment because it excludes opposite-signed price responses and trades only partially confirming, low-relative-participation reactions under a precommitted liquidity screen.

programs.code:
"""The mechanism is not that operating cash flow perfectly identifies contemporaneous cash collection, but that investors initially anchor on the reported revenue surprise and may underweight a contemporaneously disclosed, peer-relative change in sales-to-cash conversion. A positive sales surprise paired with an unusually favorable sequential conversion change provides more credible delivery evidence than the headline alone, while a negative surprise paired with unfavorable conversion indicates weaker operating delivery. The six-day forecast is therefore a narrowly event-conditioned information-diffusion signal, not a general cash-flow-quality premium."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_distinct_quarterly_value(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return update flags and the prior distinct point-in-time observation.

    Forward filling is only used to identify the last value publicly available
    before each bar.  The returned prior value is therefore causal even across
    a temporary staleness gap.
    """
    prior_available = values.ffill().shift(1)
    is_update = values.notna() & (
        prior_available.isna() | values.ne(prior_available)
    )
    prior_distinct = values.where(is_update).ffill().shift(1)
    return is_update, prior_distinct


def _industry_event_percentile(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    industries: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_peers: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rank eligible event values within same-date industry peer sets."""
    candidate = values.where(eligible & industries.notna())
    long_values = candidate.stack()

    if long_values.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    long_industries = industries.stack().reindex(long_values.index)
    has_industry = long_industries.notna()
    long_values = long_values[has_industry]
    long_industries = long_industries[has_industry]

    if long_values.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    group_keys = [long_values.index.get_level_values(0), long_industries]
    peer_count = long_values.groupby(group_keys, sort=False).transform("count")
    percentile = long_values.groupby(group_keys, sort=False).rank(pct=True)
    percentile = percentile.where(peer_count >= minimum_peers)

    return percentile.unstack().reindex(index=values.index, columns=values.columns)


@register_factor
class CashCollectionDeliverySurpriseDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-normalized agreement between sales surprises and cash delivery."""

    factor_id = "cash_collection_delivery_surprise_drift"
    name = "Peer-Normalized Sales Delivery Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "On revenue-surprise availability dates, rank revenue surprises and "
        "sequential operating-cash-flow-to-sales innovations within industry, "
        "then emphasize jointly extreme confirmations or deteriorations."
    )
    window_length = 504
    inputs = ["close", "revenueSurprise", "revenue", "operatingCashFlow", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        prior_surprise = surprise.ffill().shift(1)
        event = (
            surprise.notna()
            & prior_surprise.notna()
            & surprise.ne(prior_surprise)
        )

        revenue_update, prior_revenue = _prior_distinct_quarterly_value(revenue)
        cash_flow_update, prior_cash_flow = _prior_distinct_quarterly_value(
            operating_cash_flow
        )

        current_conversion = operating_cash_flow / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_conversion = prior_cash_flow / prior_revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        delivery_innovation = current_conversion - prior_conversion

        eligible = (
            event
            & revenue_update
            & cash_flow_update
            & surprise.notna()
            & revenue.gt(0.0)
            & prior_revenue.gt(0.0)
            & operating_cash_flow.notna()
            & prior_cash_flow.notna()
            & delivery_innovation.notna()
        )

        surprise_percentile = _industry_event_percentile(
            surprise, industry, eligible, 8
        )
        delivery_percentile = _industry_event_percentile(
            delivery_innovation, industry, eligible, 8
        )

        surprise_component = 2.0 * surprise_percentile - 1.0
        delivery_component = 2.0 * delivery_percentile - 1.0
        joint_signal = (
            surprise_component
            * delivery_component
            * np.minimum(surprise_component.abs(), delivery_component.abs())
        )

        valid_signal = (
            eligible
            & surprise_component.notna()
            & delivery_component.notna()
        )

        result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        result = result.mask(event, np.nan)
        result = result.mask(valid_signal, joint_signal)
        return result
