"""Peer-anchored revision-disagreement earnings delivery.

Mechanism: a cash-confirmed report has delayed repricing power when its surprise
resolves an industry-relative cash-flow valuation anchor but contradicts the
prior EPS revision unexplained by sales revisions.  Revision/report agreement is
likely anticipated; disagreement makes the delivered information novel.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorized same-date cross-sectional z-score."""
    lower = values.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = values.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    std = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0)


def _industry_peer_yield(
    cash_yield: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_names: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date industry median yield, retaining adequately populated groups."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=cash_yield.index, columns=cash_yield.columns)
    for row_number, timestamp in enumerate(cash_yield.index):
        values = cash_yield.iloc[row_number]
        labels = industry.iloc[row_number]
        valid = values.notna() & np.isfinite(values) & labels.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        selected_values = values.loc[valid]
        selected_labels = labels.loc[valid]
        counts = selected_values.groupby(selected_labels).count()
        medians = selected_values.groupby(selected_labels).median()
        qualifying = counts[counts.ge(minimum_names)].index
        if len(qualifying) == 0:
            continue
        mapped = selected_labels.map(medians.loc[qualifying])
        output.loc[timestamp, mapped.index] = mapped.to_numpy()
    return output


def _industry_revision_residual(
    eps_revision: pd.DataFrame,
    sales_revision: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional EPS-revision residual after industry sales-revision fit."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=eps_revision.index, columns=eps_revision.columns)
    for row_number, timestamp in enumerate(eps_revision.index):
        y = eps_revision.iloc[row_number]
        x = sales_revision.iloc[row_number]
        labels = industry.iloc[row_number]
        residual = pd.Series(np.nan, index=eps_revision.columns, dtype=float)
        valid = y.notna() & x.notna() & labels.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        for group in pd.unique(labels.loc[valid]):
            columns = labels.index[valid & labels.eq(group)]
            if len(columns) < 6:
                continue
            xv = x.loc[columns]
            yv = y.loc[columns]
            centered_x = xv - xv.mean()
            denominator = float((centered_x * centered_x).sum())
            if denominator > 0.0:
                beta = float((centered_x * (yv - yv.mean())).sum() / denominator)
                residual.loc[columns] = yv - (yv.mean() + beta * centered_x)
            else:
                residual.loc[columns] = yv - yv.mean()
        unresolved = valid & residual.isna()
        fallback = unresolved.index[unresolved]
        if len(fallback) >= 20:
            xv = x.loc[fallback]
            yv = y.loc[fallback]
            centered_x = xv - xv.mean()
            denominator = float((centered_x * centered_x).sum())
            if denominator > 0.0:
                beta = float((centered_x * (yv - yv.mean())).sum() / denominator)
                residual.loc[fallback] = yv - (yv.mean() + beta * centered_x)
            else:
                residual.loc[fallback] = yv - yv.mean()
        output.iloc[row_number] = residual
    return output


def _carry_event_score(event_score: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally carry report information for five sessions with exponential decay."""
    rows, cols = event_score.shape
    positions = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (rows, cols)),
        index=event_score.index,
        columns=event_score.columns,
    )
    last_event = positions.where(event_score.notna()).ffill()
    age = positions - last_event
    carried = event_score.ffill(limit=5)
    return (carried * np.exp(-age / 3.0)).where(age.le(5))


@register_factor
class PeerAnchoredRevisionDisagreementDelivery(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_anchored_revision_disagreement_delivery"
    name = "Peer-Anchored Revision Disagreement Delivery"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Cash-confirmed earnings delivery conditioned on a peer cash-flow-value "
        "anchor and on disagreement with the prior sales-residual EPS revision."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex_like(close)

        event = (
            (eps_actual.notna() & eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1)))
            | (revenue_actual.notna() & revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1)))
        )

        eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(21)
        revision_valid = (
            eps_estimate.notna()
            & eps_lag.notna()
            & eps_lag.abs().ge(0.01)
            & revenue_estimate.notna()
            & revenue_lag.notna()
            & revenue_lag.abs().ge(1000000.0)
            & revenue_estimate.gt(0.0)
        )
        eps_revision = ((eps_estimate - eps_lag) / eps_lag.abs()).where(revision_valid)
        sales_revision = ((revenue_estimate - revenue_lag) / revenue_lag.abs()).where(revision_valid)
        revision_residual = _industry_revision_residual(
            _cs_zscore(eps_revision), _cs_zscore(sales_revision), industry
        ).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_scaled = (eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.05)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        revenue_scaled = (revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        eps_z = _cs_zscore(eps_scaled.where(event))
        revenue_z = _cs_zscore(revenue_scaled.where(event))
        cash_z = _cs_zscore(cash_growth.where(event))

        direction = np.sign(eps_scaled)
        coherent = (
            direction.ne(0.0)
            & direction.mul(revenue_z).gt(0.0)
            & direction.mul(cash_z).gt(0.0)
        )
        confirmation = pd.concat(
            [eps_z.abs(), revenue_z.abs(), cash_z.abs()], axis=0
        ).groupby(level=0).min().reindex_like(close).clip(upper=3.0)

        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_yield = (operating_cash_flow / market_cap).where(
            operating_cash_flow.gt(0.0) & market_cap.gt(0.0)
        )
        peer_yield = _industry_peer_yield(cash_yield, industry, 3)
        anchor_gap = np.log(cash_yield / peer_yield).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        anchor_state = (2.0 * rank(anchor_gap) - 1.0)
        anchor_aligned = direction.mul(anchor_state).gt(0.0)
        anchor_strength = direction.mul(anchor_state).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        revision_disagrees = direction.mul(revision_residual).lt(0.0)
        disagreement_strength = revision_residual.abs().clip(upper=3.0)

        one_day_return = close.div(close.shift(1)).sub(1.0)
        volatility = one_day_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        reaction = one_day_return.abs().div(volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        muted_weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + reaction.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0))

        event_score = (
            eps_scaled
            * confirmation
            * (0.5 + anchor_strength)
            * (0.5 + disagreement_strength)
            * muted_weight
        ).where(event & coherent & anchor_aligned & revision_disagrees)

        carried = _carry_event_score(event_score)
        raw = carried.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return (rank(raw).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).reindex_like(close)

programs.trading_idea: A credible earnings delivery should produce the fastest six-day repricing when it both resolves an industry-relative cash-flow valuation anchor and contradicts the pre-report, sales-adjusted EPS-consensus revision. Parent B's adverse standalone direction is interpreted as evidence that revisions aligned with the report are already anticipated and therefore largely priced; disagreement identifies news whose fundamental realization is genuinely novel. Cash, revenue, and EPS confirmation establish that the surprise is not accounting noise, while a muted immediate price response leaves the peer-anchor convergence path available for subsequent drift.
programs.description: The factor carries a report-day earnings-delivery score for five sessions. It requires coherent EPS, revenue, and operating-cash-flow confirmation, surprise alignment with an industry-relative operating-cash-flow-yield anchor, and opposition between the report surprise and the industry's sales-residualized prior EPS-estimate revision, weighted toward muted initial reactions.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    for column in industry.columns:
        observed = industry[column].dropna()
        if not observed.empty:
            groups.setdefault(observed.iloc[0], []).append(column)
    return groups


def _event_industry_rank(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    event: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    global_values = values.where(event)
    global_count = global_values.notna().sum(axis=1)
    global_rank = global_values.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

    for columns in groups.values():
        if len(columns) < 3:
            continue
        local = values[columns].where(event[columns])
        count = local.notna().sum(axis=1)
        local_rank = local.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        qualified = count >= 3
        mask = np.repeat(qualified.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
        ranked = local_rank.where(mask)
        fallback_mask = np.repeat((~qualified & (global_count >= 5)).to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
        ranked = ranked.where(~fallback_mask, global_rank[columns])
        out.loc[:, columns] = ranked

    ungrouped = [column for column in values.columns if column not in out.columns[out.notna().any(axis=0)]]
    if ungrouped:
        out.loc[:, ungrouped] = global_rank[ungrouped].where(global_count >= 5, np.nan)
    return out


def _peer_return_and_breadth(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    peer = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for columns in groups.values():
        if len(columns) < 3:
            continue
        x = values[columns]
        valid = x.notna()
        total = x.where(valid, 0.0).sum(axis=1).to_numpy()[:, None]
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()[:, None]
        x_array = x.where(valid, 0.0).to_numpy()
        valid_array = valid.astype(float).to_numpy()
        excluded_count = count - valid_array
        mean_array = (total - x_array) / np.where(excluded_count > 0.0, excluded_count, np.nan)
        peer_frame = pd.DataFrame(mean_array, index=values.index, columns=columns)
        peer.loc[:, columns] = peer_frame.where(excluded_count >= 2.0)

        positive = ((x > 0.0) & valid).astype(float).to_numpy()
        negative = ((x < 0.0) & valid).astype(float).to_numpy()
        pos_count = positive.sum(axis=1)[:, None] - positive
        neg_count = negative.sum(axis=1)[:, None] - negative
        matching = np.where(mean_array > 0.0, pos_count, np.where(mean_array < 0.0, neg_count, 0.0))
        breadth.loc[:, columns] = pd.DataFrame(
            matching / np.where(excluded_count > 0.0, excluded_count, np.nan),
            index=values.index,
            columns=columns,
        ).where(excluded_count >= 2.0)
    return peer, breadth


def _relative_attention(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    activity = (close * volume).where((close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0)).rolling(3, min_periods=2).sum()
    lagged_cap = market_cap.shift(1).where(market_cap.shift(1) > 0.0)
    out = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    for columns in groups.values():
        if len(columns) < 3:
            continue
        a = activity[columns]
        c = lagged_cap[columns]
        activity_share = a.div(a.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        cap_share = c.div(c.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        deficit = np.log(cap_share.div(activity_share.replace(0.0, np.nan)))
        out.loc[:, columns] = deficit.clip(lower=0.0, upper=np.log(4.0)).div(np.log(4.0)).fillna(0.0)
    return out


@register_factor
class TriangulatedCashAuctionPeerLatency(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "triangulated_cash_auction_peer_latency"
    name = "Triangulated Cash Auction Peer Latency"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Cash-confirmed dual-surprise drift, activated only after an aligned "
        "opening-auction rejection in an under-attended stock that lags a broad "
        "same-direction industry response."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        open_price = data["open"].reindex_like(close).where(data["open"].reindex_like(close) > 0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close).where(data["volume"].reindex_like(close) > 0.0)
        groups = _industry_groups(data["industry"].reindex_like(close))

        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].reindex_like(close)
        event = (
            (eps_actual.notna() & eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1)))
            | (revenue_actual.notna() & revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1)))
        )

        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_value = (eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.05)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        revenue_value = (revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        eps_score = 2.0 * _event_industry_rank(eps_value, event, groups) - 1.0
        revenue_score = 2.0 * _event_industry_rank(revenue_value, event, groups) - 1.0
        cash_score = 2.0 * _event_industry_rank(cash_growth, event, groups) - 1.0

        positive = (eps_score > 0.0) & (revenue_score > 0.0) & (cash_score > 0.0)
        negative = (eps_score < 0.0) & (revenue_score < 0.0) & (cash_score < 0.0)
        direction = positive.astype(float) - negative.astype(float)
        conviction = np.minimum(np.minimum(eps_score.abs(), revenue_score.abs()), cash_score.abs())
        fundamental = direction * conviction

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        stock_return = close.div(prior_close).sub(1.0)
        gap = np.log(open_price.div(prior_close))
        intraday = np.log(close.div(open_price))
        peer_return, breadth = _peer_return_and_breadth(stock_return, groups)
        peer_gap, _ = _peer_return_and_breadth(gap, groups)
        idio_gap = gap - peer_gap
        gap_scale = idio_gap.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=6).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gap_strength = idio_gap.abs().div(gap_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).div(3.0)
        reversal = (-np.sign(idio_gap) * intraday).clip(lower=0.0).div(idio_gap.abs().clip(lower=0.002)).clip(upper=1.0)
        relative_volume = volume.div(volume.shift(1).rolling(12, min_periods=5).median().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        participation = np.log(relative_volume.clip(lower=1.0, upper=3.0)).div(np.log(3.0)).fillna(0.0)
        auction_rejection = gap_strength * reversal.fillna(0.0) * participation

        attention = _relative_attention(close, volume, data["marketCap"].reindex_like(close), groups)
        aligned_peer = direction * peer_return > 0.0
        aligned_gap = direction * idio_gap > 0.0
        unpaid = (direction * (peer_return - stock_return)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.15)
        broad = breadth.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        raw = fundamental * auction_rejection * attention * unpaid * broad
        active = (
            event
            & (direction != 0.0)
            & aligned_peer
            & aligned_gap
            & broad.ge(0.55)
            & attention.gt(0.0)
            & auction_rejection.gt(0.0)
            & raw.notna()
        )
        signal = 2.0 * rank(raw.where(active)) - 1.0
        return signal.reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Triangulated Cash Auction Peer Latency
programs.trading_idea: A unanimous EPS, revenue, and operating-cash-flow surprise is a high-credibility information shock, but it has the strongest six-bar drift when the opening auction initially moves in the news direction and then rejects that move intraday. Conditioning this reversal on a broad, same-direction industry response and the stock's own residual lag isolates a delayed-information state: peers have recognized the common fundamental news while the focal name's auction has temporarily mispriced it. The interaction carries edge because cash confirmation filters transient auction reversals, while auction rejection and peer-relative underreaction identify where validated earnings news has not yet been fully incorporated.
programs.description: On fresh report dates, the factor forms industry-relative ranks of normalized EPS surprise, normalized revenue surprise, and operating-cash-flow growth, retaining only unanimous three-channel signals. It scores those signals only when an aligned idiosyncratic opening gap is rejected on elevated volume, peers move broadly in the same direction, and the stock remains behind its peers despite being under-attended relative to industry capital weight.

"""Conditional on being liquid enough to trade, an unusually large daily displacement achieved on below-normal participation is consistent with a temporary liquidity imbalance or incomplete price discovery rather than broad, persistent demand. The signal deliberately does not claim to identify signed order flow or dealer inventory; it tests the narrower prediction that extreme low-participation dislocations have weaker six-session continuation and, on average, partial reversal. Screening out sparse and very low-volume names makes the hypothesis about tradable dislocations rather than mechanical stale-price or bid-ask-bounce effects."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _lagged_positive_volume_baseline(volume: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute a causal 20-session positive-volume baseline ending at t-1."""
    lagged_volume = volume.shift(1)
    positive_lagged_volume = lagged_volume.where(lagged_volume > 0.0)
    positive_count = positive_lagged_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=1).count()
    baseline = positive_lagged_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
    return baseline, positive_count


@register_factor
class ParticipationNormalizedImpactRecoil(BaseFactor):
    """Liquidity-screened low-participation price-impact dislocation rank."""

    factor_id = "participation_normalized_impact_recoil"
    name = "Liquidity-Screened Low-Participation Recoil"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of directional close-to-close impact scaled by "
        "intraday range and inverse current participation, restricted to names "
        "with adequate recent trading activity. Positive values identify upward "
        "low-participation dislocations expected to have weaker continuation or "
        "partial reversal over the next six sessions."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_previous_close = previous_close > 0.0
        valid_range = high.notna() & low.notna() & (high >= low)

        close_return = close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        range_fraction = (high - low) / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        valid_displacement = (
            valid_previous_close
            & valid_range
            & close_return.notna()
            & range_fraction.notna()
            & (range_fraction > 0.0)
        )

        volume_baseline, positive_history_count = _lagged_positive_volume_baseline(volume)
        valid_history = (positive_history_count >= 15.0) & (volume_baseline > 0.0)
        participation = volume / volume_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact = close_return * range_fraction / participation.clip(lower=0.10)

        baseline_cutoff = volume_baseline.where(valid_history).quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        sufficiently_liquid = volume_baseline.ge(baseline_cutoff, axis=0)
        eligible = (
            valid_displacement
            & valid_history
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & (volume >= 0.25 * volume_baseline)
            & sufficiently_liquid
            & impact.notna()
        )

        eligible_impact = impact.where(eligible)
        lower = eligible_impact.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = eligible_impact.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized_impact = eligible_impact.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)

        return rank(winsorized_impact) - 0.5

The signal deliberately does not claim to identify signed order flow or dealer inventory; it tests the narrower prediction that extreme low-participation dislocations have weaker six-session continuation and, on average, partial reversal. Screening out sparse and very low-volume names makes the hypothesis about tradable dislocations rather than mechanical stale-price or bid-ask-bounce effects.
programs.description: At the close of completed session t, use corporate-action-adjusted OHLC prices as supplied by the feed and define close-to-close return r_t = close_t / close_{t-1} - 1. Define the intraday range fraction q_t = (high_t - low_t) / close_{t-1}, requiring close_{t-1} > 0, high_t >= low_t, and q_t > 0. Define Vbar20_t as the arithmetic mean of volume over sessions t-20 through t-1, requiring at least 15 positive-volume observations; define participation p_t = volume_t / Vbar20_t, requiring volume_t > 0 and Vbar20_t > 0. Define impact I_t = r_t * q_t / max(p_t, 0.10), so a given directional close-to-close displacement receives greater magnitude only when contemporaneous volume is low relative to the stock's own recent participation. Before cross-sectional ranking, winsorize I_t each day at the 1st and 99th percentiles among eligible names. Eligibility requires valid I_t, at least 15 valid trailing-volume observations, current volume at least 25% of Vbar20_t, and Vbar20_t at or above the cross-sectional 30th percentile among names with valid histories; these conditions exclude zero-volume and persistently sparse names while retaining temporary below-normal participation. The factor value is the daily cross-sectional percentile rank of winsorized I_t, mapped to [-0.5, 0.5]; positive values denote positive low-participation dislocations and are expected to predict lower subsequent returns, while negative values denote negative dislocations and are expected to predict higher subsequent returns. The signal is formed only after the completed t daily bar and may be traded no earlier than the next executable bar.

"""The mechanism is not that a late consensus revision is intrinsically superior to delivered earnings information. Instead, an earnings release can reveal a measurable disagreement between pre-release analyst expectations and reported EPS/revenue news; when the market's immediate response has not moved in the direction of the pre-release residual revision, that expectation component may remain incompletely incorporated. The factor trades the direction of the pre-release residual revision only in this explicitly defined conflict state, treating it as an event-driven expectation-reconciliation signal rather than a general claim that revisions dominate surprises."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _clipped_revision(
    estimate: pd.DataFrame, short_lag: int, long_lag: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal percentage estimate revision using only estimates available before t."""
    recent = estimate.shift(short_lag)
    baseline = estimate.shift(long_lag)
    denominator = baseline.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
    return ((recent - baseline) / denominator).clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0)


def _peer_industry_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame, min_peers: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Equal-weighted same-date industry mean excluding the focal stock.

    A value is emitted only if the focal name has at least ``min_peers`` other
    eligible names with a non-missing value in its static industry.
    """
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    for row_pos in range(len(values.index)):
        row_values = values.iloc[row_pos]
        labels = industry.iloc[row_pos]
        eligible = row_values.notna() & labels.notna()
        if not bool(eligible.any()):
            continue

        selected_values = row_values.where(eligible)
        selected_labels = labels.where(eligible)
        group_sum = selected_values.groupby(selected_labels, sort=False).transform("sum")
        group_count = selected_values.groupby(selected_labels, sort=False).transform("count")
        peer_count = group_count - 1.0
        peer_mean = (group_sum - selected_values) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        output.iloc[row_pos] = peer_mean.where(peer_count >= float(min_peers))

    return output


def _trailing_revision_beta(
    stock_revision: pd.DataFrame, industry_revision: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing 252-session beta estimated strictly through the preceding bar."""
    stock_lagged = stock_revision.shift(1)
    industry_lagged = industry_revision.shift(1)

    covariance = stock_lagged.rolling(252, min_periods=126).cov(industry_lagged)
    variance = industry_lagged.rolling(252, min_periods=126).var()
    return covariance / variance.where(variance > 0.0)


@register_factor
class LateRevisionInformationDominance(BaseFactor):
    """Residual late revisions traded only when release news and price action conflict."""

    factor_id = "late_revision_information_dominance"
    name = "Pre-Release Revision Conflict Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks residual 21-session EPS estimate revisions only on detected earnings "
        "release events where late revisions conflict with reported-news surprise and "
        "have not been confirmed by the release-bar price response."
    )
    window_length = 274
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        industry = data["industry"].ffill()

        eps_revision_21 = _clipped_revision(eps_estimate, 1, 22)
        eps_revision_5 = _clipped_revision(eps_estimate, 1, 6)
        sales_revision_21 = _clipped_revision(revenue_estimate, 1, 22)
        sales_revision_5 = _clipped_revision(revenue_estimate, 1, 6)

        industry_sales_21 = _peer_industry_mean(sales_revision_21, industry, 5)
        industry_sales_5 = _peer_industry_mean(sales_revision_5, industry, 5)
        beta = _trailing_revision_beta(eps_revision_21, industry_sales_21)

        residual_21 = eps_revision_21 - beta * industry_sales_21
        residual_5 = eps_revision_5 - beta * industry_sales_5

        prior_eps_actual = eps_actual.shift(1)
        prior_revenue_actual = revenue_actual.shift(1)
        eps_new_or_changed = eps_actual.notna() & (
            prior_eps_actual.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_eps_actual)
        )
        revenue_new_or_changed = revenue_actual.notna() & (
            prior_revenue_actual.isna() | revenue_actual.ne(prior_revenue_actual)
        )
        release_event = (
            eps_actual.notna()
            & revenue_actual.notna()
            & (eps_new_or_changed | revenue_new_or_changed)
        )

        prior_eps_estimate = eps_estimate.shift(1)
        prior_revenue_estimate = revenue_estimate.shift(1)
        eps_news = data["epsSurprise"] / prior_eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revenue_news = data["revenueSurprise"] / prior_revenue_estimate.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        valid_news = release_event & eps_news.notna() & revenue_news.notna()

        eps_news_score = 2.0 * rank(eps_news.where(valid_news)) - 1.0
        revenue_news_score = 2.0 * rank(revenue_news.where(valid_news)) - 1.0
        news_composite = ((eps_news_score + revenue_news_score) / 2.0).where(valid_news)

        late_revision = (
            residual_21.notna()
            & residual_5.notna()
            & (residual_21.abs() >= 0.02)
            & ((residual_21 * residual_5) > 0.0)
            & (residual_5.abs() >= 0.60 * residual_21.abs())
        )

        release_return = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
        absolute_release_return = release_return.abs()
        median_release_move = absolute_release_return.where(release_event).median(axis=1)
        small_release_move = absolute_release_return.le(median_release_move, axis=0)
        price_conflict = ((release_return * residual_21) < 0.0) | small_release_move
        valid_price = release_return.notna() & median_release_move.notna().to_numpy()[:, None]

        news_conflict = (residual_21 * news_composite) < 0.0
        qualified = (
            release_event
            & late_revision
            & news_conflict
            & price_conflict
            & valid_price
        )

        ranked_residual = rank(residual_21.where(qualified))
        signal = (ranked_residual * np.sign(residual_21)).where(qualified, 0.0)
        return signal.fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The mechanism is not that a late consensus revision is intrinsically superior to delivered earnings information. Instead, an earnings release can reveal a measurable disagreement between pre-release analyst expectations and reported EPS/revenue news; when the market's immediate response has not moved in the direction of the pre-release residual revision, that expectation component may remain incompletely incorporated. The factor trades the direction of the pre-release residual revision only in this explicitly defined conflict state, treating it as an event-driven expectation-reconciliation signal rather than a general claim that revisions dominate surprises.
programs.description: A release event for stock i on date t is defined only when both epsActual and revenueActual are non-null at t and at least one of them is newly available or changes versus t-1; no earnings-calendar field is used. All estimate inputs are frozen strictly before the release: define the 21-session EPS revision E21_i,t = clip((epsEstimate_i,t-1 - epsEstimate_i,t-22) / max(abs(epsEstimate_i,t-22), 0.01), -2, 2), and the 5-session revision E5_i,t analogously using t-1 and t-6. Define contemporaneous industry sales revisions S21_g,t and S5_g,t as equal-weighted means of the corresponding clipped revenueEstimate percentage changes for other eligible stocks in the same static industry g, requiring at least five peers. Estimate a stock-specific beta using only data through t-1: beta_i,t = Cov(E21_i,s, S21_g,s) / Var(S21_g,s) over trailing daily observations s from t-252 through t-1, requiring at least 126 valid observations and positive industry-revision variance. Residual revisions are R21_i,t = E21_i,t - beta_i,t*S21_g,t and R5_i,t = E5_i,t - beta_i,t*S5_g,t. A revision is classified as late when abs(R21) is at least 2%, R5 and R21 have the same sign, and abs(R5) is at least 60% of abs(R21). The reported-news composite C_i,t is the average of cross-sectional percentile-rank scores, mapped to [-1,1], for epsSurprise_i,t / max(abs(epsEstimate_i,t-1), 0.01) and revenueSurprise_i,t / max(abs(revenueEstimate_i,t-1), 1,000,000), calculated among valid release events on t. A stock qualifies only when R21 and C have opposite non-zero signs. To avoid entering after the residual revision is already reflected, additionally require either the release-bar return G_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1 to have the opposite sign of R21, or abs(G_i,t) to be no greater than the cross-sectional median absolute release-bar return among valid release events that day. The signal is the cross-sectional rank of R21 among qualified names, signed in the direction of R21 and zero otherwise. Missing estimates, insufficient industry peers, unavailable trailing beta observations, stale/non-event actuals, or missing price data produce no signal. Positions are entered at the next tradable bar after t and evaluated over the fixed six-bar horizon.

programs.code:
"""The revised mechanism does not assume that every delivered EPS surprise is inferior to the prior analyst view. It applies only when an EPS surprise contradicts a strong, strictly pre-report residual consensus revision and is not corroborated by a material same-direction revenue surprise, making an earnings-only delivery more plausibly attributable to a temporary margin, expense, tax, or accounting realization rather than broad demand information. A muted completed-bar reaction identifies cases where this disagreement remains unresolved at the end of the event bar, so the position follows the pre-report residual consensus direction rather than mechanically fading all earnings surprises."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_revision_residuals(
    eps_revision: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_revision: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_group_size: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Estimate same-date, industry-specific OLS residuals causally.

    Inputs are already frozen at t-1 by the caller.  Each date's regression
    therefore uses only information available before the earnings event bar.
    """
    residual = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=eps_revision.index, columns=eps_revision.columns)
    residual_rank = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=eps_revision.index, columns=eps_revision.columns)

    for timestamp in eps_revision.index:
        y = eps_revision.loc[timestamp]
        x = revenue_revision.loc[timestamp]
        groups = industry.loc[timestamp]
        valid = y.notna() & x.notna() & groups.notna()

        if int(valid.sum()) < minimum_group_size:
            continue

        valid_groups = groups.loc[valid]
        grouped = valid_groups.groupby(valid_groups, sort=False).groups

        for _, members in grouped.items():
            if len(members) < minimum_group_size:
                continue

            x_group = x.loc[members].astype(float)
            y_group = y.loc[members].astype(float)
            x_centered = x_group - x_group.mean()
            denominator = float((x_centered * x_centered).sum())

            # With a constant revenue revision, the intercept-only OLS solution
            # is the well-defined limiting case of the regression.
            if np.isfinite(denominator) and denominator > 0.0:
                beta = float((x_centered * (y_group - y_group.mean())).sum() / denominator)
            else:
                beta = 0.0
            alpha = float(y_group.mean() - beta * x_group.mean())
            group_residual = y_group - alpha - beta * x_group

            residual.loc[timestamp, members] = group_residual.to_numpy()
            residual_rank.loc[timestamp, members] = group_residual.abs().rank(
                pct=True, method="average"
            ).to_numpy()

    return residual, residual_rank


def _earnings_event(
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify the first availability bar on which either earnings field changes."""
    actual_previous = eps_actual.shift(1)
    surprise_previous = eps_surprise.shift(1)

    actual_changed = eps_actual.notna() & (
        actual_previous.isna() | eps_actual.ne(actual_previous)
    )
    surprise_changed = eps_surprise.notna() & (
        surprise_previous.isna() | eps_surprise.ne(surprise_previous)
    )
    return actual_changed | surprise_changed


@register_factor
class ConsensusResidualDeliveryFade(BaseFactor):
    """Follow strong pre-report residual EPS revisions contradicted by unconfirmed delivery."""

    factor_id = "consensus_residual_delivery_fade"
    name = "Unconfirmed Delivery Residual Fade"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "At earnings availability events, follows the industry-residual pre-report "
        "EPS-consensus revision when the delivered EPS surprise contradicts it, "
        "revenue does not confirm the delivery, and the completed event-bar "
        "reaction is muted."
    )
    window_length = 22
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]

        # All consensus and classification inputs are explicitly frozen at t-1.
        eps_t_minus_1 = eps_estimate.shift(1)
        eps_t_minus_22 = eps_estimate.shift(22)
        revenue_t_minus_1 = revenue_estimate.shift(1)
        revenue_t_minus_22 = revenue_estimate.shift(22)
        industry_t_minus_1 = data["industry"].shift(1)

        valid_eps_revision = (
            eps_t_minus_1.notna()
            & eps_t_minus_22.notna()
            & (eps_t_minus_1 > 0.0)
            & (eps_t_minus_22 > 0.0)
        )
        valid_revenue_revision = (
            revenue_t_minus_1.notna()
            & revenue_t_minus_22.notna()
            & (revenue_t_minus_1 > 0.0)
            & (revenue_t_minus_22 > 0.0)
        )

        eps_revision = (eps_t_minus_1 / eps_t_minus_22) - 1.0
        revenue_revision = (revenue_t_minus_1 / revenue_t_minus_22) - 1.0
        eps_revision = eps_revision.where(valid_eps_revision)
        revenue_revision = revenue_revision.where(valid_revenue_revision)

        residual, residual_rank = _industry_revision_residuals(
            eps_revision,
            revenue_revision,
            industry_t_minus_1,
            8,
        )

        eps_scale = eps_t_minus_1.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revenue_scale = revenue_t_minus_1.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        standardized_eps_surprise = eps_surprise / eps_scale
        standardized_revenue_surprise = revenue_surprise / revenue_scale

        sales_confirmed = (
            (standardized_eps_surprise * standardized_revenue_surprise > 0.0)
            & (standardized_revenue_surprise.abs() >= 0.01)
        )

        event_bar_return = (close / close.shift(1)) - 1.0
        daily_return = (close / close.shift(1)) - 1.0
        pre_event_sigma = daily_return.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=15).std()

        event = _earnings_event(eps_actual, eps_surprise)
        contradictory_delivery = (
            np.sign(standardized_eps_surprise) * np.sign(residual) < 0.0
        )
        muted_reaction = event_bar_return.abs() <= (0.5 * pre_event_sigma)

        qualifies = (
            event
            & standardized_eps_surprise.notna()
            & standardized_revenue_surprise.notna()
            & (standardized_eps_surprise.abs() >= 0.02)
            & (~sales_confirmed)
            & contradictory_delivery
            & (residual_rank >= 0.80)
            & pre_event_sigma.notna()
            & muted_reaction
        )

        score = np.sign(residual) * residual_rank
        return score.where(qualifies, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

All belief variables are frozen at t-1. Using a fixed 21-bar pre-report revision window, define EPS-estimate revision rE_i,t = epsEstimate_i,t-1 / epsEstimate_i,t-22 - 1 and revenue-estimate revision rR_i,t = revenueEstimate_i,t-1 / revenueEstimate_i,t-22 - 1, requiring finite positive-denominator snapshots at both dates. Within each industry at t-1, using only stocks with valid rE and rR and at least 8 observations, estimate the cross-sectional OLS relation rE = alpha_industry + beta_industry*rR; the residual u_i,t = rE_i,t - alpha_industry - beta_industry*rR_i,t is the strictly pre-event sales-explained EPS-consensus revision. Define standardized EPS surprise z_i,t = epsSurprise_i,t / max(abs(epsEstimate_i,t-1), 0.01), and standardized revenue surprise q_i,t = revenueSurprise_i,t / max(abs(revenueEstimate_i,t-1), 1000000). Define sales confirmation C_i,t = 1 when z_i,t*q_i,t > 0 and abs(q_i,t) >= 0.01, otherwise 0; qualify only events with finite q and C=0, explicitly excluding EPS deliveries corroborated by a material same-direction revenue surprise. Require abs(z_i,t) >= 0.02, sign(z_i,t)*sign(u_i,t) < 0, and an within-industry percentile rank of abs(u_i,t) of at least 0.80 among valid pre-event residuals. The event reaction is R_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1, measured on the completed daily bar whose timestamp first makes the earnings fields available; define sigma_i,t as the sample standard deviation of daily close-to-close returns from t-21 through t-1, requiring at least 15 valid returns, and require abs(R_i,t) <= 0.5*sigma_i,t. The score for qualifying events is sign(u_i,t)*rank_industry(abs(u_i,t)); all nonqualifying observations receive zero. The signal is formed only after the completed event bar t is known, and execution is deferred to the next executable bar, t+1 open; no post-event estimate snapshot is used in the score.

programs.code:
"""Peer-anchor consensus restoration after unconfirmed earnings delivery.

Mechanism: an EPS-only delivery that contradicts residual pre-report consensus is
more likely temporary when neither revenue nor cash-flow growth corroborates it.
The restoration trade is strongest when the consensus direction also closes an
industry-relative operating-cash-flow valuation gap.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_residual_rank(
    eps_revision: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_revision: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Same-date industry residual EPS revisions and within-group magnitude ranks."""
    residual = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=eps_revision.index, columns=eps_revision.columns)
    magnitude = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=eps_revision.index, columns=eps_revision.columns)
    for timestamp in eps_revision.index:
        y = eps_revision.loc[timestamp]
        x = revenue_revision.loc[timestamp]
        labels = industry.loc[timestamp]
        valid = y.notna() & x.notna() & labels.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        for group in pd.unique(labels.loc[valid]):
            members = labels.index[valid & labels.eq(group)]
            if len(members) < 6:
                continue
            xv = x.loc[members].astype(float)
            yv = y.loc[members].astype(float)
            centered_x = xv - xv.mean()
            denominator = float((centered_x * centered_x).sum())
            if np.isfinite(denominator) and denominator > 0.0:
                beta = float((centered_x * (yv - yv.mean())).sum() / denominator)
            else:
                beta = 0.0
            fitted = yv.mean() + beta * centered_x
            group_residual = yv - fitted
            residual.loc[timestamp, members] = group_residual.to_numpy()
            magnitude.loc[timestamp, members] = group_residual.abs().rank(
                pct=True, method="average"
            ).to_numpy()
    return residual, magnitude


def _industry_peer_yield(
    cash_yield: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Map each name to its adequately populated same-date industry median yield."""
    peer = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=cash_yield.index, columns=cash_yield.columns)
    for timestamp in cash_yield.index:
        values = cash_yield.loc[timestamp]
        labels = industry.loc[timestamp]
        valid = values.notna() & np.isfinite(values) & labels.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        selected_values = values.loc[valid]
        selected_labels = labels.loc[valid]
        counts = selected_values.groupby(selected_labels).count()
        medians = selected_values.groupby(selected_labels).median()
        qualifying = counts[counts.ge(3)].index
        if len(qualifying) == 0:
            continue
        eligible = selected_labels[selected_labels.isin(qualifying)]
        peer.loc[timestamp, eligible.index] = eligible.map(medians).to_numpy()
    return peer


def _carry_event_score(event_score: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Carry a report signal for five sessions using a causal exponential kernel."""
    rows, cols = event_score.shape
    positions = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (rows, cols)),
        index=event_score.index,
        columns=event_score.columns,
    )
    last_event = positions.where(event_score.notna()).ffill()
    age = positions - last_event
    carried = event_score.ffill(limit=5)
    return (carried * np.exp(-age / 2.5)).where(age.le(5))


@register_factor
class PeerAnchorConsensusRestorationDelivery(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_anchor_consensus_restoration_delivery"
    name = "Peer-Anchor Consensus Restoration"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Follows pre-report residual consensus after an unconfirmed contradictory "
        "EPS delivery, conditional on consensus alignment with an industry cash-yield anchor."
    )
    window_length = 22
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "marketCap",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex_like(close)

        eps_pre = eps_estimate.shift(1)
        eps_old = eps_estimate.shift(22)
        revenue_pre = revenue_estimate.shift(1)
        revenue_old = revenue_estimate.shift(22)
        valid_revision = (
            eps_pre.notna()
            & eps_old.notna()
            & eps_pre.abs().ge(0.01)
            & eps_old.abs().ge(0.01)
            & revenue_pre.notna()
            & revenue_old.notna()
            & revenue_pre.abs().ge(1000000.0)
            & revenue_old.abs().ge(1000000.0)
        )
        eps_revision = ((eps_pre - eps_old) / eps_old.abs()).where(valid_revision)
        revenue_revision = ((revenue_pre - revenue_old) / revenue_old.abs()).where(valid_revision)
        residual, residual_rank = _industry_residual_rank(
            eps_revision.clip(-3.0, 3.0),
            revenue_revision.clip(-3.0, 3.0),
            industry.shift(1),
        )

        eps_scaled = eps_surprise.div(eps_pre.abs().clip(lower=0.05)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        revenue_scaled = revenue_surprise.div(
            revenue_pre.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        ).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        cash_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(close).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        eps_changed = eps_actual.notna() & (
            eps_actual.shift(1).isna() | eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
        )
        surprise_changed = eps_surprise.notna() & (
            eps_surprise.shift(1).isna() | eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1))
        )
        event = eps_changed | surprise_changed

        revenue_confirms = (
            eps_scaled.mul(revenue_scaled).gt(0.0)
            & revenue_scaled.abs().ge(0.01)
        )
        cash_confirms = (
            eps_scaled.mul(cash_growth).gt(0.0)
            & cash_growth.abs().ge(0.05)
        )
        contradictory = np.sign(eps_scaled).mul(np.sign(residual)).lt(0.0)

        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"].reindex_like(close)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex_like(close)
        cash_yield = operating_cash_flow.div(market_cap).where(
            operating_cash_flow.gt(0.0) & market_cap.gt(0.0)
        )
        peer_yield = _industry_peer_yield(cash_yield, industry)
        anchor_gap = np.log(cash_yield.div(peer_yield)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        anchor_direction = np.sign(2.0 * rank(anchor_gap) - 1.0)
        anchor_agrees = np.sign(residual).mul(anchor_direction).gt(0.0)

        daily_return = close.div(close.shift(1)).sub(1.0)
        pre_event_sigma = daily_return.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=15).std()
        muted_reaction = daily_return.abs().le(0.6 * pre_event_sigma)

        qualifies = (
            event
            & eps_scaled.notna()
            & contradictory
            & residual_rank.ge(0.75)
            & anchor_agrees
            & (~revenue_confirms)
            & (~cash_confirms)
            & pre_event_sigma.notna()
            & muted_reaction
        )
        event_score = (np.sign(residual) * residual_rank * eps_scaled.abs()).where(qualifies)
        carried = _carry_event_score(event_score)
        raw = carried.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return (rank(raw).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).reindex_like(close)

programs.trading_idea: The child treats an earnings-only surprise that contradicts pre-report residual consensus as potentially transitory, but trades only when the prior consensus direction is also supported by an industry-relative operating-cash-flow valuation anchor. This combines Parent B's distinction between unconfirmed EPS delivery and broad demand news with Parent A's peer valuation state variable: the market has two independent reasons to restore the pre-report direction, rather than merely fading a surprise. The interaction carries edge because consensus disagreement alone can reflect stale analyst views, while a valuation anchor alone cannot distinguish a credible delivery from a margin, tax, or accounting shock.
programs.description: At report events, follows the pre-report industry-residual EPS revision when an EPS surprise opposes it, revenue and cash-flow growth do not confirm the surprise, the event-bar reaction is muted, and the consensus direction agrees with the stock's industry-relative operating-cash-flow-yield valuation gap. The event score is carried for five sessions with exponential decay.

"""The signal targets delayed incorporation of a public earnings delivery only when the delivery is corroborated by contemporaneously reported cash realization and operating-margin evidence. Rather than treating a muted move as sufficient evidence of underreaction, it measures the stock's reaction shortfall relative to a fixed, out-of-sample historical model of reactions to comparable surprises, quality alignment, size, and pre-event relative performance. The position is formed only after the first fully observable reaction session has closed and is entered on the following executable bar, so the mechanism is a short-lived analyst and investor processing drift rather than same-session event trading."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _event_changes(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Detect changes relative to the immediately preceding non-null state."""
    prior_non_null = frame.ffill().shift(1)
    return frame.notna() & prior_non_null.notna() & ~frame.eq(prior_non_null)


def _static_industry_labels(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> list[object]:
    """Extract static industry labels while tolerating sparse initial rows."""
    labels: list[object] = []
    for column in industry.columns:
        values = industry[column].dropna()
        labels.append(values.iloc[0] if not values.empty else np.nan)
    return labels


def _industry_returns(
    stock_returns: pd.DataFrame, labels: list[object]
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return inclusive industry mean and leave-one-out industry return."""
    inclusive = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stock_returns.index, columns=stock_returns.columns)
    leave_one_out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stock_returns.index, columns=stock_returns.columns)

    groups: dict[object, list[int]] = {}
    for col_idx, label in enumerate(labels):
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(col_idx)

    for members in groups.values():
        block = stock_returns.iloc[:, members]
        count = block.notna().sum(axis=1)
        total = block.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        mean = total / count.replace(0, np.nan)
        inclusive.iloc[:, members] = np.repeat(mean.to_numpy()[:, None], len(members), axis=1)

        denominator = count - 1
        loo = block.rsub(total, axis=0).div(denominator.replace(0, np.nan), axis=0)
        leave_one_out.iloc[:, members] = loo

    return inclusive, leave_one_out


def _robust_cohort_confirmation(
    event_mask: np.ndarray,
    surprise: np.ndarray,
    cash_change: np.ndarray,
    margin_change: np.ndarray,
    income_quality: np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Compute same-bar MAD-standardized signed quality confirmation."""
    rows, cols = event_mask.shape
    confirmation = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    for t in range(rows):
        candidates = np.flatnonzero(
            event_mask[t]
            & np.isfinite(surprise[t])
            & np.isfinite(cash_change[t])
            & np.isfinite(margin_change[t])
            & np.isfinite(income_quality[t])
        )
        if candidates.size == 0:
            continue

        standardized: list[np.ndarray] = []
        valid_cohort = True
        for values in (cash_change[t, candidates], margin_change[t, candidates], income_quality[t, candidates]):
            median = np.median(values)
            mad = np.median(np.abs(values - median))
            if not np.isfinite(mad) or mad <= 0.0:
                valid_cohort = False
                break
            standardized.append((values - median) / (1.4826 * mad))

        if valid_cohort:
            quality_average = (standardized[0] + standardized[1] + standardized[2]) / 3.0
            confirmation[t, candidates] = np.sign(surprise[t, candidates]) * quality_average

    return confirmation


def _event_features(
    event_mask: np.ndarray,
    eps_surprise: np.ndarray,
    cash_margin: np.ndarray,
    operating_margin: np.ndarray,
    income_quality: np.ndarray,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Build event-time surprise and quarter-over-quarter quality changes."""
    rows, cols = event_mask.shape
    surprise_z = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    cash_change = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    margin_change = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    quality = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    for j in range(cols):
        event_rows = np.flatnonzero(event_mask[:, j])
        for event_number, t in enumerate(event_rows):
            prior_rows = event_rows[max(0, event_number - 8):event_number]
            if prior_rows.size >= 4:
                prior_surprises = eps_surprise[prior_rows, j]
                prior_surprises = prior_surprises[np.isfinite(prior_surprises)]
                if prior_surprises.size >= 4 and np.isfinite(eps_surprise[t, j]):
                    median = np.median(prior_surprises)
                    mad = np.median(np.abs(prior_surprises - median))
                    if np.isfinite(mad) and mad > 0.0:
                        surprise_z[t, j] = (eps_surprise[t, j] - median) / (1.4826 * mad)

            if event_number > 0:
                previous_t = event_rows[event_number - 1]
                current_cash = cash_margin[t, j]
                previous_cash = cash_margin[previous_t, j]
                current_margin = operating_margin[t, j]
                previous_margin = operating_margin[previous_t, j]
                if np.isfinite(current_cash) and np.isfinite(previous_cash):
                    cash_change[t, j] = current_cash - previous_cash
                if np.isfinite(current_margin) and np.isfinite(previous_margin):
                    margin_change[t, j] = current_margin - previous_margin

            if np.isfinite(income_quality[t, j]):
                quality[t, j] = income_quality[t, j]

    return surprise_z, cash_change, margin_change, quality


def _rolling_reaction_deficit(
    eligible: np.ndarray,
    surprise: np.ndarray,
    confirmation: np.ndarray,
    log_market_cap: np.ndarray,
    pre_event_relative_return: np.ndarray,
    reaction: np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Fit trailing pooled OLS reaction models using only strictly prior bars."""
    rows, cols = eligible.shape
    deficit = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    record_t, record_j = np.nonzero(eligible)
    if record_t.size == 0:
        return deficit

    record_s = surprise[record_t, record_j]
    record_c = confirmation[record_t, record_j]
    record_cap = log_market_cap[record_t, record_j]
    record_pre = pre_event_relative_return[record_t, record_j]
    record_y = reaction[record_t, record_j]

    for t in range(rows):
        current_j = np.flatnonzero(eligible[t])
        if current_j.size == 0:
            continue

        in_window = (record_t >= max(0, t - 252)) & (record_t < t)
        if int(in_window.sum()) < 200:
            continue

        train_s = record_s[in_window]
        train_c = record_c[in_window]
        train_cap = record_cap[in_window]
        train_pre = record_pre[in_window]
        train_y = record_y[in_window]
        train_x = np.column_stack((train_s, train_c, train_s * train_c, train_cap, train_pre))
        finite_train = np.isfinite(train_x).all(axis=1) & np.isfinite(train_y)
        if int(finite_train.sum()) < 200:
            continue

        train_x = train_x[finite_train]
        train_y = train_y[finite_train]
        lower = np.nanquantile(train_x, 0.01, axis=0)
        upper = np.nanquantile(train_x, 0.99, axis=0)
        train_x = np.clip(train_x, lower, upper)
        design = np.column_stack((np.ones(train_x.shape[0]), train_x))

        try:
            coefficients = np.linalg.lstsq(design, train_y, rcond=None)[0]
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            continue

        current_s = surprise[t, current_j]
        current_c = confirmation[t, current_j]
        current_x = np.column_stack(
            (
                current_s,
                current_c,
                current_s * current_c,
                log_market_cap[t, current_j],
                pre_event_relative_return[t, current_j],
            )
        )
        finite_current = np.isfinite(current_x).all(axis=1)
        if not finite_current.any():
            continue
        clipped = np.clip(current_x[finite_current], lower, upper)
        predicted = np.column_stack((np.ones(clipped.shape[0]), clipped)) @ coefficients
        selected_j = current_j[finite_current]
        deficit[t, selected_j] = reaction[t, selected_j] - predicted

    return deficit


@register_factor
class CredibleEarningsReactionDeficitDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks credible earnings events whose completed reaction undershoots its historical expectation."""

    factor_id = "credible_earnings_reaction_deficit_drift"
    name = "Timestamped Earnings Reaction Deficit"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Post-reaction earnings drift signal: robust event surprise and cash/margin "
        "confirmation identify credible deliveries, while a strictly trailing pooled "
        "reaction model isolates stocks whose industry-relative reaction was muted."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueActual",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "revenue",
        "operatingMargin",
        "incomeQuality",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        index = close.index
        columns = close.columns

        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns).astype(float)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns).astype(float)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns).astype(float)
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns).astype(float)
        revenue = data["revenue"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns).astype(float)
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns).astype(float)
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns).astype(float)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns).astype(float)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex(index=index, columns=columns)

        detected_events = (
            _event_changes(eps_actual)
            | _event_changes(eps_surprise)
            | _event_changes(revenue_actual)
        )
        event_array = detected_events.to_numpy(dtype=bool)

        cash_margin = operating_cash_flow / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        surprise, cash_change, margin_change, quality = _event_features(
            event_array,
            eps_surprise.to_numpy(dtype=float),
            cash_margin.to_numpy(dtype=float),
            operating_margin.to_numpy(dtype=float),
            income_quality.to_numpy(dtype=float),
        )
        confirmation = _robust_cohort_confirmation(
            event_array, surprise, cash_change, margin_change, quality
        )

        stock_return = close.pct_change()
        labels = _static_industry_labels(industry)
        industry_mean, industry_leave_one_out = _industry_returns(stock_return, labels)
        relative_return = stock_return - industry_mean
        pre_event_relative = relative_return.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
        reaction = stock_return - industry_leave_one_out

        market_cap_array = market_cap.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        log_market_cap = np.where(market_cap_array > 0.0, np.log(market_cap_array), np.nan)
        pre_array = pre_event_relative.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        reaction_array = reaction.to_numpy(dtype=float)

        eligible = (
            event_array
            & np.isfinite(surprise)
            & np.isfinite(confirmation)
            & (confirmation > 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(log_market_cap)
            & np.isfinite(pre_array)
            & np.isfinite(reaction_array)
        )
        for j, label in enumerate(labels):
            if pd.isna(label):
                eligible[:, j] = False

        deficit = _rolling_reaction_deficit(
            eligible,
            surprise,
            confirmation,
            log_market_cap,
            pre_array,
            reaction_array,
        )
        delivery = surprise * confirmation
        raw_score = delivery * (-deficit)
        valid_raw = eligible & np.isfinite(raw_score)

        event_rank = np.full(raw_score.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
        for t in range(raw_score.shape[0]):
            active = np.flatnonzero(valid_raw[t])
            if active.size:
                values = pd.Series(raw_score[t, active]).rank(pct=True, method="average").to_numpy()
                event_rank[t, active] = values

        output = np.zeros(raw_score.shape, dtype=float)
        rows, cols = output.shape
        for j in range(cols):
            latest_event = -1
            latest_score = np.nan
            for t in range(rows):
                if np.isfinite(event_rank[t, j]):
                    latest_event = t
                    latest_score = event_rank[t, j]

                age = t - latest_event
                if latest_event >= 0 and 1 <= age <= 6:
                    output[t, j] = latest_score * np.exp(-np.log(2.0) * (age - 1) / 3.0)

        return pd.DataFrame(output, index=index, columns=columns)

programs.trading_idea: The signal targets delayed incorporation of a public earnings delivery only when the delivery is corroborated by contemporaneously reported cash realization and operating-margin evidence. Rather than treating a muted move as sufficient evidence of underreaction, it measures the stock's reaction shortfall relative to a fixed, out-of-sample historical model of reactions to comparable surprises, quality alignment, size, and pre-event relative performance. The position is formed only after the first fully observable reaction session has closed and is entered on the following executable bar, so the mechanism is a short-lived analyst and investor processing drift rather than same-session event trading.
programs.description: Define an earnings event for stock i as the first point-in-time timestamp at which any of epsActual, epsSurprise, or revenueActual changes from its immediately preceding non-null reported state. This timestamp is the public-availability timestamp; no filing-date shift is applied. The reaction bar is the first regular-session daily bar whose session opens at or after that timestamp: therefore a pre-open update uses that calendar day's completed bar, while an after-close or intraday update uses the next trading day's completed bar. The factor is calculated only after the reaction bar closes and can be traded no earlier than the following executable bar. Standardized EPS surprise S is epsSurprise standardized against the stock's prior eight detected earnings events, excluding the current event, using (current surprise minus trailing-event median) divided by 1.4826 times trailing-event MAD; require at least four prior events and a positive MAD. For each event, compute cash-flow margin as operatingCashFlow / revenue and obtain its change from the preceding detected earnings event; likewise compute the change in operatingMargin and use current incomeQuality. Within the eligible same-reaction-bar event cohort, robust-standardize these three quantities using cohort median and MAD, and define signed confirmation C = sign(S) times their equal-weight average. An event is eligible only if S, all confirmation inputs, positive marketCap, industry, and sufficient price history are available, and if C is positive; this requires good-news events to have favorable cash/operating evidence and bad-news events to have unfavorable evidence. The signed delivery variable is D = S multiplied by C. Define the stock reaction return as close on the reaction bar divided by close on the preceding trading bar minus one. Define industry-relative reaction R as that return less the equal-weight mean reaction return of all price-valid stocks in the same industry on that bar, excluding the stock itself. The implied reaction is generated by a fixed pooled OLS model estimated only from eligible earnings events whose reaction bars fall in the prior 252 trading days, excluding all current-bar observations. The dependent variable is R; regressors are an intercept, S, C, S times C, log(marketCap), and the stock's pre-event 20-trading-day industry-relative close-to-close return. Continuous regressors are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles of the training observations. Require at least 200 prior eligible event observations; otherwise emit no signal. For each current event, predicted reaction is the fitted model value and reaction deficit E = R minus predicted reaction. The raw event score is D times negative E: credible positive delivery with a smaller-than-implied reaction scores positively, while credible negative delivery with a less-negative-than-implied reaction scores negatively. Cross-sectionally rank raw scores among active eligible names. Carry only the most recent eligible event per stock, replacing any prior event on a newer event, for six executable bars beginning with the bar after the reaction bar; apply deterministic exponential decay exp(-ln(2) times (k-1) / 3) for k = 1 through 6, then set the event score to zero.

"""Peer-anchored credible earnings-reaction shortfall.

Mechanism: a cash- and margin-confirmed earnings delivery can drift after an
underreaction, particularly when the delivery points toward closing an
industry-relative operating-cash-flow valuation gap.
"""

def _event_change(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify newly available report values without treating initial coverage as an event."""
    prior = frame.ffill().shift(1)
    return frame.notna() & prior.notna() & frame.ne(prior)

def _industry_leave_one_out_return(stock_return: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal same-day leave-one-out industry benchmark."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stock_return.index, columns=stock_return.columns)
    labels = []
    for column in industry.columns:
        observed = industry[column].dropna()
        labels.append(observed.iloc[0] if not observed.empty else np.nan)
    groups: dict[object, list[int]] = {}
    for j, label in enumerate(labels):
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(j)
    for members in groups.values():
        block = stock_return.iloc[:, members]
        count = block.notna().sum(axis=1)
        total = block.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        loo = block.rsub(total, axis=0).div((count - 1).replace(0, np.nan), axis=0)
        result.iloc[:, members] = loo.to_numpy()
    return result

def _industry_median(values: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Map each stock to a sufficiently populated same-date industry median."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for timestamp in values.index:
        row = values.loc[timestamp]
        labels = industry.loc[timestamp]
        valid = row.notna() & np.isfinite(row) & labels.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        selected_values = row.loc[valid]
        selected_labels = labels.loc[valid]
        counts = selected_values.groupby(selected_labels).count()
        medians = selected_values.groupby(selected_labels).median()
        eligible_groups = counts[counts.ge(4)].index
        eligible = selected_labels[selected_labels.isin(eligible_groups)]
        if not eligible.empty:
            output.loc[timestamp, eligible.index] = eligible.map(medians).to_numpy()
    return output

def _prior_pooled_expected_reaction(eligible: np.ndarray, surprise: np.ndarray, confirmation: np.ndarray, log_cap: np.ndarray, reaction: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Strictly trailing pooled OLS expectation for an event-day reaction."""
    rows, cols = eligible.shape
    expected = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    record_t, record_j = np.nonzero(eligible)
    if record_t.size == 0:
        return expected
    rec_s = surprise[record_t, record_j]
    rec_q = confirmation[record_t, record_j]
    rec_c = log_cap[record_t, record_j]
    rec_y = reaction[record_t, record_j]
    for t in range(rows):
        current = np.flatnonzero(eligible[t])
        if current.size == 0:
            continue
        history = (record_t < t) & (record_t >= max(0, t - 252))
        if int(history.sum()) < 80:
            continue
        train_x = np.column_stack((rec_s[history], rec_q[history], rec_s[history] * rec_q[history], rec_c[history]))
        train_y = rec_y[history]
        finite = np.isfinite(train_x).all(axis=1) & np.isfinite(train_y)
        if int(finite.sum()) < 80:
            continue
        train_x = train_x[finite]
        train_y = train_y[finite]
        lower = np.nanquantile(train_x, 0.02, axis=0)
        upper = np.nanquantile(train_x, 0.98, axis=0)
        clipped_train = np.clip(train_x, lower, upper)
        design = np.column_stack((np.ones(clipped_train.shape[0]), clipped_train))
        try:
            coefficient = np.linalg.lstsq(design, train_y, rcond=None)[0]
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            continue
        current_x = np.column_stack((surprise[t, current], confirmation[t, current], surprise[t, current] * confirmation[t, current], log_cap[t, current]))
        finite_current = np.isfinite(current_x).all(axis=1)
        if finite_current.any():
            predicted = np.column_stack((np.ones(int(finite_current.sum())), np.clip(current_x[finite_current], lower, upper))) @ coefficient
            expected[t, current[finite_current]] = predicted
    return expected

def _carry_after_reaction(event_score: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Enter one completed session after the event and decay over the next six bars."""
    delayed = event_score.shift(1)
    rows, cols = delayed.shape
    position = pd.DataFrame(np.broadcast_to(np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (rows, cols)), index=delayed.index, columns=delayed.columns)
    last = position.where(delayed.notna()).ffill()
    age = position - last
    carried = delayed.ffill(limit=5)
    return (carried * np.exp(-age / 3.0)).where(age.ge(0.0) & age.le(5.0))

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
