programs.trading_idea: The signal tests a narrowly defined dissemination-gap mechanism rather than treating an unchanged consensus as uniquely diagnostic of analyst delay. On a newly observable earnings release, a positive (negative) fundamental delivery that is accompanied by a smaller-than-cross-sectionally-expected same-bar upward (downward) consensus response can continue to reprice if the release also passes contemporaneous operating-cash-flow and receivables-collection checks. The quality screen is intended to remove events where a weak estimate response is more plausibly a rational judgment that the reported surprise is transitory, although the factor remains an empirical test of that distinction rather than a claim that it is identified perfectly.
programs.description: At decision bar t, define a fresh report event only when epsActual, revenueActual, epsSurprise, revenueSurprise, epsEstimate, revenueEstimate, close, marketCap, operatingCashFlowGrowth, revenueGrowth, and receivablesGrowth are all finite; close and marketCap must be strictly positive; and at least one of epsActual, revenueActual, or epsSurprise is finite at t and either was missing at t-1 or differs from its t-1 value. Require epsEstimate and revenueEstimate also to be finite at t-1, so same-bar consensus innovations are observable; values supplied as NaN by the feed are excluded, including its built-in long-staleness cases. No coverage-count field exists in scope, so low coverage is not inferred or separately filtered; the estimate-continuity requirement is the deterministic minimum-information rule. Zero actuals, zero estimates, zero surprises, and zero growth values are retained, while zero or negative close and marketCap are excluded. Define EPS delivery as epsSurprise/close and revenue delivery as revenueSurprise/marketCap. Define same-date EPS consensus innovation as (epsEstimate[t]-epsEstimate[t-1])/close and revenue consensus innovation as (revenueEstimate[t]-revenueEstimate[t-1])/marketCap. On each bar, among eligible fresh events, convert each of these four signed quantities to its cross-sectional average-tie percentile rank minus 0.5; require at least 20 eligible events or emit no signal for that bar. Delivery D is the mean of the centered EPS-delivery and revenue-delivery ranks, and consensus response R is the mean of the centered EPS-innovation and revenue-innovation ranks. Define operating cash confirmation as the centered percentile rank of operatingCashFlowGrowth and collection confirmation as the centered percentile rank of revenueGrowth minus receivablesGrowth, both ranked only within the same eligible fresh-event cross-section. Retain an event only if both confirmation ranks are at least 0, meaning neither cash-flow growth nor revenue-relative receivables collection is below the event-day median. The signed factor score is G=D-R: high values are favorable delivery with a comparatively muted upward consensus response, while low values are unfavorable delivery with a comparatively muted downward response. For portfolio construction, rank G separately among retained events with D>0 and among retained events with D<0: buy the highest 20% of the positive-delivery group and short the lowest 20% of the negative-delivery group, equal-weighted within side; if either side has fewer than five names, that side is held empty. All event detection, ranks, confirmation variables, and consensus changes use only values available at t; no later filing, later estimate revision, or post-event confirmation is used.

programs.code:
"""The tested mechanism is not symmetric cash confirmation of any earnings surprise: improving operating-cash conversion corroborates favorable dual EPS-and-revenue news, while deteriorating conversion corroborates unfavorable dual news. Conditional on this directional agreement, a small announcement-day close-to-close response relative to pre-event idiosyncratic volatility identifies incomplete initial incorporation rather than a mechanically large headline reaction. The incremental claim is specifically the three-way interaction of dual surprise agreement, change in cash-conversion state, and muted standardized response, rather than a standalone PEAD or cash-quality signal."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _event_robust_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal same-day cross-sectional winsorized median/MAD z-score."""
    masked = values.where(eligible)
    count = eligible.sum(axis=1)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    winsorized = masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)

    median = winsorized.median(axis=1)
    mad = winsorized.sub(median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
    scale = 1.4826 * mad

    zscore = winsorized.sub(median, axis=0).div(scale.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
    zscore = zscore.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
    sufficient = count >= 20
    return zscore.where(eligible & sufficient, np.nan)


def _pre_event_idiosyncratic_volatility(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing 60-bar residual volatility using only observations through t-1."""
    ret = close.div(close.shift(1)).sub(1.0)
    ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    market_return = ret.median(axis=1)

    past_ret = ret.shift(1)
    past_market = market_return.shift(1)
    covariance = past_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(past_market)
    market_variance = past_market.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
    beta = covariance.div(market_variance.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)

    residual = ret.sub(beta.mul(market_return, axis=0))
    return residual.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()


@register_factor
class CashConversionReactionElasticityBacklog(BaseFactor):
    """Dual earnings-revenue surprise drift confirmed by cash conversion and muted reaction."""

    factor_id = "cash_conversion_reaction_elasticity_backlog"
    name = "Cash-State Dual-Surprise Underreaction"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Event-only dual EPS and revenue surprise score retained when operating "
        "cash conversion changes in the same direction and the announcement-day "
        "reaction is muted relative to trailing idiosyncratic volatility."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "revenue",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]

        prior_eps_actual = eps_actual.shift(1)
        prior_revenue_actual = revenue_actual.shift(1)
        event = (
            eps_actual.notna()
            & revenue_actual.notna()
            & eps_estimate.notna()
            & revenue_estimate.notna()
            & prior_eps_actual.notna()
            & prior_revenue_actual.notna()
            & eps_actual.ne(prior_eps_actual)
            & revenue_actual.ne(prior_revenue_actual)
        )

        eps_denominator = eps_actual.abs().add(eps_estimate.abs())
        revenue_denominator = revenue_actual.abs().add(revenue_estimate.abs())
        eps_surprise = eps_actual.sub(eps_estimate).div(eps_denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        revenue_surprise = revenue_actual.sub(revenue_estimate).div(
            revenue_denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        cash_conversion = operating_cash_flow.div(revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        prior_revenue = revenue.shift(1)
        prior_cash_conversion = cash_conversion.shift(1)
        cash_valid = (
            revenue.gt(0.0)
            & prior_revenue.gt(0.0)
            & cash_conversion.notna()
            & prior_cash_conversion.notna()
            & np.isfinite(cash_conversion)
            & np.isfinite(prior_cash_conversion)
        )
        delta_cash_conversion = cash_conversion.sub(prior_cash_conversion)

        eligible = (
            event
            & eps_denominator.gt(0.0)
            & revenue_denominator.gt(0.0)
            & cash_valid
            & eps_surprise.notna()
            & revenue_surprise.notna()
            & delta_cash_conversion.notna()
            & np.isfinite(delta_cash_conversion)
        )

        z_eps = _event_robust_zscore(eps_surprise, eligible)
        z_revenue = _event_robust_zscore(revenue_surprise, eligible)
        z_cash = _event_robust_zscore(delta_cash_conversion, eligible)

        positive_dual = z_eps.gt(0.0) & z_revenue.gt(0.0)
        negative_dual = z_eps.lt(0.0) & z_revenue.lt(0.0)
        dual_score = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        dual_score = dual_score.where(~positive_dual, z_eps.where(z_eps.le(z_revenue), z_revenue))
        dual_score = dual_score.where(~negative_dual, z_eps.where(z_eps.ge(z_revenue), z_revenue))

        coherent_cash_state = (dual_score.gt(0.0) & z_cash.gt(0.0)) | (
            dual_score.lt(0.0) & z_cash.lt(0.0)
        )

        daily_return = close.div(close.shift(1)).sub(1.0)
        idiosyncratic_volatility = _pre_event_idiosyncratic_volatility(close)
        standardized_reaction = daily_return.div(
            idiosyncratic_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        muted_weight = (1.0 - standardized_reaction.abs()).clip(lower=0.0)

        raw_score = dual_score.mul(z_cash.abs()).mul(muted_weight)
        raw_score = raw_score.where(eligible & coherent_cash_state, 0.0)
        return raw_score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The tested mechanism is not symmetric cash confirmation of any earnings surprise: improving operating-cash conversion corroborates favorable dual EPS-and-revenue news, while deteriorating conversion corroborates unfavorable dual news. Conditional on this directional agreement, a small announcement-day close-to-close response relative to pre-event idiosyncratic volatility identifies incomplete initial incorporation rather than a mechanically large headline reaction. The incremental claim is specifically the three-way interaction of dual surprise agreement, change in cash-conversion state, and muted standardized response, rather than a standalone PEAD or cash-quality signal.
programs.description: At date t, define an event solely from PIT fields: epsActual, revenueActual, epsEstimate, and revenueEstimate must all be non-null, and both epsActual and revenueActual must differ from their respective t-1 values; all other dates receive a zero signal. For event names, define bounded proportional surprises s_eps=(epsActual-epsEstimate)/(abs(epsActual)+abs(epsEstimate)) and s_rev=(revenueActual-revenueEstimate)/(abs(revenueActual)+abs(revenueEstimate)); exclude zero denominators. On the event cross-section, winsorize each surprise at its 5th and 95th percentiles, standardize using (x-cross-sectional median)/(1.4826 times cross-sectional median absolute deviation), and clip standardized values to [-3,3]. Define the dual-surprise score D as min(z_eps,z_rev) when both standardized surprises are positive, max(z_eps,z_rev) when both are negative, and zero otherwise. Define cash conversion C=operatingCashFlow/revenue, requiring positive current and prior-bar revenue and finite C at t and t-1; delta_C=C_t-C_(t-1) is winsorized, median/MAD-standardized, and clipped identically on the event cross-section. Retain positive D only when standardized delta_C is positive and negative D only when it is negative, so the cash-state leg is directionally coherent. Compute the announcement-day return r_t=close_t/close_(t-1)-1. Estimate a market proxy as the cross-sectional median daily close return, estimate each stock's beta using a trailing 60-bar rolling covariance with that proxy divided by its rolling proxy variance using observations through t-1 only, and define residual returns as stock return minus beta times proxy return. The idiosyncratic-volatility estimate sigma is the trailing 60-bar standard deviation of residual returns through t-1, requiring at least 40 valid observations. Let a=r_t/sigma and let the muted-response weight be M=max(0,1-abs(a)); this gives full weight to no close-to-close reaction and zero weight at or above one pre-event idiosyncratic-volatility move. The raw event score is D times abs(z_delta_C) times M, with sign inherited from D; require at least 20 eligible event names before cross-sectional statistics are formed. The close at t is used only to measure the reaction: positions are formed at the next executable bar's open, t+1, and evaluated over the fixed subsequent six-bar horizon. As a mandatory factor-book overlay and validation test, residualize the event score cross-sectionally against the contemporaneous approved scores of earnings_surprise_cashflow_confirmation, fresh_eps_surprise_drift, operating_delivery_disbelief_release, and credible_disclosure_downside_rejection_cascade; retain only the residual score and require positive incremental alpha after that neutralization. The raw calculation itself uses only the listed PIT fundamental fields and daily OHLC data.

"""Cash-confirmed, tax-clean earnings news masked by sector basket flow."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_transform(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, method: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Apply a same-date aggregation within static sector labels."""
    return frame.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform(method).T


def _basket_state_and_residual(
    intraday_return: pd.DataFrame,
    abnormal_volume: pd.DataFrame,
    sector_panel: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Sector-relative return and broad positive-volume basket-flow indicator."""
    columns = intraday_return.columns
    supplied = sector_panel.reindex(columns=columns).iloc[0].astype(object)
    fallback = pd.Series(["__single_" + str(c) for c in columns], index=columns)
    labels = supplied.where(supplied.notna(), fallback)

    sector_return = _sector_transform(intraday_return, labels, "median")
    residual = intraday_return - sector_return
    count = _sector_transform(abnormal_volume.notna().astype(float), labels, "sum")
    breadth = _sector_transform(
        abnormal_volume.gt(0.0).astype(float).where(abnormal_volume.notna()),
        labels,
        "mean",
    )
    typical_excess = _sector_transform(abnormal_volume, labels, "median")
    active = count.ge(3.0) & breadth.ge(0.60) & typical_excess.ge(0.15)
    active.loc[:, supplied.isna()] = False
    return residual, active


@register_factor
class CashCleanBasketContradictionCatchup(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_clean_basket_contradiction_catchup"
    name = "Cash-Clean Basket Contradiction Catchup"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks cash-confirmed and tax-clean report surprises whose sector-relative "
        "same-day return moved in the opposite direction during broad basket flow."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "marketCap",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "operatingIncome",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].reindex_like(close)
        event = (
            eps_actual.notna()
            & (eps_actual.shift(1).isna() | eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1)))
        ) | (
            revenue_actual.notna()
            & (revenue_actual.shift(1).isna() | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1)))
        )

        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        cash_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(close)

        eps_norm = eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.05)
        revenue_norm = revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        eps_score = 2.0 * rank(eps_norm.where(event)) - 1.0
        revenue_score = 2.0 * rank(revenue_norm.where(event)) - 1.0
        cash_score = 2.0 * rank(cash_growth.where(event)) - 1.0

        positive = (eps_score > 0.0) & (revenue_score > 0.0) & (cash_score > 0.0)
        negative = (eps_score < 0.0) & (revenue_score < 0.0) & (cash_score < 0.0)
        direction = positive.astype(float) - negative.astype(float)
        conviction = pd.concat(
            [eps_score.abs(), revenue_score.abs(), cash_score.abs()], axis=0
        ).groupby(level=0).min().reindex_like(close)
        news = direction * conviction

        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex_like(close).where(
            data["marketCap"].reindex_like(close) > 0.0
        )
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"].reindex_like(close)
        pretax = data["incomeBeforeTax"].reindex_like(close)
        tax_expense = data["incomeTaxExpense"].reindex_like(close)
        prior_pretax = pretax.shift(252)
        prior_tax = tax_expense.shift(252)
        prior_operating = operating_income.shift(252)

        current_etr = (tax_expense / pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)
        prior_etr = (prior_tax / prior_pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)
        operating_change = (operating_income - prior_operating) / market_cap
        tax_effect = (-pretax * (current_etr - prior_etr)) / market_cap
        operating_attribution = direction * operating_change
        tax_attribution = direction * tax_effect
        tax_clean = (
            (pretax > 0.0)
            & (prior_pretax > 0.0)
            & operating_attribution.gt(0.0)
            & operating_attribution.ge(tax_attribution.clip(lower=0.0))
        )

        safe_open = data["open"].reindex_like(close).where(data["open"].reindex_like(close) > 0.0)
        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        intraday_return = np.log(safe_close / safe_open)
        log_volume = np.log1p(data["volume"].reindex_like(close).where(data["volume"].reindex_like(close) >= 0.0))
        volume_history = log_volume.shift(1)
        volume_mean = volume_history.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_std = volume_history.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        abnormal_volume = (log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        abnormal_volume = abnormal_volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        residual, basket_active = _basket_state_and_residual(
            intraday_return, abnormal_volume, data["sector"]
        )
        contradiction = (-np.sign(news) * residual).clip(lower=0.0)
        signal = (news * contradiction).where(
            event
            & tax_clean
            & (direction != 0.0)
            & basket_active
            & contradiction.notna()
        )
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(close).astype(float)

"""Following a newly public earnings report, investors may initially weight the EPS headline more heavily than whether the earnings surprise is supported by a seasonally comparable improvement in operating income rather than a change in the effective tax rate. The signal isolates the portion of the quarterly net-income change mechanically attributable to a tax-rate change, but only for profitable firms with economically meaningful pre-tax income and a well-defined effective tax rate. It is an incremental post-announcement information-assimilation signal: positive operating-supported surprises are bought and tax-supported surprises are sold, conditional on the same report-date event."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _calendar_seasonal_baseline(
    field: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_days: int = 200,
    maximum_days: int = 450,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return each field's latest available observation 200--450 days ago.

    Availability dates are inferred from changes in the point-in-time step
    function.  The lookup is causal: for date t it only selects observations
    dated on or before t - minimum_days.
    """
    index = field.index
    n_rows, n_cols = field.shape
    values = field.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)

    if n_rows == 0:
        empty = field.copy()
        return empty, pd.DataFrame(False, index=index, columns=field.columns)

    previous = field.shift(1)
    available = field.notna() & (previous.isna() | field.ne(previous))

    row_positions = np.arange(n_rows, dtype=float)[:, None]
    observation_positions = np.where(available.to_numpy(), row_positions, np.nan)
    last_positions = pd.DataFrame(
        observation_positions, index=index, columns=field.columns
    ).ffill().to_numpy()

    timestamps = index.asi8
    minimum_ns = int(minimum_days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000_000_000)
    maximum_ns = int(maximum_days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000_000_000)
    anchor_rows = np.searchsorted(timestamps, timestamps - minimum_ns, side="right") - 1
    lower_bound = timestamps - maximum_ns

    source_positions = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    usable_anchor = anchor_rows >= 0
    if usable_anchor.any():
        source_positions[usable_anchor] = last_positions[anchor_rows[usable_anchor]]

    valid_position = np.isfinite(source_positions)
    clipped_positions = np.where(valid_position, source_positions, 0).astype(int)
    baseline_values = np.take_along_axis(values, clipped_positions, axis=0)
    baseline_values = np.where(valid_position, baseline_values, np.nan)

    source_times = np.where(valid_position, timestamps[clipped_positions], np.iinfo(np.int64).min)
    in_calendar_range = valid_position & (source_times >= lower_bound[:, None])
    baseline_values = np.where(in_calendar_range, baseline_values, np.nan)

    baseline = pd.DataFrame(baseline_values, index=index, columns=field.columns)
    valid = pd.DataFrame(in_calendar_range, index=index, columns=field.columns)
    return baseline, valid


@register_factor
class TaxCharacterEarningsAssimilationGap(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks report-day EPS surprises by operating versus tax support."""

    factor_id = "tax_character_earnings_assimilation_gap"
    name = "Seasonally Matched Tax-Character Surprise"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "On newly available EPS report dates, ranks standardized EPS surprise and "
        "seasonally matched operating-income improvement, while penalizing the "
        "portion of income change mechanically explained by an effective-tax-rate change."
    )
    window_length = 450
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "revenue",
        "operatingIncome",
        "marketCap",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        pretax = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax_expense = data["incomeTaxExpense"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        prior_eps = eps_actual.shift(1)
        report_event = eps_actual.notna() & (prior_eps.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_eps))

        pretax_base, pretax_base_valid = _calendar_seasonal_baseline(pretax)
        tax_base, tax_base_valid = _calendar_seasonal_baseline(tax_expense)
        revenue_base, revenue_base_valid = _calendar_seasonal_baseline(revenue)
        operating_base, operating_base_valid = _calendar_seasonal_baseline(operating_income)

        current_etr = (tax_expense / pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)
        baseline_etr = (tax_base / pretax_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)

        tax_driven_change = (
            -pretax * (current_etr - baseline_etr)
        ) / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        operating_improvement = (
            operating_income - operating_base
        ) / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        standardized_eps_surprise = (
            (eps_actual - eps_estimate) / (eps_estimate.abs() + 0.01)
        )

        economically_meaningful = (
            (pretax > 0.0)
            & (pretax_base > 0.0)
            & (revenue > 0.0)
            & (revenue_base > 0.0)
            & (pretax.abs() >= 0.01 * revenue)
            & (pretax_base.abs() >= 0.01 * revenue_base)
            & (market_cap > 0.0)
        )
        baseline_available = (
            pretax_base_valid
            & tax_base_valid
            & revenue_base_valid
            & operating_base_valid
        )
        quantity_available = (
            eps_estimate.notna()
            & tax_expense.notna()
            & tax_base.notna()
            & operating_income.notna()
            & operating_base.notna()
            & current_etr.notna()
            & baseline_etr.notna()
            & tax_driven_change.notna()
            & operating_improvement.notna()
            & standardized_eps_surprise.notna()
        )
        eligible = report_event & economically_meaningful & baseline_available & quantity_available

        eps_rank = rank(standardized_eps_surprise.where(eligible))
        operating_rank = rank(operating_improvement.where(eligible))
        tax_rank = rank(tax_driven_change.where(eligible))
        raw_score = eps_rank + operating_rank - tax_rank

        exposure = rank(raw_score.where(eligible)) - 0.5
        exposure = exposure.where(eligible & report_event, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        return exposure.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: Following a newly public earnings report, investors may initially weight the EPS headline more heavily than whether the earnings surprise is supported by a seasonally comparable improvement in operating income rather than a change in the effective tax rate. The signal isolates the portion of the quarterly net-income change mechanically attributable to a tax-rate change, but only for profitable firms with economically meaningful pre-tax income and a well-defined effective tax rate. It is an incremental post-announcement information-assimilation signal: positive operating-supported surprises are bought and tax-supported surprises are sold, conditional on the same report-date event.
programs.description: At each daily bar, define a report event only when epsActual differs from its value on the immediately preceding daily bar; trade the first such eligible bar and assign zero on all non-event bars. For each ticker at an event, use the current point-in-time quarterly observations and the prior publicly available observation approximately four quarters earlier, defined as the last available value of each field at least 200 and at most 450 calendar days before the event date. Require current and baseline incomeBeforeTax > 0, current and baseline revenue > 0, and absolute current and baseline incomeBeforeTax each at least 1% of their respective revenue; otherwise set the tax component and final score to zero. Define ETR_t = clip(incomeTaxExpense_t / incomeBeforeTax_t, 0, 0.50) and ETR_base = clip(incomeTaxExpense_base / incomeBeforeTax_base, 0, 0.50). Define tax_driven_income_change = -incomeBeforeTax_t * (ETR_t - ETR_base), scaled by current marketCap, and define seasonally matched operating improvement = (operatingIncome_t - operatingIncome_base) / marketCap_t. Define raw EPS surprise as epsActual_t - epsEstimate_t, requiring non-missing epsEstimate_t; scale it by abs(epsEstimate_t) + 0.01. On each event date, cross-sectionally percentile-rank the three eligible quantities: standardized EPS surprise, seasonally matched operating improvement, and tax_driven_income_change. The deterministic score is rank(EPS surprise) + rank(operating improvement) - rank(tax-driven income change). Convert the score to a cross-sectional percentile rank among eligible event names, demean it by 0.5, and use it directly as the factor exposure: long positive exposures and short negative exposures. No price-move adjustment, discretionary clipping beyond the stated ETR bounds, or repeated trading of forward-filled values is used.

"""Cash-confirmed disclosure reactions that fail to propagate are contrarian.

Mechanism: a unanimous EPS, revenue, and operating-cash-flow confirmation
identifies economically meaningful news.  If the immediate reaction is an
abnormal high-volume impulse but next-day price discovery and participation
both contract while price remains at the impulse endpoint, the reaction is
treated as over-assimilated rather than as continuing information diffusion.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _event_confirmation(
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_actual: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    cash_flow_growth: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fresh-report, cross-sectionally normalized three-channel confirmation."""
    eps_event = eps_actual.notna() & eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
    revenue_event = revenue_actual.notna() & revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1))
    event = eps_event | revenue_event

    normalized_eps = eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.05)
    normalized_revenue = revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().clip(lower=1_000_000.0)

    eps_rank = normalized_eps.where(event).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    revenue_rank = normalized_revenue.where(event).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    cash_rank = cash_flow_growth.where(event).rank(axis=1, pct=True)

    eps_score = 2.0 * eps_rank - 1.0
    revenue_score = 2.0 * revenue_rank - 1.0
    cash_score = 2.0 * cash_rank - 1.0

    positive = (eps_score > 0.0) & (revenue_score > 0.0) & (cash_score > 0.0)
    negative = (eps_score < 0.0) & (revenue_score < 0.0) & (cash_score < 0.0)
    common_sign = positive.astype(float) - negative.astype(float)
    conviction = np.minimum(
        np.minimum(eps_score.abs(), revenue_score.abs()), cash_score.abs()
    )

    sufficient_event_universe = event.sum(axis=1).ge(10)
    sufficient_panel = pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(sufficient_event_universe.to_numpy()[:, None], len(event.columns), axis=1),
        index=event.index,
        columns=event.columns,
    )
    return (common_sign * conviction).where(
        event & sufficient_panel & (common_sign != 0.0)
    )


@register_factor
class CashConfirmedEndpointExhaustionReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_confirmed_endpoint_exhaustion_reversal"
    name = "Cash-Confirmed Endpoint Exhaustion Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Contrarian signal for cash-confirmed earnings disclosures whose immediate "
        "abnormal-volume reaction remains endpoint-directed but loses range and "
        "volume on the following bar."
    )
    window_length = 23
    inputs = [
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"].reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close)

        confirmation = _event_confirmation(
            data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close),
            data["revenueActual"].reindex_like(close),
            data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
            data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close),
            data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
            data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close),
            data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(close),
        )

        # The report is known on t-1; t observes whether its initial reaction
        # propagated into additional range and participation.
        prior_confirmation = confirmation.shift(1)
        daily_return = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
        absolute_return = daily_return.abs()
        baseline_move = absolute_return.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        baseline_volume = volume.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()

        impulse_return = close.shift(1) / close.shift(2) - 1.0
        impulse_range = (high.shift(1) - low.shift(1)) / close.shift(2)
        current_range = (high - low) / close.shift(1)
        range_ratio = current_range / impulse_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume_ratio = volume / volume.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        impulse_multiple = impulse_return.abs() / baseline_move.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        abnormal_volume = volume.shift(1) / baseline_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        intraday_range = high - low
        close_location = (2.0 * close - high - low) / intraday_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        aligned = np.sign(impulse_return) * np.sign(prior_confirmation) > 0.0
        eligible = (
            prior_confirmation.notna()
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & close.shift(1).gt(0.0)
            & close.shift(2).gt(0.0)
            & high.gt(low)
            & high.shift(1).gt(low.shift(1))
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & volume.shift(1).gt(0.0)
            & baseline_move.gt(0.0)
            & baseline_volume.gt(0.0)
            & impulse_multiple.ge(2.0)
            & abnormal_volume.ge(1.5)
            & range_ratio.le(0.80)
            & volume_ratio.le(0.80)
            & close_location.abs().ge(0.60)
            & (np.sign(impulse_return) * close_location).ge(0.60)
            & aligned
        )

        exhaustion = (
            impulse_multiple.clip(upper=5.0)
            * abnormal_volume.clip(upper=5.0)
            * (1.0 - range_ratio).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
            * (1.0 - volume_ratio).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
            * close_location.abs()
        )

        signal = -prior_confirmation * exhaustion
        return signal.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Cash-confirmed EPS and revenue surprises identify disclosures with genuine valuation relevance, while the next-day failed-excitation state identifies cases where the initial directional repricing attracted abnormal participation but could not sustain expanding range or volume. The child trades against the report-direction only when these mechanisms coincide: credible news makes the initial move salient, but contracting post-event discovery indicates that the marginal informational response has already been exhausted and inventory/liquidity pressure is more likely to unwind. Neither parent alone distinguishes a low-quality price impulse from an over-assimilated reaction to unusually credible fundamental news.
programs.description: The factor forms a directionally unanimous, cross-sectionally normalized EPS-surprise, revenue-surprise, and operating-cash-flow-growth signal on fresh reports. On the following bar it activates only if the report-direction impulse was abnormally large and high-volume but ends with simultaneous range and volume contraction, then takes the contrarian side of that exhausted reaction.

programs.code:
"""Large industry moves can propagate unevenly across constituents when participation is sparse: stocks trading at unusually low relative volume may initially adjust less than their historically estimated industry exposure. This is a delayed common-shock transmission hypothesis, not a claim that high conditional beta is necessarily mispricing. It predicts that, conditional on a large industry shock and no contemporaneous earnings-surprise update, the relative laggards should outperform their industry peers after positive shocks and underperform after negative shocks over the subsequent six bars."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    """Build static industry-to-column membership without using future labels."""
    if industry.empty:
        return {}

    labels = industry.iloc[0]
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    for column in industry.columns:
        label = labels[column]
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column)
    return groups


def _stock_excluded_industry_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    lagged_market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute cap-weighted same-industry returns excluding each stock itself."""
    peer_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for columns in groups.values():
        group_ret = ret[columns]
        group_cap = lagged_market_cap[columns]
        valid = group_ret.notna() & group_cap.notna() & (group_cap > 0.0)

        valid_cap = group_cap.where(valid, 0.0)
        weighted_ret = (group_ret * group_cap).where(valid, 0.0)
        total_cap = valid_cap.sum(axis=1)
        total_weighted_ret = weighted_ret.sum(axis=1)
        total_count = valid.astype(float).sum(axis=1)

        excluded_cap = total_cap.to_frame().values - valid_cap.values
        excluded_weighted_ret = (
            total_weighted_ret.to_frame().values - weighted_ret.values
        )
        excluded_count = total_count.to_frame().values - valid.astype(float).values

        group_peer_return = pd.DataFrame(
            excluded_weighted_ret / np.where(excluded_cap > 0.0, excluded_cap, np.nan),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )
        group_peer_count = pd.DataFrame(
            excluded_count,
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )

        peer_return.loc[:, columns] = group_peer_return.where(
            (group_peer_count >= 10.0) & (excluded_cap > 0.0)
        )
        peer_count.loc[:, columns] = group_peer_count

    return peer_return, peer_count


def _trailing_beta(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    industry_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int = 60,
    min_pairs: int = 40,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS beta using observations through t-1 only."""
    x = industry_ret.shift(1)
    y = stock_ret.shift(1)
    paired = x.notna() & y.notna()

    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    x0 = x.where(paired, 0.0)
    y0 = y.where(paired, 0.0)

    sum_x = x0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_y = y0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xx = (x0 * x0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xy = (x0 * y0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    safe_count = count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    denominator = sum_xx - (sum_x * sum_x / safe_count)
    numerator = sum_xy - (sum_x * sum_y / safe_count)

    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count >= min_pairs)


def _surprise_update(surprise: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag newly public or revised earnings/revenue surprise values at t."""
    previous = surprise.shift(1)
    newly_non_null = surprise.notna() & previous.isna()
    revised = surprise.notna() & previous.notna() & surprise.ne(previous)
    return newly_non_null | revised


def _industry_equal_gross_rank(
    underreaction: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize, rank, demean, and equal-gross scale each industry daily."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=underreaction.index, columns=underreaction.columns)

    for columns in groups.values():
        values = underreaction[columns].where(eligible[columns])
        count = values.notna().sum(axis=1)
        sufficient = count >= 5

        lower = values.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = values.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        ranks = clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        demeaned = ranks.sub(ranks.mean(axis=1), axis=0).where(sufficient, 0.0)

        gross = demeaned.abs().sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        scaled = demeaned.div(gross, axis=0).where(eligible[columns], 0.0)
        output.loc[:, columns] = scaled.fillna(0.0)

    return output


@register_factor
class ShockPropagationLiquidityDelay(BaseFactor):
    """Low-participation constituents catch up after large common industry shocks."""

    factor_id = "shock_propagation_liquidity_delay"
    name = "Low-Participation Industry-Shock Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral, equal-gross rank of stocks whose current return "
        "lags their trailing-beta-implied response to a large stock-excluded "
        "industry shock while current participation is unusually low."
    )
    window_length = 62
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        stock_ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).where(
            close.notna() & previous_close.notna() & (close > 0.0) & (previous_close > 0.0)
        )

        groups = _industry_groups(industry)
        lagged_market_cap = market_cap.shift(1).where(market_cap.shift(1) > 0.0)
        industry_ret, _ = _stock_excluded_industry_return(
            stock_ret, lagged_market_cap, groups
        )

        prior_abs_industry = industry_ret.abs().shift(1)
        shock_threshold = prior_abs_industry.rolling(60, min_periods=48).quantile(0.80)
        large_shock = industry_ret.abs() > shock_threshold

        beta = _trailing_beta(stock_ret, industry_ret, 60, 40)
        signed_gap = (
            np.sign(industry_ret) * (beta * industry_ret - stock_ret)
        ).where(beta.notna() & industry_ret.notna() & stock_ret.notna())

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        median_prior_volume = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        min_prior_volume = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).min()
        low_participation = (
            (volume > 0.0)
            & (min_prior_volume > 0.0)
            & (median_prior_volume > 0.0)
            & ((volume / median_prior_volume) <= 0.75)
        )

        prior_dollar_volume = (close.shift(1) * volume.shift(1)).where(
            (close.shift(1) > 0.0) & (volume.shift(1) > 0.0)
        )
        liquid_enough = prior_dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median() >= 5_000_000.0

        earnings_update = _surprise_update(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue_update = _surprise_update(data["revenueSurprise"])
        no_company_event = ~(earnings_update | revenue_update)

        eligible = (
            large_shock
            & low_participation
            & liquid_enough
            & no_company_event
            & signed_gap.notna()
        )

        return _industry_equal_gross_rank(signed_gap, eligible, groups).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Large industry moves can propagate unevenly across constituents when participation is sparse: stocks trading at unusually low relative volume may initially adjust less than their historically estimated industry exposure. This is a delayed common-shock transmission hypothesis, not a claim that high conditional beta is necessarily mispricing. It predicts that, conditional on a large industry shock and no contemporaneous earnings-surprise update, the relative laggards should outperform their industry peers after positive shocks and underperform after negative shocks over the subsequent six bars.
programs.description: At the close of day t, define r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. Industry membership is the static point-in-time industry field. For each stock i, construct its stock-excluded industry return I_-i,t as the marketCap-weighted mean of same-industry peer returns r_j,t, using marketCap_j,t-1 as weights; require at least 10 valid peers and positive aggregate peer market capitalization. Define a large industry shock when |I_-i,t| exceeds the 80th percentile of that industry's valid absolute stock-excluded daily returns over t-60 through t-1; require at least 48 prior industry-return observations. Estimate normal industry beta using only information through t-1: beta_i,t = sum[(r_i,s-rbar_i)(I_-i,s-Ibar)] / sum[(I_-i,s-Ibar)^2] over s=t-60,...,t-1, requiring at least 40 paired observations and nonzero denominator. Define the signed underreaction gap u_i,t = sign(I_-i,t) * (beta_i,t * I_-i,t - r_i,t), so a larger positive value identifies a stock that lagged its expected response in the direction of the common shock. Restrict candidates to names with volume_i,t / median(volume_i,t-20,...,t-1) <= 0.75, positive current and trailing volume, and median(close_i,s * volume_i,s, s=t-20,...,t-1) >= USD 5,000,000. Exclude a name if epsSurprise or revenueSurprise is newly non-null or changes between t-1 and t, preventing direct earnings-release repricing from being treated as liquidity delay. Within each shocked industry, winsorize u at that day's 1st and 99th eligible-percentile values, percentile-rank it, and subtract the industry mean rank; require at least 5 eligible names per industry. The final factor is this industry-demeaned rank, with zero exposure for ineligible names. A positive factor loading means long the largest relative underreaction gaps and short the smallest within the same industry, producing industry-neutral equal-gross books; industries are equally gross-scaled and the aggregate book is dollar-neutral. All inputs through close t, including close_t and volume_t, are observed only after the close. Positions therefore enter no earlier than open t+1 and exit at open t+7, six daily bars after entry.

programs.code:
"""A broad, internally coherent sector shock may be incorporated first into actively traded sector leaders, while moderately less-active but historically sector-sensitive names adjust with delay. The signal does not treat the sector mode as a fair-value target unconditionally: it is activated only following a broad sector-mode shock, uses strictly pre-shock loading estimates, and excludes extremely illiquid names where adverse selection and trading costs are most likely to dominate. The expected effect is a six-bar catch-up of sector-mode laggards relative to contemporaneous overshooters, conditional on the shock representing a sector-wide rather than stock-specific event."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorized_equal_weight(values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Causal row-wise 5/95-percentile winsorized equal-weight return."""
    result = np.full(values.shape[0], np.nan, dtype=float)
    for row_index in range(values.shape[0]):
        row = values[row_index]
        valid = row[np.isfinite(row)]
        if valid.size == 0:
            continue
        if valid.size >= 3:
            lower, upper = np.percentile(valid, [5.0, 95.0])
            valid = np.clip(valid, lower, upper)
        result[row_index] = float(np.mean(valid))
    return result


def _first_pc_mode_and_betas(
    history: np.ndarray,
    equal_weight_history: np.ndarray,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Estimate a correlation-PC sector mode and trailing OLS member betas.

    The PCA is computed only from the supplied pre-shock history.  Missing
    standardized observations contribute no contemporaneous cross-product;
    this preserves the available-return requirement without forward filling
    prices or returns.
    """
    n_obs, n_names = history.shape
    means = np.nanmean(history, axis=0)
    scales = np.nanstd(history, axis=0, ddof=1)
    valid_scale = np.isfinite(scales) & (scales > 0.0)
    if n_names == 0 or not valid_scale.all():
        return np.full(n_obs, np.nan), np.full(n_names, np.nan)

    standardized = (history - means) / scales
    observed = np.isfinite(standardized)
    standardized = np.where(observed, standardized, 0.0)

    pair_count = observed.T @ observed
    cross_product = standardized.T @ standardized
    denominator = np.maximum(pair_count - 1.0, 1.0)
    corr = cross_product / denominator
    corr = np.where(np.isfinite(corr), corr, 0.0)
    corr = (corr + corr.T) * 0.5
    np.fill_diagonal(corr, 1.0)

    try:
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eigh(corr)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return np.full(n_obs, np.nan), np.full(n_names, np.nan)

    component = eigenvectors[:, int(np.argmax(eigenvalues))]
    weight_scale = np.sum(np.abs(component))
    if not np.isfinite(weight_scale) or weight_scale <= 0.0:
        return np.full(n_obs, np.nan), np.full(n_names, np.nan)
    component = component / weight_scale

    raw_history = np.where(np.isfinite(history), history, 0.0)
    mode_history = raw_history @ component
    common = np.isfinite(mode_history) & np.isfinite(equal_weight_history)
    if common.sum() >= 3:
        mode_std = np.std(mode_history[common], ddof=1)
        ew_std = np.std(equal_weight_history[common], ddof=1)
        if mode_std > 0.0 and ew_std > 0.0:
            orientation = np.corrcoef(mode_history[common], equal_weight_history[common])[0, 1]
            if np.isfinite(orientation) and orientation < 0.0:
                component = -component
                mode_history = -mode_history

    betas = np.full(n_names, np.nan, dtype=float)
    for member in range(n_names):
        paired = np.isfinite(history[:, member]) & np.isfinite(mode_history)
        if paired.sum() < 100:
            continue
        x = mode_history[paired]
        y = history[paired, member]
        x_centered = x - np.mean(x)
        x_variance = float(np.dot(x_centered, x_centered))
        if x_variance <= 0.0 or not np.isfinite(x_variance):
            continue
        y_centered = y - np.mean(y)
        beta = float(np.dot(x_centered, y_centered) / x_variance)
        if np.isfinite(beta):
            betas[member] = beta

    return mode_history, betas


def _sector_mode_lag_portfolio(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build the daily sector-balanced delayed-adjustment long-short weights."""
    index = close.index
    columns = close.columns
    n_rows, n_cols = close.shape
    output = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
    dollar_volume = safe_close * safe_volume

    prior_return_count = ret.shift(1).rolling(126, min_periods=126).count()
    prior_dollar_median = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    prior_volume_median = safe_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    prior_volatility = ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()

    ret_values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    close_values = safe_close.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_values = safe_volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    count_values = prior_return_count.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    dollar_median_values = prior_dollar_median.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_median_values = prior_volume_median.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volatility_values = prior_volatility.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    sector_values = sector.reindex(index=index, columns=columns).to_numpy()

    for t in range(126, n_rows):
        current_return = ret_values[t]
        base_eligible = (
            (count_values[t] >= 100.0)
            & np.isfinite(close_values[t])
            & np.isfinite(volume_values[t])
            & np.isfinite(current_return)
            & np.isfinite(dollar_median_values[t])
            & (dollar_median_values[t] > 0.0)
        )
        if base_eligible.sum() < 15:
            continue

        universe_dollar = dollar_median_values[t, base_eligible]
        try:
            liquidity_cutoff = float(np.nanpercentile(universe_dollar, 30.0))
        except (ValueError, IndexError):
            continue
        if not np.isfinite(liquidity_cutoff):
            continue

        eligible = base_eligible & (dollar_median_values[t] > liquidity_cutoff)
        labels = sector_values[t]
        active_sector_weights: list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]] = []

        valid_labels = pd.unique(labels[eligible])
        for label in valid_labels:
            if pd.isna(label):
                continue
            member_mask = eligible & (labels == label)
            member_positions = np.flatnonzero(member_mask)
            if member_positions.size < 15:
                continue

            history = ret_values[t - 126:t, :][:, member_positions]
            if np.any(np.sum(np.isfinite(history), axis=0) < 100):
                continue

            ew_history = _winsorized_equal_weight(history)
            if np.isfinite(ew_history).sum() < 100:
                continue
            shock_std = float(np.nanstd(ew_history, ddof=1))
            if not np.isfinite(shock_std) or shock_std <= 0.0:
                continue

            current_members = current_return[member_positions]
            finite_current = np.isfinite(current_members)
            if finite_current.sum() < 15:
                continue
            current_valid = current_members[finite_current]
            lower, upper = np.percentile(current_valid, [5.0, 95.0])
            sector_return = float(np.mean(np.clip(current_valid, lower, upper)))
            if not np.isfinite(sector_return) or abs(sector_return) <= 1.5 * shock_std:
                continue

            same_sign = np.sum(np.sign(current_valid) == np.sign(sector_return))
            if same_sign / float(current_valid.size) < 0.65:
                continue

            _, betas = _first_pc_mode_and_betas(history, ew_history)
            residual = current_members - betas * sector_return

            current_volume = volume_values[t, member_positions]
            median_volume = volume_median_values[t, member_positions]
            relative_volume = current_volume / median_volume
            delayed = (
                np.isfinite(residual)
                & np.isfinite(relative_volume)
                & (relative_volume >= 0.50)
                & (relative_volume <= 0.90)
            )
            if delayed.sum() < 5:
                continue

            delayed_residual = residual[delayed]
            residual_low, residual_high = np.percentile(delayed_residual, [5.0, 95.0])
            clipped_residual = np.clip(delayed_residual, residual_low, residual_high)
            residual_rank = pd.Series(clipped_residual).rank(pct=True, method="average").to_numpy()

            delayed_positions = member_positions[delayed]
            long_local = residual_rank <= 0.20
            short_local = residual_rank >= 0.80
            if long_local.sum() == 0 or short_local.sum() == 0:
                continue

            selected_volatility = volatility_values[t, delayed_positions]
            valid_volatility = selected_volatility[np.isfinite(selected_volatility) & (selected_volatility > 0.0)]
            if valid_volatility.size == 0:
                continue
            vol_cap = float(np.percentile(valid_volatility, 90.0))
            if not np.isfinite(vol_cap) or vol_cap <= 0.0:
                continue
            safe_volatility = np.where(
                np.isfinite(selected_volatility) & (selected_volatility > 0.0),
                np.minimum(selected_volatility, vol_cap),
                np.nan,
            )
            inverse_volatility = 1.0 / safe_volatility

            long_weights = np.where(long_local, inverse_volatility, 0.0)
            short_weights = np.where(short_local, inverse_volatility, 0.0)
            long_total = float(np.nansum(long_weights))
            short_total = float(np.nansum(short_weights))
            if long_total <= 0.0 or short_total <= 0.0:
                continue

            active_sector_weights.append(
                (
                    delayed_positions,
                    long_weights / long_total,
                    short_weights / short_total,
                )
            )

        if not active_sector_weights:
            continue

        sector_scale = 1.0 / float(len(active_sector_weights))
        for positions, long_weights, short_weights in active_sector_weights:
            output[t, positions] += sector_scale * (long_weights - short_weights)

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=index, columns=columns)


@register_factor
class SparseModeLoadingDelayedCatchup(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-PC residual catch-up portfolio conditioned on broad common shocks."""

    factor_id = "sparse_mode_loading_delayed_catchup"
    name = "Tradable Sector-Mode Lag Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "A sector-balanced long-short portfolio that buys moderately low-volume "
        "laggards and sells overshooters after a broad sector common-mode shock, "
        "using strictly pre-shock first-PC loading estimates."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return _sector_mode_lag_portfolio(
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
            data["sector"],
        )
programs.name: Tradable Sector-Mode Lag Catch-Up
programs.trading_idea: A broad, internally coherent sector shock may be incorporated first into actively traded sector leaders, while moderately less-active but historically sector-sensitive names adjust with delay. The signal does not treat the sector mode as a fair-value target unconditionally: it is activated only following a broad sector-mode shock, uses strictly pre-shock loading estimates, and excludes extremely illiquid names where adverse selection and trading costs are most likely to dominate. The expected effect is a six-bar catch-up of sector-mode laggards relative to contemporaneous overshooters, conditional on the shock representing a sector-wide rather than stock-specific event.
programs.description: Use daily close-to-close returns, with r[t] = close[t]/close[t-1]-1. At each daily close t, form the signal only after all close and volume observations for t are known; trade execution is no earlier than the next bar's open (t+1 open), with positions held for six daily bars and rebalanced daily. Within each static sector, define the eligible estimation universe as stocks having at least 100 valid daily returns during the trailing 126-bar window [t-126,t-1], positive close and volume on t, and trailing median daily dollar volume (close*volume) above the cross-sectional 30th percentile of the full eligible universe; sectors require at least 15 such stocks, otherwise their signal is zero. Estimate the sector's first common mode from the first principal component of the correlation matrix of standardized member returns over [t-126,t-1], retaining exactly one mode and orienting its sign so that its correlation with the sector equal-weight return is positive. Estimate each stock's loading beta_i by an OLS regression of its trailing returns on that lagged first-PC mode over the same window, requiring at least 100 paired observations; stocks without a valid beta receive zero signal. On date t, compute the realized sector-mode return as the equal-weight return of eligible sector members after winsorizing member returns at the sector's contemporaneous 5th and 95th percentiles. Activate a sector only when this sector return has absolute value greater than 1.5 times its trailing 126-bar standard deviation and at least 65% of valid sector members have returns with the same sign as the sector return; this broad-participation condition is intended to reject shocks dominated by one or a few firm-specific events. For each stock, compute residual_i[t] = r_i[t] - beta_i*mode_return[t]. Define relative volume as volume_i[t] divided by its trailing 20-bar median volume using [t-20,t-1]. Retain only stocks with relative volume between 0.50 and 0.90: below-normal participation is required for delayed adjustment, but the lowest-activity names are excluded to limit stale-price, spread, and impact exposure. Within each activated sector, winsorize residuals at the 5th and 95th percentiles and rank them cross-sectionally. The predictive score is the negative sector-demeaned residual rank: the most negative residuals after a positive common shock, or most positive residuals after a negative common shock, are expected to move toward the sector mode over the next six bars. Construct a sector-balanced long-short portfolio by longing the bottom residual quintile and shorting the top residual quintile within each activated sector, equal-weighting names within each side and equal-weighting active sectors; gross long and short exposure are matched, and weights are scaled inversely by trailing 20-bar return volatility capped at the 90th percentile to prevent a few volatile names dominating. Short positions are opened only where the execution system confirms shortability and borrow availability; unavailable shorts receive zero weight and the corresponding sector long exposure is reduced to preserve approximate dollar neutrality. New listings, halted names, missing close/volume observations, stale fundamental classifications, insufficient trailing history, and stocks without a next-bar executable open are excluded rather than imputed. Empirical evaluation must compare net-of-cost results against ordinary sector-beta residual reversal, one-day reversal, volume-conditioned reversal, and liquidity controls, with costs and borrow charges stressed most heavily for the lower-volume selected names.

programs.code:
"""A broad industry return shock may initially be incorporated unevenly across constituents. This signal trades only stocks that have both an economically signed residual underreaction to a three-day-old leave-one-out industry shock and a strictly defined transition from below-proportional industry dollar-volume participation to recovering participation. The mechanism is not that volume alone predicts returns: the proposed continuation is conditional on an unresolved beta-adjusted price gap, while the participation recovery is used to identify a possible delayed-transmission window rather than a generic high-volume event."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_reengagement_scores(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute the fixed-event-universe, leave-one-out delayed-transmission score."""
    n_dates, n_names = close.shape
    output = np.full((n_dates, n_names), np.nan, dtype=float)

    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_values = volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    cap_values = market_cap.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    dollar_values = close_values * volume_values
    returns_values = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).to_numpy(dtype=float)

    # Industry is documented as static.  Taking its first supplied row avoids
    # using later price or fundamental observations in grouping decisions.
    labels = industry.iloc[0].to_numpy()
    groups: dict[object, list[int]] = {}
    for column, label in enumerate(labels):
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column)

    for t in range(63, n_dates):
        s = t - 3
        pre_start = s - 60

        for members_list in groups.values():
            members = np.asarray(members_list, dtype=int)
            if members.size < 9:
                continue

            pre_ret = returns_values[pre_start:s, members]
            event_ret = returns_values[s, members]
            event_dollar = dollar_values[s, members]

            # A name can enter the fixed event universe only when it itself
            # meets the peer eligibility conditions specified at event time.
            eligible = (
                (np.isfinite(pre_ret).sum(axis=0) >= 50)
                & np.isfinite(event_ret)
                & np.isfinite(event_dollar)
                & (event_dollar > 0.0)
            )
            local = np.flatnonzero(eligible)
            if local.size < 9:
                continue

            positions = members[local]
            x_pre = returns_values[pre_start:s, positions]
            x_valid = np.isfinite(x_pre)
            x_zeroed = np.where(x_valid, x_pre, 0.0)

            # For every candidate, its peer set is the same eligible universe
            # excluding itself.  Totals therefore provide exact leave-one-out
            # peer returns without allowing the event universe to drift.
            total_count = x_valid.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
            total_sum = x_zeroed.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
            peer_count = total_count - x_valid.astype(float)
            peer_sum = total_sum - x_zeroed
            peer_valid = peer_count >= 8.0
            peer_ret = np.divide(
                peer_sum,
                peer_count,
                out=np.full_like(peer_sum, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=peer_valid,
            )

            paired = x_valid & peer_valid & np.isfinite(peer_ret)
            paired_n = paired.sum(axis=0).astype(float)
            if not np.any(paired_n >= 50.0):
                continue

            pair_x = np.where(paired, x_pre, 0.0)
            pair_y = np.where(paired, peer_ret, 0.0)
            sum_x = pair_x.sum(axis=0)
            sum_y = pair_y.sum(axis=0)
            sum_xy = (pair_x * pair_y).sum(axis=0)
            sum_yy = (pair_y * pair_y).sum(axis=0)
            covariance = sum_xy - np.divide(
                sum_x * sum_y,
                paired_n,
                out=np.zeros_like(sum_x),
                where=paired_n > 0.0,
            )
            variance_peer = sum_yy - np.divide(
                sum_y * sum_y,
                paired_n,
                out=np.zeros_like(sum_y),
                where=paired_n > 0.0,
            )
            beta = np.divide(
                covariance,
                variance_peer,
                out=np.full_like(covariance, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=variance_peer > 0.0,
            )

            # Stock volatility is estimated strictly before the shock.
            own_n = x_valid.sum(axis=0).astype(float)
            own_sum = x_zeroed.sum(axis=0)
            own_ss = (x_zeroed * x_zeroed).sum(axis=0)
            own_var_num = own_ss - np.divide(
                own_sum * own_sum,
                own_n,
                out=np.zeros_like(own_sum),
                where=own_n > 0.0,
            )
            sigma = np.sqrt(
                np.divide(
                    own_var_num,
                    own_n - 1.0,
                    out=np.full_like(own_var_num, np.nan, dtype=float),
                    where=own_n > 1.0,
                )
            )

            # Shock eligibility uses leave-one-out peer history and event-day
            # coherence, preserving the economically signed industry move.
            hist_count = peer_valid.sum(axis=0).astype(float)
            hist_sum = np.where(peer_valid, peer_ret, 0.0).sum(axis=0)
            hist_mean = np.divide(
                hist_sum,
                hist_count,
                out=np.full_like(hist_sum, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=hist_count >= 50.0,
            )
            centered_peer = np.where(peer_valid, peer_ret - hist_mean, 0.0)
            hist_std = np.sqrt(
                np.divide(
                    (centered_peer * centered_peer).sum(axis=0),
                    hist_count - 1.0,
                    out=np.full_like(hist_sum, np.nan, dtype=float),
                    where=hist_count > 1.0,
                )
            )

            event_x = returns_values[s, positions]
            event_valid = np.isfinite(event_x)
            event_total = np.where(event_valid, event_x, 0.0).sum()
            event_count = float(event_valid.sum())
            loo_event_count = event_count - event_valid.astype(float)
            loo_event_sum = event_total - np.where(event_valid, event_x, 0.0)
            event_peer = np.divide(
                loo_event_sum,
                loo_event_count,
                out=np.full_like(event_x, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=loo_event_count >= 8.0,
            )
            shock_deviation = event_peer - hist_mean
            shock_sign = np.sign(shock_deviation)
            shock_ok = (
                np.isfinite(shock_deviation)
                & np.isfinite(hist_std)
                & (hist_std > 0.0)
                & (np.abs(shock_deviation) > 1.5 * hist_std)
            )

            all_signs = np.sign(event_x)
            matches = (all_signs[:, None] == shock_sign[None, :]) & event_valid[:, None]
            matches[np.arange(local.size), np.arange(local.size)] = False
            matching_count = matches.sum(axis=0).astype(float)
            coherent = matching_count >= 0.65 * loo_event_count
            shock_ok &= coherent

            # Construct the beta-adjusted response from event date through t.
            event_path = returns_values[s : t + 1, positions]
            path_valid = np.isfinite(event_path)
            path_zeroed = np.where(path_valid, event_path, 0.0)
            path_total_sum = path_zeroed.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
            path_total_count = path_valid.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
            path_peer_count = path_total_count - path_valid.astype(float)
            path_peer_sum = path_total_sum - path_zeroed
            path_peer = np.divide(
                path_peer_sum,
                path_peer_count,
                out=np.full_like(path_peer_sum, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=path_peer_count >= 8.0,
            )
            path_ok = (
                path_valid.all(axis=0)
                & np.isfinite(path_peer).all(axis=0)
                & (path_peer_count >= 8.0).all(axis=0)
            )
            response_gap = path_zeroed.sum(axis=0) - beta * np.nansum(path_peer, axis=0)
            underreacting = np.isfinite(response_gap) & ((shock_sign * response_gap) < 0.0)

            # The participation universe is P union {i}, which equals the
            # eligible event universe for every candidate under leave-one-out.
            path_dollar = dollar_values[s : t + 1, positions]
            path_cap = cap_values[s : t + 1, positions]
            valid_dollar = np.isfinite(path_dollar)
            valid_cap = np.isfinite(path_cap) & (path_cap > 0.0)
            dollar_denominator = np.nansum(path_dollar, axis=1)
            cap_denominator = np.nansum(path_cap, axis=1)
            universe_ok = (
                valid_dollar.all(axis=0)
                & valid_cap.all(axis=0)
                & np.isfinite(dollar_denominator).all()
                & (dollar_denominator > 0.0).all()
                & np.isfinite(cap_denominator).all()
                & (cap_denominator > 0.0).all()
            )
            attention_share = path_dollar / dollar_denominator[:, None]
            cap_share = path_cap / cap_denominator[:, None]
            relative_share = np.divide(
                attention_share,
                cap_share,
                out=np.full_like(attention_share, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=cap_share > 0.0,
            )

            baseline_attention = (attention_share[0] + attention_share[1]) / 2.0
            initial_deficit = (relative_share[0] <= 0.75) & (relative_share[1] <= 0.75)
            recovery_ratio = np.divide(
                attention_share[3],
                baseline_attention,
                out=np.full_like(baseline_attention, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=baseline_attention > 0.0,
            )
            share_recovery = (
                (recovery_ratio >= 1.25)
                & (attention_share[3] > attention_share[2])
            )
            strength = np.clip(recovery_ratio - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0)

            prior_dollar = pd.DataFrame(dollar_values[t - 20 : t, positions]).median(
                axis=0, skipna=True
            ).to_numpy(dtype=float)
            prior_positive_volume = (volume_values[t - 20 : t, positions] > 0.0).sum(axis=0)
            current_dollar = dollar_values[t, positions]
            dollar_ratio = np.divide(
                current_dollar,
                prior_dollar,
                out=np.full_like(prior_dollar, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=np.isfinite(prior_dollar) & (prior_dollar > 0.0),
            )
            liquidity_ok = (
                np.isfinite(prior_dollar)
                & (prior_dollar >= 1_000_000.0)
                & np.isfinite(dollar_ratio)
                & (dollar_ratio >= 1.10)
                & (dollar_ratio <= 3.0)
                & (prior_positive_volume >= 16)
                & np.isfinite(close_values[t, positions])
                & (close_values[t, positions] >= 1.0)
            )

            qualifies = (
                shock_ok
                & (paired_n >= 50.0)
                & np.isfinite(beta)
                & (beta >= 0.0)
                & (beta <= 2.0)
                & np.isfinite(sigma)
                & (sigma > 0.0)
                & path_ok
                & underreacting
                & universe_ok
                & initial_deficit
                & share_recovery
                & liquidity_ok
            )
            scores = -np.divide(
                response_gap,
                sigma,
                out=np.full_like(response_gap, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=sigma > 0.0,
            ) * strength
            output[t, positions[qualifies]] = scores[qualifies]

    raw = pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    ranked = raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    return (2.0 * ranked - 1.0).where(raw.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class IndustryAttentionReengagementCompletion(BaseFactor):
    """Delayed industry-shock completion after below-share attention recovers."""

    factor_id = "industry_attention_reengagement_completion"
    name = "Industry Participation Deficit Completion"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Ranks qualifying stocks whose beta-adjusted response to a coherent "
        "three-day-old leave-one-out industry shock remains incomplete while "
        "their initially below-cap-share dollar-volume participation recovers."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return _industry_reengagement_scores(
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
            data["marketCap"],
            data["industry"],
        )
