"""Efficient price-discovery leaders during coherent sector repricings.

Mechanism: a sector residual leader is informative only when its directional move is
confirmed by participation without unusually large range-per-volume.  Efficient
impact distinguishes common-information price discovery from sparse-liquidity
order-imbalance noise, so efficient leaders should retain short-horizon drift.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_impulse(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Leave-one-out sector return and same-direction peer breadth."""
    sector_ret = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].tolist()
        if len(cols) < 12:
            continue
        block = ret.loc[:, cols]
        valid = block.notna()
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total = block.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)

        other_count = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(count.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=cols,
        ) - valid.astype(float)
        other_sum = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(total.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=cols,
        ) - block.fillna(0.0)
        loo = other_sum.div(other_count.where(other_count > 0.0))

        positive = block.gt(0.0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        negative = block.lt(0.0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        pos_other = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(positive.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=cols,
        ) - block.gt(0.0).astype(float)
        neg_other = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(negative.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=cols,
        ) - block.lt(0.0).astype(float)
        same = pos_other.where(loo.gt(0.0), neg_other.where(loo.lt(0.0)))

        sector_ret.loc[:, cols] = loo.where(other_count >= 10.0)
        breadth.loc[:, cols] = same.div(other_count.where(other_count > 0.0))

    return sector_ret, breadth


def _prior_beta(ret: pd.DataFrame, sector_ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing beta whose estimation sample ends at the prior bar."""
    y = ret.shift(1)
    x = sector_ret.shift(1).where(y.notna())
    cov = y.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(x)
    var = x.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
    return cov.div(var.replace(0.0, np.nan))


def _sector_rank(
    value: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Percentile rank only against eligible contemporaneous sector peers."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=value.index, columns=value.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].tolist()
        if len(cols) > 0:
            result.loc[:, cols] = value.loc[:, cols].where(eligible.loc[:, cols]).rank(
                axis=1, pct=True
            )
    return result


@register_factor
class SectorCoherentImpactEfficiencyLeaderDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_coherent_impact_efficiency_leader_drift"
    name = "Coherent Sector Efficient-Leader Drift"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks beta-adjusted directional sector leaders and weights them by low "
        "range-per-abnormal-volume, retaining efficient common-information "
        "price discovery rather than sparse-liquidity overshoots."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = data["sector"].ffill().iloc[-1]

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        ret = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        sector_ret, breadth = _sector_impulse(ret, labels)
        beta = _prior_beta(ret, sector_ret)
        directional_residual = np.sign(sector_ret) * (ret - beta * sector_ret)

        sector_sign = np.sign(sector_ret)
        same_sign_days = (
            sector_sign.eq(sector_sign.shift(1))
            & sector_sign.eq(sector_sign.shift(2))
            & sector_sign.ne(0.0)
        )
        persistent_move = sector_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().abs().gt(0.0)
        coherent = breadth.ge(0.65) & same_sign_days & persistent_move

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        volume_ratio = volume.div(prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        participation = volume_ratio.ge(1.0)
        range_fraction = (high - low).div(close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        impact = range_fraction.div(volume_ratio.clip(lower=0.25))

        eligible = (
            coherent
            & participation
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & directional_residual.notna()
            & impact.notna()
        )
        leader_rank = _sector_rank(directional_residual, eligible, labels)
        impact_rank = _sector_rank(impact, eligible, labels)

        leader_strength = (leader_rank - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0) * 2.0
        efficiency = (1.0 - impact_rank).clip(lower=0.0)
        score = (np.sign(sector_ret) * leader_strength * efficiency).where(eligible, 0.0)
        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Coherent Sector Efficient-Leader Drift
programs.trading_idea: A broad, persistent sector repricing contains information that is incorporated unevenly across constituents: stocks with the largest beta-adjusted move in the sector direction are likely early price-discovery leaders. The sparse-liquidity mechanism is used as a conditioning variable rather than a reversal trade: a leader move that achieves its return with low range per unit of abnormal volume is more likely informed and executable, whereas a high-impact leader move is more plausibly noisy order-imbalance transmission. This interaction identifies sector information leaders whose price discovery is efficient enough to continue over the next six sessions, a distinction absent from either unconditional leader drift or unconditional impact reversal.
programs.description: The factor finds coherent leave-one-out sector impulses, estimates each stock's prior beta-adjusted residual return, and ranks directional residual leaders within sector. It weights those leaders by sector-relative impact efficiency, defined as low intraday range relative to current volume normalized by prior volume.

programs.code:
"""A broad sector move can be incorporated unevenly across constituents even when those constituents are actively traded: differences in order-routing, benchmark-trade scheduling, and stock-specific price discovery can leave a high-participation name temporarily behind its historically expected sector response. The signal treats abnormal volume as evidence that the underresponse is not simply inactivity, and trades the residual in the sector-shock direction while hedging the contemporaneous sector component. This is a reduced-form price-discovery/completion hypothesis based on daily bars, not a claim that dealer inventory or ETF hedging is directly identified."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_baskets(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Build causal dynamic leave-one-out sector baskets and breadth measures."""
    basket = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns, dtype=float)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    agreement = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns, dtype=float)

    for sector_name in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        columns = labels.index[labels.eq(sector_name)].tolist()
        if not columns:
            continue

        group_ret = ret.loc[:, columns]
        group_eligible = eligible.loc[:, columns]
        eligible_ret = group_ret.where(group_eligible)
        count = group_eligible.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total_return = eligible_ret.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)

        peers = count.sub(1.0, axis=0)
        loo = total_return.to_frame().sub(group_ret, axis=0).div(peers.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        loo = loo.where(group_eligible & peers.gt(0.0).to_frame().reindex(columns=columns, fill_value=True))

        # The reindex above preserves the row-wise peer condition across columns.
        peer_ok = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(peers.gt(0.0).to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )
        loo = loo.where(group_eligible & peer_ok)
        basket.loc[:, columns] = loo

        peer_count.loc[:, columns] = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(peers.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )

        basket_sign = np.sign(loo)
        same_direction = (
            np.sign(group_ret).eq(basket_sign)
            & basket_sign.ne(0.0)
            & group_eligible
        )
        same_total = same_direction.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        same_peers = same_total.to_frame().sub(same_direction.astype(float), axis=0)
        agreement.loc[:, columns] = same_peers.div(peers.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)

    return basket, peer_count, agreement


def _daily_neutral_targets(
    underresponse: pd.DataFrame,
    beta: pd.DataFrame,
    shock: pd.DataFrame,
    abnormal_volume: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Create sector-neutral daily sleeves from top-tercile underresponses."""
    target = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=underresponse.index, columns=underresponse.columns)

    for timestamp in underresponse.index:
        sleeves: list[tuple[list[str], np.ndarray]] = []

        for sector_name in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
            columns = labels.index[labels.eq(sector_name)].tolist()
            if not columns:
                continue

            eligible_names = [
                column
                for column in columns
                if bool(shock.at[timestamp, column])
                and bool(abnormal_volume.at[timestamp, column])
                and np.isfinite(underresponse.at[timestamp, column])
                and np.isfinite(beta.at[timestamp, column])
            ]

            if len(eligible_names) < 3:
                continue

            values = underresponse.loc[timestamp, eligible_names]
            ordered = values.rank(method="first", ascending=True)
            selected_names = ordered.index[ordered.gt((2.0 * len(eligible_names)) / 3.0)].tolist()

            # Two neutrality constraints require at least three tradable names.
            if len(selected_names) < 3:
                continue

            percentile_score = ordered.loc[selected_names] / float(len(eligible_names))
            direction = np.sign(
                np.nanmedian(
                    underresponse.loc[timestamp, selected_names].to_numpy(dtype=float)
                )
            )

            # Direction comes from the sector shock rather than from U itself.
            # Underresponse is signed by the basket direction, so recover that
            # direction from the raw sector shock condition through score sign.
            basket_direction = np.sign(
                np.nanmedian(
                    shock.loc[timestamp, selected_names].astype(float).to_numpy()
                )
            )
            if basket_direction == 0.0:
                basket_direction = 1.0

            y = basket_direction * percentile_score.to_numpy(dtype=float)
            x = beta.loc[timestamp, selected_names].to_numpy(dtype=float)
            x_centered = x - np.mean(x)
            y_centered = y - np.mean(y)
            denominator = float(np.dot(x_centered, x_centered))

            if denominator > 1.0e-14:
                slope = float(np.dot(x_centered, y_centered) / denominator)
                residual = y_centered - slope * x_centered
            else:
                # A constant beta makes the beta constraint identical to the
                # dollar-neutral intercept constraint.
                residual = y_centered

            gross = float(np.abs(residual).sum())
            if gross <= 1.0e-14:
                continue

            sleeves.append((selected_names, residual / gross))

        if not sleeves:
            continue

        sector_weight = 1.0 / float(len(sleeves))
        for names, sleeve in sleeves:
            target.loc[timestamp, names] = sleeve * sector_weight

        # Every sleeve is dollar neutral, so a common gross normalization
        # preserves both dollar and beta neutrality while giving equal books.
        gross_total = float(target.loc[timestamp].abs().sum())
        if gross_total > 1.0e-14:
            target.loc[timestamp] = target.loc[timestamp] / gross_total

    return target


@register_factor
class SectorInventoryTransferCompletion(BaseFactor):
    """Abnormal-volume sector underresponse completion with sector-neutral sleeves."""

    factor_id = "sector_inventory_transfer_completion"
    name = "Abnormal-Volume Sector Residual Completion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Identifies actively traded constituents that lag a broad, high-breadth "
        "sector shock relative to their trailing leave-one-out sector beta, then "
        "forms dollar- and beta-neutral equal-gross sector sleeves."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        volume_ratio = volume / prior_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        abnormal_volume = volume_ratio.ge(1.5) & volume_ratio.notna()

        # A name must have returns for the current bar and prior sixty bars.
        complete_return_history = ret.notna().rolling(61, min_periods=61).sum().eq(61)
        eligible = (
            complete_return_history
            & ret.notna()
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & prior_volume_median.notna()
        )

        # Sector is static by contract.  Forward filling only handles sparse
        # vendor representation without creating a price or volume look-ahead.
        labels = sector.ffill().iloc[-1]
        basket, peer_count, sign_agreement = _sector_baskets(ret, eligible, labels)

        basket_std = basket.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=60).std()
        shock = (
            peer_count.ge(8.0)
            & basket.abs().gt(1.5 * basket_std)
            & sign_agreement.ge(0.70)
            & basket.notna()
        )

        lagged_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lagged_basket = basket.shift(1)
        covariance = lagged_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=60).cov(lagged_basket)
        basket_variance = lagged_basket.rolling(60, min_periods=60).var()
        raw_beta = covariance / basket_variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = 0.5 * raw_beta + 0.5

        underresponse = np.sign(basket) * (beta * basket - ret)
        daily_target = _daily_neutral_targets(
            underresponse=underresponse,
            beta=beta,
            shock=shock,
            abnormal_volume=abnormal_volume,
            labels=labels,
        )

        # Six equal-capital, trailing daily vintages implement the prescribed
        # overlapping holding period without using information after each bar.
        held_signal = daily_target.rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum() / 6.0
        return held_signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

The signal treats abnormal volume as evidence that the underresponse is not simply inactivity, and trades the residual in the sector-shock direction while hedging the contemporaneous sector component. This is a reduced-form price-discovery/completion hypothesis based on daily bars, not a claim that dealer inventory or ETF hedging is directly identified.
programs.description: Use daily close-to-close return r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. At completed bar t, form an equal-weighted leave-one-out sector basket return B_i,t from all other eligible names in i's sector; a sector constituent is eligible only with non-missing returns for t and the prior 60 completed bars, positive current volume, and a non-missing 20-bar trailing volume median. A sector shock is present only when i has at least 8 eligible sector peers, |B_i,t| exceeds 1.5 times the trailing 60-bar standard deviation of that leave-one-out basket computed through t-1, and at least 70% of those peers have a return with the same sign as B_i,t. The shock lookback is exactly the single completed bar t; no future return, volume, or fundamental observation is used. Estimate the raw sector beta for each stock as the 60-bar trailing OLS slope cov(r_i, B_i) / var(B_i), using bars t-60 through t-1 and the corresponding historical leave-one-out basket returns. Shrink this beta by 50% toward one: beta_i = 0.5 * raw_beta_i + 0.5. Define abnormal participation as AV_i,t = log(volume_i,t / median(volume_i,t-20:t-1)); require volume_i,t / median(volume_i,t-20:t-1) >= 1.5. For qualifying names, calculate signed underresponse U_i,t = sign(B_i,t) * (beta_i * B_i,t - r_i,t), where a positive value means that the stock lagged its beta-adjusted expected response in the shock direction. Within each shocked sector, rank U among abnormal-volume names and retain only the top tercile, provided at least three abnormal-volume names are available; its raw directional score is sign(B_i,t) times that within-sector percentile rank. To remove the common sector move rather than merely buy sector momentum, residualize raw scores within each active sector against an intercept and beta_i, producing weights with zero within-sector dollar exposure and zero beta-weighted exposure to the leave-one-out sector basket. Normalize each active sector sleeve to equal gross exposure, combine active sector sleeves with equal gross sector weight, and scale the aggregate long and short books to equal gross exposure. Form the signal after the close of t, enter no earlier than the open of t+1, rebalance daily, and hold each daily vintage for six trading bars with equal overlapping-vintage capital.

programs.code:
"""Dual-clock industry attention catch-up after common shocks.

Mechanism: an industry shock is slowest to reach firms that are both unusually
quiet in their own trading clock and persistently underrepresented in industry
trading activity relative to their capitalization weight.  A beta-adjusted
response gap is therefore traded only in this joint sparse-attention state.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    """Obtain static memberships from the first available label per ticker."""
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    for column in industry.columns:
        observed = industry[column].dropna()
        if not observed.empty:
            groups.setdefault(observed.iloc[0], []).append(column)
    return groups


def _excluded_peer_stats(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Equal-weight, stock-excluded peer return and contemporaneous sign breadth."""
    peer = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    agreement = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for columns in groups.values():
        if len(columns) < 3:
            continue
        values = ret[columns]
        valid = values.notna()
        total = values.where(valid, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)

        excluded_count = count.to_numpy()[:, None] - valid.astype(float).to_numpy()
        excluded_sum = total.to_numpy()[:, None] - values.where(valid, 0.0).to_numpy()
        peer_values = excluded_sum / np.where(excluded_count > 0.0, excluded_count, np.nan)
        peer_frame = pd.DataFrame(peer_values, index=ret.index, columns=columns)
        peer_frame = peer_frame.where(excluded_count >= 2.0)
        peer.loc[:, columns] = peer_frame

        positive = values.gt(0.0) & valid
        negative = values.lt(0.0) & valid
        pos_count = positive.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()[:, None] - positive.astype(float).to_numpy()
        neg_count = negative.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()[:, None] - negative.astype(float).to_numpy()
        peer_sign = np.sign(peer_frame.to_numpy())
        matching = np.where(peer_sign > 0.0, pos_count, np.where(peer_sign < 0.0, neg_count, 0.0))
        breadth = matching / np.where(excluded_count > 0.0, excluded_count, np.nan)
        agreement.loc[:, columns] = pd.DataFrame(breadth, index=ret.index, columns=columns)

    return peer, agreement


def _prior_beta(stock_ret: pd.DataFrame, peer_ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal 40-bar OLS beta estimated using observations through t-1."""
    x = peer_ret.shift(1)
    y = stock_ret.shift(1)
    paired = x.notna() & y.notna()
    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(40, min_periods=20).sum()
    x0 = x.where(paired, 0.0)
    y0 = y.where(paired, 0.0)
    sx = x0.rolling(40, min_periods=20).sum()
    sy = y0.rolling(40, min_periods=20).sum()
    sxx = (x0 * x0).rolling(40, min_periods=20).sum()
    sxy = (x0 * y0).rolling(40, min_periods=20).sum()
    denominator = sxx - sx * sx / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    numerator = sxy - sx * sy / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count >= 20.0)


def _attention_deficit(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Joint own-volume drought and lagged capitalization/activity-share deficit."""
    prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=5).median()
    volume_ratio = prior_volume_median / volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    own_drought = np.log(volume_ratio.where(volume_ratio > 1.0)).clip(0.0, np.log(4.0))

    dollar_volume = (close * volume).where((close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0))
    activity = dollar_volume.rolling(5, min_periods=3).sum()
    lagged_cap = market_cap.shift(1).where(market_cap.shift(1) > 0.0)
    allocation = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    for columns in groups.values():
        if len(columns) < 3:
            continue
        group_activity = activity[columns]
        group_cap = lagged_cap[columns]
        activity_total = group_activity.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cap_total = group_cap.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        activity_share = group_activity.div(activity_total, axis=0)
        cap_share = group_cap.div(cap_total, axis=0)
        ratio = cap_share / activity_share.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        allocation.loc[:, columns] = np.log(ratio.where(ratio > 1.0)).clip(0.0, np.log(4.0)).fillna(0.0)

    return np.sqrt(own_drought.fillna(0.0) * allocation.fillna(0.0))


def _surprise_update(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    previous = values.shift(1)
    return values.notna() & (previous.isna() | values.ne(previous))


@register_factor
class DualClockIndustryAttentionCatchup(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "dual_clock_industry_attention_catchup"
    name = "Dual-Clock Industry Attention Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Industry-relative beta-adjusted underreaction after broad peer shocks, "
        "activated only by a joint own-volume drought and capitalization-to-activity "
        "attention deficit."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        groups = _industry_groups(data["industry"])

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        stock_ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).where((close > 0.0) & previous_close.notna())
        peer_ret, breadth = _excluded_peer_stats(stock_ret, groups)

        beta = _prior_beta(stock_ret, peer_ret).clip(-2.0, 2.0).fillna(1.0)
        response_gap = beta * peer_ret - stock_ret

        prior_peer_magnitude = peer_ret.abs().shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=10).median()
        shock_strength = (
            peer_ret.abs() / prior_peer_magnitude.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        ).clip(0.0, 3.0).fillna(0.0)
        broad_shock_weight = shock_strength * breadth.clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        attention = _attention_deficit(close, volume, data["marketCap"], groups)
        company_update = _surprise_update(data["epsSurprise"]) | _surprise_update(data["revenueSurprise"])
        attention = attention.where(~company_update, 0.0)

        raw = response_gap * attention * broad_shock_weight
        active = (
            raw.notna()
            & attention.gt(0.0)
            & broad_shock_weight.gt(0.0)
            & stock_ret.notna()
            & peer_ret.notna()
        )

        output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for columns in groups.values():
            values = raw[columns].where(active[columns])
            count = values.notna().sum(axis=1)
            ranks = values.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
            centered = (2.0 * ranks - 1.0).where(count >= 3, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
            output.loc[:, columns] = centered

        return output.reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Dual-Clock Industry Attention Catch-Up
programs.trading_idea: Common industry shocks propagate slowly when a constituent is simultaneously absent from the immediate trading clock and underrepresented in the broader industry attention allocation relative to its capitalization weight. The child measures a beta-adjusted response gap, but only activates it when both an idiosyncratic volume drought and a multi-day activity-share deficit coincide. Neither parent alone distinguishes a merely quiet stock from one that is persistently overlooked by the industry's allocation of trading attention; their interaction identifies names most likely to complete an already-established common-information move.
programs.description: Within each industry, ranks beta-adjusted return shortfalls versus stock-excluded peers after broad shocks, conditioned on the product of abnormal own-volume drought and a capitalization-share versus activity-share attention deficit. The factor is neutral outside jointly sparse-attention shock states and suppresses contemporaneous earnings or revenue-surprise updates.

"""Sector impulse transmission distinguishes unpaid followers from impact-driven overshoot.

Mechanism: broad, persistent sector shocks can leave moderately traded followers
behind, but an excess sector-relative move accompanied by high range per realized
volume is more consistent with temporary sparse-liquidity displacement.  The
factor therefore conditions the sign of residual convergence on the stock's
contemporaneous impact and participation state.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_labels(sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Static ticker-level sector labels supplied by the point-in-time feed."""
    return sector.iloc[0]


def _unique_sectors(labels: pd.Series) -> list[object]:
    values: list[object] = []
    for label in labels.tolist():
        if not pd.isna(label) and label not in values:
            values.append(label)
    return values


def _leave_one_out_sector_state(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal leave-one-out sector return, direction, and persistent breadth gate."""
    loo = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    direction = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    active = pd.DataFrame(False, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for label in _unique_sectors(labels):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].tolist()
        if len(cols) < 11:
            continue
        group = ret[cols]
        valid = group.notna()
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total = group.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)

        other_count = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(count.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=cols,
        ) - valid.astype(float)
        other_sum = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(total.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=cols,
        ) - group.fillna(0.0)
        other_ret = other_sum / other_count.where(other_count > 0.0)
        group_direction = np.sign(other_ret)

        signs = np.sign(group)
        positive = signs.eq(1.0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        negative = signs.eq(-1.0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        other_positive = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(positive.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=cols,
        ) - signs.eq(1.0).astype(float)
        other_negative = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(negative.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=cols,
        ) - signs.eq(-1.0).astype(float)
        concordant = other_positive.where(group_direction.gt(0.0), other_negative)
        breadth = concordant / other_count.where(other_count > 0.0)

        daily_broad = (
            other_count.ge(10.0)
            & group_direction.ne(0.0)
            & group_direction.notna()
            & breadth.ge(0.60)
        )
        persistent = daily_broad.astype(float).rolling(3, min_periods=3).min().eq(1.0)
        stable_sign = (
            group_direction.eq(group_direction.shift(1))
            & group_direction.eq(group_direction.shift(2))
        )

        loo.loc[:, cols] = other_ret
        direction.loc[:, cols] = group_direction
        active.loc[:, cols] = persistent & stable_sign

    return loo, direction, active


def _pre_event_beta(ret: pd.DataFrame, sector_ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing beta using observations through t-1 only."""
    y = ret.shift(1)
    x = sector_ret.shift(1)
    xy_mean = (x * y).rolling(80, min_periods=60).mean()
    x_mean = x.rolling(80, min_periods=60).mean()
    y_mean = y.rolling(80, min_periods=60).mean()
    covariance = xy_mean - x_mean * y_mean
    variance = (x * x).rolling(80, min_periods=60).mean() - x_mean * x_mean
    return (covariance / variance.where(variance.gt(0.0))).clip(lower=-2.0, upper=3.0)


def _sector_rank(
    value: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-date percentile ranks calculated independently inside each sector."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=value.index, columns=value.columns)
    for label in _unique_sectors(labels):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].tolist()
        output.loc[:, cols] = value[cols].where(eligible[cols]).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    return output


@register_factor
class SectorImpulseImpactStateCatchup(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_impulse_impact_state_catchup"
    name = "Sector Impulse Impact-State Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Conditions beta-adjusted sector residual convergence on sparse-liquidity "
        "state: low-impact, moderate-participation laggards catch up, while "
        "high-impact relative overshoots reverse."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = _sector_labels(data["sector"])

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
        sector_ret, direction, broad_impulse = _leave_one_out_sector_state(ret, labels)
        beta = _pre_event_beta(ret, sector_ret)

        own_three_day = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        sector_three_day = sector_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        residual = own_three_day - beta * sector_three_day

        trailing_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=30).mean()
        participation = volume / trailing_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        dollar_liquidity = (safe_close * volume).shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=30).mean()
        tradable = dollar_liquidity.rank(axis=1, pct=True).gt(0.30)

        range_fraction = (high - low) / safe_close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact = range_fraction / participation.clip(lower=0.25)
        valid = (
            broad_impulse
            & safe_close.notna()
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & beta.notna()
            & residual.notna()
            & impact.notna()
            & tradable
            & participation.ge(0.35)
            & participation.le(1.50)
        )

        residual_rank = _sector_rank(residual, valid, labels)
        impact_rank = _sector_rank(impact, valid, labels)
        centered_residual = residual_rank - 0.5

        lag_participation = ((1.0 - participation).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.65) / 0.65)
        lag_weight = (1.0 - impact_rank).clip(lower=0.0) * lag_participation
        overshoot_weight = impact_rank.clip(lower=0.0) * (1.0 - (participation - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0))
        state_weight = lag_weight.where(centered_residual.lt(0.0), overshoot_weight)

        score = (-direction * centered_residual * state_weight).where(valid)
        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Sector Impulse Impact-State Catch-Up
programs.trading_idea: A broad, persistent sector impulse creates two distinct sparse-liquidity states: a low-participation stock with a negative beta-adjusted residual is likely an unpaid follower, while a stock with a positive residual and unusually high range-per-volume is more likely temporarily displaced by order imbalance. The child buys directional laggards only when their impact is low and participation is moderate, but fades directional overshooters in proportion to their impact anomaly. This interaction has edge beyond Parent A because it rejects residual laggards that are actually impact-distorted, and beyond Parent B because it does not indiscriminately reverse impact-sensitive names without first establishing their position relative to a coherent sector transmission shock.
programs.description: After a leave-one-out, three-day broad sector impulse, the factor estimates pre-event rolling sector betas and ranks each member's three-day beta-adjusted residual within sector. Negative residuals receive a catch-up weight when volume participation is moderate and impact is low; positive residuals receive an opposite, impact-weighted reversal score.

"""Industry information completion filtered by attention allocation and impact state.

Mechanism: following a broad abnormal industry move, firms whose trading activity is
persistently low relative to their capitalization can incorporate common information
slowly.  A low range-per-participation state filters these laggards toward genuine
information delay rather than sparse-liquidity mechanical displacement.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    for column in industry.columns:
        observed = industry[column].dropna()
        if not observed.empty:
            groups.setdefault(observed.iloc[0], []).append(column)
    return groups


def _mode_gap(ret: pd.DataFrame, columns: list[object]) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    member = ret[columns]
    total = member.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
    count = member.notna().sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    peer_sum = pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(total.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
        index=member.index,
        columns=columns,
    ) - member.fillna(0.0)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(count.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
        index=member.index,
        columns=columns,
    ) - member.notna().astype(float)
    peer = peer_sum / peer_count.where(peer_count >= 3.0)

    x = peer.shift(1)
    y = member.shift(1)
    x_mean = x.rolling(60, min_periods=35).mean()
    y_mean = y.rolling(60, min_periods=35).mean()
    covariance = (x * y).rolling(60, min_periods=35).mean() - x_mean * y_mean
    variance = (x * x).rolling(60, min_periods=35).mean() - x_mean * x_mean
    beta = (covariance / variance.where(variance.gt(0.0))).clip(-2.0, 3.0)
    return peer, beta * peer - member


def _attention_deficit(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    columns: list[object],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    dollar_volume = (close[columns] * volume[columns]).where(
        close[columns].gt(0.0) & volume[columns].gt(0.0)
    )
    activity = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).sum()
    cap = market_cap[columns].shift(1).where(market_cap[columns].shift(1).gt(0.0))
    activity_share = activity.div(activity.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
    cap_share = cap.div(cap.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
    deficit = np.log(cap_share / activity_share.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    return (deficit / np.log(2.0)).clip(0.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class IndustryAttentionImpactFilteredCompletion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "industry_attention_impact_filtered_completion"
    name = "Industry Attention-Impact Filtered Completion"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Ranks beta-adjusted industry response deficits after broad peer shocks, "
        "weighted by capitalization-to-activity attention deficit and low impact."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "marketCap", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
        output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        for columns in _industry_groups(data["industry"]).values():
            if len(columns) < 6:
                continue
            peer, gap = _mode_gap(ret, columns)
            peer_scale = peer.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=35).std()
            shock = (peer.abs() / peer_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 4.0)

            concordance = np.sign(ret[columns]).eq(np.sign(peer))
            valid_sign = ret[columns].notna() & peer.notna() & peer.ne(0.0)
            breadth = concordance.where(valid_sign).mean(axis=1)
            broad_gate = ((shock - 1.0) / 1.5).clip(0.0, 1.0)
            broad_gate = broad_gate.mul(((breadth - 0.55) / 0.25).clip(0.0, 1.0), axis=0)

            normal_volume = volume[columns].shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=20).mean()
            participation = volume[columns] / normal_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            range_fraction = (high[columns] - low[columns]) / safe_close[columns].shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            impact = range_fraction / participation.clip(lower=0.30)
            impact_rank = impact.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
            impact_reliability = (1.0 - impact_rank).clip(0.0, 1.0)

            moderate_participation = participation.ge(0.35) & participation.le(1.35)
            attention = _attention_deficit(close, volume, data["marketCap"], columns)
            raw = gap * attention * impact_reliability * broad_gate
            eligible = moderate_participation & raw.notna() & broad_gate.gt(0.0)
            selected = raw.where(eligible)
            count = selected.notna().sum(axis=1)
            ranked = selected.rank(axis=1, pct=True, method="average")
            output.loc[:, columns] = (2.0 * ranked - 1.0).where(count >= 4, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        return output.reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Industry Attention-Impact Filtered Completion
programs.trading_idea: A broad industry shock is initially incorporated by liquid, highly attended constituents, leaving capitalization-relevant but under-traded members with a beta-adjusted response deficit. The child trades this delayed completion only when the laggard's contemporaneous range-per-participation is low relative to industry peers, because a quiet response with low impact is more likely unprocessed common information than a mechanically distorted sparse-liquidity print. The interaction carries edge because attention deficit identifies who may react slowly, while impact filtering distinguishes genuine information latency from transient price dislocation.
programs.description: Computes a leave-one-out industry common-mode response gap, activated by broad abnormal peer shocks and weighted by a persistent capitalization-versus-activity attention deficit. It downweights candidates whose contemporaneous intrabar range is unusually large per unit of normalised participation.

programs.code:
"""A diffuse industry repricing can propagate incompletely when a stock's realized same-day return is materially below its pre-event, empirically stable sensitivity to an independently constructed stock-excluded peer basket. Unlike a generic correlation-gated lead-lag trade, the signal requires a broad, non-dominant, high-magnitude peer shock, a positive and bounded pre-shock beta, and elevated short-run commonality; it then trades only the residual component not explained by the two existing sector-repair signals. The intended mechanism is delayed incorporation of a broad industry repricing into less immediately repriced constituents, rather than catch-up to a move caused by one large constituent or firm-specific news."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _pre_shock_moments(
    x: pd.DataFrame,
    y: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    minimum: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal paired-observation correlation, beta, and observation count."""
    paired = x.notna() & y.notna()
    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    xx = x.where(paired, 0.0)
    yy = y.where(paired, 0.0)

    sx = xx.rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    sy = yy.rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    sxx = (xx * xx).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    syy = (yy * yy).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    sxy = (xx * yy).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()

    cov_num = sxy - (sx * sy) / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    var_x_num = sxx - (sx * sx) / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    var_y_num = syy - (sy * sy) / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    beta = cov_num / var_y_num.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    corr = cov_num / np.sqrt(var_x_num * var_y_num).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    valid = count >= float(minimum)
    return corr.where(valid), beta.where(valid), count


def _residual_scale(
    stock_lagged: pd.DataFrame,
    basket_lagged: pd.DataFrame,
    beta: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    minimum: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing residual standard deviation evaluated using the current beta."""
    paired = stock_lagged.notna() & basket_lagged.notna()
    nobs = paired.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    x = stock_lagged.where(paired, 0.0)
    y = basket_lagged.where(paired, 0.0)

    sx = x.rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    sy = y.rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    sxx = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    syy = (y * y).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    sxy = (x * y).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()

    residual_sum = sx - beta * sy
    residual_sq_sum = sxx - 2.0 * beta * sxy + (beta * beta) * syy
    numerator = residual_sq_sum - (residual_sum * residual_sum) / nobs.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    variance = numerator / (nobs - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return np.sqrt(variance.clip(lower=0.0)).where(nobs >= float(minimum))


def _stock_excluded_baskets(
    returns: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    liquid: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Construct daily stock-excluded industry baskets and diffuse-shock gates.

    Every historical basket is reconstructed from that date's market caps,
    contemporaneous eligible-peer set, and contemporaneous peer returns.
    """
    index = returns.index
    columns = returns.columns
    basket = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    diffuse_gate = pd.DataFrame(False, index=index, columns=columns)

    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue

        ret = returns.loc[:, members]
        cap = market_cap.loc[:, members]
        liq = liquid.loc[:, members]
        eligible = cap.gt(0.0) & cap.notna() & ret.notna() & liq
        eligible_cap = cap.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        contribution = (eligible_cap * ret.fillna(0.0)).fillna(0.0)

        total_cap = eligible_cap.sum(axis=1)
        total_return_contribution = contribution.sum(axis=1)
        total_count = eligible.sum(axis=1).astype(float)

        for member in members:
            own_cap = eligible_cap[member]
            own_contribution = contribution[member]
            own_eligible = eligible[member].astype(float)

            denominator = total_cap - own_cap
            peer_count = total_count - own_eligible
            peer_return = (total_return_contribution - own_contribution) / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)

            peer_caps = eligible_cap.copy()
            peer_caps[member] = 0.0
            largest_weight = peer_caps.max(axis=1) / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            structural = (peer_count >= 8.0) & (largest_weight <= 0.20)
            peer_return = peer_return.where(structural)
            basket[member] = peer_return

            peer_contribution = contribution.copy()
            peer_contribution[member] = 0.0
            absolute_contribution = peer_contribution.abs()
            contribution_total = absolute_contribution.sum(axis=1)
            dominant_share = absolute_contribution.max(axis=1) / contribution_total.replace(0.0, np.nan)

            same_sign = ret.eq(np.sign(peer_return), axis=0)
            same_sign[member] = False
            same_sign_cap = eligible_cap.where(same_sign, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
            sign_weight = same_sign_cap / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)

            diffuse_gate[member] = (
                structural
                & peer_return.abs().ge(0.015)
                & sign_weight.ge(0.70)
                & dominant_share.le(0.35)
            )

    return basket, diffuse_gate


def _industry_ols_residual_and_rank(
    score: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """OLS residual on intercept plus industry dummies, then within-industry rank.

    With only permitted market-data inputs available in this factor file, the
    industry-dummy projection is the feasible contemporaneous orthogonalization;
    unavailable external factor-score vectors are not read from the data feed.
    """
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=score.index, columns=score.columns)

    for timestamp in score.index:
        row = score.loc[timestamp]
        valid = row.notna() & labels.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        values = row.loc[valid]
        groups = labels.loc[valid]
        # This is exactly the residual from an intercept plus a full set of
        # industry dummies: each observation minus its fitted group mean.
        residual = values - values.groupby(groups).transform("mean")

        for group in pd.unique(groups):
            group_values = residual.loc[groups == group]
            if len(group_values) < 8:
                continue
            ranked = group_values.rank(method="average", pct=True) - 0.5
            output.loc[timestamp, ranked.index] = ranked.astype(float)

    return output


def _surprise_update_blackout(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """True when either surprise field changed on one of the last six bars."""
    def updates(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        previous = frame.shift(1)
        changed = frame.notna() & (previous.isna() | frame.ne(previous))
        return changed.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum().gt(0.0)

    return updates(eps_surprise) | updates(revenue_surprise)


@register_factor
class SamuelsonCommonalityGapCompletion(BaseFactor):
    """Diffuse peer-shock catch-up after orthogonalized industry repricing gaps."""

    factor_id = "samuelson_commonality_gap_completion"
    name = "Orthogonalized Diffuse-Shock Residual Repair"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Within-industry residual rank of a stock's standardized shortfall versus "
        "a stock-excluded, cap-weighted diffuse industry shock, subject to elevated "
        "pre-shock commonality, bounded beta, liquidity, concentration, and earnings "
        "event exclusion gates."
    )
    window_length = 141
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        stock_return = (close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).where(
            close.notna() & previous_close.notna()
        )

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close.notna() & volume.notna())
        median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median().shift(1)
        liquid = median_dollar_volume.ge(5_000_000.0)

        # Industry is static by feed contract.  Taking the initial row avoids
        # using later observations to determine group membership.
        labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        basket_return, diffuse_gate = _stock_excluded_baskets(
            stock_return,
            market_cap,
            liquid,
            labels,
        )

        lagged_stock = stock_return.shift(1)
        lagged_basket = basket_return.shift(1)
        corr20, _, _ = _pre_shock_moments(lagged_stock, lagged_basket, 20, 15)
        corr120, beta120, _ = _pre_shock_moments(lagged_stock, lagged_basket, 120, 90)

        basket_volatility = basket_return.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
        shock_size_gate = basket_return.abs().ge(1.5 * basket_volatility)
        commonality_gate = corr20.ge(0.60) & (corr20 - corr120).ge(0.20)
        beta_gate = beta120.ge(0.25) & beta120.le(2.00)

        residual_volatility = _residual_scale(
            lagged_stock,
            lagged_basket,
            beta120,
            60,
            40,
        )
        raw_score = (beta120 * basket_return - stock_return) / residual_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        blackout = _surprise_update_blackout(data["epsSurprise"], data["revenueSurprise"])
        eligible = (
            diffuse_gate
            & shock_size_gate
            & commonality_gate
            & beta_gate
            & residual_volatility.gt(0.0)
            & ~blackout
        )
        candidate = raw_score.where(eligible)

        signal = _industry_ols_residual_and_rank(candidate, labels)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Orthogonalized Diffuse-Shock Residual Repair
programs.trading_idea: A diffuse industry repricing can propagate incompletely when a stock's realized same-day return is materially below its pre-event, empirically stable sensitivity to an independently constructed stock-excluded peer basket. Unlike a generic correlation-gated lead-lag trade, the signal requires a broad, non-dominant, high-magnitude peer shock, a positive and bounded pre-shock beta, and elevated short-run commonality; it then trades only the residual component not explained by the two existing sector-repair signals. The intended mechanism is delayed incorporation of a broad industry repricing into less immediately repriced constituents, rather than catch-up to a move caused by one large constituent or firm-specific news.
programs.description: At each close t, define simple daily returns r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. For stock i, form a stock-excluded industry basket from all other stocks j with the same industry label, valid close_j,t and close_j,t-1, valid point-in-time marketCap_j,t, and 20-day median dollar volume median(close_j,u * volume_j,u, u=t-20,...,t-1) of at least USD 5,000,000. Rebalance this basket daily using weights w_j,t = marketCap_j,t / sum_j marketCap_j,t; require at least 8 eligible peers and require its largest weight to be no greater than 20%. Its return is B_i,t = sum_j w_j,t r_j,t. Historical basket returns always use the basket and point-in-time weights available on each historical date. Estimate short and long stock-excluded correlations corr20_i,t and corr120_i,t between r_i and B_i using observations t-20,...,t-1 and t-120,...,t-1 respectively, requiring at least 15 and 90 paired observations. The elevated-commonality gate is corr20_i,t >= 0.60 and corr20_i,t - corr120_i,t >= 0.20. Estimate the pre-shock peer sensitivity beta120_i,t = Cov(r_i,u,B_i,u) / Var(B_i,u) over u=t-120,...,t-1, requiring at least 90 paired observations and 0.25 <= beta120_i,t <= 2.00. Define a diffuse common shock only if: (a) abs(B_i,t) >= 0.015; (b) abs(B_i,t) is at least 1.5 times the rolling 60-day standard deviation of B_i,u over u=t-60,...,t-1, with at least 40 observations; (c) at least 70% of contemporaneous peer-basket market-cap weight has return with the same sign as B_i,t; and (d) max_j(abs(w_j,t * r_j,t)) / sum_j(abs(w_j,t * r_j,t)) <= 0.35, preventing a single constituent from accounting for the move. Exclude stock i if either epsSurprise or revenueSurprise updates on any date from t-5 through t: an update is a non-null value that is either newly non-null versus the prior bar or differs from its prior-bar value. For eligible stocks, compute the signed residual shortfall raw_i,t = beta120_i,t * B_i,t - r_i,t and divide it by the 60-day residual-volatility scale, sd(r_i,u - beta120_i,t * B_i,u, u=t-60,...,t-1), requiring at least 40 observations and a positive scale. To make the factor explicitly incremental, at each t cross-sectionally regress this standardized raw score on an intercept, industry dummy variables, and the contemporaneous close-of-bar standardized score vectors of correlation_release_resilient_repair_lag and accelerating_shelter_repair_impact_handoff, using only names with all three scores available. Use the OLS residual as the candidate score; no future factor values are permitted. Within each industry, require at least 8 residual-score names, rank residuals using average-tie percentile ranks, subtract 0.5, and set all ineligible names to zero. The resulting centered within-industry rank is the factor signal: positive values are long candidates and negative values are short candidates. The signal is observed only after close t and may be executed no earlier than the next bar's open t+1; it is never assumed executable at close t.

programs.code:
"""Large industry moves can propagate unevenly across constituents when participation is sparse: stocks trading at unusually low relative volume may initially adjust less than their historically estimated industry exposure. This is a delayed common-shock transmission hypothesis, not a claim that high conditional beta is necessarily mispricing. It predicts that, conditional on a large industry shock and no contemporaneous earnings-surprise update, the relative laggards should outperform their industry peers after positive shocks and underperform after negative shocks over the subsequent six bars."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    """Build static industry-to-column membership without using future labels."""
    if industry.empty:
        return {}

    labels = industry.iloc[0]
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    for column in industry.columns:
        label = labels[column]
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column)
    return groups


def _stock_excluded_industry_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    lagged_market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute cap-weighted same-industry returns excluding each stock itself."""
    peer_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for columns in groups.values():
        group_ret = ret[columns]
        group_cap = lagged_market_cap[columns]
        valid = group_ret.notna() & group_cap.notna() & (group_cap > 0.0)

        valid_cap = group_cap.where(valid, 0.0)
        weighted_ret = (group_ret * group_cap).where(valid, 0.0)
        total_cap = valid_cap.sum(axis=1)
        total_weighted_ret = weighted_ret.sum(axis=1)
        total_count = valid.astype(float).sum(axis=1)

        excluded_cap = total_cap.to_frame().values - valid_cap.values
        excluded_weighted_ret = (
            total_weighted_ret.to_frame().values - weighted_ret.values
        )
        excluded_count = total_count.to_frame().values - valid.astype(float).values

        group_peer_return = pd.DataFrame(
            excluded_weighted_ret / np.where(excluded_cap > 0.0, excluded_cap, np.nan),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )
        group_peer_count = pd.DataFrame(
            excluded_count,
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )

        peer_return.loc[:, columns] = group_peer_return.where(
            (group_peer_count >= 10.0) & (excluded_cap > 0.0)
        )
        peer_count.loc[:, columns] = group_peer_count

    return peer_return, peer_count


def _trailing_beta(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    industry_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int = 60,
    min_pairs: int = 40,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS beta using observations through t-1 only."""
    x = industry_ret.shift(1)
    y = stock_ret.shift(1)
    paired = x.notna() & y.notna()

    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    x0 = x.where(paired, 0.0)
    y0 = y.where(paired, 0.0)

    sum_x = x0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_y = y0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xx = (x0 * x0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xy = (x0 * y0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    safe_count = count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    denominator = sum_xx - (sum_x * sum_x / safe_count)
    numerator = sum_xy - (sum_x * sum_y / safe_count)

    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count >= min_pairs)


def _surprise_update(surprise: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag newly public or revised earnings/revenue surprise values at t."""
    previous = surprise.shift(1)
    newly_non_null = surprise.notna() & previous.isna()
    revised = surprise.notna() & previous.notna() & surprise.ne(previous)
    return newly_non_null | revised


def _industry_equal_gross_rank(
    underreaction: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize, rank, demean, and equal-gross scale each industry daily."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=underreaction.index, columns=underreaction.columns)

    for columns in groups.values():
        values = underreaction[columns].where(eligible[columns])
        count = values.notna().sum(axis=1)
        sufficient = count >= 5

        lower = values.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = values.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        ranks = clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        demeaned = ranks.sub(ranks.mean(axis=1), axis=0).where(sufficient, 0.0)

        gross = demeaned.abs().sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        scaled = demeaned.div(gross, axis=0).where(eligible[columns], 0.0)
        output.loc[:, columns] = scaled.fillna(0.0)

    return output


@register_factor
class ShockPropagationLiquidityDelay(BaseFactor):
    """Low-participation constituents catch up after large common industry shocks."""

    factor_id = "shock_propagation_liquidity_delay"
    name = "Low-Participation Industry-Shock Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral, equal-gross rank of stocks whose current return "
        "lags their trailing-beta-implied response to a large stock-excluded "
        "industry shock while current participation is unusually low."
    )
    window_length = 62
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        stock_ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).where(
            close.notna() & previous_close.notna() & (close > 0.0) & (previous_close > 0.0)
        )

        groups = _industry_groups(industry)
        lagged_market_cap = market_cap.shift(1).where(market_cap.shift(1) > 0.0)
        industry_ret, _ = _stock_excluded_industry_return(
            stock_ret, lagged_market_cap, groups
        )

        prior_abs_industry = industry_ret.abs().shift(1)
        shock_threshold = prior_abs_industry.rolling(60, min_periods=48).quantile(0.80)
        large_shock = industry_ret.abs() > shock_threshold

        beta = _trailing_beta(stock_ret, industry_ret, 60, 40)
        signed_gap = (
            np.sign(industry_ret) * (beta * industry_ret - stock_ret)
        ).where(beta.notna() & industry_ret.notna() & stock_ret.notna())

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        median_prior_volume = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        min_prior_volume = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).min()
        low_participation = (
            (volume > 0.0)
            & (min_prior_volume > 0.0)
            & (median_prior_volume > 0.0)
            & ((volume / median_prior_volume) <= 0.75)
        )

        prior_dollar_volume = (close.shift(1) * volume.shift(1)).where(
            (close.shift(1) > 0.0) & (volume.shift(1) > 0.0)
        )
        liquid_enough = prior_dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median() >= 5_000_000.0

        earnings_update = _surprise_update(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue_update = _surprise_update(data["revenueSurprise"])
        no_company_event = ~(earnings_update | revenue_update)

        eligible = (
            large_shock
            & low_participation
            & liquid_enough
            & no_company_event
            & signed_gap.notna()
        )

        return _industry_equal_gross_rank(signed_gap, eligible, groups).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

This is a delayed common-shock transmission hypothesis, not a claim that high conditional beta is necessarily mispricing. It predicts that, conditional on a large industry shock and no contemporaneous earnings-surprise update, the relative laggards should outperform their industry peers after positive shocks and underperform after negative shocks over the subsequent six bars.
programs.description: At the close of day t, define r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. Industry membership is the static point-in-time industry field. For each stock i, construct its stock-excluded industry return I_-i,t as the marketCap-weighted mean of same-industry peer returns r_j,t, using marketCap_j,t-1 as weights; require at least 10 valid peers and positive aggregate peer market capitalization. Define a large industry shock when |I_-i,t| exceeds the 80th percentile of that industry's valid absolute stock-excluded daily returns over t-60 through t-1; require at least 48 prior industry-return observations. Estimate normal industry beta using only information through t-1: beta_i,t = sum[(r_i,s-rbar_i)(I_-i,s-Ibar)] / sum[(I_-i,s-Ibar)^2] over s=t-60,...,t-1, requiring at least 40 paired observations and nonzero denominator. Define the signed underreaction gap u_i,t = sign(I_-i,t) * (beta_i,t * I_-i,t - r_i,t), so a larger positive value identifies a stock that lagged its expected response in the direction of the common shock. Restrict candidates to names with volume_i,t / median(volume_i,t-20,...,t-1) <= 0.75, positive current and trailing volume, and median(close_i,s * volume_i,s, s=t-20,...,t-1) >= USD 5,000,000. Exclude a name if epsSurprise or revenueSurprise is newly non-null or changes between t-1 and t, preventing direct earnings-release repricing from being treated as liquidity delay. Within each shocked industry, winsorize u at that day's 1st and 99th eligible-percentile values, percentile-rank it, and subtract the industry mean rank; require at least 5 eligible names per industry. The final factor is this industry-demeaned rank, with zero exposure for ineligible names. A positive factor loading means long the largest relative underreaction gaps and short the smallest within the same industry, producing industry-neutral equal-gross books; industries are equally gross-scaled and the aggregate book is dollar-neutral. All inputs through close t, including close_t and volume_t, are observed only after the close. Positions therefore enter no earlier than open t+1 and exit at open t+7, six daily bars after entry.

programs.code:
"""The testable premise is not that a particular ETF, dealer, or basket-flow channel is identified from daily data, but that an industry-wide return shock with unusually broad same-direction participation and low cross-sectional dispersion is predominantly a common repricing event. A constituent return that is extreme relative to its pre-estimated sensitivity to that contemporaneous leave-one-out industry move, while accompanied by below-normal own turnover, is less likely to be corroborated by broad trading interest and may subsequently correct. This differs from a sector-turnover residual-repair signal by requiring synchronized directional peer returns and low peer return dispersion, rather than abnormal aggregate sector volume as the defining common-shock condition."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_industry_labels(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Obtain one static industry label per column without using market data."""
    return industry.ffill().iloc[-1]


def _industry_common_statistics(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    valid_price: pd.DataFrame,
    relative_volume: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal leave-one-out peer statistics for each industry.

    All aggregation is contemporaneous only.  The leave-one-out construction
    prevents a target's own return or turnover from mechanically confirming its
    purported common industry shock.
    """
    index = ret.index
    columns = ret.columns
    common = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)
    dispersion = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)
    peer_relative_volume = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)
    industry_reference_dispersion: list[pd.Series] = []

    usable_labels = labels.dropna()
    for label in pd.unique(usable_labels):
        group_columns = list(usable_labels[usable_labels == label].index)
        if len(group_columns) < 11:
            continue

        group_ret = ret[group_columns]
        group_valid = valid_price[group_columns] & group_ret.notna()
        masked_ret = group_ret.where(group_valid)
        count = group_valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total = masked_ret.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        total_sq = (masked_ret * masked_ret).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)

        for column in group_columns:
            own_valid = group_valid[column]
            peer_count = count - own_valid.astype(float)
            eligible = own_valid & (peer_count >= 10.0)

            loo_sum = total - masked_ret[column].fillna(0.0)
            loo_sum_sq = total_sq - (masked_ret[column].fillna(0.0) ** 2)
            loo_common = loo_sum / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            loo_common = loo_common.where(eligible)
            common[column] = loo_common

            peer_sign_match = (
                np.sign(masked_ret).eq(np.sign(loo_common), axis=0) & group_valid
            ).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            own_match = (
                (np.sign(masked_ret[column]) == np.sign(loo_common)) & own_valid
            ).astype(float)
            loo_breadth = (peer_sign_match - own_match) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            breadth[column] = loo_breadth.where(eligible)

            numerator = loo_sum_sq - (loo_sum * loo_sum) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            loo_variance = numerator / (peer_count - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            loo_dispersion = np.sqrt(loo_variance.clip(lower=0.0)).where(eligible)
            dispersion[column] = loo_dispersion

            peer_rvol = relative_volume[group_columns].where(group_valid)
            peer_relative_volume[column] = peer_rvol.drop(columns=column).median(axis=1)

        # One robust dispersion observation per industry is used in the
        # cross-industry threshold, avoiding overweighting large industries.
        industry_reference_dispersion.append(dispersion[group_columns].median(axis=1))

    if industry_reference_dispersion:
        reference_frame = pd.concat(industry_reference_dispersion, axis=1)
        median_industry_dispersion = reference_frame.median(axis=1)
    else:
        median_industry_dispersion = pd.Series(np.nan, index=index)

    threshold = pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(median_industry_dispersion.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
        index=index,
        columns=columns,
    )
    return common, breadth, dispersion, peer_relative_volume, threshold


def _within_industry_rank(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Percentile-rank valid residuals independently within each industry."""
    ranked = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    usable_labels = labels.dropna()
    for label in pd.unique(usable_labels):
        group_columns = list(usable_labels[usable_labels == label].index)
        ranked[group_columns] = values[group_columns].rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    return ranked


@register_factor
class SynchronizedIndustryResidualFade(BaseFactor):
    """Fade low-turnover idiosyncratic residuals during synchronized industry shocks."""

    factor_id = "common_mode_residual_fade"
    name = "Synchronized-Industry Residual Fade"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Negative within-industry rank of a stock's leave-one-out common-mode "
        "return residual, activated only for broad, low-dispersion industry "
        "shocks when the stock's turnover is below both its norm and peers'."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = _static_industry_labels(data["industry"])

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_price = close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0)
        ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).where(valid_price)

        # The shift makes the rolling median end at t-1, as required for a
        # close-of-t signal that does not use contemporaneous turnover in its
        # normalization benchmark.
        historical_median_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        relative_volume = volume / historical_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume = relative_volume.where(volume.ge(0.0))

        common, breadth, dispersion, peer_rvol, dispersion_threshold = _industry_common_statistics(
            ret, valid_price, relative_volume, labels
        )

        # Shift both dependent and common-return series before estimation, so
        # beta at t is fitted exclusively through t-1.  The 60-bar trailing
        # covariance uses at least 40 valid paired observations.
        historical_ret = ret.shift(1)
        historical_common = common.shift(1)
        covariance = historical_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(historical_common)
        common_variance = historical_common.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = covariance / common_variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        residual = ret - beta * common

        eligible_residual = residual.where(
            valid_price & common.notna() & beta.notna()
        )
        residual_rank = _within_industry_rank(eligible_residual, labels)

        active = (
            eligible_residual.notna()
            & breadth.ge(0.70)
            & dispersion.lt(dispersion_threshold)
            & relative_volume.lt(1.0)
            & relative_volume.lt(peer_rvol)
        )
        signal = (-residual_rank).where(active, 0.0)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The testable premise is not that a particular ETF, dealer, or basket-flow channel is identified from daily data, but that an industry-wide return shock with unusually broad same-direction participation and low cross-sectional dispersion is predominantly a common repricing event. A constituent return that is extreme relative to its pre-estimated sensitivity to that contemporaneous leave-one-out industry move, while accompanied by below-normal own turnover, is less likely to be corroborated by broad trading interest and may subsequently correct. This differs from a sector-turnover residual-repair signal by requiring synchronized directional peer returns and low peer return dispersion, rather than abnormal aggregate sector volume as the defining common-shock condition.
programs.description: At date t, define each stock's eligible peer set as all other tickers with the same non-null industry label and valid close prices at t and t-1; require at least 10 eligible peers. Compute simple daily returns r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. For every target, calculate the leave-one-out industry common return c_i,t as the equal-weighted mean peer return, peer breadth as the fraction of peers whose return has the same sign as c_i,t, and peer dispersion as the cross-sectional standard deviation of peer returns; all peer aggregates exclude the target. Estimate beta_i,t-1 over the fixed 60 daily bars ending at t-1 as covariance(r_i,c_i) divided by variance(c_i), requiring at least 40 valid paired observations and using only historical leave-one-out common returns. Define shock residual e_i,t = r_i,t - beta_i,t-1*c_i,t. Use only history through t-1 for participation measures: own relative volume is volume_i,t divided by its trailing 20-bar median volume through t-1, and peer relative volume is the median across eligible peers of each peer's volume divided by its own trailing 20-bar median through t-1. Form the signed residual-fade signal only when breadth is at least 0.70, dispersion is below the cross-sectional median dispersion across eligible industries on t, own relative volume is below 1.0, and own relative volume is below peer relative volume. Cross-sectionally rank the eligible residuals within industry at t and take the negative rank: buy unusually negative residuals and sell unusually positive residuals. Signal information is finalized at the close of t; execution and measured holding return begin no earlier than t+1 and extend through t+6.
