"""Repair residual liquidation after a cohesive industry shock has cooled.

Mechanism: broad, low-dispersion peer selling supplies a common-shock anchor.
A thin constituent with an unconfirmed beta-adjusted excess decline is bought only
when its range is cooling and balance-sheet resilience makes distress less likely.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_peer_state(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal contemporaneous leave-one-out peer return, breadth, and dispersion."""
    peer = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    dispersion = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    usable = labels.dropna()
    for label in pd.unique(usable):
        members = list(usable[usable == label].index)
        if len(members) < 8:
            continue

        group = ret[members]
        valid = group.notna()
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total = group.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        total_sq = (group * group).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)

        for ticker in members:
            own_valid = valid[ticker]
            others = count - own_valid.astype(float)
            eligible = own_valid & others.ge(7.0)
            own = group[ticker].fillna(0.0)
            loo_sum = total - own
            loo = loo_sum / others.replace(0.0, np.nan)

            loo_sq = total_sq - own * own
            variance = (
                loo_sq - loo_sum * loo_sum / others.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            ) / (others - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)

            other_returns = group.drop(columns=ticker)
            aligned = other_returns.mul(np.sign(loo), axis=0).gt(0.0).sum(axis=1)
            peer[ticker] = loo.where(eligible)
            breadth[ticker] = (aligned / others.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(eligible)
            dispersion[ticker] = np.sqrt(variance.clip(lower=0.0)).where(eligible)

    return peer, breadth, dispersion


def _resilience(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Two-source cross-sectional solvency score, avoiding one-field imputations."""
    cash = rank(data["cashRatio"].where(data["cashRatio"] >= 0.0))
    debt = rank(-data["debtToCapital"].where(data["debtToCapital"] >= 0.0))
    valid = cash.notna().astype(float) + debt.notna().astype(float)
    return ((cash.fillna(0.0) + debt.fillna(0.0)) / valid.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
        valid.ge(2.0)
    )


@register_factor
class CohesiveShockCoolingResidualRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cohesive_shock_cooling_residual_repair"
    name = "Cohesive Shock Cooling Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Long resilient thin names with a large beta-adjusted downside residual in "
        "a broad low-dispersion industry selloff, once elevated range has cooled "
        "and own turnover remains below normal."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close", "high", "low", "volume", "marketCap", "industry",
        "cashRatio", "debtToCapital",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        labels = data["industry"].ffill().iloc[-1]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).where(
            close.gt(0.0) & previous_close.gt(0.0)
        )
        peer, breadth, dispersion = _industry_peer_state(ret, labels)

        peer_scale = peer.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        dispersion_base = dispersion.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=25).median()
        cohesive_down = (
            peer.lt(-0.5 * peer_scale)
            & breadth.ge(0.70)
            & dispersion.lt(dispersion_base)
        )
        recent_cohesive_down = cohesive_down.rolling(3, min_periods=1).max().astype(bool)

        lag_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lag_peer = peer.shift(1)
        observations = (lag_ret.notna() & lag_peer.notna()).astype(float).rolling(
            60, min_periods=40
        ).sum()
        covariance = lag_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(lag_peer)
        variance = lag_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            observations.ge(40.0)
        ).clip(0.0, 2.0)
        excess_downside = (beta * peer - ret).clip(lower=0.0)
        residual_scale = ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        standardized_excess = excess_downside / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        dollar_volume = close * volume
        turnover = (dollar_volume / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0) & market_cap.gt(0.0)
        )
        turnover_base = turnover.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        average_turnover = turnover.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        quiet_turnover = turnover.lt(turnover_base)
        structurally_thin = rank(average_turnover).le(0.45)

        log_range = np.log(high / low).where(high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0))
        range_base = log_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        current_range = log_range.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean()
        prior_range = log_range.shift(2).rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean()
        cooling_amount = ((prior_range - current_range) / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
            lower=0.0, upper=3.0
        )
        cooling = prior_range.gt(range_base) & current_range.lt(prior_range)

        resilience = _resilience(data)
        eligible = (
            recent_cohesive_down
            & ret.lt(0.0)
            & beta.notna()
            & standardized_excess.gt(0.0)
            & quiet_turnover
            & structurally_thin
            & cooling
            & resilience.ge(0.50)
        )
        strength = (
            standardized_excess.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
            * cooling_amount
            * resilience
        ).where(eligible)
        return rank(strength).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A broad, low-dispersion industry selloff is treated as a common repricing state rather than issuer-specific information. Within that state, a stock whose beta-adjusted decline is unusually severe but occurs on subdued turnover is more likely to reflect transient local liquidity pressure; the signal only acts once its elevated range begins to cool and its balance sheet is comparatively resilient. The interaction adds edge because common-mode filtering alone can fade still-active information shocks, while cooling alone can mistake distress for exhaustion: their conjunction identifies an unconfirmed residual liquidation that has likely completed.

Industry peer returns, breadth, and dispersion are leave-one-out.

programs.code:
"""A broad, same-direction industry move can be incorporated more slowly by constituents with persistently low trading turnover because arbitrage capital and price discovery are constrained in sparsely traded names. The hypothesis is not that low volatility or entropy identifies informed flow; it is that a clearly broad industry shock combined with low constituent turnover and no firm-specific volume event predicts delayed convergence toward the industry move. The prediction should fail for liquid constituents, for industries without a broad common move, and when the apparent laggard is experiencing unusually high idiosyncratic trading activity."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _industry_leave_one_out(ret: pd.DataFrame, industry_codes: np.ndarray) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal daily leave-one-out industry returns and shock eligibility."""
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    loo = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    shocked = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)
    valid_codes = np.unique(industry_codes[industry_codes >= 0])
    for code in valid_codes:
        members = np.flatnonzero(industry_codes == code)
        if members.size < 8:
            continue
        group_returns = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(group_returns)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        total = np.where(valid, group_returns, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        retained = count >= 8
        group_mean = np.divide(total, count, out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float), where=count > 0)
        direction = np.sign(group_mean)
        same_direction = (np.sign(group_returns) == direction[:, None]) & valid
        concentration = np.divide(same_direction.sum(axis=1), count, out=np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=float), where=count > 0)
        peer_count = count[:, None] - valid.astype(int)
        peer_return = np.divide(total[:, None] - np.where(valid, group_returns, 0.0), peer_count, out=np.full_like(group_returns, np.nan, dtype=float), where=valid & (peer_count >= 7))
        loo[:, members] = peer_return
        broad = retained & (direction != 0.0) & (concentration >= 0.75)
        shocked[:, members] = valid & broad[:, None] & np.isfinite(peer_return) & (np.abs(peer_return) >= 0.01)
    return (pd.DataFrame(loo, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns), pd.DataFrame(shocked, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns))

def _capped_side_weights(member_codes: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Allocate a side equally within industries, capping each industry at 20%."""
    n_members = member_codes.size
    weights = np.zeros(n_members, dtype=float)
    if n_members == 0:
        return weights
    codes, inverse = np.unique(member_codes, return_inverse=True)
    n_groups = codes.size
    if n_groups < 5:
        return weights
    counts = np.bincount(inverse).astype(float)
    allocation = counts / float(n_members)
    cap = 0.2
    for _ in range(n_groups + 1):
        over = allocation > cap + 1e-12
        if not over.any():
            break
        excess = float((allocation[over] - cap).sum())
        allocation[over] = cap
        recipients = allocation < cap - 1e-12
        if not recipients.any():
            return np.zeros(n_members, dtype=float)
        allocation[recipients] += excess / float(recipients.sum())
    if np.any(allocation > cap + 1e-10) or allocation.sum() <= 0.0:
        return weights
    allocation /= allocation.sum()
    weights = allocation[inverse] / counts[inverse]
    return weights

def _portfolio_from_scores(scores: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, industry_codes: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize candidate underreaction scores and form capped long/short weights."""
    score_values = scores.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    eligible_values = eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool, copy=False)
    output = np.zeros_like(score_values, dtype=float)
    for row in range(score_values.shape[0]):
        mask = eligible_values[row] & np.isfinite(score_values[row])
        positions = np.flatnonzero(mask)
        if positions.size < 5:
            continue
        row_scores = score_values[row, positions]
        lower, upper = np.nanquantile(row_scores, [0.02, 0.98])
        clipped = np.clip(row_scores, lower, upper)
        percentile = pd.Series(clipped).rank(method='average', pct=True).to_numpy()
        long_local = np.flatnonzero(percentile >= 0.8)
        short_local = np.flatnonzero(percentile <= 0.2)
        if long_local.size == 0 or short_local.size == 0:
            continue
        long_positions = positions[long_local]
        short_positions = positions[short_local]
        long_weights = _capped_side_weights(industry_codes[long_positions])
        short_weights = _capped_side_weights(industry_codes[short_positions])
        output[row, long_positions] += long_weights
        output[row, short_positions] -= short_weights
    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=scores.index, columns=scores.columns)

@register_factor
class SparseLiquidityIndustryRepricing(BaseFactor):
    """Delayed industry-shock repricing among low-turnover constituents."""
    factor_id = 'sparse_liquidity_industry_repricing_j'
    name = 'Sparse-Liquidity Industry Repricing'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Industry-shock underreaction portfolio: after a broad same-direction industry move, long low-turnover constituents lagging their beta-adjusted leave-one-out industry return and short low-turnover overreactors, while excluding idiosyncratic return and volume events.'
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float)
        market_cap = data['marketCap'].astype(float)
        industry = data['industry']
        valid_close = (close > 0.0) & (close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).where(valid_close)
        valid_turnover = (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0) & (market_cap > 0.0)
        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap).where(valid_turnover)
        average_turnover = turnover.rolling(19, min_periods=15).mean()
        labels = industry.iloc[0].to_numpy(dtype=object, copy=False)
        industry_codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels, sort=False)
        loo, shocked_industry = _industry_leave_one_out(ret, industry_codes)
        lagged_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lagged_loo = loo.shift(1)
        paired = (lagged_ret.notna() & lagged_loo.notna()).astype(float)
        paired_count = paired.rolling(55, min_periods=40).sum()
        covariance = lagged_ret.rolling(66, min_periods=40).cov(lagged_loo)
        variance = lagged_loo.rolling(62, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(paired_count >= 40)
        beta = beta.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
        predicted = beta * loo
        underreaction = predicted - ret
        residual = ret - predicted
        base_eligible = shocked_industry & beta.notna() & turnover.notna() & average_turnover.notna() & (residual.abs() <= 0.04) & (turnover <= 2.0 * average_turnover)
        eligible_values = base_eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool, copy=True)
        avg_values = average_turnover.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
        for row in range(eligible_values.shape[0]):
            positions = np.flatnonzero(eligible_values[row] & np.isfinite(avg_values[row]))
            if positions.size == 0:
                continue
            cutoff = np.nanquantile(avg_values[row, positions], 0.3)
            eligible_values[row, positions] &= avg_values[row, positions] <= cutoff
        low_liquidity_eligible = pd.DataFrame(eligible_values, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        return _portfolio_from_scores(underreaction, low_liquidity_eligible, industry_codes)

programs.trading_idea: A broad, same-direction industry move can be incorporated more slowly by constituents with persistently low trading turnover because arbitrage capital and price discovery are constrained in sparsely traded names. The hypothesis is not that low volatility or entropy identifies informed flow; it is that a clearly broad industry shock combined with low constituent turnover and no firm-specific volume event predicts delayed convergence toward the industry move. The prediction should fail for liquid constituents, for industries without a broad common move, and when the apparent laggard is experiencing unusually high idiosyncratic trading activity.
programs.description: At each date t, use only data through the date-t close. Define stock return r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1 and daily turnover TV_i,t = close_i,t * volume_i,t / marketCap_i,t; observations with nonpositive close, volume, or marketCap are invalid. Define each stock's 20-day average turnover as the arithmetic mean of TV over t-19 through t, requiring at least 15 valid observations. Within each static industry, retain an industry only when at least 8 valid constituents have date-t returns. For each retained stock, compute the leave-one-out equal-weight industry return R_-i,t from other valid constituents, requiring at least 7 peers. A common industry shock exists only if at least 75% of the valid industry constituents have the same sign as the full equal-weight industry return and abs(R_-i,t) is at least 1.0%; otherwise the signal is zero. Estimate beta_i,t as the slope from an OLS regression of the stock's daily returns on its leave-one-out industry returns over t-60 through t-1, requiring at least 40 paired observations; clip beta to [0, 2]. Define contemporaneous residual underreaction U_i,t = beta_i,t * R_-i,t - r_i,t. Exclude a stock if abs(r_i,t - beta_i,t * R_-i,t) exceeds 4%, or if its date-t turnover exceeds 2 times its own trailing-20-day average turnover, so the factor does not treat a likely firm-specific event as delayed industry repricing. Among remaining stocks in shocked industries, define low-liquidity eligibility as trailing-20-day turnover in the bottom 30% of all eligible stocks on date t. """Coherent common-shock completion among persistently sparse names.

Mechanism: synchronized, low-dispersion industry returns identify a common
repricing event.  A quiet constituent with structurally low turnover can lag
that mode because limited arbitrage capacity delays price discovery; its
beta-adjusted gap should close over the following several sessions.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_mode(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal contemporaneous leave-one-out industry mean and coherence stats."""
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    common = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    breadth = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    dispersion = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    threshold = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    group_reference: list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]] = []

    for code in np.unique(codes[codes >= 0]):
        members = np.flatnonzero(codes == code)
        if members.size < 8:
            continue
        group = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(group)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total = np.where(valid, group, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        total_sq = np.where(valid, group * group, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        group_dispersion = np.full((n_rows, members.size), np.nan, dtype=float)

        for local, column in enumerate(members):
            own_valid = valid[:, local]
            peer_count = count - own_valid.astype(float)
            usable = own_valid & (peer_count >= 7.0)
            own_ret = np.where(own_valid, group[:, local], 0.0)
            peer_sum = total - own_ret
            peer_mean = np.divide(
                peer_sum,
                peer_count,
                out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=peer_count > 0.0,
            )
            peer_mean[~usable] = np.nan
            common[:, column] = peer_mean

            direction = np.sign(peer_mean)
            matches = ((np.sign(group) == direction[:, None]) & valid).sum(axis=1)
            own_match = ((np.sign(group[:, local]) == direction) & own_valid).astype(float)
            peer_breadth = np.divide(
                matches - own_match,
                peer_count,
                out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=peer_count > 0.0,
            )
            breadth[:, column] = np.where(usable, peer_breadth, np.nan)

            peer_sq = total_sq - own_ret * own_ret
            numerator = peer_sq - peer_sum * peer_sum / np.where(peer_count > 0.0, peer_count, np.nan)
            peer_var = np.divide(
                numerator,
                peer_count - 1.0,
                out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=peer_count > 1.0,
            )
            peer_std = np.sqrt(np.maximum(peer_var, 0.0))
            peer_std[~usable] = np.nan
            dispersion[:, column] = peer_std
            group_dispersion[:, local] = peer_std

        group_reference.append((members, np.nanmedian(group_dispersion, axis=1)))

    if group_reference:
        reference = np.column_stack([item[1] for item in group_reference])
        cross_industry_threshold = np.nanmedian(reference, axis=1)
        for members, _ in group_reference:
            threshold[:, members] = cross_industry_threshold[:, None]

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(common, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(breadth, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(dispersion, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(threshold, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
    )


@register_factor
class CoherentSparseModeGapCompletion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "coherent_sparse_mode_gap_completion"
    name = "Coherent Sparse-Mode Gap Completion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Beta-adjusted lag versus a synchronized leave-one-out industry mode, "
        "activated only for persistently low-turnover names trading quietly."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].astype(float)
        industry = data["industry"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_price = close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0)
        ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).where(valid_price)

        labels = industry.iloc[0]
        codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels.to_numpy(dtype=object, copy=False), sort=False)
        common, breadth, dispersion, dispersion_limit = _leave_one_out_mode(ret, codes)

        historical_ret = ret.shift(1)
        historical_common = common.shift(1)
        covariance = historical_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(historical_common)
        variance = historical_common.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        residual = ret - beta * common
        residual_scale = residual.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=25).std()
        standardized_gap = (-residual / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        valid_turnover = close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0) & market_cap.gt(0.0)
        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap).where(valid_turnover)
        normal_turnover = turnover.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        quiet_turnover = turnover.le(normal_turnover)

        common_shock = (
            common.abs().ge(0.008)
            & breadth.ge(0.70)
            & dispersion.le(dispersion_limit)
            & beta.notna()
        )
        base_active = (
            valid_price
            & common_shock
            & standardized_gap.notna()
            & normal_turnover.notna()
            & quiet_turnover
        )

        low_turnover_cutoff = normal_turnover.where(base_active).quantile(0.35, axis=1)
        persistently_sparse = normal_turnover.le(low_turnover_cutoff, axis=0)
        active = base_active & persistently_sparse

        ranked_gap = standardized_gap.where(active).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return ranked_gap.where(active, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

"""A broad, same-direction industry move can be incorporated more slowly by constituents with persistently low trading turnover because arbitrage capital and price discovery are constrained in sparsely traded names. The hypothesis is not that low volatility or entropy identifies informed flow; it is that a clearly broad industry shock combined with low constituent turnover and no firm-specific volume event predicts delayed convergence toward the industry move. The prediction should fail for liquid constituents, for industries without a broad common move, and when the apparent laggard is experiencing unusually high idiosyncratic trading activity."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_leave_one_out(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, industry_codes: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal daily leave-one-out industry returns and shock eligibility."""
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    loo = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    shocked = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)

    valid_codes = np.unique(industry_codes[industry_codes >= 0])
    for code in valid_codes:
        members = np.flatnonzero(industry_codes == code)
        if members.size < 8:
            continue

        group_returns = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(group_returns)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        total = np.where(valid, group_returns, 0.0).sum(axis=1)

        retained = count >= 8
        group_mean = np.divide(
            total,
            count,
            out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=count > 0,
        )
        direction = np.sign(group_mean)
        same_direction = (np.sign(group_returns) == direction[:, None]) & valid
        concentration = np.divide(
            same_direction.sum(axis=1),
            count,
            out=np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=float),
            where=count > 0,
        )

        peer_count = count[:, None] - valid.astype(int)
        peer_return = np.divide(
            total[:, None] - np.where(valid, group_returns, 0.0),
            peer_count,
            out=np.full_like(group_returns, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=(valid & (peer_count >= 7)),
        )
        loo[:, members] = peer_return

        broad = retained & (direction != 0.0) & (concentration >= 0.75)
        shocked[:, members] = (
            valid
            & broad[:, None]
            & np.isfinite(peer_return)
            & (np.abs(peer_return) >= 0.01)
        )

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(loo, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(shocked, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
    )


def _capped_side_weights(member_codes: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Allocate a side equally within industries, capping each industry at 20%."""
    n_members = member_codes.size
    weights = np.zeros(n_members, dtype=float)
    if n_members == 0:
        return weights

    codes, inverse = np.unique(member_codes, return_inverse=True)
    n_groups = codes.size
    # A 20% industry cap is infeasible with fewer than five represented groups.
    if n_groups < 5:
        return weights

    counts = np.bincount(inverse).astype(float)
    allocation = counts / float(n_members)
    cap = 0.20

    # Water-fill excess equally across industries still below the cap.
    for _ in range(n_groups + 1):
        over = allocation > cap + 1e-12
        if not over.any():
            break
        excess = float((allocation[over] - cap).sum())
        allocation[over] = cap
        recipients = allocation < cap - 1e-12
        if not recipients.any():
            return np.zeros(n_members, dtype=float)
        allocation[recipients] += excess / float(recipients.sum())

    if np.any(allocation > cap + 1e-10) or allocation.sum() <= 0.0:
        return weights

    allocation /= allocation.sum()
    weights = allocation[inverse] / counts[inverse]
    return weights


def _portfolio_from_scores(
    scores: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, industry_codes: np.ndarray
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize candidate underreaction scores and form capped long/short weights."""
    score_values = scores.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    eligible_values = eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool, copy=False)
    output = np.zeros_like(score_values, dtype=float)

    for row in range(score_values.shape[0]):
        mask = eligible_values[row] & np.isfinite(score_values[row])
        positions = np.flatnonzero(mask)
        if positions.size < 5:
            continue

        row_scores = score_values[row, positions]
        lower, upper = np.nanquantile(row_scores, [0.02, 0.98])
        clipped = np.clip(row_scores, lower, upper)
        percentile = pd.Series(clipped).rank(method="average", pct=True).to_numpy()

        long_local = np.flatnonzero(percentile >= 0.80)
        short_local = np.flatnonzero(percentile <= 0.20)
        if long_local.size == 0 or short_local.size == 0:
            continue

        long_positions = positions[long_local]
        short_positions = positions[short_local]
        long_weights = _capped_side_weights(industry_codes[long_positions])
        short_weights = _capped_side_weights(industry_codes[short_positions])

        output[row, long_positions] += long_weights
        output[row, short_positions] -= short_weights

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=scores.index, columns=scores.columns)


@register_factor
class SparseLiquidityIndustryRepricing(BaseFactor):
    """Delayed industry-shock repricing among low-turnover constituents."""

    factor_id = "sparse_liquidity_industry_repricing"
    name = "Sparse-Liquidity Industry Repricing"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Industry-shock underreaction portfolio: after a broad same-direction "
        "industry move, long low-turnover constituents lagging their beta-adjusted "
        "leave-one-out industry return and short low-turnover overreactors, while "
        "excluding idiosyncratic return and volume events."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].astype(float)
        industry = data["industry"]

        valid_close = (close > 0.0) & (close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).where(valid_close)

        valid_turnover = (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0) & (market_cap > 0.0)
        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap).where(valid_turnover)
        average_turnover = turnover.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()

        # Industry is static by contract; labels absent on the first bar are invalid.
        labels = industry.iloc[0].to_numpy(dtype=object, copy=False)
        industry_codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels, sort=False)
        loo, shocked_industry = _industry_leave_one_out(ret, industry_codes)

        lagged_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lagged_loo = loo.shift(1)
        paired = (lagged_ret.notna() & lagged_loo.notna()).astype(float)
        paired_count = paired.rolling(60, min_periods=40).sum()
        covariance = lagged_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(lagged_loo)
        variance = lagged_loo.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(paired_count >= 40)
        beta = beta.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        predicted = beta * loo
        underreaction = predicted - ret
        residual = ret - predicted

        base_eligible = (
            shocked_industry
            & beta.notna()
            & turnover.notna()
            & average_turnover.notna()
            & (residual.abs() <= 0.04)
            & (turnover <= 2.0 * average_turnover)
        )

        eligible_values = base_eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool, copy=True)
        avg_values = average_turnover.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
        for row in range(eligible_values.shape[0]):
            positions = np.flatnonzero(eligible_values[row] & np.isfinite(avg_values[row]))
            if positions.size == 0:
                continue
            cutoff = np.nanquantile(avg_values[row, positions], 0.30)
            eligible_values[row, positions] &= avg_values[row, positions] <= cutoff

        low_liquidity_eligible = pd.DataFrame(
            eligible_values, index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        )
        return _portfolio_from_scores(underreaction, low_liquidity_eligible, industry_codes)
