from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_impulse(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, industry_codes: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal leave-one-out peer returns and broad contemporaneous impulses."""
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    peer_values = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    broad_values = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)

    for code in np.unique(industry_codes[industry_codes >= 0]):
        members = np.flatnonzero(industry_codes == code)
        if members.size < 8:
            continue

        group = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(group)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        total = np.where(valid, group, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        mean = np.divide(
            total,
            count,
            out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=count > 0,
        )
        direction = np.sign(mean)
        concordant = ((np.sign(group) == direction[:, None]) & valid).sum(axis=1)
        breadth = np.divide(
            concordant,
            count,
            out=np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=float),
            where=count > 0,
        )

        peer_count = count[:, None] - valid.astype(int)
        peer = np.divide(
            total[:, None] - np.where(valid, group, 0.0),
            peer_count,
            out=np.full_like(group, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=valid & (peer_count >= 7),
        )
        peer_values[:, members] = peer

        broad = (
            (count >= 8)
            & (direction != 0.0)
            & (breadth >= 0.75)
            & (np.abs(mean) >= 0.006)
        )
        broad_values[:, members] = valid & broad[:, None] & np.isfinite(peer)

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(peer_values, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(broad_values, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
    )


@register_factor
class CashValidatedImpulseDecayBacklog(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_validated_impulse_decay_backlog"
    name = "Cash-Validated Impulse Decay Backlog"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cash-confirmed reporting news is traded in the report direction when a "
        "persistent accelerating peer impulse leaves a beta-adjusted three-bar "
        "response backlog in a low-turnover name whose participation is decaying."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)

        valid_close = (close > 0.0) & (close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).where(valid_close)

        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        event = (
            (eps_actual.notna() & eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1)))
            | (revenue_actual.notna() & revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1)))
        )

        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        cash_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)

        eps_scaled = eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.05)
        revenue_scaled = revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        cash_scaled = cash_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        positive = (eps_scaled > 0.0) & (revenue_scaled > 0.0) & (cash_scaled > 0.0)
        negative = (eps_scaled < 0.0) & (revenue_scaled < 0.0) & (cash_scaled < 0.0)
        report_direction = positive.astype(float) - negative.astype(float)
        event_direction = report_direction.where(event, 0.0)
        recent_direction = np.sign(event_direction.rolling(3, min_periods=1).sum())
        recent_event = event.rolling(3, min_periods=1).max().astype(bool)

        eps_strength = eps_scaled.abs().clip(upper=5.0)
        revenue_strength = revenue_scaled.abs().clip(upper=5.0)
        cash_strength = cash_scaled.abs().clip(upper=5.0)
        conviction = np.minimum(np.minimum(eps_strength, revenue_strength), cash_strength)
        recent_conviction = conviction.where(event).rolling(3, min_periods=1).max()

        labels = data["industry"].reindex_like(close).iloc[0].to_numpy(dtype=object)
        industry_codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels, sort=False)
        peer_return, broad_peer = _leave_one_out_impulse(ret, industry_codes)

        peer_direction = np.sign(peer_return)
        persistent = (
            (peer_direction != 0.0)
            & (peer_direction == peer_direction.shift(1))
            & (peer_direction == peer_direction.shift(2))
        )
        peer_baseline = peer_return.abs().rolling(15, min_periods=10).mean()
        accelerating = (
            (peer_return.abs() >= 1.15 * peer_baseline)
            & (peer_return.abs() >= 0.006)
        )
        propagation = broad_peer & persistent & accelerating

        lagged_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lagged_peer = peer_return.shift(1)
        paired = (lagged_ret.notna() & lagged_peer.notna()).astype(float)
        paired_count = paired.rolling(60, min_periods=40).sum()
        covariance = lagged_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(lagged_peer)
        variance = lagged_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(paired_count >= 40)
        beta = beta.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        cumulative_peer = peer_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        cumulative_ret = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        backlog = beta * cumulative_peer - cumulative_ret
        normalized_backlog = backlog / cumulative_peer.abs().clip(lower=0.008)
        signed_backlog = recent_direction * normalized_backlog.clip(-2.0, 2.0)

        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap).where(
            (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0) & (market_cap > 0.0)
        )
        slow_turnover = turnover.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        recent_turnover = turnover.rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean()
        participation_decay = recent_turnover <= slow_turnover
        liquidity_rank = slow_turnover.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        sparse = liquidity_rank <= 0.35

        aligned = np.sign(peer_return) == recent_direction
        residual = ret - beta * peer_return
        eligible = (
            recent_event
            & (recent_direction != 0.0)
            & (recent_conviction > 0.0)
            & propagation
            & aligned
            & beta.notna()
            & sparse
            & participation_decay
            & (residual.abs() <= 0.04)
        )

        signal = recent_direction * recent_conviction * signed_backlog
        return signal.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Cash-Validated Impulse Decay Backlog
programs.trading_idea: A cash-confirmed earnings surprise makes a firm's directional information credible, while a broad, persistent and accelerating industry impulse indicates that the same information is still propagating through peers. The child targets firms whose own multi-day beta-adjusted response remains behind the cumulative peer move specifically when their trading participation is decaying below normal after the report, a state in which sparse-liquidity price discovery is least able to clear the remaining backlog. Parent A lacks a firm-level credibility anchor and parent B primarily tests contemporaneous quietness; the interaction identifies validated news whose peer transmission persists after issuer-specific attention has faded.
programs.description: The signal measures a three-bar beta-adjusted peer-response backlog following a recent cash-confirmed earnings and revenue surprise, conditional on broad accelerating industry propagation and declining low-turnover participation. It is signed in the validated report direction, so laggards are bought or sold toward the peer-implied response while overreactors receive the opposite sign.

programs.code:
"""Industry-anchored residual liquidation repair after volatility cooling.

Mechanism: broad peer selling establishes a common information shock.  A thin,
financially resilient constituent that falls further than its historical peer beta,
with high range per unit participation but subsequently cooling volatility, is more
likely to be reversing a transient local liquidity displacement than repricing news.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _peer_return_and_shock(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Leave-one-out industry return and broad negative industry shock mask."""
    peer = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    broad = pd.DataFrame(False, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    groups: dict[object, list[str]] = {}
    for ticker, label in labels.items():
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(ticker)

    for members in groups.values():
        if len(members) < 8:
            continue
        x = ret[members]
        valid = x.notna()
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total = x.where(valid).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        industry_ret = total / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        direction = np.sign(industry_ret)
        breadth = x.mul(direction, axis=0).gt(0.0).sum(axis=1) / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        shock = industry_ret.le(-0.01) & breadth.ge(0.70) & count.ge(8.0)

        for ticker in members:
            own_valid = valid[ticker]
            others = count - own_valid.astype(float)
            loo = (total - x[ticker].fillna(0.0)) / others.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            peer[ticker] = loo.where(own_valid & others.ge(7.0))
            broad[ticker] = (shock & own_valid & others.ge(7.0)).fillna(False)

    return peer, broad


def _recent_information_event(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Issuer-level report or consensus changes observed in the previous six bars."""
    fields = [
        "epsActual", "revenueActual", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate", "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    template = data[fields[0]]
    event = pd.DataFrame(False, index=template.index, columns=template.columns)
    for field in fields:
        x = data[field].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        previous = x.shift(1)
        changed = x.notna() & (previous.isna() | x.ne(previous))
        event = event | changed
    return event.rolling(6, min_periods=1).max().fillna(0.0).astype(bool)


def _resilience(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional solvency composite, requiring two independently valid fields."""
    cash = rank(data["cashRatio"].where(data["cashRatio"] >= 0.0))
    debt = rank(-data["debtToCapital"].where(data["debtToCapital"] >= 0.0))
    coverage = rank(data["interestCoverage"].where(data["interestCoverage"] > 0.0))
    count = cash.notna().astype(float) + debt.notna().astype(float) + coverage.notna().astype(float)
    total = cash.fillna(0.0) + debt.fillna(0.0) + coverage.fillna(0.0)
    return (total / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count.ge(2.0))


@register_factor
class IndustryResidualCoolingResilienceRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "industry_residual_cooling_resilience_repair"
    name = "Industry Residual Cooling Resilience Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Longs thin, resilient stocks with an excessive beta-adjusted decline during "
        "a broad industry selloff when high range elasticity is cooling without fresh news."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close", "high", "low", "volume", "marketCap", "industry",
        "cashRatio", "debtToCapital", "interestCoverage", "epsActual",
        "revenueActual", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise", "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        prev = close.shift(1)
        ret = (close / prev - 1.0).where(close.gt(0.0) & prev.gt(0.0))
        labels = data["industry"].ffill().bfill().iloc[-1]
        peer, broad_down = _peer_return_and_shock(ret, labels)

        lag_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lag_peer = peer.shift(1)
        observations = (lag_ret.notna() & lag_peer.notna()).astype(float).rolling(60, min_periods=40).sum()
        covariance = lag_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(lag_peer)
        variance = lag_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(observations.ge(40.0)).clip(0.0, 2.0)
        excess_downside = (beta * peer - ret).clip(lower=0.0)

        dollar_volume = close * volume
        turnover = (dollar_volume / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0) & market_cap.gt(0.0)
        )
        mean_turnover = turnover.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        thin = rank(mean_turnover).le(0.40)
        quiet_participation = turnover.le(2.0 * mean_turnover)

        log_range = np.log(high / low).where(high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0))
        range_base = log_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        participation = dollar_volume / dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        elasticity = (log_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)) / participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        prior_shock_range = log_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().shift(3)
        current_range = log_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        cooling = 1.0 - current_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_excess = (prior_shock_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        recent_industry_selloff = broad_down.rolling(3, min_periods=1).max().astype(bool)

        resilience = _resilience(data)
        no_event = ~_recent_information_event(data)
        eligible = (
            recent_industry_selloff
            & thin
            & quiet_participation
            & beta.notna()
            & excess_downside.gt(0.0)
            & elasticity.notna()
            & elasticity.ge(1.0)
            & range_excess.gt(0.0)
            & cooling.gt(0.0)
            & resilience.notna()
            & no_event
        )
        repair_strength = (
            excess_downside
            * elasticity.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
            * range_excess
            * cooling.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
            * resilience
        ).where(eligible)
        return rank(repair_strength).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Industry Residual Cooling Resilience Repair
programs.trading_idea: A broad industry selloff supplies a common-shock anchor, while a thin constituent whose beta-adjusted decline is materially worse than peers is a candidate for local forced-flow overshoot. The signal activates only after the excess range has begun to cool, participation is not abnormal, and balance-sheet resilience makes a distress interpretation less likely; it also excludes fresh earnings or estimate events. This interaction adds edge because Parent A identifies low-information residual displacement but not whether liquidation has exhausted, whereas Parent B identifies cooling repair but gains a stronger low-confirmation industry-residual filter.
programs.description: Ranks resilient, low-turnover names with a beta-adjusted downside residual during a recent broad industry selloff, requiring elevated range elasticity followed by cooling volatility and no recent issuer-information event. Higher values indicate a more likely six-bar rebound from transient local selling pressure.

programs.code:
"""Following a concordant downside move in an industry's other constituents, a financially fragile and previously illiquid stock that declines less than its own trailing beta implies should face delayed downside adjustment. The distinguishing feature is not a generic industry-downside screen: it is a target-excluded, beta-implied contemporaneous return shortfall, conditioned on liquidity measured before the shock. The factor therefore takes short exposure only where the stock's observed same-day return is materially above its leave-one-out industry-beta-implied return during a broad peer selloff."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_industry_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute contemporaneous target-excluded industry returns and breadth.

    Each row is grouped only by the supplied static industry labels.  Returns
    from ineligible names are excluded before group aggregation, so the target
    is never included in its own benchmark.
    """
    usable_ret = ret.where(eligible)
    group_sum = usable_ret.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    group_count = eligible.astype(float).T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    group_negative = (
        usable_ret.lt(0.0).astype(float).where(eligible, 0.0).T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    )

    peer_count = group_count - 1.0
    loo_return = (group_sum - usable_ret) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    peer_negative_fraction = (
        group_negative - usable_ret.lt(0.0).astype(float)
    ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    valid_peer_set = eligible & peer_count.ge(8.0)
    return (
        loo_return.where(valid_peer_set),
        peer_negative_fraction.where(valid_peer_set),
        peer_count.where(eligible),
    )


def _trailing_beta(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    peer_ret: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal 60-bar beta using paired observations ending at t-1."""
    x = stock_ret.shift(1)
    y = peer_ret.shift(1)
    paired = x.notna() & y.notna()
    x_pair = x.where(paired)
    y_pair = y.where(paired)

    pair_count = paired.astype(float).rolling(60, min_periods=40).sum()
    covariance = x_pair.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(y_pair)
    peer_variance = y_pair.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
    beta = covariance / peer_variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return beta.where(pair_count.ge(40.0))


def _winsorized_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, valid: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally winsorize at 1/99 percent before percentile ranking."""
    masked = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    return clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True)


@register_factor
class FundingFragilityCommonShockLag(BaseFactor):
    """Short delayed downside after a leave-one-out industry funding shock."""

    factor_id = "funding_fragility_common_shock_lag"
    name = "Leave-One-Out Fragility Shock Lag"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks financially fragile, historically illiquid names that lag their "
        "positive-beta leave-one-out industry benchmark during a broad peer "
        "selloff; high scores predict lower subsequent returns."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    expected_sign = -1

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # Industry is static by contract; taking its initial row avoids any
        # dependence on a future bar while retaining the supplied taxonomy.
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0]

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        current_universe = ret.notna() & market_cap.notna() & industry_labels.notna()

        peer_ret, peer_negative_fraction, _ = _leave_one_out_industry_return(
            ret,
            current_universe,
            industry_labels,
        )

        peer_std_prior = peer_ret.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
        beta = _trailing_beta(ret, peer_ret)
        residual = ret - beta * peer_ret

        common_downside = (
            peer_ret.le(-1.5 * peer_std_prior)
            & peer_negative_fraction.ge(0.70)
            & peer_std_prior.notna()
        )
        shock_residual_eligible = (
            current_universe
            & common_downside
            & beta.gt(0.0)
            & residual.gt(0.0)
        )

        # This is exactly the pre-shock [t-20, t-1] liquidity measure.
        dollar_turnover = (close * volume) / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        dollar_turnover = dollar_turnover.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        pre_shock_liquidity = dollar_turnover.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        liquidity_eligible = shock_residual_eligible & pre_shock_liquidity.notna()
        liquidity_rank = pre_shock_liquidity.where(liquidity_eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        illiquidity = 1.0 - liquidity_rank

        debt_to_assets = data["debtToAssets"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        operating_cash_flow_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        fundamental_valid = (
            debt_to_assets.notna()
            & current_ratio.notna()
            & operating_cash_flow_growth.notna()
        )

        debt_rank = _winsorized_rank(debt_to_assets, fundamental_valid)
        current_ratio_rank = _winsorized_rank(current_ratio, fundamental_valid)
        ocf_growth_rank = _winsorized_rank(operating_cash_flow_growth, fundamental_valid)
        fragility = (
            0.40 * debt_rank
            + 0.30 * (1.0 - current_ratio_rank)
            + 0.30 * (1.0 - ocf_growth_rank)
        ).where(fundamental_valid)

        final_eligible = liquidity_eligible & fundamental_valid & fragility.notna()
        residual_rank = residual.where(final_eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        score = (residual_rank * fragility * illiquidity).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        positive_score_eligible = final_eligible & score.gt(0.0)

        # The strategy is inactive unless there are enough names to form a
        # meaningful cross-sectional top decile.
        eligible_count = positive_score_eligible.astype(float).sum(axis=1)
        enough_names = eligible_count.ge(20.0)
        qualified = positive_score_eligible.mul(enough_names.astype(float), axis=0).astype(bool)

        # Retain only the daily top decile.  The portfolio layer can then apply
        # equal short weights and overlap each daily sleeve for six bars.
        selection_rank = score.where(qualified).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        selected = qualified & selection_rank.ge(0.90)
        return score.where(selected, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Leave-One-Out Fragility Shock Lag
programs.trading_idea: Following a concordant downside move in an industry's other constituents, a financially fragile and previously illiquid stock that declines less than its own trailing beta implies should face delayed downside adjustment. The distinguishing feature is not a generic industry-downside screen: it is a target-excluded, beta-implied contemporaneous return shortfall, conditioned on liquidity measured before the shock. The factor therefore takes short exposure only where the stock's observed same-day return is materially above its leave-one-out industry-beta-implied return during a broad peer selloff.
programs.description: At each date t, define the universe as tickers with a non-null static industry label, valid close prices at t and t-1, non-null marketCap, and at least the required trailing observations below. Industry groups use the supplied industry field; no sector substitution is permitted. Let r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. For stock i, define the leave-one-out industry return R_-i,t as the equal-weighted mean of r_j,t over all other eligible tickers j with the same industry label, requiring at least 8 peers. A common downside shock occurs only if (1) R_-i,t is less than or equal to -1.5 times the trailing 60-bar standard deviation of R_-i ending at t-1, computed with at least 40 observations, and (2) at least 70% of those leave-one-out peers have negative returns at t. Estimate beta_i,t using only the 60 daily paired observations ending at t-1: beta_i,t = Cov(r_i,s, R_-i,s) / Var(R_-i,s), requiring at least 40 paired observations and beta_i,t > 0. The contemporaneous underreaction residual is u_i,t = r_i,t - beta_i,t * R_-i,t; only u_i,t > 0 is eligible, because a positive residual means the stock fell less than its beta-implied response to the negative peer shock. Liquidity is measured strictly before the shock as median_s in [t-20,t-1] of (close_i,s * volume_i,s / marketCap_i,s), requiring 15 valid observations; its illiquidity component is the inverse cross-sectional percentile rank of this measure among eligible names. Financial fragility uses debtToAssets, currentRatio, and operatingCashFlowGrowth as point-in-time quarterly fields available at t. For each field, winsorize cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles among names with all three inputs, convert to percentile ranks, and calculate Fragility_i,t = 0.40*rank(debtToAssets) + 0.30*(1-rank(currentRatio)) + 0.30*(1-rank(operatingCashFlowGrowth)). The final score is rank(u_i,t) * Fragility_i,t * Illiquidity_i,t, where rank(u_i,t) is the percentile rank among names satisfying the same-day shock, positive-residual, beta, and data requirements. At the close of t the score is formed using information through t only; trades occur no earlier than the open of t+1. Each day, short the equal-weighted top decile of eligible positive scores, with no position if fewer than 20 names qualify; hold each daily sleeve for exactly 6 subsequent bars, creating overlapping daily-rebalanced sleeves. A higher score predicts lower subsequent return, so expected_sign is -1.

programs.code:
"""Polarity-sorted repair of sparse constituents during coherent industry shocks.

Mechanism: a low-turnover residual opposite a verified common industry move is
an incomplete diffusion of that move, while a residual in the same direction is
more likely an uncorroborated idiosyncratic overshoot.  Sorting residuals by
this polarity selects continuation versus reversion rather than assuming that
all common-mode residuals have the same repair direction.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_mode_stats(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Contemporaneous leave-one-out industry mode, breadth, and dispersion."""
    index = ret.index
    columns = ret.columns
    common = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)
    dispersion = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)

    usable = labels.dropna()
    for label in pd.unique(usable):
        members = list(usable[usable == label].index)
        if len(members) < 8:
            continue
        group = ret[members]
        valid = group.notna()
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total = group.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
        total_sq = (group.fillna(0.0) ** 2).sum(axis=1)

        for column in members:
            own_valid = valid[column]
            peer_count = count - own_valid.astype(float)
            eligible = own_valid & peer_count.ge(7.0)
            own = group[column].fillna(0.0)
            peer_sum = total - own
            peer_mean = (peer_sum / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(eligible)
            common[column] = peer_mean

            matching = (
                np.sign(group).eq(np.sign(peer_mean), axis=0) & valid
            ).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            own_matching = (
                np.sign(group[column]).eq(np.sign(peer_mean)) & own_valid
            ).astype(float)
            breadth[column] = (
                (matching - own_matching) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            ).where(eligible)

            peer_sq = total_sq - own * own
            variance = (
                peer_sq - peer_sum * peer_sum / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            ) / (peer_count - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            dispersion[column] = np.sqrt(variance.clip(lower=0.0)).where(eligible)

    return common, breadth, dispersion


@register_factor
class PolaritySortedCommonModeImpedance(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "polarity_sorted_common_mode_impedance"
    name = "Polarity-Sorted Common-Mode Impedance"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "During coherent industry shocks, quiet sparse names with residuals "
        "opposing the mode are traded as catch-ups, while residuals reinforcing "
        "the mode are traded as low-participation overshoot fades."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].astype(float)
        labels = data["industry"].ffill().iloc[-1]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_price = close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0)
        ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).where(valid_price)
        common, breadth, dispersion = _industry_mode_stats(ret, labels)

        hist_ret = ret.shift(1)
        hist_common = common.shift(1)
        covariance = hist_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(hist_common)
        variance = hist_common.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 3.0)
        residual = ret - beta * common
        residual_scale = residual.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=25).std()
        z_residual = (residual / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        valid_turnover = close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0) & market_cap.gt(0.0)
        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap).where(valid_turnover)
        normal_turnover = turnover.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        quiet = turnover.le(normal_turnover)
        sparse_cutoff = normal_turnover.quantile(0.40, axis=1)
        structurally_sparse = normal_turnover.le(sparse_cutoff, axis=0)

        historical_dispersion = dispersion.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=25).median()
        historical_mode_vol = common.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=25).std()
        coherent = (
            common.abs().gt(historical_mode_vol)
            & breadth.ge(0.70)
            & dispersion.le(historical_dispersion)
        )
        active = (
            valid_price
            & coherent
            & beta.notna()
            & z_residual.notna()
            & quiet
            & structurally_sparse
        )

        opposing_mode = (residual * common).lt(0.0)
        catchup = -np.sign(common) * z_residual
        fade = -z_residual
        raw_signal = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(opposing_mode, catchup, fade),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        signal = raw_signal.where(active).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return signal.where(active, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Polarity-Sorted Common-Mode Impedance
programs.trading_idea: A coherent, broad industry move is a common-information state, but a sparse constituent can either be a delayed follower or an idiosyncratic overshooter. The child separates these cases by residual polarity: a residual opposing the industry mode is treated as an underreaction and traded toward the mode, whereas a residual reinforcing the mode is treated as an uncorroborated low-turnover overshoot and faded. This interaction carries edge beyond either parent because residual magnitude alone cannot distinguish delayed common-shock diffusion from transient idiosyncratic displacement; the residual's sign relative to the verified common mode identifies which repair mechanism should dominate.
programs.description: Within broad, low-dispersion industry shocks, estimates each stock's pre-estimated-beta residual versus a leave-one-out industry return. Quiet, structurally low-turnover names are scored as mode catch-ups when the residual opposes the mode and as residual fades when it reinforces the mode.

programs.code:
"""Condition industry-shock completion on liquidity elasticity.

Mechanism: low-turnover names can incorporate broad peer shocks gradually when
price movement is orderly, but a large residual range move on ordinary volume is
more consistent with a transient low-confirmation displacement and should fade.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _peer_returns_and_shocks(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal leave-one-out peer returns and broad industry-shock flags."""
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    peer_out = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    shock_out = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)

    for code in np.unique(codes[codes >= 0]):
        members = np.flatnonzero(codes == code)
        if members.size < 8:
            continue
        block = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(block)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        total = np.where(valid, block, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        industry_ret = np.divide(
            total,
            count,
            out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=count > 0,
        )
        industry_series = pd.Series(industry_ret, index=ret.index)
        threshold = industry_series.abs().shift(1).rolling(
            60, min_periods=45
        ).quantile(0.90).to_numpy()
        direction = np.sign(industry_ret)
        concordant = ((np.sign(block) == direction[:, None]) & valid).sum(axis=1)
        breadth = np.divide(
            concordant,
            count,
            out=np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=float),
            where=count > 0,
        )
        broad = (
            (count >= 8)
            & np.isfinite(threshold)
            & (np.abs(industry_ret) >= threshold)
            & (breadth >= 0.65)
            & (direction != 0.0)
        )

        peers = count[:, None] - valid.astype(int)
        peer_ret = np.divide(
            total[:, None] - np.where(valid, block, 0.0),
            peers,
            out=np.full_like(block, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=valid & (peers >= 7),
        )
        peer_out[:, members] = peer_ret
        shock_out[:, members] = valid & broad[:, None] & np.isfinite(peer_ret)

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(peer_out, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(shock_out, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
    )


def _recent_information_event(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Detect point-in-time report, surprise, and consensus changes."""
    fields = [
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    event = pd.DataFrame(False, index=data[fields[0]].index, columns=data[fields[0]].columns)
    for field in fields:
        value = data[field].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        previous = value.shift(1)
        event = event | (value.notna() & (previous.isna() | value.ne(previous)))
    return event.rolling(6, min_periods=1).max().fillna(0.0).astype(bool)


@register_factor
class SparseElasticityRegimeIndustryCompletion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sparse_elasticity_regime_industry_completion"
    name = "Sparse Elasticity Industry Completion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Conditionally completes beta-adjusted industry underreaction in thin, "
        "orderly names and fades thin-name residual overshoots with elevated "
        "range elasticity after broad industry shocks."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)

        valid_close = close.gt(0.0) & close.shift(1).gt(0.0)
        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).where(valid_close)

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].to_numpy(dtype=object, copy=False)
        codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels, sort=False)
        peer, shocked = _peer_returns_and_shocks(ret, codes)

        lag_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lag_peer = peer.shift(1)
        paired = lag_ret.notna() & lag_peer.notna()
        pair_count = paired.astype(float).rolling(60, min_periods=45).sum()
        covariance = lag_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=45).cov(lag_peer)
        variance = lag_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=45).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(pair_count >= 45)
        beta = beta.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        predicted = beta * peer
        residual = ret - predicted
        underreaction = predicted - ret
        residual_scale = residual.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=30).std()
        standardized_gap = (underreaction / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        standardized_fade = (-residual / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        prior_dollar_median = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        participation = dollar_volume / prior_dollar_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        turnover = (dollar_volume / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(market_cap.gt(0.0))
        average_turnover = turnover.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        turnover_rank = average_turnover.rank(axis=1, pct=True, method="average")

        log_range = np.log(high / low).where(high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0))
        prior_range = log_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        elasticity = (
            (log_range / prior_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
            / participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0)

        recent_event = _recent_information_event(data)
        common = (
            shocked
            & beta.notna()
            & residual_scale.notna()
            & turnover_rank.notna()
            & elasticity.notna()
            & participation.notna()
            & turnover_rank.le(0.35)
            & ~recent_event
        )

        orderly_laggard = common & elasticity.le(1.35) & participation.le(1.75)
        elastic_overshoot = (
            common
            & elasticity.ge(1.50)
            & participation.ge(0.50)
            & participation.le(1.30)
        )

        raw_signal = standardized_gap.where(orderly_laggard)
        raw_signal = raw_signal.where(~elastic_overshoot, standardized_fade)
        active = orderly_laggard | elastic_overshoot
        centered = raw_signal.sub(raw_signal.where(active).mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return centered.where(active, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Sparse Elasticity Industry Completion
programs.trading_idea: Broad industry shocks propagate differently through thin names depending on whether the stock-specific displacement looks like orderly delayed incorporation or a low-confirmation price overshoot. Low-turnover laggards with ordinary range elasticity should continue toward their beta-implied peer move because sparse arbitrage capacity delays common-shock transmission; in contrast, low-turnover names with an unusually large range despite normal participation should reverse because their residual move is more likely transient inventory or quote-dislocation pressure. The interaction creates edge because liquidity alone cannot distinguish a delayed follower from a temporary overshooter, while range elasticity alone does not identify the names in which common-shock convergence is slow.
programs.description: After a broad leave-one-out industry shock, the factor uses trailing peer beta residuals and turnover to identify thin names, then conditionally trades beta-adjusted underreaction when range elasticity is orderly and fades residual overshoot when elasticity is elevated. Recent earnings and estimate-update names are excluded so that issuer-specific information is not mistaken for a mechanical dislocation.

programs.code:
"""Industry-anchored repair of transient downside overshoots in thin names.

Mechanism: a broad industry selloff establishes a peer-implied fundamental price
move, while sparse liquidity can make a constituent's local forced selling exceed
that anchor.  A cooling range shock and financial resilience identify cases where
the excess idiosyncratic pressure has likely exhausted rather than revealed distress.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_industry_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return causal peer return and broad-negative-industry eligibility."""
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    peer = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    broad_down = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)

    for code in np.unique(codes[codes >= 0]):
        members = np.flatnonzero(codes == code)
        if members.size < 8:
            continue
        x = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(x)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        total = np.where(valid, x, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        group_mean = np.divide(
            total, count, out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan), where=count > 0
        )
        direction = np.sign(group_mean)
        same_sign = (np.sign(x) == direction[:, None]) & valid
        concentration = np.divide(
            same_sign.sum(axis=1), count,
            out=np.zeros(n_rows), where=count > 0
        )
        peer_count = count[:, None] - valid.astype(int)
        loo = np.divide(
            total[:, None] - np.where(valid, x, 0.0),
            peer_count,
            out=np.full_like(x, np.nan),
            where=valid & (peer_count >= 7),
        )
        peer[:, members] = loo
        broad = (
            (count >= 8)
            & (group_mean <= -0.01)
            & (concentration >= 0.75)
        )
        broad_down[:, members] = valid & broad[:, None] & np.isfinite(loo)

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(peer, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(broad_down, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
    )


def _downside_cooling(
    close: pd.DataFrame, high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Completed downside shock, its excess range, and subsequent cooling."""
    prev = close.shift(1)
    valid = (close > 0.0) & (prev > 0.0) & high.notna() & low.notna()
    ret = (close / prev - 1.0).where(valid)
    bar_range = ((high - low) / prev).where(valid)

    completed_down = (-ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().shift(3)).clip(lower=0.0)
    shock_range = bar_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().shift(3)
    baseline = bar_range.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(6)
    current_range = bar_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
    excess_range = (shock_range / baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0)
    cooling = 1.0 - current_range / baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return completed_down, excess_range, cooling


def _resilience(
    cash_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_capital: pd.DataFrame,
    interest_coverage: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional resilience composite requiring at least two valid inputs."""
    cash = rank(cash_ratio)
    debt = rank(-debt_to_capital)
    coverage = rank(interest_coverage.where(interest_coverage > 0.0))
    total = cash.fillna(0.0) + debt.fillna(0.0) + coverage.fillna(0.0)
    count = cash.notna().astype(float) + debt.notna().astype(float) + coverage.notna().astype(float)
    return (total / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count >= 2.0)


@register_factor
class IndustryAnchoredThinnameCoolingRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "industry_anchored_thinname_cooling_repair"
    name = "Industry-Anchored Thin-Name Cooling Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks low-turnover stocks whose downside return exceeds a broad negative "
        "leave-one-out industry shock after local volatility cools and resilience "
        "supports repair, versus fragile unresolved excess-selling cases."
    )
    window_length = 70
    inputs = [
        "close", "high", "low", "volume", "marketCap", "industry",
        "cashRatio", "debtToCapital", "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].astype(float)
        prev = close.shift(1)
        ret = (close / prev - 1.0).where((close > 0.0) & (prev > 0.0))

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].to_numpy(dtype=object, copy=False)
        codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels, sort=False)
        peer_ret, broad_down = _leave_one_out_industry_return(ret, codes)

        lagged_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lagged_peer = peer_ret.shift(1)
        pair_count = (lagged_ret.notna() & lagged_peer.notna()).astype(float).rolling(60, min_periods=40).sum()
        cov = lagged_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(lagged_peer)
        var = lagged_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (cov / var.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(pair_count >= 40.0).clip(0.0, 2.0)
        excess_downside = (beta * peer_ret - ret).clip(lower=0.0)

        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0) & (market_cap > 0.0)
        )
        average_turnover = turnover.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        thin = rank(average_turnover) <= 0.35
        quiet_volume = turnover <= 2.0 * average_turnover

        shock_down, range_excess, cooling = _downside_cooling(
            close, data["high"].astype(float), data["low"].astype(float)
        )
        resilience = _resilience(
            data["cashRatio"].astype(float),
            data["debtToCapital"].astype(float),
            data["interestCoverage"].astype(float),
        )

        eligible = (
            broad_down & thin & quiet_volume & beta.notna()
            & excess_downside.notna() & (excess_downside > 0.0)
            & (shock_down > 0.0) & (range_excess > 0.0) & resilience.notna()
        )
        repair = (excess_downside * shock_down * range_excess * cooling.clip(lower=0.0) * resilience).where(eligible)
        unresolved = (
            excess_downside * shock_down * range_excess
            * (-cooling).clip(lower=0.0) * (1.0 - resilience)
        ).where(eligible)

        return (rank(repair) - rank(unresolved)).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Industry-Anchored Thin-Name Cooling Repair
programs.trading_idea: A thinly traded constituent can suffer an excessive downside move when a broad industry selloff coincides with transient local order-flow pressure: sparse liquidity slows arbitrage back toward the economically relevant peer-implied return. The child only buys residual selloffs that exceed the leave-one-out industry move after their range shock is cooling and the issuer has sufficient balance-sheet resilience, distinguishing temporary forced-flow overshoot from genuine distress. Parent A supplies the peer-information anchor and turnover constraint, while Parent B supplies evidence that the idiosyncratic downside-pressure component has already exhausted; neither alone separates excess local liquidation from a valid common-shock repricing.
programs.description: After a broad negative leave-one-out industry shock, the factor identifies low-turnover constituents whose beta-adjusted return is excessively negative versus peers. It ranks resilient names with a completed downside-range shock that is cooling against fragile names whose excess selloff remains volatility-persistent.

programs.code:
"""Fragile quiet industry-selloff completion factor.

Mechanism: broad peer selloffs should propagate with delay to financially fragile,
thinly traded constituents when those constituents underreact without an
idiosyncratic volume event.  Quiet trading distinguishes constrained price
discovery from a firm-specific information shock.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_peer_state(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Target-excluded peer return, negative breadth, and peer count."""
    usable = ret.where(eligible)
    group_sum = usable.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    group_count = eligible.astype(float).T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    negative_count = (
        usable.lt(0.0).astype(float).where(eligible, 0.0).T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    )
    peer_count = group_count - 1.0
    loo = (group_sum - usable) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    peer_negative_fraction = (
        negative_count - usable.lt(0.0).astype(float)
    ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    valid = eligible & peer_count.ge(8.0)
    return loo.where(valid), peer_negative_fraction.where(valid), peer_count.where(eligible)


def _prior_beta(stock_ret: pd.DataFrame, peer_ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing 60-bar beta ending at t-1, avoiding shock-date leakage."""
    y = stock_ret.shift(1)
    x = peer_ret.shift(1)
    paired = y.notna() & x.notna()
    y = y.where(paired)
    x = x.where(paired)
    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(60, min_periods=40).sum()
    cov = y.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(x)
    var = x.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
    return (cov / var.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count.ge(40.0))


def _cross_section_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, valid: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Finite, lightly winsorized cross-sectional percentile rank."""
    masked = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


@register_factor
class FragileQuietPeerSelloffCompletion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "fragile_quiet_peer_selloff_completion"
    name = "Fragile Quiet Selloff Completion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks financially fragile and persistently illiquid constituents that "
        "quietly underdecline their leave-one-out industry beta benchmark during "
        "a broad peer selloff; high values predict delayed downside completion."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    expected_sign = -1

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0]

        prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        universe = ret.notna() & market_cap.gt(0.0) & labels.notna()
        peer_ret, peer_negative_fraction, _ = _leave_one_out_peer_state(ret, universe, labels)

        peer_std = peer_ret.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
        beta = _prior_beta(ret, peer_ret).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.5)
        predicted = beta * peer_ret
        residual = ret - predicted
        broad_selloff = (
            peer_ret.le(-1.25 * peer_std)
            & peer_negative_fraction.ge(0.75)
            & peer_std.notna()
        )

        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        prior_turnover = turnover.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        quiet_trading = turnover.le(2.0 * prior_turnover)

        debt = data["debtToAssets"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ocf_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        fundamental_valid = debt.notna() & current_ratio.notna() & ocf_growth.notna()
        debt_rank = _cross_section_rank(debt, fundamental_valid)
        liquidity_rank = _cross_section_rank(current_ratio, fundamental_valid)
        cashflow_rank = _cross_section_rank(ocf_growth, fundamental_valid)
        fragility = (
            0.45 * debt_rank
            + 0.30 * (1.0 - liquidity_rank)
            + 0.25 * (1.0 - cashflow_rank)
        ).where(fundamental_valid)

        event_eligible = (
            universe
            & broad_selloff
            & beta.gt(0.0)
            & residual.gt(0.0)
            & prior_turnover.notna()
            & quiet_trading
            & fundamental_valid
        )
        turnover_rank = prior_turnover.where(event_eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        thin_and_quiet = event_eligible & turnover_rank.le(0.35)

        residual_rank = residual.where(thin_and_quiet).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        score = (residual_rank * fragility * (1.0 - turnover_rank)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        valid_score = thin_and_quiet & score.gt(0.0)
        enough_names = valid_score.astype(float).sum(axis=1).ge(15.0)
        qualified = valid_score.mul(enough_names.astype(float), axis=0).astype(bool)
        selection_rank = score.where(qualified).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        selected = qualified & selection_rank.ge(0.80)
        return score.where(selected, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A broad industry selloff is incorporated slowly when a financially fragile constituent is both structurally illiquid and unusually quiet in its own trading, indicating that the apparent resilience is not firm-specific informed demand. Financial fragility makes the peer shock more relevant because funding-sensitive firms have less capacity to absorb sector-wide risk repricing, while low turnover prevents arbitrageurs from immediately closing the beta-implied downside gap. Parent A identifies fragile underdecliners but can confuse firm-specific volume-driven information with delayed repricing; Parent B identifies quiet illiquid laggards but does not isolate the asymmetric downside susceptibility created by weak balance sheets.
programs.description: After a broad leave-one-out industry selloff, the factor selects financially fragile, low-turnover names whose return is above their trailing-beta-implied peer return, provided their current turnover is not unusually elevated. programs.code:
"""A broad industry-wide price shock can create short-lived cross-sectional dislocations when individual names move substantially more or less than their historically estimated exposure to the industry move. The signal does not interpret OHLCV range as identified dealer depth or prove forced ETF flow; instead, it treats an unusually large idiosyncratic residual accompanied by elevated range but unexceptional participation as a low-confirmation price displacement. Such residual dislocations are expected to partially reverse after the industry shock, unless a recent earnings or estimate update provides issuer-specific information."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _recent_information_event(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag report or estimate fields whose point-in-time value changes today."""
    fields = [
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    event = pd.DataFrame(False, index=data[fields[0]].index, columns=data[fields[0]].columns)
    for field in fields:
        value = data[field].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        previous = value.shift(1)
        changed = value.notna() & (previous.isna() | value.ne(previous))
        event = event | changed
    return event.rolling(6, min_periods=1).max().fillna(0.0).astype(bool)


def _industry_peer_panel(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, dict[object, pd.DataFrame]]:
    """Construct causal daily industry and leave-one-out equal-weight returns."""
    peer = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    shocks: dict[object, pd.DataFrame] = {}

    groups: dict[object, list[str]] = {}
    for ticker, label in labels.items():
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(ticker)

    for label, columns in groups.items():
        group_ret = ret[columns]
        valid = eligible[columns] & group_ret.notna()
        masked_ret = group_ret.where(valid)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        total = masked_ret.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        industry_ret = total / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        history_threshold = (
            industry_ret.abs().shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=45).quantile(0.90)
        )
        direction = np.sign(industry_ret)
        same_direction = masked_ret.mul(direction, axis=0).gt(0.0).sum(axis=1)
        breadth = same_direction / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        industry_shock = (
            industry_ret.abs().gt(history_threshold)
            & breadth.ge(0.60)
            & direction.ne(0.0)
        )
        shocks[label] = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(industry_shock.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )

        for ticker in columns:
            own_valid = valid[ticker]
            others = count - own_valid.astype(float)
            peer_value = (total - masked_ret[ticker].fillna(0.0)) / others.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            peer[ticker] = peer_value.where(own_valid & others.gt(0.0))
            peer_count[ticker] = others.where(own_valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

    return peer, peer_count, shocks


def _trailing_peer_beta(ret: pd.DataFrame, peer: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Estimate each stock's beta on its leave-one-out peer return using completed days."""
    paired_ret = ret.where(ret.notna() & peer.notna()).shift(1)
    paired_peer = peer.where(ret.notna() & peer.notna()).shift(1)
    paired_count = paired_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=45).count()
    covariance = paired_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=45).cov(paired_peer)
    variance = paired_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=45).var()
    beta = covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return beta.where(paired_count.ge(45) & variance.gt(0.0))


@register_factor
class IndustryLiquidityElasticityOvershootUnwind(BaseFactor):
    """Fade low-participation, high-range residual overshoots after industry shocks."""

    factor_id = "industry_liquidity_elasticity_overshoot_unwind"
    name = "Beta-Residual Low-Participation Industry Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Six-bar overlapping industry-neutral reversal sleeves formed from stock-specific "
        "leave-one-out peer-beta residuals after broad industry shocks, restricted to "
        "high-range but normal-participation dislocations without recent information events."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        ret = close.pct_change()
        dollar_volume = (close * volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        prior_dollar_median = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        prior_return_count = ret.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=45).count()

        valid_bar = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & high.gt(0.0)
            & low.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
        )
        eligible = (
            valid_bar
            & close.ge(5.0)
            & prior_dollar_median.ge(5_000_000.0)
            & prior_return_count.ge(45)
        )

        # Industry is static by construction; ffill/bfill merely tolerates sparse label storage.
        industry_frame = data["industry"].ffill().bfill()
        labels = industry_frame.iloc[-1]
        peer, peer_count, shock_by_industry = _industry_peer_panel(ret, eligible, labels)
        beta = _trailing_peer_beta(ret, peer)
        residual = ret - beta * peer

        participation = dollar_volume / prior_dollar_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        log_range = np.log(high / low)
        prior_range_median = log_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        elasticity = (log_range / prior_range_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)) / participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        elasticity = elasticity.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        mean_participation = participation.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()

        recent_event = _recent_information_event(data)
        base = (
            eligible
            & peer_count.ge(8.0)
            & beta.notna()
            & residual.notna()
            & elasticity.notna()
            & ~recent_event
            & participation.le(2.0)
            & mean_participation.le(1.5)
        )

        masked_residual = residual.where(base)
        lower = masked_residual.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = masked_residual.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized_residual = masked_residual.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        elasticity_rank = elasticity.where(base).rank(axis=1, pct=True, method="average")

        shocked = pd.DataFrame(False, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for label, shock in shock_by_industry.items():
            columns = [ticker for ticker, ticker_label in labels.items() if ticker_label == label]
            if columns:
                shocked.loc[:, columns] = shock.loc[:, columns]

        retained = (
            base
            & shocked
            & elasticity_rank.ge(0.80)
            & participation.ge(0.50)
            & participation.le(1.25)
        )

        vintage = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        groups: dict[object, list[str]] = {}
        for ticker, label in labels.items():
            if pd.notna(label):
                groups.setdefault(label, []).append(ticker)

        for timestamp in close.index:
            sleeves: list[tuple[list[str], list[str]]] = []
            for columns in groups.values():
                members = retained.loc[timestamp, columns]
                selected = members.index[members].tolist()
                if len(selected) < 10:
                    continue
                ranked = winsorized_residual.loc[timestamp, selected].rank(pct=True, method="average")
                longs = ranked.index[ranked.le(0.20)].tolist()
                shorts = ranked.index[ranked.ge(0.80)].tolist()
                if longs and shorts:
                    sleeves.append((longs, shorts))

            if sleeves:
                sleeve_weight = 1.0 / len(sleeves)
                for longs, shorts in sleeves:
                    vintage.loc[timestamp, longs] = sleeve_weight / len(longs)
                    vintage.loc[timestamp, shorts] = -sleeve_weight / len(shorts)

        # Each daily formation sleeve remains active for six daily bars; this is the
        # equal-capital average of the currently active overlapping vintages.
        combined = vintage.rolling(6, min_periods=1).mean()
        return combined.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A broad industry-wide price shock can create short-lived cross-sectional dislocations when individual names move substantially more or less than their historically estimated exposure to the industry move. The signal does not interpret OHLCV range as identified dealer depth or prove forced ETF flow; instead, it treats an unusually large idiosyncratic residual accompanied by elevated range but unexceptional participation as a low-confirmation price displacement. Such residual dislocations are expected to partially reverse after the industry shock, unless a recent earnings or estimate update provides issuer-specific information.
programs.description: All inputs at decision date t use completed daily bars through t only; orders are submitted no earlier than the next eligible bar open at t+1. Define close-to-close return r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. The eligible universe at t contains stocks with valid positive close, high, low, and volume at t; close_i,t >= 5 USD; median(close_i,s * volume_i,s) over s=t-20,...,t-1 >= 5,000,000 USD; and at least 45 valid daily returns during t-60,...,t-1. Industry is the static data['industry'] label. For every industry g and day s, compute the equal-weight industry return R_g,s from all valid eligible constituent returns. For stock i, use the leave-one-out peer return R_-i,s, equal-weighted across valid members of i's industry excluding i; require at least 8 peers on the current day and at least 45 paired observations in the trailing 60 completed days. Estimate beta_i,t = cov(r_i,s,R_-i,s)/var(R_-i,s) over paired observations s=t-60,...,t-1, with beta set missing if the peer-return variance is zero. Current residual is e_i,t = r_i,t - beta_i,t * R_-i,t. An industry is in shock only when (1) abs(R_g,t) exceeds its own trailing 60-day 90th percentile of abs(R_g,s), using at least 45 valid historical industry-return observations, and (2) at least 60% of valid industry constituents have returns with the same sign as R_g,t. Define dollar volume DV_i,t = close_i,t * volume_i,t, participation P_i,t = DV_i,t / median(DV_i,s) for s=t-20,...,t-1, and range expansion Q_i,t = log(high_i,t/low_i,t) / median(log(high_i,s/low_i,s)) for s=t-20,...,t-1; require positive finite denominators. The low-confirmation elasticity proxy is L_i,t = Q_i,t / P_i,t, clipped to [0,5]. This is explicitly a range-versus-participation diagnostic, not a claim that daily OHLCV measures displayed depth or signed-flow price impact. Define an information-event flag J_i,t when any of epsActual, revenueActual, epsSurprise, revenueSurprise, epsEstimate, or revenueEstimate is non-null at t and either was null at t-1 or differs from its value at t-1. Exclude a stock if J_i,u occurred on any u in t-5,...,t. Also exclude stocks with P_i,t > 2.0 or with mean(P_i,t-2,...,t) > 1.5, thereby removing one-day and sustained abnormal-participation moves. On each date, winsorize e_i,t at the 1st and 99th percentiles across all remaining eligible stocks and rank L_i,t cross-sectionally; retain only stocks in shocked industries with L rank at or above the 80th percentile and 0.5 <= P_i,t <= 1.25. Within each qualifying industry containing at least 10 retained stocks, rank winsorized residuals within that industry: buy the lowest residual quintile and short the highest residual quintile, equal-weighting names within each side and scaling each industry sleeve to equal long and short gross exposure. Equal-weight qualifying industry sleeves so no one industry dominates. Recompute after every completed close and hold each sleeve for six daily bars using overlapping vintages. This differs implementation-wise from a sector-return residual repair or generic participation-normalized impact recoil because the return benchmark is a rolling 60-day, leave-one-out, stock-specific peer-beta model rather than a contemporaneous sector residual; an explicit own-history industry-shock threshold plus same-sign breadth condition is required; and the trade universe is restricted to low-participation, high-range residuals while excluding both current and sustained abnormal-volume moves and recent report/estimate changes. Incremental exposure-neutralized testing against the named book factors is required before production use.

"""Industry catch-up after a disclosure-silent thin idiosyncratic countershock.

A low-turnover constituent that moves sharply against a broad industry impulse on
little participation can be temporarily displaced by sparse liquidity.  The
industry move supplies the directional anchor while the idiosyncratic impact
signature identifies a reversible, non-disclosure-driven obstruction to price
discovery.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


_DISCLOSURE_FIELDS = [
    "epsActual",
    "revenueActual",
    "epsEstimate",
    "revenueEstimate",
]


def _industry_loo_and_breadth(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Leave-one-out industry return and broad same-direction shock flag."""
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    loo_values = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    broad_values = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(ret.columns), sort=False)

    for code in np.unique(codes[codes >= 0]):
        members = np.flatnonzero(codes == code)
        if members.size < 8:
            continue
        group = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(group)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        total = np.where(valid, group, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        mean_ret = np.divide(
            total, count, out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan), where=count > 0
        )
        direction = np.sign(mean_ret)
        concordant = ((np.sign(group) == direction[:, None]) & valid).sum(axis=1)
        breadth = np.divide(
            concordant, count, out=np.zeros(n_rows), where=count > 0
        )
        peers = count[:, None] - valid.astype(int)
        peer_ret = np.divide(
            total[:, None] - np.where(valid, group, 0.0),
            peers,
            out=np.full_like(group, np.nan),
            where=valid & (peers >= 7),
        )
        is_broad = (
            (count >= 8)
            & (direction != 0.0)
            & (breadth >= 0.75)
            & (np.abs(mean_ret) >= 0.01)
        )
        loo_values[:, members] = peer_ret
        broad_values[:, members] = valid & is_broad[:, None]

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(loo_values, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(broad_values, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
    )


def _disclosure_silent(
    data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], index: pd.Index, columns: pd.Index
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """No selected point-in-time reporting-field update in the past six bars."""
    changed_recently = pd.DataFrame(False, index=index, columns=columns)
    for field in _DISCLOSURE_FIELDS:
        values = data[field].reindex(index=index, columns=columns)
        values = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        changed = values.notna() & (values.shift(1).isna() | values.ne(values.shift(1)))
        changed_recently = changed_recently | (
            changed.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum() > 0.0
        )
    return ~changed_recently


@register_factor
class SilentThinCountershockIndustryCatchup(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "silent_thin_countershock_industry_catchup"
    name = "Silent Thin Countershock Industry Catchup"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Targets low-turnover names with a disclosure-silent, high-impact residual "
        "move opposite a broad beta-adjusted industry shock; score points toward "
        "the implied industry catch-up direction."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).astype(float)

        prev_close = close.shift(1)
        ret = (close / prev_close - 1.0).where(
            (close > 0.0) & (prev_close > 0.0)
        )
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0]
        loo, broad = _industry_loo_and_breadth(ret, labels)

        lag_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lag_loo = loo.shift(1)
        beta = lag_ret.rolling(50, min_periods=30).cov(lag_loo) / lag_loo.rolling(
            50, min_periods=30
        ).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = beta.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
        predicted = beta * loo
        residual = ret - predicted
        countershock = (residual * predicted) < 0.0

        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap).where(
            (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0) & (market_cap > 0.0)
        )
        avg_turnover = turnover.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        low_turnover = rank(-avg_turnover) >= 0.70

        prior_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0).shift(1)
        median_volume = prior_volume.rolling(40, min_periods=25).median()
        relative_volume = volume / median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        normalized_range = ((high - low) / prev_close).where(
            (prev_close > 0.0) & (high >= low)
        )
        impact = normalized_range / relative_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        high_impact = rank(impact) >= 0.80
        low_participation = relative_volume <= 1.0

        endpoint = (
            np.sign(residual)
            * (2.0 * close - high - low)
            / (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        extreme_residual = rank(residual.abs()) >= 0.80
        silent = _disclosure_silent(data, close.index, close.columns)

        qualifies = (
            broad
            & beta.notna()
            & countershock
            & low_turnover
            & low_participation
            & high_impact
            & extreme_residual
            & (endpoint >= 0.50)
            & silent
        )
        gap_strength = rank((predicted - ret).abs())
        score = np.sign(predicted) * gap_strength * impact.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return score.where(qualifies, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: A broad industry shock creates a directional common-value anchor, but a low-turnover constituent can temporarily move against that anchor when a disclosure-silent, low-participation liquidity vacuum produces disproportionate idiosyncratic impact. The child buys names with an upward industry impulse but a thin, downward idiosyncratic displacement, and shorts the symmetric case. Parent A alone treats idiosyncratic moves mainly as exclusions, while Parent B alone reverses an idiosyncratic impact shock without knowing its economically correct destination; their interaction identifies repair episodes whose reversal is reinforced by delayed industry-level information diffusion.

The signed signal points toward the industry-implied price level, with larger industry-versus-stock gaps receiving stronger scores.
