from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_industry(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    loo_values = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    broad_values = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)

    for code in np.unique(codes[codes >= 0]):
        members = np.flatnonzero(codes == code)
        if members.size < 6:
            continue

        group = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(group)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        total = np.where(valid, group, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        mean = np.divide(
            total,
            count,
            out=np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=count > 0,
        )
        direction = np.sign(mean)
        concordant = ((np.sign(group) == direction[:, None]) & valid).sum(axis=1)
        breadth = np.divide(
            concordant,
            count,
            out=np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=float),
            where=count > 0,
        )

        peer_count = count[:, None] - valid.astype(int)
        peer_return = np.divide(
            total[:, None] - np.where(valid, group, 0.0),
            peer_count,
            out=np.full_like(group, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=valid & (peer_count >= 5),
        )
        broad = (count >= 6) & (breadth >= 0.70) & (np.abs(mean) >= 0.007)
        loo_values[:, members] = peer_return
        broad_values[:, members] = valid & broad[:, None] & np.isfinite(peer_return)

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(loo_values, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(broad_values, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns),
    )


def _low_turnover_mask(eligible: pd.DataFrame, turnover: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    eligible_values = eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool, copy=True)
    turnover_values = turnover.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    output = np.zeros_like(eligible_values, dtype=bool)

    for row in range(eligible_values.shape[0]):
        positions = np.flatnonzero(
            eligible_values[row] & np.isfinite(turnover_values[row])
        )
        if positions.size < 5:
            continue
        cutoff = np.nanquantile(turnover_values[row, positions], 0.35)
        output[row, positions] = turnover_values[row, positions] <= cutoff

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=eligible.index, columns=eligible.columns)


@register_factor
class CashConfirmedSparsePeerLag(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'cash_confirmed_sparse_peer_lag'
    name = 'Cash-Confirmed Sparse Peer Lag'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Fresh cash-confirmed earnings news is traded only when a low-turnover '
        'name underreacts to a broad concordant leave-one-out industry move.'
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = [
        'close',
        'volume',
        'marketCap',
        'industry',
        'epsActual',
        'revenueActual',
        'epsSurprise',
        'epsEstimate',
        'revenueSurprise',
        'revenueEstimate',
        'operatingCashFlowGrowth',
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        market_cap = data['marketCap'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)

        valid_return = (close > 0.0) & (close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).where(valid_return)

        eps_actual = data['epsActual'].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_actual = data['revenueActual'].reindex_like(close)
        event = (
            (eps_actual.notna() & eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1)))
            | (revenue_actual.notna() & revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1)))
        )

        eps_surprise = data['epsSurprise'].reindex_like(close)
        eps_estimate = data['epsEstimate'].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data['revenueSurprise'].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_estimate = data['revenueEstimate'].reindex_like(close)
        cash_growth = data['operatingCashFlowGrowth'].reindex_like(close)

        eps_signal = eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.05)
        revenue_signal = revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        cash_signal = cash_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        positive = (eps_signal > 0.0) & (revenue_signal > 0.0) & (cash_signal > 0.0)
        negative = (eps_signal < 0.0) & (revenue_signal < 0.0) & (cash_signal < 0.0)
        report_direction = positive.astype(float) - negative.astype(float)

        eps_conviction = eps_signal.abs().where(event).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        revenue_conviction = revenue_signal.abs().where(event).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        cash_conviction = cash_signal.abs().where(event).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        conviction = pd.concat(
            [eps_conviction, revenue_conviction, cash_conviction], axis=0
        ).groupby(level=0).min().reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        labels = data['industry'].reindex_like(close).iloc[0].to_numpy(dtype=object)
        codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels, sort=False)
        peer_return, broad_industry = _leave_one_out_industry(ret, codes)

        lagged_ret = ret.shift(1)
        lagged_peer = peer_return.shift(1)
        paired = (lagged_ret.notna() & lagged_peer.notna()).astype(float)
        paired_count = paired.rolling(60, min_periods=40).sum()
        covariance = lagged_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(lagged_peer)
        variance = lagged_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(paired_count >= 40)
        beta = beta.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        predicted_move = beta * peer_return
        signed_gap = report_direction * (predicted_move - ret)
        relative_gap = signed_gap / peer_return.abs().clip(lower=0.005)
        lag_strength = relative_gap.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        turnover = (close * volume / market_cap).where(
            (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0) & (market_cap > 0.0)
        )
        average_turnover = turnover.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        no_volume_event = turnover <= 2.0 * average_turnover
        concordant_peer = np.sign(peer_return) == report_direction

        eligible = (
            event
            & (report_direction != 0.0)
            & broad_industry
            & concordant_peer
            & beta.notna()
            & average_turnover.notna()
            & no_volume_event
            & (lag_strength > 0.0)
        )
        sparse = _low_turnover_mask(eligible, average_turnover)
        signal = report_direction * conviction * lag_strength
        return signal.where(sparse, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Cash-confirmed earnings surprises identify firm-specific news that is less likely to reverse, while a broad same-direction industry move establishes that the information has already begun diffusing through economically related names. The child only trades when a low-turnover firm has both a directionally unanimous EPS, revenue, and cash-flow report and has underreacted relative to its beta-adjusted leave-one-out industry move. This interaction has edge because fundamental confirmation determines whether peer momentum is informative, while sparse liquidity identifies the names least able to assimilate that validated information immediately.
programs.description: On fresh reports, the factor requires unanimous normalized EPS surprise, revenue surprise, and operating-cash-flow-growth direction. It scores low-turnover names whose return lags a broad, concordant leave-one-out industry shock, scaled by report conviction and the size of the unpriced peer-implied move.

"""A broad, internally coherent sector shock may be incorporated first into actively traded sector leaders, while moderately less-active but historically sector-sensitive names adjust with delay. The signal does not treat the sector mode as a fair-value target unconditionally: it is activated only following a broad sector-mode shock, uses strictly pre-shock loading estimates, and excludes extremely illiquid names where adverse selection and trading costs are most likely to dominate. The expected effect is a six-bar catch-up of sector-mode laggards relative to contemporaneous overshooters, conditional on the shock representing a sector-wide rather than stock-specific event."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorized_equal_weight(values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Causal row-wise 5/95-percentile winsorized equal-weight return."""
    result = np.full(values.shape[0], np.nan, dtype=float)
    for row_index in range(values.shape[0]):
        row = values[row_index]
        valid = row[np.isfinite(row)]
        if valid.size == 0:
            continue
        if valid.size >= 3:
            lower, upper = np.percentile(valid, [5.0, 95.0])
            valid = np.clip(valid, lower, upper)
        result[row_index] = float(np.mean(valid))
    return result


def _first_pc_mode_and_betas(
    history: np.ndarray,
    equal_weight_history: np.ndarray,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Estimate a correlation-PC sector mode and trailing OLS member betas.

    The PCA is computed only from the supplied pre-shock history.  Missing
    standardized observations contribute no contemporaneous cross-product;
    this preserves the available-return requirement without forward filling
    prices or returns.
    """
    n_obs, n_names = history.shape
    means = np.nanmean(history, axis=0)
    scales = np.nanstd(history, axis=0, ddof=1)
    valid_scale = np.isfinite(scales) & (scales > 0.0)
    if n_names == 0 or not valid_scale.all():
        return np.full(n_obs, np.nan), np.full(n_names, np.nan)

    standardized = (history - means) / scales
    observed = np.isfinite(standardized)
    standardized = np.where(observed, standardized, 0.0)

    pair_count = observed.T @ observed
    cross_product = standardized.T @ standardized
    denominator = np.maximum(pair_count - 1.0, 1.0)
    corr = cross_product / denominator
    corr = np.where(np.isfinite(corr), corr, 0.0)
    corr = (corr + corr.T) * 0.5
    np.fill_diagonal(corr, 1.0)

    try:
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eigh(corr)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return np.full(n_obs, np.nan), np.full(n_names, np.nan)

    component = eigenvectors[:, int(np.argmax(eigenvalues))]
    weight_scale = np.sum(np.abs(component))
    if not np.isfinite(weight_scale) or weight_scale <= 0.0:
        return np.full(n_obs, np.nan), np.full(n_names, np.nan)
    component = component / weight_scale

    raw_history = np.where(np.isfinite(history), history, 0.0)
    mode_history = raw_history @ component
    common = np.isfinite(mode_history) & np.isfinite(equal_weight_history)
    if common.sum() >= 3:
        mode_std = np.std(mode_history[common], ddof=1)
        ew_std = np.std(equal_weight_history[common], ddof=1)
        if mode_std > 0.0 and ew_std > 0.0:
            orientation = np.corrcoef(mode_history[common], equal_weight_history[common])[0, 1]
            if np.isfinite(orientation) and orientation < 0.0:
                component = -component
                mode_history = -mode_history

    betas = np.full(n_names, np.nan, dtype=float)
    for member in range(n_names):
        paired = np.isfinite(history[:, member]) & np.isfinite(mode_history)
        if paired.sum() < 100:
            continue
        x = mode_history[paired]
        y = history[paired, member]
        x_centered = x - np.mean(x)
        x_variance = float(np.dot(x_centered, x_centered))
        if x_variance <= 0.0 or not np.isfinite(x_variance):
            continue
        y_centered = y - np.mean(y)
        beta = float(np.dot(x_centered, y_centered) / x_variance)
        if np.isfinite(beta):
            betas[member] = beta

    return mode_history, betas


def _sector_mode_lag_portfolio(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build the daily sector-balanced delayed-adjustment long-short weights."""
    index = close.index
    columns = close.columns
    n_rows, n_cols = close.shape
    output = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
    dollar_volume = safe_close * safe_volume

    prior_return_count = ret.shift(1).rolling(126, min_periods=126).count()
    prior_dollar_median = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    prior_volume_median = safe_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    prior_volatility = ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()

    ret_values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    close_values = safe_close.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_values = safe_volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    count_values = prior_return_count.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    dollar_median_values = prior_dollar_median.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_median_values = prior_volume_median.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volatility_values = prior_volatility.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    sector_values = sector.reindex(index=index, columns=columns).to_numpy()

    for t in range(126, n_rows):
        current_return = ret_values[t]
        base_eligible = (
            (count_values[t] >= 100.0)
            & np.isfinite(close_values[t])
            & np.isfinite(volume_values[t])
            & np.isfinite(current_return)
            & np.isfinite(dollar_median_values[t])
            & (dollar_median_values[t] > 0.0)
        )
        if base_eligible.sum() < 15:
            continue

        universe_dollar = dollar_median_values[t, base_eligible]
        try:
            liquidity_cutoff = float(np.nanpercentile(universe_dollar, 30.0))
        except (ValueError, IndexError):
            continue
        if not np.isfinite(liquidity_cutoff):
            continue

        eligible = base_eligible & (dollar_median_values[t] > liquidity_cutoff)
        labels = sector_values[t]
        active_sector_weights: list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]] = []

        valid_labels = pd.unique(labels[eligible])
        for label in valid_labels:
            if pd.isna(label):
                continue
            member_mask = eligible & (labels == label)
            member_positions = np.flatnonzero(member_mask)
            if member_positions.size < 15:
                continue

            history = ret_values[t - 126:t, :][:, member_positions]
            if np.any(np.sum(np.isfinite(history), axis=0) < 100):
                continue

            ew_history = _winsorized_equal_weight(history)
            if np.isfinite(ew_history).sum() < 100:
                continue
            shock_std = float(np.nanstd(ew_history, ddof=1))
            if not np.isfinite(shock_std) or shock_std <= 0.0:
                continue

            current_members = current_return[member_positions]
            finite_current = np.isfinite(current_members)
            if finite_current.sum() < 15:
                continue
            current_valid = current_members[finite_current]
            lower, upper = np.percentile(current_valid, [5.0, 95.0])
            sector_return = float(np.mean(np.clip(current_valid, lower, upper)))
            if not np.isfinite(sector_return) or abs(sector_return) <= 1.5 * shock_std:
                continue

            same_sign = np.sum(np.sign(current_valid) == np.sign(sector_return))
            if same_sign / float(current_valid.size) < 0.65:
                continue

            _, betas = _first_pc_mode_and_betas(history, ew_history)
            residual = current_members - betas * sector_return

            current_volume = volume_values[t, member_positions]
            median_volume = volume_median_values[t, member_positions]
            relative_volume = current_volume / median_volume
            delayed = (
                np.isfinite(residual)
                & np.isfinite(relative_volume)
                & (relative_volume >= 0.50)
                & (relative_volume <= 0.90)
            )
            if delayed.sum() < 5:
                continue

            delayed_residual = residual[delayed]
            residual_low, residual_high = np.percentile(delayed_residual, [5.0, 95.0])
            clipped_residual = np.clip(delayed_residual, residual_low, residual_high)
            residual_rank = pd.Series(clipped_residual).rank(pct=True, method="average").to_numpy()

            delayed_positions = member_positions[delayed]
            long_local = residual_rank <= 0.20
            short_local = residual_rank >= 0.80
            if long_local.sum() == 0 or short_local.sum() == 0:
                continue

            selected_volatility = volatility_values[t, delayed_positions]
            valid_volatility = selected_volatility[np.isfinite(selected_volatility) & (selected_volatility > 0.0)]
            if valid_volatility.size == 0:
                continue
            vol_cap = float(np.percentile(valid_volatility, 90.0))
            if not np.isfinite(vol_cap) or vol_cap <= 0.0:
                continue
            safe_volatility = np.where(
                np.isfinite(selected_volatility) & (selected_volatility > 0.0),
                np.minimum(selected_volatility, vol_cap),
                np.nan,
            )
            inverse_volatility = 1.0 / safe_volatility

            long_weights = np.where(long_local, inverse_volatility, 0.0)
            short_weights = np.where(short_local, inverse_volatility, 0.0)
            long_total = float(np.nansum(long_weights))
            short_total = float(np.nansum(short_weights))
            if long_total <= 0.0 or short_total <= 0.0:
                continue

            active_sector_weights.append(
                (
                    delayed_positions,
                    long_weights / long_total,
                    short_weights / short_total,
                )
            )

        if not active_sector_weights:
            continue

        sector_scale = 1.0 / float(len(active_sector_weights))
        for positions, long_weights, short_weights in active_sector_weights:
            output[t, positions] += sector_scale * (long_weights - short_weights)

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=index, columns=columns)


@register_factor
class SparseModeLoadingDelayedCatchup(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-PC residual catch-up portfolio conditioned on broad common shocks."""

    factor_id = "sparse_mode_loading_delayed_catchup"
    name = "Tradable Sector-Mode Lag Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "A sector-balanced long-short portfolio that buys moderately low-volume "
        "laggards and sells overshooters after a broad sector common-mode shock, "
        "using strictly pre-shock first-PC loading estimates."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return _sector_mode_lag_portfolio(
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
            data["sector"],
        )

programs.trading_idea: A broad, internally coherent sector shock may be incorporated first into actively traded sector leaders, while moderately less-active but historically sector-sensitive names adjust with delay. The signal does not treat the sector mode as a fair-value target unconditionally: it is activated only following a broad sector-mode shock, uses strictly pre-shock loading estimates, and excludes extremely illiquid names where adverse selection and trading costs are most likely to dominate. The expected effect is a six-bar catch-up of sector-mode laggards relative to contemporaneous overshooters, conditional on the shock representing a sector-wide rather than stock-specific event.
programs.description: Use daily close-to-close returns, with r[t] = close[t]/close[t-1]-1. At each daily close t, form the signal only after all close and volume observations for t are known; trade execution is no earlier than the next bar's open (t+1 open), with positions held for six daily bars and rebalanced daily. Within each static sector, define the eligible estimation universe as stocks having at least 100 valid daily returns during the trailing 126-bar window [t-126,t-1], positive close and volume on t, and trailing median daily dollar volume (close*volume) above the cross-sectional 30th percentile of the full eligible universe; sectors require at least 15 such stocks, otherwise their signal is zero. Estimate the sector's first common mode from the first principal component of the correlation matrix of standardized member returns over [t-126,t-1], retaining exactly one mode and orienting its sign so that its correlation with the sector equal-weight return is positive. Estimate each stock's loading beta_i by an OLS regression of its trailing returns on that lagged first-PC mode over the same window, requiring at least 100 paired observations; stocks without a valid beta receive zero signal. On date t, compute the realized sector-mode return as the equal-weight return of eligible sector members after winsorizing member returns at the sector's contemporaneous 5th and 95th percentiles. Activate a sector only when this sector return has absolute value greater than 1.5 times its trailing 126-bar standard deviation and at least 65% of valid sector members have returns with the same sign as the sector return; this broad-participation condition is intended to reject shocks dominated by one or a few firm-specific events. For each stock, compute residual_i[t] = r_i[t] - beta_i*mode_return[t]. Define relative volume as volume_i[t] divided by its trailing 20-bar median volume using [t-20,t-1]. Retain only stocks with relative volume between 0.50 and 0.90: below-normal participation is required for delayed adjustment, but the lowest-activity names are excluded to limit stale-price, spread, and impact exposure. Within each activated sector, winsorize residuals at the 5th and 95th percentiles and rank them cross-sectionally. The predictive score is the negative sector-demeaned residual rank: the most negative residuals after a positive common shock, or most positive residuals after a negative common shock, are expected to move toward the sector mode over the next six bars. Construct a sector-balanced long-short portfolio by longing the bottom residual quintile and shorting the top residual quintile within each activated sector, equal-weighting names within each side and equal-weighting active sectors; gross long and short exposure are matched, and weights are scaled inversely by trailing 20-bar return volatility capped at the 90th percentile to prevent a few volatile names dominating. Short positions are opened only where the execution system confirms shortability and borrow availability; unavailable shorts receive zero weight and the corresponding sector long exposure is reduced to preserve approximate dollar neutrality. New listings, halted names, missing close/volume observations, stale fundamental classifications, insufficient trailing history, and stocks without a next-bar executable open are excluded rather than imputed. Empirical evaluation must compare net-of-cost results against ordinary sector-beta residual reversal, one-day reversal, volume-conditioned reversal, and liquidity controls, with costs and borrow charges stressed most heavily for the lower-volume selected names.

"""Sector-mode residual catch-up conditioned on volume-first relative assimilation.

Mechanism: broad coherent sector shocks are incorporated unevenly.  A stock's
sector-mode residual is traded only when its industry-relative price-volume
path shows participation preceding a same-direction relative-price response,
which is evidence of delayed assimilation rather than a transient price-first
displacement.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Replicate same-date group medians, leaving undersized groups at zero."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == label].intersection(values.columns)
        if len(members) < minimum:
            continue
        group_values = values.loc[:, members]
        median = group_values.median(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        output.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    return output


def _sector_coherence(
    stock_return: pd.DataFrame, sector_return: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fraction of each sector whose current return agrees with its sector move."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=stock_return.index, columns=stock_return.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == label].intersection(stock_return.columns)
        if len(members) < 5:
            continue
        group_return = stock_return.loc[:, members].fillna(0.0)
        group_sector = sector_return.loc[:, members].iloc[:, 0]
        agreement = group_return.mul(group_sector, axis=0).gt(0.0).mean(axis=1)
        output.loc[:, members] = np.tile(agreement.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    return output


@register_factor
class CoherentSectorCurlLoadingCatchup(BaseFactor):
    """Sector shock catch-up gated by directional volume-first assimilation."""

    factor_id = "coherent_sector_curl_loading_catchup"
    name = "Coherent Sector Curl Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Sector-beta residual catch-up after broad coherent sector shocks, "
        "activated only by an industry-relative volume-first price-volume curl "
        "aligned with the sector impulse."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].where(data["volume"] >= 0.0)
        columns = close.columns

        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0].reindex(columns)
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(columns)

        stock_return = np.log(close).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector_return = _group_median(stock_return, sector_labels, 5)
        industry_return = _group_median(stock_return, industry_labels, 5)

        sector_scale = (
            sector_return.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=15).std().clip(lower=0.0005)
        )
        sector_shock = (sector_return / sector_scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        coherence = _sector_coherence(stock_return, sector_return, sector_labels)
        broad_shock = (sector_shock.abs() - 0.75).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0) / 2.0
        broad_shock = broad_shock * ((coherence - 0.50).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.50) * 2.0)

        prior_stock = stock_return.shift(1)
        prior_sector = sector_return.shift(1)
        sector_variance = prior_sector.rolling(60, min_periods=30).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = prior_stock.rolling(60, min_periods=30).cov(prior_sector) / sector_variance
        beta = beta.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        loading_confidence = (beta.abs() / 1.5).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        mode_residual = stock_return - beta * sector_return
        residual_scale = (
            mode_residual.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.0005)
        )
        residual_z = (mode_residual / residual_scale).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        industry_residual = stock_return - industry_return
        industry_scale = (
            industry_residual.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.0005)
        )
        price_z = (industry_residual / industry_scale).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume)
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.01)
        volume_z = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        curl_increment = price_z.shift(1) * volume_z - volume_z.shift(1) * price_z
        curl = curl_increment.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().fillna(0.0)

        # A volume-first move followed by a relative-price move in the sector
        # shock direction has positive aligned_curl for either shock sign.
        aligned_curl = -curl * np.sign(sector_return.fillna(0.0))
        assimilation = (aligned_curl / 6.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        raw = -residual_z * broad_shock * loading_confidence * assimilation
        sector_neutral = raw - _group_median(raw, sector_labels, 5)
        return rank(sector_neutral.fillna(0.0)) * 2.0 - 1.0
programs.name: Coherent Sector Curl Catch-Up
programs.trading_idea: A broad and directionally coherent sector shock creates a common-information impulse, but historically sector-sensitive constituents can still lag the sector mode when their own trading participation arrives before their relative-price adjustment. The child buys sector-mode laggards and sells overshooters only when a directionally aligned volume-first price-volume curl indicates delayed assimilation rather than a price-first transient displacement. """Tax-fragility conditioned industry-support unwind.

Mechanism: tax-led estimate optimism can keep fragile firms relatively supported
through an industry selloff.  Relative price resilience followed by abnormal
participation during that common shock is interpreted as transient support,
whose unwind should be negative over the next several bars.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date percentile rank with invalid numerical values removed."""
    return values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Replicate causal same-date industry medians, with market fallback."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(members) == 0:
            continue
        median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
        out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    market_median = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return out.T.fillna(market_median).T


def _safe_revision(current: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale-free positive-lag revision, robust to zero denominators."""
    previous = current.shift(lag)
    return (current - previous) / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class TaxFragilityIndustrySupportUnwind(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "tax_fragility_industry_support_unwind"
    name = "Tax-Fragility Industry Support Unwind"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Shorts tax-led, financially fragile upgrades that retain relative price "
        "support and attract abnormal volume during a negative industry impulse."
    )
    window_length = 42
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        stock_return = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        industry_return = _group_median(stock_return, industry_labels)
        industry_three_day = industry_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = (
            industry_three_day.shift(1)
            .rolling(20, min_periods=10)
            .std()
            .clip(lower=0.002)
        )
        downside_impulse = (-industry_three_day / industry_scale).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        downside_impulse = downside_impulse.fillna(0.0)

        stock_three_day = stock_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        relative_resilience = stock_three_day - industry_three_day
        prior_resilience = _cs_rank(relative_resilience.shift(1)).fillna(0.5)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume >= 0.0))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean()
        volume_scale = (
            log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).std().clip(lower=0.05)
        )
        abnormal_participation = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_scale).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        abnormal_participation = abnormal_participation.fillna(0.0)

        eps_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data["epsEstimate"], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        sales_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        tax_rate = data["incomeTaxExpense"] / data["incomeBeforeTax"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = _cs_rank(tax_rate.shift(42) - tax_rate).fillna(0.5)

        # High only when the optimistic EPS change is more tax-led than
        # revenue-confirmed; the continuous construction retains broad coverage.
        tax_led_upgrade = eps_revision * tax_decline * (1.0 - sales_revision)

        debt = _cs_rank(data["debtToAssets"]).fillna(0.5)
        illiquidity = _cs_rank(-data["currentRatio"]).fillna(0.5)
        weak_coverage = _cs_rank(-data["interestCoverage"]).fillna(0.5)
        fragility = (debt + illiquidity + weak_coverage) / 3.0

        support_sequence = prior_resilience * abnormal_participation
        unwind_risk = tax_led_upgrade * fragility * downside_impulse * support_sequence

        # Invert the risk rank: high returned factor values predict higher returns.
        alpha = 0.5 - _cs_rank(unwind_risk).fillna(0.5)
        return alpha.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A tax-led EPS upgrade in a financially fragile company can sustain optimistic relative pricing even when revenue-estimate confirmation is weak. Following a negative industry impulse, a stock that remains relatively resilient and then attracts abnormal participation is likely receiving delayed benchmark or liquidity support rather than revealing durable information; the common shock exposes the fragility of that support. Parent A supplies the shock-propagation and price-then-participation timing state, while Parent B identifies the accounting-quality and balance-sheet state in which apparent support is most vulnerable to a short-horizon unwind.

The returned alpha is the inverse cross-sectional rank of this unwind-risk score, so highly supported fragile names receive negative scores.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(members) > 0:
            median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
            out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    market = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return out.T.fillna(market).T


def _safe_revision(values: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    previous = values.shift(lag)
    return (values - previous) / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _prior_range_volatility(high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    valid = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0)
    log_range = np.log((high / low).where(valid))
    return np.sqrt(log_range.pow(2.0).rolling(20, min_periods=12).mean().shift(1))


@register_factor
class CalmSupportFailureIndustryBreak(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "calm_support_failure_industry_break"
    name = "Calm Support-Failure Industry Break"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "High values identify tax-led, fragile firms whose earlier relative support "
        "during an industry selloff is failing through a fresh calm-regime downside break."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        log_return = np.log(close.where(close > 0.0)).diff()
        industry_return = _group_median(log_return, industry_labels)

        industry_three_day = industry_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = industry_three_day.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.002)
        industry_downside = (-industry_three_day / industry_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        stock_three_day = log_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        prior_resilience = _cs_rank((stock_three_day - industry_three_day).shift(1)).fillna(0.5)
        stock_two_day = log_return.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        industry_two_day = industry_return.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        relative_break = _cs_rank(-(stock_two_day - industry_two_day)).fillna(0.5)

        log_volume = np.log1p(data["volume"].where(data["volume"] >= 0.0))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).std().clip(lower=0.05)
        participation = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)
        participation_gate = 0.5 + 0.5 * (participation / 3.0)

        eps_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data["epsEstimate"], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        sales_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        tax_rate = data["incomeTaxExpense"] / data["incomeBeforeTax"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = _cs_rank(tax_rate.shift(42) - tax_rate).fillna(0.5)
        tax_led_upgrade = eps_revision * tax_decline * (1.0 - sales_revision)

        debt = _cs_rank(data["debtToAssets"]).fillna(0.5)
        illiquidity = _cs_rank(-data["currentRatio"]).fillna(0.5)
        weak_coverage = _cs_rank(-data["interestCoverage"]).fillna(0.5)
        weak_cashflow = _cs_rank(-data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"]).fillna(0.5)
        fragility = (debt + illiquidity + weak_coverage + weak_cashflow) / 4.0

        calmness = (1.0 - _cs_rank(_prior_range_volatility(data["high"], data["low"]))).fillna(0.5)
        raw_risk = (
            tax_led_upgrade
            * fragility
            * industry_downside
            * prior_resilience
            * calmness
            * relative_break
            * participation_gate
        )
        return _cs_rank(raw_risk).fillna(0.5).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

"""Large industry moves can propagate unevenly across constituents when participation is sparse: stocks trading at unusually low relative volume may initially adjust less than their historically estimated industry exposure. This is a delayed common-shock transmission hypothesis, not a claim that high conditional beta is necessarily mispricing. It predicts that, conditional on a large industry shock and no contemporaneous earnings-surprise update, the relative laggards should outperform their industry peers after positive shocks and underperform after negative shocks over the subsequent six bars."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    """Build static industry-to-column membership without using future labels."""
    if industry.empty:
        return {}

    labels = industry.iloc[0]
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    for column in industry.columns:
        label = labels[column]
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column)
    return groups


def _stock_excluded_industry_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    lagged_market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute cap-weighted same-industry returns excluding each stock itself."""
    peer_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for columns in groups.values():
        group_ret = ret[columns]
        group_cap = lagged_market_cap[columns]
        valid = group_ret.notna() & group_cap.notna() & (group_cap > 0.0)

        valid_cap = group_cap.where(valid, 0.0)
        weighted_ret = (group_ret * group_cap).where(valid, 0.0)
        total_cap = valid_cap.sum(axis=1)
        total_weighted_ret = weighted_ret.sum(axis=1)
        total_count = valid.astype(float).sum(axis=1)

        excluded_cap = total_cap.to_frame().values - valid_cap.values
        excluded_weighted_ret = (
            total_weighted_ret.to_frame().values - weighted_ret.values
        )
        excluded_count = total_count.to_frame().values - valid.astype(float).values

        group_peer_return = pd.DataFrame(
            excluded_weighted_ret / np.where(excluded_cap > 0.0, excluded_cap, np.nan),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )
        group_peer_count = pd.DataFrame(
            excluded_count,
            index=ret.index,
            columns=columns,
        )

        peer_return.loc[:, columns] = group_peer_return.where(
            (group_peer_count >= 10.0) & (excluded_cap > 0.0)
        )
        peer_count.loc[:, columns] = group_peer_count

    return peer_return, peer_count


def _trailing_beta(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    industry_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int = 60,
    min_pairs: int = 40,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS beta using observations through t-1 only."""
    x = industry_ret.shift(1)
    y = stock_ret.shift(1)
    paired = x.notna() & y.notna()

    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    x0 = x.where(paired, 0.0)
    y0 = y.where(paired, 0.0)

    sum_x = x0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_y = y0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xx = (x0 * x0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xy = (x0 * y0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    safe_count = count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    denominator = sum_xx - (sum_x * sum_x / safe_count)
    numerator = sum_xy - (sum_x * sum_y / safe_count)

    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count >= min_pairs)


def _surprise_update(surprise: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag newly public or revised earnings/revenue surprise values at t."""
    previous = surprise.shift(1)
    newly_non_null = surprise.notna() & previous.isna()
    revised = surprise.notna() & previous.notna() & surprise.ne(previous)
    return newly_non_null | revised


def _industry_equal_gross_rank(
    underreaction: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize, rank, demean, and equal-gross scale each industry daily."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=underreaction.index, columns=underreaction.columns)

    for columns in groups.values():
        values = underreaction[columns].where(eligible[columns])
        count = values.notna().sum(axis=1)
        sufficient = count >= 5

        lower = values.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = values.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        ranks = clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        demeaned = ranks.sub(ranks.mean(axis=1), axis=0).where(sufficient, 0.0)

        gross = demeaned.abs().sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        scaled = demeaned.div(gross, axis=0).where(eligible[columns], 0.0)
        output.loc[:, columns] = scaled.fillna(0.0)

    return output


@register_factor
class ShockPropagationLiquidityDelay(BaseFactor):
    """Low-participation constituents catch up after large common industry shocks."""

    factor_id = "shock_propagation_liquidity_delay"
    name = "Low-Participation Industry-Shock Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral, equal-gross rank of stocks whose current return "
        "lags their trailing-beta-implied response to a large stock-excluded "
        "industry shock while current participation is unusually low."
    )
    window_length = 62
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        stock_ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).where(
            close.notna() & previous_close.notna() & (close > 0.0) & (previous_close > 0.0)
        )

        groups = _industry_groups(industry)
        lagged_market_cap = market_cap.shift(1).where(market_cap.shift(1) > 0.0)
        industry_ret, _ = _stock_excluded_industry_return(
            stock_ret, lagged_market_cap, groups
        )

        prior_abs_industry = industry_ret.abs().shift(1)
        shock_threshold = prior_abs_industry.rolling(60, min_periods=48).quantile(0.80)
        large_shock = industry_ret.abs() > shock_threshold

        beta = _trailing_beta(stock_ret, industry_ret, 60, 40)
        signed_gap = (
            np.sign(industry_ret) * (beta * industry_ret - stock_ret)
        ).where(beta.notna() & industry_ret.notna() & stock_ret.notna())

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        median_prior_volume = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        min_prior_volume = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).min()
        low_participation = (
            (volume > 0.0)
            & (min_prior_volume > 0.0)
            & (median_prior_volume > 0.0)
            & ((volume / median_prior_volume) <= 0.75)
        )

        prior_dollar_volume = (close.shift(1) * volume.shift(1)).where(
            (close.shift(1) > 0.0) & (volume.shift(1) > 0.0)
        )
        liquid_enough = prior_dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median() >= 5_000_000.0

        earnings_update = _surprise_update(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue_update = _surprise_update(data["revenueSurprise"])
        no_company_event = ~(earnings_update | revenue_update)

        eligible = (
            large_shock
            & low_participation
            & liquid_enough
            & no_company_event
            & signed_gap.notna()
        )

        return _industry_equal_gross_rank(signed_gap, eligible, groups).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Large industry moves can propagate unevenly across constituents when participation is sparse: stocks trading at unusually low relative volume may initially adjust less than their historically estimated industry exposure. This is a delayed common-shock transmission hypothesis, not a claim that high conditional beta is necessarily mispricing. It predicts that, conditional on a large industry shock and no contemporaneous earnings-surprise update, the relative laggards should outperform their industry peers after positive shocks and underperform after negative shocks over the subsequent six bars.
programs.description: At the close of day t, define r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. Industry membership is the static point-in-time industry field. For each stock i, construct its stock-excluded industry return I_-i,t as the marketCap-weighted mean of same-industry peer returns r_j,t, using marketCap_j,t-1 as weights; require at least 10 valid peers and positive aggregate peer market capitalization. Define a large industry shock when |I_-i,t| exceeds the 80th percentile of that industry's valid absolute stock-excluded daily returns over t-60 through t-1; require at least 48 prior industry-return observations. Estimate normal industry beta using only information through t-1: beta_i,t = sum[(r_i,s-rbar_i)(I_-i,s-Ibar)] / sum[(I_-i,s-Ibar)^2] over s=t-60,...,t-1, requiring at least 40 paired observations and nonzero denominator. Define the signed underreaction gap u_i,t = sign(I_-i,t) * (beta_i,t * I_-i,t - r_i,t), so a larger positive value identifies a stock that lagged its expected response in the direction of the common shock. Restrict candidates to names with volume_i,t / median(volume_i,t-20,...,t-1) <= 0.75, positive current and trailing volume, and median(close_i,s * volume_i,s, s=t-20,...,t-1) >= USD 5,000,000. Exclude a name if epsSurprise or revenueSurprise is newly non-null or changes between t-1 and t, preventing direct earnings-release repricing from being treated as liquidity delay. Within each shocked industry, winsorize u at that day's 1st and 99th eligible-percentile values, percentile-rank it, and subtract the industry mean rank; require at least 5 eligible names per industry. The final factor is this industry-demeaned rank, with zero exposure for ineligible names. A positive factor loading means long the largest relative underreaction gaps and short the smallest within the same industry, producing industry-neutral equal-gross books; industries are equally gross-scaled and the aggregate book is dollar-neutral. All inputs through close t, including close_t and volume_t, are observed only after the close. Positions therefore enter no earlier than open t+1 and exit at open t+7, six daily bars after entry.

"""Stress-gated credibility polarity for idiosyncratic volume arrivals.

Mechanism: following a negative industry impulse, prior relative resilience and a
late idiosyncratic participation burst can be either informed counterflow or
transient support.  Revenue- and margin-supported revisions validate the burst;
tax-led and financially fragile revisions raise the threshold for continuation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date group median with a same-date market-median fallback."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(group)]
        if len(members) > 0:
            median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
            out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    market = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return out.T.fillna(market).T


def _cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust contemporaneous cross-sectional z-score."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lo = clean.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    hi = clean.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = clean.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    scale = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(scale, axis=0)


def _revision(current: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    previous = current.shift(lag)
    return ((current - previous) / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )


@register_factor
class StressGatedRevisionArrivalPolarity(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "stress_gated_revision_arrival_polarity"
    name = "Stress-Gated Credible Arrival Polarity"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks sector-residual rare signed-volume arrivals after relative resilience "
        "in an industry selloff, continuing only arrivals validated by operating "
        "revision credibility and reversing the rest."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        stock_ret = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        industry_ret = _group_median(stock_ret, labels)
        industry_move = industry_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = industry_move.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.002)
        downside = (-industry_move / industry_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        stock_move = stock_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        prior_resilience = (stock_move - industry_move).shift(1).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        stress_state = np.tanh(downside) * prior_resilience

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        positive_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
        volume_base = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=12).median().shift(1)
        volume_ratio = volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rare_cutoff = volume_ratio.rolling(60, min_periods=40).quantile(0.95).shift(1)
        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        direction = np.sign(close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
        valid = close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0) & high.gt(low)
        rare = valid & volume_ratio.ge(rare_cutoff)
        marked_arrival = (
            direction * location.abs() * volume_ratio.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        ).where(rare, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        arrival_memory = marked_arrival.ewm(halflife=3, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
        idio_arrival = arrival_memory - _group_median(arrival_memory, labels)

        eps = data["epsEstimate"]
        sales = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        pretax = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax = data["incomeTaxExpense"]

        eps_rev = _revision(eps, 42)
        sales_rev = _revision(sales, 42)
        margin = operating_income / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        margin_change = margin - margin.shift(42)
        tax_rate = tax / pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = tax_rate.shift(42) - tax_rate

        eps_sign = np.sign(eps_rev)
        sales_support = eps_sign * _cs_zscore(sales_rev).fillna(0.0)
        margin_support = eps_sign * _cs_zscore(margin_change).fillna(0.0)
        tax_penalty = _cs_zscore(tax_decline).fillna(0.0).where(eps_sign.gt(0.0), 0.0)
        update = eps.notna() & eps.shift(1).notna() & eps.ne(eps.shift(1))
        credibility_impulse = (
            eps_sign * (0.55 * sales_support + 0.45 * margin_support - 0.40 * tax_penalty)
        ).clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0).where(update, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        credibility = credibility_impulse.ewm(halflife=10, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

        debt = data["debtToAssets"].rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        liquidity_weakness = (-data["currentRatio"]).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        coverage_weakness = (-data["interestCoverage"]).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        fragility = (debt + liquidity_weakness + coverage_weakness) / 3.0

        arrival_sign = np.sign(idio_arrival)
        alignment = arrival_sign * credibility
        polarity = np.tanh(2.0 * (alignment - 0.30 * fragility) - 0.35)
        signal = stress_state * idio_arrival * polarity
        return signal.rank(axis=1, pct=True).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Stress-Gated Credible Arrival Polarity
programs.trading_idea: An idiosyncratic volume arrival during an industry downside impulse is especially informative only after the stock has first shown relative resilience: this is the common-shock support state identified by Parent A. Parent B supplies the polarity test: revenue- and margin-confirmed estimate revisions make the arrival likely informed counterflow and therefore continuation, whereas tax-led or financially fragile revisions make the same support more likely transient liquidity demand and therefore reversal. The interaction distinguishes genuine information-driven sheltering from mechanically supported resilience, which neither industry stress nor signed-volume arrivals identify alone.
programs.description: The signal isolates sector-residual rare signed-volume arrivals following relative resilience during a negative industry impulse, then flips their direction unless they agree with a decaying revenue/margin-supported and tax-discounted EPS-revision state. Financial fragility raises the credibility threshold required for continuation.

"""Sector-mode catch-up gated by volume-first participation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == label].intersection(values.columns)
        if len(members) < minimum:
            continue
        group = values.loc[:, members]
        median = group.median(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        output.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    return output


def _sector_coherence(stock_return: pd.DataFrame, sector_return: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=stock_return.index, columns=stock_return.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == label].intersection(stock_return.columns)
        if len(members) < 5:
            continue
        member_return = stock_return.loc[:, members].fillna(0.0)
        sector_move = sector_return.loc[:, members].iloc[:, 0]
        agreement = member_return.mul(sector_move, axis=0).gt(0.0).mean(axis=1)
        output.loc[:, members] = np.tile(agreement.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    return output


@register_factor
class SectorModeParticipationLeadCatchup(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_mode_participation_lead_catchup"
    name = "Sector Participation-Lead Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Sector-beta residual catch-up after coherent sector shocks, activated "
        "only when moderate participation and an aligned volume-first relative "
        "price-volume curl indicate incomplete assimilation."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].where(data["volume"] >= 0.0)
        columns = close.columns
        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0].reindex(columns)
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(columns)

        stock_return = np.log(close).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector_return = _group_median(stock_return, sector_labels, 5)
        industry_return = _group_median(stock_return, industry_labels, 5)

        sector_scale = sector_return.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().clip(lower=0.0005)
        sector_z = (sector_return / sector_scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        coherence = _sector_coherence(stock_return, sector_return, sector_labels)
        shock_gate = (sector_z.abs() - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0) / 2.0
        shock_gate = shock_gate * ((coherence - 0.60).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.40) / 0.40)

        prior_stock = stock_return.shift(1)
        prior_sector = sector_return.shift(1)
        sector_var = prior_sector.rolling(60, min_periods=30).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = prior_stock.rolling(60, min_periods=30).cov(prior_sector) / sector_var
        beta = beta.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        loading_gate = (beta.abs() / 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        residual = stock_return - beta * sector_return
        residual_scale = residual.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.0005)
        residual_z = (residual / residual_scale).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        relative_price = stock_return - industry_return
        price_scale = relative_price.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.0005)
        price_z = (relative_price / price_scale).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume)
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.01)
        volume_z = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)
        relative_volume = volume / volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        moderate_participation = ((relative_volume - 0.45).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.50) / 0.50).fillna(0.0)

        curl_step = price_z.shift(1) * volume_z - volume_z.shift(1) * price_z
        curl = curl_step.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().fillna(0.0)
        aligned_curl = -curl * np.sign(sector_return.fillna(0.0))
        assimilation_gate = (aligned_curl / 5.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        raw = -residual_z * shock_gate * loading_gate * moderate_participation * assimilation_gate
        sector_neutral = raw - _group_median(raw, sector_labels, 5)
        return rank(sector_neutral.fillna(0.0)) * 2.0 - 1.0
programs.name: Sector Participation-Lead Catch-Up
programs.trading_idea: A broad coherent sector impulse is initially incorporated by liquid leaders, while historically sector-sensitive constituents with moderate current participation can retain an unpaid sector-mode residual. The child trades that residual only when an industry-relative volume-first price-volume curl shows that participation arrived before the constituent's relative-price adjustment. This interaction separates genuine delayed common-information assimilation from ordinary residual reversal: Parent A supplies the sector shock and pre-event loading gap, while Parent B supplies evidence that the lag is caused by sequencing of trading participation rather than a completed transient move.
programs.description: The signal estimates sector-beta residuals after coherent sector shocks, then ranks laggards versus overshooters only when current activity is moderate and a trailing industry-relative volume-price curl is aligned with the sector impulse. It is sector-neutralized cross-sectionally.

"""This is a conditional price-pressure continuation hypothesis rather than an identified claim about informed absorption. Repeated high-relative-volume closes near the same end of the daily range may indicate persistent imbalance or constrained liquidity replenishment when the stock has not yet moved materially across days; the opposite pattern indicates persistent downside pressure. The effect is explicitly conditional on no large overnight or same-day repricing event, where daily OHLCV cannot distinguish liquidity pressure from public-information incorporation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _historical_volume_median_and_mad(
    log_volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Trailing t-20 through t-1 robust volume baseline and observation count."""
    history = log_volume.shift(1)
    count = history.notna().rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    median = history.rolling(20, min_periods=1).median()

    def median_absolute_deviation(values: np.ndarray) -> float:
        center = np.nanmedian(values)
        return float(np.nanmedian(np.abs(values - center)))

    mad = history.rolling(20, min_periods=1).apply(
        median_absolute_deviation,
        raw=True,
    )
    return median, mad, count


@register_factor
class NeutralReturnVolumeLocationCoherenceDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks persistent signed range-location pressure during neutral trends."""

    factor_id = "neutral_return_volume_location_coherence_drift"
    name = "Neutral-Return Volume-Location Coherence"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of ten-session coherence between robust abnormal "
        "volume and close location, restricted to non-shock names whose ten-day "
        "close return remains near neutral."
    )
    window_length = 31
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        finite_ohlcv = (
            np.isfinite(open_)
            & np.isfinite(high)
            & np.isfinite(low)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
        )
        bar_valid = (
            finite_ohlcv
            & (open_ > 0.0)
            & (high > 0.0)
            & (low > 0.0)
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (volume >= 0.0)
            & (high >= low)
        )

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        overnight_return = open_ / previous_close - 1.0
        daily_return = close / previous_close - 1.0
        valid_observation = (
            bar_valid
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & (previous_close > 0.0)
            & (overnight_return.abs() <= 0.08)
            & (daily_return.abs() <= 0.12)
        )

        price_range = high - low
        clv = (2.0 * (close - low) / price_range - 1.0).where(
            price_range > 0.0,
            0.0,
        )
        clv = clv.where(bar_valid)

        volume_valid = np.isfinite(volume) & (volume >= 0.0)
        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume_valid))
        baseline_median, baseline_mad, baseline_count = (
            _historical_volume_median_and_mad(log_volume)
        )
        volume_z = (log_volume - baseline_median) / (1.4826 * baseline_mad)
        volume_z = volume_z.where(baseline_mad > 0.0, 0.0).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        signed_location_volume = (clv * volume_z).where(valid_observation)
        coherence_count = valid_observation.astype(float).rolling(
            10,
            min_periods=1,
        ).sum()
        coherence = signed_location_volume.rolling(10, min_periods=1).sum()
        coherence = coherence / coherence_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        coherence = coherence.where(coherence_count >= 7.0)

        return_10 = close / close.shift(10) - 1.0
        neutral_weight = (1.0 - return_10.abs() / 0.10).clip(lower=0.0)
        raw_score = coherence * neutral_weight

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(
            np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (volume >= 0.0)
        )
        median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        liquid_large_cap = (
            np.isfinite(market_cap)
            & (market_cap >= 1_000_000_000.0)
            & (median_dollar_volume >= 10_000_000.0)
        )

        eligible = (
            valid_observation
            & (baseline_count >= 15.0)
            & return_10.notna()
            & liquid_large_cap
        )
        return rank(raw_score.where(eligible))
programs.name: Neutral-Return Volume-Location Coherence
programs.trading_idea: This is a conditional price-pressure continuation hypothesis rather than an identified claim about informed absorption. Repeated high-relative-volume closes near the same end of the daily range may indicate persistent imbalance or constrained liquidity replenishment when the stock has not yet moved materially across days; the opposite pattern indicates persistent downside pressure. The effect is explicitly conditional on no large overnight or same-day repricing event, where daily OHLCV cannot distinguish liquidity pressure from public-information incorporation.
programs.description: For stock i on day t, define close location CLV_t = 2*(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t)-1 when high_t>low_t, and CLV_t=0 when high_t=low_t. Let x_t=log(1+volume_t). Estimate abnormal log volume using only days t-20 through t-1: m_t is the rolling median of x, d_t is the rolling median of |x-m_t|, and z_t=(x_t-m_t)/(1.4826*d_t) when d_t>0; otherwise z_t=0. Clip z_t to [-3,3]. Define a valid non-shock observation as one with valid OHLCV, |open_t/close_{t-1}-1|<=0.08, and |close_t/close_{t-1}-1|<=0.12. The 10-day coherence is C_t=mean(CLV_s*clip(z_s,-3,3)) over valid observations s=t-9,...,t, requiring at least 7 valid observations; invalid observations are omitted from the mean. Define the cumulative close return R10_t=close_t/close_{t-10}-1 and the fixed neutral-trend weight W_t=max(0,1-|R10_t|/0.10). The raw score is S_t=C_t*W_t, set to missing when the current day is invalid, the 20-day volume baseline has fewer than 15 valid observations, or R10_t is unavailable. Each day, rank S_t cross-sectionally among eligible names into a percentile score; higher scores are long candidates and lower scores are short candidates. For implementation, restrict the trading universe ex ante to names with marketCap>=1 billion USD and trailing 20-day median(close*volume)>=10 million USD, both measured using information available by t. This differs from endpoint-price/volume-acceptance signals by requiring a robust relative-volume interaction with range location to persist across ten non-shock sessions while mechanically attenuating stocks that have already moved more than 10% over the same period. Before adoption, conduct a redundancy test against idiosyncratic_volume_arrival_information_score, lagged_signed_volume_price_acceptance, lagged_burst_acceptance_resilience_carry, persistent_downside_pressure_amplification, and volume_time_impact_convexity_exhaustion: report daily cross-sectional correlations and test the six-bar return efficacy of S_t residualized cross-sectionally on those signals; do not treat the factor as distinct unless the residualized version retains economically meaningful net-of-cost performance.
