"""A broad, unusually high-participation sector sell-off with low within-sector dispersion is treated as a common liquidity shock rather than as a collection of independent information events. Within that shock, the weakest relative names that remain near their lows are the most likely to have absorbed disproportionate basket, redemption, or inventory-reduction pressure; once this mechanical pressure is completed, they should rebound relative to sector peers over the next six daily bars. The intended distinct component is not standalone close-location or volume pressure, but the synchronized sector-shock gate followed by a within-sector cross-sectional dislocation ranking."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _issuer_event_exclusion(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag the availability/change date and the following two signal dates."""
    event = pd.DataFrame(
        False,
        index=data["close"].index,
        columns=data["close"].columns,
    )
    for field in ("epsActual", "revenueActual", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise"):
        value = data[field]
        prior = value.shift(1)
        changed = value.notna() & (prior.isna() | value.ne(prior))
        event = event | changed.fillna(False)

    return (
        event
        | event.shift(1).fillna(False)
        | event.shift(2).fillna(False)
    ).astype(bool)


def _sector_statistics(
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    abnormal_volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Calculate qualified-sector return, participation, volume, and dispersion.

    A sector observation is recorded only when it has at least ten eligible
    members.  Consequently the later historical-dispersion calculation uses
    only prior daily observations that were themselves tradable sector panels.
    """
    raw_labels = pd.unique(sector.to_numpy().ravel())
    labels = [label for label in raw_labels if pd.notna(label)]
    index = ret.index

    sector_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=labels, dtype=float)
    participation = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=labels, dtype=float)
    median_abvol = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=labels, dtype=float)
    dispersion = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=labels, dtype=float)

    for row_pos, timestamp in enumerate(index):
        row_sector = sector.iloc[row_pos]
        row_eligible = eligible.iloc[row_pos] & row_sector.notna()
        if not bool(row_eligible.any()):
            continue

        members = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "sector": row_sector.loc[row_eligible],
                "return": ret.iloc[row_pos].loc[row_eligible],
                "abvol": abnormal_volume.iloc[row_pos].loc[row_eligible],
            }
        )
        for group_name, group in members.groupby("sector", sort=False):
            if len(group) < 10:
                continue
            sector_return.at[timestamp, group_name] = group["return"].mean()
            participation.at[timestamp, group_name] = (
                ((group["return"] < 0.0) & (group["abvol"] >= 1.5)).mean()
            )
            median_abvol.at[timestamp, group_name] = group["abvol"].median()
            dispersion.at[timestamp, group_name] = group["return"].std(ddof=1)

    return sector_return, participation, median_abvol, dispersion


@register_factor
class SectorShockRelativeAcceptanceContinuation(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-neutral reversal after synchronized sector liquidity shocks."""

    factor_id = "sector_shock_relative_acceptance_continuation"
    name = "Synchronized Sector Shock Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Detects broad, low-dispersion sector sell-offs with elevated volume, "
        "then buys the weakest low-acceptance members and shorts the strongest "
        "members within each shocked sector."
    )
    window_length = 81
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        ret = close.div(prior_close).sub(1.0)

        valid_dollar = close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0)
        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(valid_dollar)
        prior_median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).median()
        abnormal_volume = dollar_volume.div(
            prior_median_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        base_eligible = (
            close.notna()
            & prior_close.notna()
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & prior_close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.notna()
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & close.ge(5.0)
            & prior_median_dollar_volume.notna()
            & prior_median_dollar_volume.gt(0.0)
            & sector.notna()
            & ret.notna()
            & abnormal_volume.notna()
        ).fillna(False)

        sector_return, participation, median_abvol, dispersion = _sector_statistics(
            sector,
            base_eligible,
            ret,
            abnormal_volume,
        )

        qualified_count = sector_return.count(axis=1)
        return_cutoff = sector_return.quantile(0.20, axis=1)
        prior_dispersion_median = dispersion.shift(1).rolling(
            60, min_periods=60
        ).median()

        return_tail = sector_return.le(return_cutoff, axis=0)
        shock_sector = (
            sector_return.lt(0.0)
            & return_tail
            & participation.ge(0.70)
            & median_abvol.ge(1.5)
            & dispersion.le(prior_dispersion_median)
            & prior_dispersion_median.notna()
            & qualified_count.ge(5).to_numpy()[:, None]
        ).fillna(False)

        bar_range = high - low
        valid_hlc = high.notna() & low.notna() & close.notna()
        close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            valid_hlc
        )
        flat_bar = valid_hlc & bar_range.eq(0.0)
        close_location = close_location.where(~flat_bar, 0.5).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        persistent_acceptance = close_location.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()

        event_excluded = _issuer_event_exclusion(data)

        for row_pos, timestamp in enumerate(close.index):
            row_sector = sector.iloc[row_pos]
            row_gate = shock_sector.iloc[row_pos]
            candidate = (
                base_eligible.iloc[row_pos]
                & ~event_excluded.iloc[row_pos]
                & persistent_acceptance.iloc[row_pos].notna()
                & row_sector.notna()
            )
            if not bool(candidate.any()):
                continue

            members = pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "sector": row_sector.loc[candidate],
                    "return": ret.iloc[row_pos].loc[candidate],
                    "acceptance": persistent_acceptance.iloc[row_pos].loc[candidate],
                }
            )

            for group_name, group in members.groupby("sector", sort=False):
                if group_name not in row_gate.index or not bool(row_gate[group_name]):
                    continue

                sector_mean_return = sector_return.at[timestamp, group_name]
                if not np.isfinite(sector_mean_return):
                    continue

                group = group.copy()
                group["relative_return"] = group["return"] - sector_mean_return
                return_rank = group["relative_return"].rank(
                    pct=True, ascending=True, method="average"
                )
                acceptance_rank = group["acceptance"].rank(
                    pct=True, ascending=True, method="average"
                )
                score = 1.0 - 0.5 * (return_rank + acceptance_rank)
                score_rank = score.rank(pct=True, ascending=True, method="average")

                long_names = group.index[score_rank > 0.80]
                short_names = group.index[score_rank <= 0.20]
                if len(long_names) < 2 or len(short_names) < 2:
                    continue

                output.loc[timestamp, long_names] = 1.0 / float(len(long_names))
                output.loc[timestamp, short_names] = -1.0 / float(len(short_names))

        return output
programs.name: Synchronized Sector Shock Reversal
programs.trading_idea: A broad, unusually high-participation sector sell-off with low within-sector dispersion is treated as a common liquidity shock rather than as a collection of independent information events. Within that shock, the weakest relative names that remain near their lows are the most likely to have absorbed disproportionate basket, redemption, or inventory-reduction pressure; once this mechanical pressure is completed, they should rebound relative to sector peers over the next six daily bars. The intended distinct component is not standalone close-location or volume pressure, but the synchronized sector-shock gate followed by a within-sector cross-sectional dislocation ranking.
programs.description: At signal-date close t, define each stock's daily return as close[t]/close[t-1]-1. The base eligible universe contains stocks with non-missing positive closes at t and t-1, non-missing positive volume at t, close[t] >= 5 USD, a valid trailing 20-bar median dollar-volume baseline median(close*volume) over bars t-20 through t-1, and a non-missing static sector label. A stock's abnormal volume is dollar volume[t] divided by that trailing median; stocks without 20 prior valid observations are ineligible. For every sector with at least 10 base-eligible stocks, sector return is the equal-weighted mean member return, broad participation is the fraction of members simultaneously having negative return and abnormal volume >= 1.5, and sector dispersion is the cross-sectional standard deviation of member returns. A sector is a synchronized-shock sector only if: (1) its return is negative and at or below the 20th percentile of contemporaneous qualified-sector returns, with at least five qualified sectors available; (2) broad participation is at least 70%; (3) its median member abnormal volume is at least 1.5; and (4) its current dispersion is no greater than the median of its own prior 60 valid daily dispersion observations. All percentile, median, and historical calculations use only data available through t. Exclude a stock from trading if epsActual, revenueActual, epsSurprise, or revenueSurprise first becomes available or changes relative to the prior bar on any of t, t-1, or t-2; this is a deterministic two-bar post-availability issuer-event exclusion. For remaining members of a synchronized-shock sector, relative return is stock return minus equal-weight sector return. Close location is (close-low)/(high-low), set to 0.5 when high equals low; persistent acceptance is the arithmetic mean close location over t-2 through t, requiring all three observations. Within each qualifying sector, calculate ascending percentile ranks of relative return and persistent acceptance, and define dislocation score as 1 minus one-half times the sum of those two ranks. Go equally dollar-long the highest-score quintile and equally dollar-short the lowest-score quintile, requiring at least two stocks on each side; weight long and short legs equally within each sector to maintain sector neutrality. The signal is formed after the close at t and positions are entered no earlier than the next tradable bar. It must be evaluated as an incremental net-of-cost spread versus sector_basket_volume_residual_repair, persistent_downside_pressure_amplification, lagged_signed_volume_price_acceptance, and downside_volume_stress_amplification, rather than accepted merely on overlapping gross performance.

"""Tax-fragility conditioned industry-support unwind.

Mechanism: tax-led estimate optimism can keep fragile firms relatively supported
through an industry selloff.  Relative price resilience followed by abnormal
participation during that common shock is interpreted as transient support,
whose unwind should be negative over the next several bars.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _cs_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date percentile rank with invalid numerical values removed."""
    return values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)

def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Replicate causal same-date industry medians, with market fallback."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(members) == 0:
            continue
        median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
        out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    market_median = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return out.T.fillna(market_median).T

def _safe_revision(current: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale-free positive-lag revision, robust to zero denominators."""
    previous = current.shift(lag)
    return (current - previous) / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)

@register_factor
class TaxFragilityIndustrySupportUnwind(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'tax_fragility_industry_support_unwind_j'
    name = 'Tax-Fragility Industry Support Unwind'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = 'Shorts tax-led, financially fragile upgrades that retain relative price support and attract abnormal volume during a negative industry impulse.'
    window_length = 42
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'industry', 'epsEstimate', 'revenueEstimate', 'incomeBeforeTax', 'incomeTaxExpense', 'debtToAssets', 'currentRatio', 'interestCoverage']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume']
        industry_labels = data['industry'].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        stock_return = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        industry_return = _group_median(stock_return, industry_labels)
        industry_three_day = industry_return.rolling(4, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = industry_three_day.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.002)
        downside_impulse = (-industry_three_day / industry_scale).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        downside_impulse = downside_impulse.fillna(0.0)
        stock_three_day = stock_return.rolling(4, min_periods=3).sum()
        relative_resilience = stock_three_day - industry_three_day
        prior_resilience = _cs_rank(relative_resilience.shift(1)).fillna(0.5)
        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume >= 0.0))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(14, min_periods=8).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(14, min_periods=8).std().clip(lower=0.05)
        abnormal_participation = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_scale).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        abnormal_participation = abnormal_participation.fillna(0.0)
        eps_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data['epsEstimate'], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        sales_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data['revenueEstimate'], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        tax_rate = data['incomeTaxExpense'] / data['incomeBeforeTax'].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = _cs_rank(tax_rate.shift(44) - tax_rate).fillna(0.5)
        tax_led_upgrade = eps_revision * tax_decline * (1.0 - sales_revision)
        debt = _cs_rank(data['debtToAssets']).fillna(0.5)
        illiquidity = _cs_rank(-data['currentRatio']).fillna(0.5)
        weak_coverage = _cs_rank(-data['interestCoverage']).fillna(0.5)
        fragility = (debt + illiquidity + weak_coverage) / 3.0
        support_sequence = prior_resilience * abnormal_participation
        unwind_risk = tax_led_upgrade * fragility * downside_impulse * support_sequence
        alpha = 0.5 - _cs_rank(unwind_risk).fillna(0.5)
        return alpha.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A tax-led EPS upgrade in a financially fragile company can sustain optimistic relative pricing even when revenue-estimate confirmation is weak. Following a negative industry impulse, a stock that remains relatively resilient and then attracts abnormal participation is likely receiving delayed benchmark or liquidity support rather than revealing durable information; the common shock exposes the fragility of that support. Parent A supplies the shock-propagation and price-then-participation timing state, while Parent B identifies the accounting-quality and balance-sheet state in which apparent support is most vulnerable to a short-horizon unwind.
programs.description: Computes a continuous tax-led-upgrade and financial-fragility state, then identifies stocks showing prior relative resilience and current abnormal volume during a negative industry shock. The returned alpha is the inverse cross-sectional rank of this unwind-risk score, so highly supported fragile names receive negative scores.

"""Industry-stress confirmed post-earnings drift.

Mechanism: fresh earnings news is incorporated more slowly when an industry-wide
selloff competes for investor attention.  A surprise-aligned idiosyncratic price
response with abnormal participation distinguishes informative repricing from
mechanical common-shock flow and extends post-event drift over several bars.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date industry median panel, with market median for unlabelled names."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == group].intersection(values.columns)
        if len(members) > 0:
            median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
            out.loc[:, members] = np.repeat(median.to_numpy()[:, None], len(members), axis=1)
    market = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return out.T.fillna(market).T

def _fresh_signed_surprise(surprise: pd.DataFrame, estimate: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal signed cross-sectional score, nonzero only on fresh report values."""
    prior = surprise.shift(1)
    event = surprise.notna() & (prior.isna() | ((surprise - prior).abs() > 1e-12))
    denom = estimate.abs().where(estimate.abs() >= 0.01, 0.01)
    standardized = (surprise / denom).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    eligible = event & standardized.notna()
    count = eligible.sum(axis=1)
    percentile = standardized.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    score = (2.0 * percentile - 1.0).where(eligible, 0.0)
    return score.where(count >= 8, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

@register_factor
class FreshSurpriseIndustryStressConfirmationDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'fresh_surprise_industry_stress_confirmation_drif'
    name = 'Industry-Stress Confirmed Surprise Drift'
    category = 'momentum'
    description = "Signed fresh EPS surprises, activated during negative industry shocks only when the stock's residual response agrees with the surprise and volume confirms participation."
    window_length = 42
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'industry', 'epsSurprise', 'epsEstimate']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume'].reindex_like(close)
        surprise = data['epsSurprise'].reindex_like(close)
        estimate = data['epsEstimate'].reindex_like(close)
        labels = data['industry'].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        event_score = _fresh_signed_surprise(surprise, estimate)
        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        stock_ret = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        industry_ret = _group_median(stock_ret, labels)
        industry_move = industry_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = industry_move.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.002)
        downside_state = (-industry_move / industry_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0) / 3.0
        residual_move = stock_ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum() - industry_ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        residual_scale = residual_move.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.003)
        aligned_response = (np.sign(event_score) * residual_move / residual_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        aligned_response = (aligned_response / 3.0).fillna(0.0)
        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume >= 0.0))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).std().clip(lower=0.05)
        participation = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        participation = (participation / 3.0).fillna(0.0)
        signal = event_score * downside_state * aligned_response * participation
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Industry-Stress Confirmed Surprise Drift
programs.trading_idea: A fresh earnings surprise is more informative when it arrives during a negative industry impulse: common-shock selling creates a benchmark-driven attention constraint, while an aligned idiosyncratic price response identifies the firm-specific information that is escaping that pressure. Abnormal participation is used as confirmation that the relative move reflects informed repricing rather than a mechanically thin quote. Neither parent has this interaction alone: the surprise supplies signed fundamental news, while the industry-shock, relative-resilience, and volume state selectively extends drift into the fixed six-bar horizon.
programs.description: On fresh EPS-surprise events, the factor takes the cross-sectional signed standardized surprise and weights it by a negative industry-shock state, surprise-aligned residual price response, and abnormal volume confirmation. Positive confirmed surprises receive positive values and negative confirmed surprises receive negative values.

from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _group_panel(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame, minimum_members: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal cross-sectional group mean and dispersion for each name."""
    mean_out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    disp_out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for i in range(len(values.index)):
        row_labels = labels.iloc[i]
        row_values = values.iloc[i]
        valid = row_labels.notna() & row_values.notna()
        if not bool(valid.any()):
            continue
        frame = pd.DataFrame({'label': row_labels.loc[valid], 'value': row_values.loc[valid]})
        for label, group in frame.groupby('label', sort=False):
            if len(group) < minimum_members:
                continue
            members = group.index
            mean_out.loc[values.index[i], members] = group['value'].mean()
            disp_out.loc[values.index[i], members] = group['value'].std(ddof=1)
    return (mean_out, disp_out)

def _group_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise percentile rank within the contemporaneous sector."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for i in range(len(values.index)):
        row_labels = labels.iloc[i]
        row_values = values.iloc[i]
        valid = row_labels.notna() & row_values.notna()
        if not bool(valid.any()):
            continue
        frame = pd.DataFrame({'label': row_labels.loc[valid], 'value': row_values.loc[valid]})
        for _, group in frame.groupby('label', sort=False):
            if len(group) < 5:
                continue
            out.loc[values.index[i], group.index] = group['value'].rank(pct=True, method='average')
    return out

@register_factor
class SynchronizedSupportFailureCascade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'synchronized_support_failure_cascade_j'
    name = 'Synchronized Support-Failure Cascade'
    category = 'momentum'
    description = 'Ranks failed relative shelters during broad, high-participation sector liquidations; high values indicate likely downside continuation.'
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        high = data['high']
        low = data['low']
        volume = data['volume']
        sector = data['sector']
        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        ret = close.div(prior_close).sub(1.0).where(close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0))
        sector_ret, sector_dispersion = _group_panel(ret, sector, 10)
        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0))
        prior_dollar = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=15).median()
        abnormal_volume = dollar_volume.div(prior_dollar.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        negative_participation = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for i in range(len(close.index)):
            row_sector = sector.iloc[i]
            row_ret = ret.iloc[i]
            row_abvol = abnormal_volume.iloc[i]
            valid = row_sector.notna() & row_ret.notna() & row_abvol.notna()
            if not bool(valid.any()):
                continue
            frame = pd.DataFrame({'sector': row_sector.loc[valid], 'ret': row_ret.loc[valid], 'abvol': row_abvol.loc[valid]})
            for _, group in frame.groupby('sector', sort=False):
                if len(group) < 10:
                    continue
                share = ((group['ret'] < 0.0) & (group['abvol'] >= 1.25)).mean()
                negative_participation.loc[close.index[i], group.index] = share
        sector_scale = sector_ret.shift(1).rolling(18, min_periods=12).std().clip(lower=0.003)
        prior_dispersion = sector_dispersion.shift(1).rolling(43, min_periods=25).median()
        common_shock = (sector_ret.le(-sector_scale) & negative_participation.ge(0.65) & sector_dispersion.le(prior_dispersion) & prior_dispersion.notna()).fillna(False)
        prior_stock_move = ret.rolling(4, min_periods=3).sum().shift(2)
        prior_sector_move = sector_ret.rolling(4, min_periods=3).sum().shift(2)
        prior_resilience = _group_rank(prior_stock_move - prior_sector_move, sector)
        fresh_stock_move = ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        fresh_sector_move = sector_ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        fresh_relative_break = _group_rank(-(fresh_stock_move - fresh_sector_move), sector)
        bar_range = high - low
        location = (close - low).div(bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        flat = high.eq(low) & high.notna() & low.notna()
        location = location.where(~flat, 0.5).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        low_acceptance = _group_rank(-location.rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean(), sector)
        volume_pressure = abnormal_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).div(3.0)
        raw = prior_resilience * fresh_relative_break * low_acceptance * volume_pressure
        signal = raw.where(common_shock, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: A synchronized, high-participation sector sell-off is first classified as a common liquidity shock rather than issuer-specific news. Within that state, the signal identifies names that had been relatively sheltered before the shock but now suffer an unusually sharp relative break, close near the low, and trade on abnormal volume; this transition indicates that prior support or inventory capacity has failed, leaving unfinished forced selling and negative continuation. Parent A captures oversold names likely to rebound, while Parent B's failure concept lacked a clean common-flow origin; conditioning support failure on a coherent sector liquidation separates genuine exhaustion from a late-stage cascade.

"""Tax-fragility phase-locked industry-shock continuation.

Mechanism: after a common industry downside impulse, a tax-led and cash-quality
fragile issuer that first resists the shock and subsequently receives abnormal
participation can face a persistent supply-absorption imbalance.  The signed
price-volume phase area distinguishes this sequential absorption from ordinary
same-bar turnover.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile ranks after removing numerical infinities."""
    return values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _industry_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date industry median, with the cross-sectional median as fallback."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(members) > 0:
            med = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
            output.loc[:, members] = np.tile(med.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    market_med = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return output.T.fillna(market_med).T


def _revision(current: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal, scale-free estimate revision with protected denominators."""
    previous = current.shift(lag)
    return (current - previous) / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _phase_area(price_channel: pd.DataFrame, flow_channel: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing signed area of a two-channel path.

    Positive values arise when relative-price movement tends to lead subsequent
    participation, rather than both channels moving as a contemporaneous burst.
    All lags are positive, so the transform is causal.
    """
    increment = (
        price_channel.shift(1) * flow_channel
        - flow_channel.shift(1) * price_channel
    )
    return increment.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()


@register_factor
class TaxFragilityPhaseLockedShockContinuation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "tax_fragility_phase_locked_shock_continuation"
    name = "Tax-Fragility Phase-Locked Shock Continuation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Long tax-led, weak-cash-quality leveraged firms whose relative-price "
        "resilience leads abnormal participation during an industry downside shock."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "incomeQuality",
        "debtToAssets",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        log_close = np.log(close.where(close > 0.0))
        stock_ret = log_close.diff()
        industry_ret = _industry_median(stock_ret, labels)
        relative_ret = stock_ret - industry_ret

        industry_move = industry_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = (
            industry_move.shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=15).std().clip(lower=0.002)
        )
        downside_shock = (-industry_move / industry_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        downside_shock = downside_shock.fillna(0.0)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume >= 0.0))
        vol_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        vol_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.05)
        volume_surprise = ((log_volume - vol_mean) / vol_std).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        volume_surprise = volume_surprise.fillna(0.0)

        relative_resilience = _cs_rank(
            relative_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().shift(1)
        ).fillna(0.5)
        phase_lead = _cs_rank(_phase_area(relative_ret.fillna(0.0), volume_surprise, 4)).fillna(0.5)
        participation = _cs_rank(volume_surprise.clip(lower=0.0)).fillna(0.5)

        eps_upgrade = _cs_rank(_revision(data["epsEstimate"], 63)).fillna(0.5)
        revenue_upgrade = _cs_rank(_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], 63)).fillna(0.5)
        tax_rate = data["incomeTaxExpense"] / data["incomeBeforeTax"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = _cs_rank(tax_rate.shift(63) - tax_rate).fillna(0.5)
        tax_led_state = eps_upgrade * tax_decline * (1.0 - revenue_upgrade)

        poor_cash_quality = _cs_rank(-data["incomeQuality"]).fillna(0.5)
        leverage = _cs_rank(data["debtToAssets"]).fillna(0.5)
        fragility_state = tax_led_state * poor_cash_quality * leverage

        absorption_sequence = relative_resilience * phase_lead * participation
        score = downside_shock * fragility_state * absorption_sequence
        alpha = _cs_rank(score).fillna(0.5) - 0.5
        return alpha.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

"""A negative industry shock can force indiscriminate selling, but financially constrained firms with recently improving operating-cash-flow coverage of interest expense may be better able to absorb the shock than similarly leveraged peers. The required sequence—industry drawdown, stock-specific resilience during that drawdown, then elevated participation after the shock—targets names where demand persists after common-shock selling rather than treating an EPS revision as evidence of tax relief. This replaces the unsupported tax-cash-shield claim with an observable debt-service-capacity mechanism using point-in-time operating cash flow and interest expense."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_shock_panel(
    stock_returns: pd.DataFrame,
    industry_labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Map valid equal-weighted industry returns and shock flags back to stocks.

    Industry membership is static.  The aggregation only uses returns observed
    at the current bar and requires five valid constituent returns, preventing
    thin industries from creating spurious common-shock classifications.
    """
    grouped = stock_returns.T.groupby(industry_labels, sort=False)
    industry_return = grouped.mean().T
    industry_count = grouped.count().T
    valid_industry_return = industry_return.where(industry_count >= 5)

    shock_cutoff = valid_industry_return.quantile(0.20, axis=1)
    industry_shock = valid_industry_return.le(shock_cutoff, axis=0)

    mapped_return = valid_industry_return.reindex(columns=industry_labels.to_numpy())
    mapped_return.columns = stock_returns.columns
    mapped_shock = industry_shock.reindex(columns=industry_labels.to_numpy())
    mapped_shock.columns = stock_returns.columns

    return mapped_return, mapped_shock.fillna(False)


@register_factor
class IndustryShockCashcoverageAccumulation(BaseFactor):
    """Select resilient, cash-coverage-improving firms after industry selling."""

    factor_id = "industry_shock_cashcoverage_accumulation"
    name = "Industry-Shock Cash-Coverage Selection"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Ranks financially constrained firms that outperform during a valid "
        "five-member industry drawdown, attract post-shock volume, and show "
        "improving operating-cash-flow interest coverage while filtering tax "
        "rate and estimate-revision effects."
    )
    window_length = 64
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "debtToEquity",
        "currentRatio",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "interestExpense",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        # r_i = close[t-2] / close[t-7] - 1, deliberately ending before the
        # t-1 through t participation measurement interval.
        shock_return = close.shift(2) / close.shift(7).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0

        # Industry is static in this feed, so the first row is the causal
        # membership assignment for all subsequent daily observations.
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        industry_return, industry_shock = _industry_shock_panel(
            shock_return,
            industry_labels,
        )
        relative_resilience = shock_return - industry_return

        # Current two-bar volume is measured strictly after the drawdown return
        # endpoint; the trailing baseline covers t-22 through t-3 inclusive.
        current_volume = volume.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean()
        baseline_volume = volume.shift(3).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        abnormal_volume = (
            current_volume / baseline_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        )

        dollar_volume = close * volume
        baseline_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.shift(3).rolling(
            20,
            min_periods=20,
        ).mean()
        dollar_volume_median = baseline_dollar_volume.quantile(0.50, axis=1)
        liquid_enough = baseline_dollar_volume.ge(dollar_volume_median, axis=0)

        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"]
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"]
        high_debt = debt_to_equity.ge(debt_to_equity.quantile(0.75, axis=1), axis=0)
        low_liquidity = current_ratio.le(current_ratio.quantile(0.50, axis=1), axis=0)

        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]
        interest_expense = data["interestExpense"]
        pretax_income = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        cash_interest_coverage = operating_cash_flow / interest_expense.abs().replace(
            0.0,
            np.nan,
        )
        prior_coverage = cash_interest_coverage.shift(63)
        coverage_improvement = (
            cash_interest_coverage / prior_coverage.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        )
        cash_coverage_valid = (
            (operating_cash_flow > 0.0)
            & (interest_expense > 0.0)
            & (pretax_income > 0.0)
            & (cash_interest_coverage > 0.0)
            & prior_coverage.notna()
            & (coverage_improvement > 0.0)
        )

        effective_tax_rate = data["incomeTaxExpense"] / pretax_income.replace(
            0.0,
            np.nan,
        )
        tax_rate_change = (effective_tax_rate - effective_tax_rate.shift(63)).abs()
        tax_change_cutoff = tax_rate_change.quantile(0.75, axis=1)
        stable_tax_rate = (
            effective_tax_rate.notna()
            & effective_tax_rate.shift(63).notna()
            & tax_rate_change.le(tax_change_cutoff, axis=0)
        )

        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        prior_eps_estimate = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        prior_revenue_estimate = revenue_estimate.shift(21)
        eps_revision = (
            (eps_estimate - prior_eps_estimate)
            / prior_eps_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        )
        revenue_revision = (
            (revenue_estimate - prior_revenue_estimate)
            / prior_revenue_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        )
        eps_revision_cutoff = eps_revision.abs().quantile(0.75, axis=1)
        revenue_revision_cutoff = revenue_revision.abs().quantile(0.75, axis=1)
        quiet_estimates = (
            eps_estimate.notna()
            & prior_eps_estimate.notna()
            & revenue_estimate.notna()
            & prior_revenue_estimate.notna()
            & eps_revision.abs().le(eps_revision_cutoff, axis=0)
            & revenue_revision.abs().le(revenue_revision_cutoff, axis=0)
        )

        cash_flow_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"]
        eligible = (
            industry_shock
            & (relative_resilience > 0.0)
            & (abnormal_volume > 0.25)
            & liquid_enough
            & high_debt
            & low_liquidity
            & cash_coverage_valid
            & stable_tax_rate
            & quiet_estimates
            & cash_flow_growth.notna()
        )

        score = (
            rank(relative_resilience)
            + rank(abnormal_volume)
            + rank(coverage_improvement)
            + rank(cash_flow_growth)
        ) / 4.0

        return score.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A negative industry shock can force indiscriminate selling, but financially constrained firms with recently improving operating-cash-flow coverage of interest expense may be better able to absorb the shock than similarly leveraged peers. The required sequence—industry drawdown, stock-specific resilience during that drawdown, then elevated participation after the shock—targets names where demand persists after common-shock selling rather than treating an EPS revision as evidence of tax relief. This replaces the unsupported tax-cash-shield claim with an observable debt-service-capacity mechanism using point-in-time operating cash flow and interest expense.
programs.description: All quantities are computed after the final required daily bar t has completed, and orders are submitted no earlier than the next bar, t+1, for the fixed six-bar holding horizon. Define each stock's shock-window return as r_i = close_t-2 / close_t-7 - 1 and its industry return as the equal-weighted mean r_i among valid members of its industry, requiring at least five members. An industry is in shock when this industry return is at or below the cross-sectional 20th percentile of industry returns. Relative resilience is RR_i = r_i minus its industry return; require RR_i > 0. The post-shock participation measure is AV_i = mean(volume_i from t-1 through t) / mean(volume_i from t-22 through t-3) - 1; require AV_i > 0.25, so resilience is measured before abnormal volume rather than contemporaneously with it. Require prior 20-bar average dollar volume, mean(close*volume from t-22 through t-3), to be at least the cross-sectional median, limiting exposure to the least tradable stressed names. Financial-constraint eligibility requires debtToEquity at or above the cross-sectional 75th percentile and currentRatio at or below the median. Define cash interest coverage CIC_i = operatingCashFlow_i / abs(interestExpense_i), requiring positive operatingCashFlow, positive interestExpense, positive incomeBeforeTax, and valid current and t-63 values. Require CIC_i > 0 and CIC_i / CIC_i,t-63 - 1 > 0. To avoid relabeling tax-accounting effects as cash-flow improvement, compute the reported effective-tax-rate proxy ETR_i = incomeTaxExpense_i / incomeBeforeTax_i and exclude names whose abs(ETR_i - ETR_i,t-63) is above the cross-sectional 75th percentile; deferred-tax, valuation-allowance, and specifically identified one-off tax effects cannot be separately identified with the available fields and are therefore not used as a positive signal. EPS and revenue estimates are used only as an anti-overlap filter, not as a return predictor: define 21-bar revisions EPSRev_i = (epsEstimate_i - epsEstimate_i,t-21) / max(abs(epsEstimate_i,t-21), 0.01) and RevRev_i = (revenueEstimate_i - revenueEstimate_i,t-21) / max(abs(revenueEstimate_i,t-21), 0.01), require valid observations, and exclude names for which either absolute revision exceeds its cross-sectional 75th percentile. Among eligible names in shocked industries, the long score is the equal-weighted average of cross-sectional percentile ranks of RR_i, AV_i, CIC improvement, and operatingCashFlowGrowth; buy the highest-score names. This is formula-level distinct from the named tax-fragility and tax-revision factors: it has no positive tax-led EPS or weak-revenue-revision residual, explicitly filters large estimate revisions and unstable reported tax rates, and requires the ordered industry-shock -> relative-resilience -> post-shock-volume sequence.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _group_panel(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_members: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal cross-sectional group mean and dispersion for each name."""
    mean_out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    disp_out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for i in range(len(values.index)):
        row_labels = labels.iloc[i]
        row_values = values.iloc[i]
        valid = row_labels.notna() & row_values.notna()
        if not bool(valid.any()):
            continue
        frame = pd.DataFrame({"label": row_labels.loc[valid], "value": row_values.loc[valid]})
        for label, group in frame.groupby("label", sort=False):
            if len(group) < minimum_members:
                continue
            members = group.index
            mean_out.loc[values.index[i], members] = group["value"].mean()
            disp_out.loc[values.index[i], members] = group["value"].std(ddof=1)
    return mean_out, disp_out


def _group_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise percentile rank within the contemporaneous sector."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for i in range(len(values.index)):
        row_labels = labels.iloc[i]
        row_values = values.iloc[i]
        valid = row_labels.notna() & row_values.notna()
        if not bool(valid.any()):
            continue
        frame = pd.DataFrame({"label": row_labels.loc[valid], "value": row_values.loc[valid]})
        for _, group in frame.groupby("label", sort=False):
            if len(group) < 5:
                continue
            out.loc[values.index[i], group.index] = group["value"].rank(pct=True, method="average")
    return out


@register_factor
class SynchronizedSupportFailureCascade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "synchronized_support_failure_cascade"
    name = "Synchronized Support-Failure Cascade"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks failed relative shelters during broad, high-participation sector "
        "liquidations; high values indicate likely downside continuation."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        ret = close.div(prior_close).sub(1.0).where(close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0))
        sector_ret, sector_dispersion = _group_panel(ret, sector, 10)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0))
        prior_dollar = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        abnormal_volume = dollar_volume.div(prior_dollar.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        negative_participation = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for i in range(len(close.index)):
            row_sector = sector.iloc[i]
            row_ret = ret.iloc[i]
            row_abvol = abnormal_volume.iloc[i]
            valid = row_sector.notna() & row_ret.notna() & row_abvol.notna()
            if not bool(valid.any()):
                continue
            frame = pd.DataFrame(
                {"sector": row_sector.loc[valid], "ret": row_ret.loc[valid], "abvol": row_abvol.loc[valid]}
            )
            for _, group in frame.groupby("sector", sort=False):
                if len(group) < 10:
                    continue
                share = ((group["ret"] < 0.0) & (group["abvol"] >= 1.25)).mean()
                negative_participation.loc[close.index[i], group.index] = share

        sector_scale = sector_ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).std().clip(lower=0.003)
        prior_dispersion = sector_dispersion.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=25).median()
        common_shock = (
            sector_ret.le(-sector_scale)
            & negative_participation.ge(0.65)
            & sector_dispersion.le(prior_dispersion)
            & prior_dispersion.notna()
        ).fillna(False)

        prior_stock_move = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().shift(2)
        prior_sector_move = sector_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().shift(2)
        prior_resilience = _group_rank(prior_stock_move - prior_sector_move, sector)

        fresh_stock_move = ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        fresh_sector_move = sector_ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        fresh_relative_break = _group_rank(-(fresh_stock_move - fresh_sector_move), sector)

        bar_range = high - low
        location = (close - low).div(bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        flat = high.eq(low) & high.notna() & low.notna()
        location = location.where(~flat, 0.5).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        low_acceptance = _group_rank(-location.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean(), sector)

        volume_pressure = abnormal_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).div(3.0)
        raw = prior_resilience * fresh_relative_break * low_acceptance * volume_pressure
        signal = raw.where(common_shock, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: A synchronized, high-participation sector sell-off is first classified as a common liquidity shock rather than issuer-specific news. Within that state, the signal identifies names that had been relatively sheltered before the shock but now suffer an unusually sharp relative break, close near the low, and trade on abnormal volume; this transition indicates that prior support or inventory capacity has failed, leaving unfinished forced selling and negative continuation. Parent A captures oversold names likely to rebound, while Parent B's failure concept lacked a clean common-flow origin; conditioning support failure on a coherent sector liquidation separates genuine exhaustion from a late-stage cascade.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].intersection(values.columns)
        if len(members) < minimum:
            continue
        median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    return out


def _sector_coherence(ret: pd.DataFrame, sector_ret: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].intersection(ret.columns)
        if len(members) < 5:
            continue
        sector_move = sector_ret.loc[:, members].iloc[:, 0]
        agreement = ret.loc[:, members].fillna(0.0).mul(sector_move, axis=0).gt(0.0).mean(axis=1)
        out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(agreement.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    return out


def _leave_one_out_industry_return(
    trailing_return: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    peer_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=trailing_return.index, columns=trailing_return.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=trailing_return.index, columns=trailing_return.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].intersection(trailing_return.columns)
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        group = trailing_return.loc[:, members]
        valid = group.notna()
        total = group.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        for ticker in members:
            own_valid = valid[ticker].astype(float)
            other_count = count - own_valid
            other_sum = total - group[ticker].fillna(0.0)
            peer_return.loc[:, ticker] = (other_sum / other_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(other_count.ge(5.0))
            peer_count.loc[:, ticker] = other_count
    return peer_return, peer_count


@register_factor
class StaleUpgradeSectorUnpaidTransmissionFade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "stale_upgrade_sector_unpaid_transmission_fade"
    name = "Stale Upgrade Sector-Transmission Fade"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Fresh EPS-only upgrades after an inactive consensus spell, ranked only when "
        "prior industry leadership meets a coherent sector downside shock and an unpaid "
        "positive sector residual. High scores are expected to fade."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector", "industry", "epsEstimate", "revenueEstimate"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].where(data["volume"] >= 0.0)
        eps = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue = data["revenueEstimate"]
        columns = close.columns
        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0].reindex(columns)
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(columns)

        ret = np.log(close).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector_ret = _group_median(ret, sector_labels, 5)
        coherence = _sector_coherence(ret, sector_ret, sector_labels)

        sector_scale = sector_ret.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().clip(lower=0.0005)
        sector_z = (sector_ret / sector_scale).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        downside_impulse = ((-sector_z - 0.75) / 2.25).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
        coherence_gate = ((coherence - 0.60) / 0.30).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        lagged_stock = ret.shift(1)
        lagged_sector = sector_ret.shift(1)
        sector_var = lagged_sector.rolling(60, min_periods=30).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = lagged_stock.rolling(60, min_periods=30).cov(lagged_sector) / sector_var
        beta_gate = (beta.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.5) / 0.8).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        residual = ret - beta * sector_ret
        residual_scale = residual.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.0005)
        unpaid_residual = (residual / residual_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0) / 3.0

        previous_eps = eps.shift(1)
        eps_revision = (eps - previous_eps) / previous_eps.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        unchanged = eps.notna() & previous_eps.notna() & eps.eq(previous_eps)
        inactive_before_update = unchanged.shift(1).astype(float).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().eq(20.0)
        fresh_upgrade = eps.notna() & previous_eps.notna() & eps_revision.ge(0.02)

        previous_revenue = revenue.shift(1)
        revenue_revision = (revenue - previous_revenue) / previous_revenue.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        revenue_nonconfirmation = (
            revenue.notna() & previous_revenue.notna() & revenue_revision.le(0.0)
        )

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        old_close = close.shift(21)
        valid_prices = prior_close.gt(0.0) & old_close.gt(0.0)
        trailing_return = ((prior_close / old_close) - 1.0).where(valid_prices)
        industry_return, peer_count = _leave_one_out_industry_return(trailing_return, industry_labels)
        relative_lead = trailing_return - industry_return
        lead_strength = rank(relative_lead).fillna(0.0)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume)
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        volume_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.05)
        participation = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_std).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0) / 3.0

        eligible = (
            fresh_upgrade
            & inactive_before_update
            & revenue_nonconfirmation
            & valid_prices
            & industry_return.notna()
            & peer_count.ge(5.0)
        )
        upgrade_strength = (eps_revision.clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.20) / 0.20).fillna(0.0)
        raw_risk = (
            upgrade_strength
            * lead_strength
            * downside_impulse
            * coherence_gate
            * beta_gate
            * unpaid_residual
            * (0.5 + 0.5 * participation)
        )
        risk_rank = raw_risk.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return risk_rank.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Stale Upgrade Sector-Transmission Fade
programs.trading_idea: A delayed EPS-only upgrade after prior relative price leadership is prone to analyst extrapolation, but it becomes materially more bearish when a coherent sector selloff supplies a common-information catalyst that the stock has not yet fully absorbed. The child targets high-beta names whose sector-residual return remains unusually supported during that downside impulse, making the stale upgrade a temporary excuse for delayed sector-risk transmission rather than independent good news. Parent A identifies the direction and unpaid common-shock exposure, while Parent B identifies the behavioural state in which that residual support is least credible.
programs.description: Ranks fresh positive EPS-only upgrades following a long inactive consensus spell, conditional on pre-event industry leadership, a coherent negative sector impulse, positive sector beta, and an unusually positive current sector residual. Higher values identify names expected to fade as sector repricing catches up.

"""This is a reduced-form volume-conditioned continuation signal, not an identified measure of metaorders, aggressive signed flow, or Hawkes self-excitation. Recent same-direction return-volume shocks that accelerate relative to their slower baseline may indicate persistent trading pressure, but only when the associated three-day price displacement has been modest. The economic claim is empirical: underreaction or gradual information diffusion can produce continuation over the subsequent six trading days, whereas liquidity replenishment, event reversals, and transient auction-driven volume can cause failure."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _positive_finite(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a finite, strictly-positive availability mask."""
    return df.gt(0.0) & np.isfinite(df)


def _zero_initialized_ewm(impulse: pd.DataFrame, alpha: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Recursive EWM with a zero state before the first calendar bar.

    This differs from pandas' default EWM initialization, whose first value is
    the first observation rather than alpha times the first observation.
    """
    values = impulse.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    values = np.nan_to_num(values, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    state = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    previous = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    decay = 1.0 - alpha
    for row in range(n_rows):
        previous = decay * previous + alpha * values[row, :]
        state[row, :] = previous

    return pd.DataFrame(state, index=impulse.index, columns=impulse.columns)


@register_factor
class SelfExcitationCompensatorPriceGap(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks accelerating directional volume pressure not yet reflected in price."""

    factor_id = "self_excitation_compensator_price_gap"
    name = "Volume-Conditioned Continuation Gap"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional percentile rank of accelerated signed volume-surprise "
        "intensity, attenuated when its directional three-day price move has "
        "already occurred and restricted to liquid, valid observations."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        close_ok = _positive_finite(close)
        previous_close_ok = _positive_finite(previous_close)
        volume_ok = _positive_finite(volume)

        price_ratio = close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        raw_return = np.log(price_ratio)
        valid = (
            close_ok
            & previous_close_ok
            & volume_ok
            & np.isfinite(raw_return)
            & raw_return.abs().le(np.log(1.5))
        )

        # Invalid price observations deliberately contribute zero impulse.
        ret = raw_return.clip(lower=-0.20, upper=0.20).where(valid, 0.0)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).where(volume.shift(1).gt(0.0))
        prior_volume_count = prior_volume.notna().rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
        volume_median = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        volume_baseline_available = prior_volume_count.eq(20.0) & volume_median.gt(0.0)

        log_volume_surprise = np.log(volume / volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        volume_surprise = (
            log_volume_surprise.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
            .where(valid & volume_baseline_available, 0.0)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )

        signed_impulse = np.sign(ret) * volume_surprise
        positive_impulse = signed_impulse.clip(lower=0.0)
        negative_impulse = (-signed_impulse).clip(lower=0.0)

        fast_positive = _zero_initialized_ewm(positive_impulse, 0.50)
        slow_positive = _zero_initialized_ewm(positive_impulse, 0.125)
        fast_negative = _zero_initialized_ewm(negative_impulse, 0.50)
        slow_negative = _zero_initialized_ewm(negative_impulse, 0.125)

        intensity_positive = (fast_positive - slow_positive).clip(lower=0.0)
        intensity_negative = (fast_negative - slow_negative).clip(lower=0.0)
        net_intensity = intensity_positive - intensity_negative

        displacement = ret + ret.shift(1).fillna(0.0) + ret.shift(2).fillna(0.0)
        prior_abs_return = ret.abs().shift(1)
        amplitude = prior_abs_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median().clip(lower=0.002)

        directional_displacement = (
            np.sign(net_intensity) * displacement / (3.0 * amplitude.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        )
        attenuation = directional_displacement.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        raw_score = net_intensity * (1.0 - attenuation)

        prior_valid_count = valid.rolling(60, min_periods=60).sum()
        valid_history = prior_valid_count.eq(60.0)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close_ok & volume_ok)
        prior_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.shift(1)
        prior_dollar_count = prior_dollar_volume.notna().rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
        dollar_volume_median = prior_dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        liquid = prior_dollar_count.eq(20.0) & dollar_volume_median.gt(1_000_000.0)

        eligible = (
            _positive_finite(market_cap)
            & valid
            & valid_history
            & volume_baseline_available
            & amplitude.notna()
            & liquid
            & np.isfinite(raw_score)
        )

        eligible_score = raw_score.where(eligible)
        lower = eligible_score.quantile(0.025, axis=1)
        upper = eligible_score.quantile(0.975, axis=1)
        winsorized = eligible_score.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)

        return winsorized.rank(axis=1, pct=True, ascending=True).where(eligible)

programs.trading_idea: This is a reduced-form volume-conditioned continuation signal, not an identified measure of metaorders, aggressive signed flow, or Hawkes self-excitation. Recent same-direction return-volume shocks that accelerate relative to their slower baseline may indicate persistent trading pressure, but only when the associated three-day price displacement has been modest. The economic claim is empirical: underreaction or gradual information diffusion can produce continuation over the subsequent six trading days, whereas liquidity replenishment, event reversals, and transient auction-driven volume can cause failure.
programs.description: At daily close t, use only bars through t. Define raw log return rRaw_t = log(close_t / close_{t-1}). A bar is valid when close_t, close_{t-1}, and volume_t are positive and finite and abs(rRaw_t) <= log(1.5); the last condition conservatively removes likely split, corporate-action, or unusable price-discontinuity observations. Define r_t = clip(rRaw_t, -0.20, 0.20) on valid bars and 0 otherwise; zero returns therefore produce zero signed impulse. Let VMed_t be the rolling median of volume over bars t-20 through t-1, requiring all 20 observations to be positive and finite. Define the clipped positive log-volume surprise v_t = clip(log(volume_t / VMed_t), 0, 3) when valid and VMed_t is available, otherwise 0. The signed impulse is u_t = sign(r_t) * v_t, with sign(0) = 0. Set p_t = max(u_t, 0) and n_t = max(-u_t, 0). For every ticker, recursively update four causal EWM states on every calendar bar, treating unavailable impulses as zero: Fplus_t = (1-0.50)*Fplus_{t-1} + 0.50*p_t; Splus_t = (1-0.125)*Splus_{t-1} + 0.125*p_t; Fminus_t = (1-0.50)*Fminus_{t-1} + 0.50*n_t; Sminus_t = (1-0.125)*Sminus_{t-1} + 0.125*n_t. These correspond to fixed EWM spans of 3 and 15 bars, respectively, and all states are initialized to zero before the first available bar. Define positive directional acceleration states Iplus_t = max(Fplus_t - Splus_t, 0) and Iminus_t = max(Fminus_t - Sminus_t, 0), and net directional intensity I_t = Iplus_t - Iminus_t. Define a trailing realized-price displacement M_t = r_t + r_{t-1} + r_{t-2}. Let A_t be the median of abs(r) over t-20 through t-1, floored at 0.002. Define directional displacement D_t = sign(I_t) * M_t / (3*A_t), with sign(0)=0, and attenuation H_t = clip(D_t, 0, 1). The raw continuation score is Score_t = I_t * (1-H_t): accelerated directional volume shocks receive their directional sign, while price movement already aligned with that direction attenuates the score; no future bar is used. The eligible universe at t contains tickers with positive marketCap, valid current data, 60 consecutive valid close/volume bars through t, available 20-bar baselines, and prior-20-bar median dollar volume median(close*volume) greater than USD 1,000,000. No corporate-action metadata or adjusted-price field is available, so the stated discontinuity filter is the conservative in-scope treatment. Within the eligible universe, winsorize raw scores at the cross-sectional 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles and convert them to ascending cross-sectional percentile ranks; higher rank is more bullish. Compute the signal after close t, enter no earlier than open t+1, and define the six-bar realized target as open_{t+7} / open_{t+1} - 1, corresponding to entry at the next executable open and exit six daily-bar intervals later. A long-short implementation buys the highest-ranked names and shorts the lowest-ranked names subject to separate turnover, borrow, spread, and impact controls.

"""Peer-ignited self-excitation: local flow acceleration after an industry impulse.

Mechanism: an industry volume shock is informative only when it recruits a target's
own same-direction, accelerating volume-pressure process.  The interaction separates
propagating execution demand from broad industry shocks that may otherwise reverse.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _broadcast_industry_sum(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally broadcast a same-date static-industry sum to each constituent."""
    grouped = frame.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum(min_count=1).T
    result = grouped.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy())
    result.columns = frame.columns
    return result


@register_factor
class PeerIgnitedSelfExcitationGap(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks unfinished local flow acceleration confirmed by industry peers."""

    factor_id = "peer_ignited_self_excitation_gap"
    name = "Peer-Ignited Flow Acceleration Gap"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks unfinished signed volume-pressure acceleration only when a "
        "leave-one-out industry volume shock agrees with the target's local flow."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        label_available = pd.DataFrame(
            np.broadcast_to(labels.notna().to_numpy(), close.shape),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_bar = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & previous_close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
        )
        ret = np.log(close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        ret = ret.clip(lower=-0.20, upper=0.20).where(valid_bar, 0.0)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).where(volume.shift(1).gt(0.0))
        volume_count = prior_volume.notna().rolling(15, min_periods=15).sum()
        volume_base = prior_volume.rolling(15, min_periods=15).median()
        volume_ready = volume_count.eq(15.0) & volume_base.gt(0.0)
        volume_surprise = np.log(volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        volume_surprise = volume_surprise.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        volume_surprise = volume_surprise.where(valid_bar & volume_ready, 0.0)

        signed_impulse = np.sign(ret) * volume_surprise
        positive = signed_impulse.clip(lower=0.0)
        negative = (-signed_impulse).clip(lower=0.0)
        fast = positive.ewm(alpha=0.50, adjust=False).mean() - negative.ewm(
            alpha=0.50, adjust=False
        ).mean()
        slow = positive.ewm(alpha=0.125, adjust=False).mean() - negative.ewm(
            alpha=0.125, adjust=False
        ).mean()
        local_acceleration = fast - slow

        market_return = ret.where(valid_bar & label_available).median(axis=1)
        excess_return = ret.sub(market_return, axis=0)
        peer_mark = (excess_return * volume_surprise).where(valid_bar & volume_ready)
        industry_sum = _broadcast_industry_sum(peer_mark, labels)
        industry_count = _broadcast_industry_sum(
            peer_mark.notna().astype(float), labels
        )
        peer_count = industry_count - peer_mark.notna().astype(float)
        peer_mark = (industry_sum - peer_mark.fillna(0.0)).div(
            peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        trailing_scale = ret.abs().shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=15).median()
        trailing_scale = trailing_scale.clip(lower=0.002)
        peer_standardized = peer_mark.div(trailing_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        agreement = np.sign(local_acceleration) * peer_standardized
        ignition_strength = agreement.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        displacement = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        directional_displacement = (
            np.sign(local_acceleration) * displacement
        ).div((3.0 * trailing_scale).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        unpaid_fraction = 1.0 - directional_displacement.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        raw_score = local_acceleration * ignition_strength * unpaid_fraction

        eligible = (
            label_available
            & valid_bar
            & volume_ready
            & peer_count.ge(2.0)
            & trailing_scale.notna()
            & np.isfinite(raw_score)
        )
        masked = raw_score.where(eligible)
        lower = masked.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        upper = masked.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        winsorized = masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        ranked = winsorized.rank(axis=1, pct=True) * 2.0 - 1.0
        return ranked.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Peer-Ignited Flow Acceleration Gap
programs.trading_idea: Industry shocks alone can be dominated by common-news overshoot and liquidity-driven reversal, explaining why the peer-only parent realized the opposite of its proposed continuation sign. The child requires an industry peer shock to be directionally confirmed by the target's own accelerating signed volume-pressure state, identifying names where the external industry impulse has ignited a local execution program rather than merely moved the entire group. The signal is further restricted to targets whose own recent price displacement remains incomplete, so it targets delayed propagation rather than already-paid contagion.
programs.description: Computes accelerating signed volume-surprise intensity for each stock, then weights it only when contemporaneous leave-one-out industry peer volume shocks agree in direction. The score is attenuated after a large same-direction three-bar move and cross-sectionally ranked, with unavailable observations assigned a neutral value.
