"""This is a daily-bar proxy for unstable, attention-driven directional moves rather than a measure of signed order flow, true market impact, or liquidity-buffer thinning. A move is treated as potentially exhausted when volatility-adjusted returns become increasingly large per unit of return-signed relative volume over successive fixed calendar intervals, but that return-per-participation measure then declines in the final interval. The proposed reversal mechanism is behavioral: a mature run with a nonlinear acceleration followed by a weaker final response to directional participation may reflect late-stage extrapolative trading whose continuation demand is fading."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _two_day_leg_sum(frame: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the causal two-session sum ending lag sessions before today."""
    return frame.shift(lag).rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()


def _impact_convexity(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    participation: pd.DataFrame,
    sigma: pd.DataFrame,
    direction: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Build three fixed causal legs and their return-per-participation ratios."""
    ret_1 = _two_day_leg_sum(ret, 4)
    ret_2 = _two_day_leg_sum(ret, 2)
    ret_3 = _two_day_leg_sum(ret, 0)

    part_1 = _two_day_leg_sum(participation, 4)
    part_2 = _two_day_leg_sum(participation, 2)
    part_3 = _two_day_leg_sum(participation, 0)

    safe_sigma = sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    d_1 = direction * ret_1 / safe_sigma
    d_2 = direction * ret_2 / safe_sigma
    d_3 = direction * ret_3 / safe_sigma

    q_1 = direction * part_1
    q_2 = direction * part_2
    q_3 = direction * part_3

    i_1 = d_1 / q_1.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    i_2 = d_2 / q_2.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    i_3 = d_3 / q_3.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    convexity = i_2 - i_1

    positive_legs = (d_1 > 0.0) & (d_2 > 0.0) & (d_3 > 0.0)
    positive_legs &= (q_1 > 0.0) & (q_2 > 0.0) & (q_3 > 0.0)
    return convexity, i_2, i_3, positive_legs


@register_factor
class VolumeTimeImpactConvexityExhaustion(BaseFactor):
    """Fade mature directional runs whose return-per-participation convexity is exhausted."""

    factor_id = "volume_time_impact_convexity_exhaustion"
    name = "Return-Volume Convexity Exhaustion"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Ranks the acceleration in volatility-adjusted return per unit of "
        "directional relative-volume participation, then fades mature runs "
        "whose final two-day response weakens."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)

        safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sigma = np.sqrt(ret.pow(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean())
        relative_volume = volume / volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume = relative_volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        participation = np.sign(ret) * relative_volume

        mature_z = ret.rolling(12, min_periods=12).sum() / (
            np.sqrt(12.0) * sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        mature_z = mature_z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        direction = np.sign(mature_z)
        mature_run = rank(mature_z.abs()) >= 0.80

        convexity, impact_2, impact_3, positive_legs = _impact_convexity(
            ret, participation, sigma, direction
        )
        convexity = convexity.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        otherwise_eligible = mature_run & positive_legs & convexity.notna()
        convexity_rank = rank(convexity.where(otherwise_eligible))
        high_convexity = convexity_rank >= 0.80
        exhausted = impact_3 < impact_2

        eligible = otherwise_eligible & high_convexity & exhausted
        score = (-direction * convexity_rank).where(eligible, 0.0)
        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Return-Volume Convexity Exhaustion
programs.trading_idea: This is a daily-bar proxy for unstable, attention-driven directional moves rather than a measure of signed order flow, true market impact, or liquidity-buffer thinning. A move is treated as potentially exhausted when volatility-adjusted returns become increasingly large per unit of return-signed relative volume over successive fixed calendar intervals, but that return-per-participation measure then declines in the final interval. The proposed reversal mechanism is behavioral: a mature run with a nonlinear acceleration followed by a weaker final response to directional participation may reflect late-stage extrapolative trading whose continuation demand is fading.
programs.description: At each close t, compute daily return r=close/close.shift(1)-1, 20-day realized volatility sigma=sqrt(mean(r^2 over t-19 through t)), relative volume v=volume/mean(volume over t-19 through t), and the explicitly proxy-only directional-participation series p=sign(r)*v. Compute the mature-run statistic Z=sum(r over t-11 through t)/(sqrt(12)*sigma), set direction s=sign(Z), and retain names whose |Z| is at or above the cross-sectional 80th percentile. Split the most recent six sessions into three fixed two-day legs. For each leg i, compute volatility-adjusted directional displacement d_i=s*sum(r in leg i)/sigma and directional participation q_i=s*sum(p in leg i); require d_i>0 and q_i>0 for all three legs. Define return-per-participation I_i=d_i/q_i, convexity C=I_2-I_1, and require C to be at or above the cross-sectional 80th percentile among otherwise eligible names and I_3<I_2. The final alpha score is -s times the cross-sectional percentile rank of C, with zero score for ineligible names: it is negative after exhausted upward runs and positive after exhausted downward runs. All inputs are known at the close of t; trade at the next bar's open and evaluate over the fixed six-bar forecast horizon.

"""Fresh high-volume endpoint pressure after a quiet state as an exhaustion reversal."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _refractory_endpoint_score(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal continuous refractory gate for lagged volume/endpoint exhaustion."""
    safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
    safe_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
    prior_close = safe_close.shift(1)

    log_volume = np.log1p(safe_volume)
    volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean()
    volume_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).std()
    volume_z = (
        (log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    bar_range = high - low
    close_location = (
        (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    close_location = close_location.where(
        bar_range.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0), 0.0
    )

    ret = (safe_close / prior_close - 1.0).clip(-0.20, 0.20)
    direction = np.sign(close_location)
    prior_abnormal = volume_z.shift(1).ge(0.5)

    same_direction_count = pd.DataFrame(
        0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns
    )
    for lag in range(1, 9):
        same_direction = np.sign(ret.shift(lag)).eq(direction)
        same_direction_count = same_direction_count + (
            same_direction & prior_abnormal.shift(lag)
        ).astype(float)

    prior_displacement = (
        safe_close.shift(1) / safe_close.shift(5) - 1.0
    ).abs().clip(0.0, 0.20)
    refractory_weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + same_direction_count)
    displacement_weight = (1.0 - prior_displacement / 0.08).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    prior_impulse = volume_z.shift(1).clip(lower=0.0)
    endpoint_pressure = prior_impulse * close_location
    score = -endpoint_pressure * refractory_weight * displacement_weight
    return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class RefractoryEndpointExhaustionReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "refractory_endpoint_exhaustion_reversal"
    name = "Refractory Endpoint Exhaustion Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks fresh lagged abnormal-volume impulses whose following bar closes "
        "at a directional range endpoint, interpreting isolated endpoint pressure "
        "after a quiet state as a six-bar exhaustion and reversal signal."
    )
    window_length = 24
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        score = _refractory_endpoint_score(
            data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
        )
        return (2.0 * rank(score) - 1.0).fillna(0.0)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _broadcast_industry_sum(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:

    expanded = grouped.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy())

@register_factor
class PeerImpulseLocalBranchingGap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_impulse_local_branching_gap"
    name = "Peer-Impulse Local Branching Gap"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Leave-one-out industry volume-price impulses are retained only when "
        "they ignite same-direction local flow acceleration before the target "
        "has fully repriced."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        label_available = pd.DataFrame(
            np.broadcast_to(labels.notna().to_numpy(), close.shape),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        prev_close = close.shift(1)
        valid = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & prev_close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
        )
        ret = np.log(close / prev_close.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        ret = ret.clip(lower=-0.20, upper=0.20).where(valid, 0.0)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).where(volume.shift(1).gt(0.0))
        volume_base = prior_volume.rolling(10, min_periods=8).median()
        volume_ready = volume_base.gt(0.0)
        volume_surprise = np.log(volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        volume_surprise = volume_surprise.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.5)
        volume_surprise = volume_surprise.where(valid & volume_ready, 0.0)

        signed_flow = np.sign(ret) * volume_surprise
        fast_flow = signed_flow.ewm(alpha=0.50, adjust=False).mean()
        slow_flow = signed_flow.ewm(alpha=0.15, adjust=False).mean()
        local_acceleration = fast_flow - slow_flow

        market_return = ret.where(valid & label_available).median(axis=1)
        excess_return = ret.sub(market_return, axis=0)
        marked_impulse = (excess_return * volume_surprise).where(
            valid & volume_ready & label_available
        )

        industry_sum = _broadcast_industry_sum(marked_impulse, labels)
        industry_count = _broadcast_industry_sum(
            marked_impulse.notna().astype(float), labels
        )
        peer_count = industry_count - marked_impulse.notna().astype(float)
        peer_impulse = (industry_sum - marked_impulse.fillna(0.0)).div(
            peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        scale = ret.abs().shift(1).rolling(12, min_periods=8).median()
        scale = scale.clip(lower=0.002)
        peer_standardized = peer_impulse.div(scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        peer_standardized = peer_standardized.clip(lower=-4.0, upper=4.0)

        directional_agreement = np.sign(peer_standardized) * local_acceleration
        confirmation = directional_agreement.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        displacement = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        paid_fraction = (
            np.sign(peer_standardized) * displacement
        ).div((3.0 * scale).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        unpaid_fraction = 1.0 - paid_fraction.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        raw = peer_standardized * confirmation * unpaid_fraction
        eligible = (
            valid
            & volume_ready
            & label_available
            & peer_count.ge(2.0)
            & scale.notna()
            & np.isfinite(raw)
        )
        raw = raw.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0)

        lower = raw.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        upper = raw.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        winsorized = raw.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        return winsorized.rank(axis=1, pct=True).mul(2.0).sub(1.0).fillna(0.0)

"""Peer-confirmed flow ignition followed by failed propagation reversal.

Mechanism: an industry shock is more credible when it ignites same-direction local
flow, but a subsequent endpoint close with contracting range and participation
signals that the cross-excited event has exhausted rather than propagated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _broadcast_industry_sum(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast same-date industry sums back to each constituent."""
    grouped = frame.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum(min_count=1).T
    output = grouped.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy())
    output.columns = frame.columns
    return output


@register_factor
class PeerIgnitedFailedPropagationReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_ignited_failed_propagation_reversal"
    name = "Peer-Ignited Failed Propagation Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Contrarian rank of peer-confirmed local flow impulses whose following "
        "bar retains the directional endpoint while both range and volume cool."
    )
    window_length = 24
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        label_available = pd.DataFrame(
            np.broadcast_to(labels.notna().to_numpy(), close.shape),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_bar = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & previous_close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
        )
        ret = np.log(close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        ret = ret.clip(lower=-0.20, upper=0.20).where(valid_bar, 0.0)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).where(volume.shift(1).gt(0.0))
        volume_base = prior_volume.rolling(15, min_periods=15).median()
        volume_ready = prior_volume.rolling(15, min_periods=15).count().eq(15.0)
        volume_ready = volume_ready & volume_base.gt(0.0)
        volume_surprise = np.log(volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        volume_surprise = volume_surprise.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        volume_surprise = volume_surprise.where(valid_bar & volume_ready, 0.0)

        signed_pressure = np.sign(ret) * volume_surprise
        fast_pressure = signed_pressure.ewm(alpha=0.50, adjust=False).mean()
        slow_pressure = signed_pressure.ewm(alpha=0.125, adjust=False).mean()
        local_acceleration = fast_pressure - slow_pressure

        market_ret = ret.where(valid_bar & label_available).median(axis=1)
        excess_ret = ret.sub(market_ret, axis=0)
        peer_mark = (excess_ret * volume_surprise).where(valid_bar & volume_ready)
        industry_sum = _broadcast_industry_sum(peer_mark, labels)
        industry_count = _broadcast_industry_sum(peer_mark.notna().astype(float), labels)
        peer_count = industry_count - peer_mark.notna().astype(float)
        leave_one_out_peer = (industry_sum - peer_mark.fillna(0.0)).div(
            peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        trailing_move = ret.abs().shift(2).rolling(15, min_periods=15).median()
        prior_acceleration = local_acceleration.shift(1)
        peer_confirmation = leave_one_out_peer.shift(1)
        ignition = np.sign(prior_acceleration) * peer_confirmation

        impulse_return = close.shift(1) / close.shift(2).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        impulse_multiple = impulse_return.abs().div(trailing_move.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        impulse_range = (high.shift(1) - low.shift(1)).div(close.shift(2).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        current_range = (high - low).div(close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        range_ratio = current_range.div(impulse_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        volume_ratio = volume.div(volume.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan))

        bar_range = high - low
        close_location = (2.0 * close - high - low).div(bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        directional_endpoint = np.sign(impulse_return) * close_location

        eligible = (
            label_available
            & valid_bar
            & volume_ready
            & peer_count.shift(1).ge(2.0)
            & trailing_move.gt(0.0)
            & impulse_multiple.ge(1.5)
            & prior_acceleration.abs().gt(0.0)
            & ignition.gt(0.0)
            & high.gt(low)
            & high.shift(1).gt(low.shift(1))
            & directional_endpoint.ge(0.55)
            & range_ratio.le(0.80)
            & volume_ratio.le(0.80)
        )

        raw_score = (
            np.sign(impulse_return)
            * impulse_multiple.clip(upper=5.0)
            * prior_acceleration.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
            * ignition.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
            * directional_endpoint.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
            * (1.0 - range_ratio).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
            * (1.0 - volume_ratio).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        ).where(eligible)

        lower = raw_score.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        upper = raw_score.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        winsorized = raw_score.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        ranked = winsorized.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return ranked.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

"""Quarterly releases can trigger headline-driven order-flow cascades around EPS results, while the relative sales outcome and the working-capital intensity of that sales outcome receive less uniform attention. The signal does not interpret receivables growth as evidence of misconduct; rather, it treats unusually high receivables growth relative to year-over-year sales growth as a cautionary quality condition for an EPS-led beat, and unusually low relative receivables growth as support for a sales-led result despite an EPS miss. The expected return is a six-day correction away from the headline EPS-versus-sales contradiction only when the receivables condition has the matching directional sign."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _event_standardized_surprises(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Create release anchors and causal, issuer-specific surprise z-scales.

    A surprise is only recorded when either reported surprise changes from the
    immediately preceding bar (including a newly available value).  The current
    observation is excluded from its own scale estimate.
    """
    index = eps_surprise.index
    columns = eps_surprise.columns
    eps_values = eps_surprise.astype(float).to_numpy()
    rev_values = revenue_surprise.astype(float).to_numpy()

    n_rows, n_cols = eps_values.shape
    anchors = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)
    eps_z = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    rev_z = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    for col in range(n_cols):
        eps_history: list[float] = []
        rev_history: list[float] = []
        previous_eps = np.nan
        previous_rev = np.nan

        for row in range(n_rows):
            current_eps = eps_values[row, col]
            current_rev = rev_values[row, col]

            eps_new = not np.isnan(current_eps)
            rev_new = not np.isnan(current_rev)
            eps_changed = eps_new and (np.isnan(previous_eps) or current_eps != previous_eps)
            rev_changed = rev_new and (np.isnan(previous_rev) or current_rev != previous_rev)
            is_anchor = (eps_changed or rev_changed) and eps_new and rev_new

            if is_anchor:
                anchors[row, col] = True
                prior_eps = eps_history[-8:]
                prior_rev = rev_history[-8:]

                if len(prior_eps) >= 6 and len(prior_rev) >= 6:
                    eps_std = np.std(prior_eps, ddof=1)
                    rev_std = np.std(prior_rev, ddof=1)
                    if np.isfinite(eps_std) and eps_std > 0.0 and np.isfinite(current_eps):
                        eps_z[row, col] = current_eps / eps_std
                    if np.isfinite(rev_std) and rev_std > 0.0 and np.isfinite(current_rev):
                        rev_z[row, col] = current_rev / rev_std

                if np.isfinite(current_eps):
                    eps_history.append(float(current_eps))
                if np.isfinite(current_rev):
                    rev_history.append(float(current_rev))

            previous_eps = current_eps
            previous_rev = current_rev

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(anchors, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(eps_z, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(rev_z, index=index, columns=columns),
    )


def _receivables_growth_gap(
    receivables: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Calculate the gap to the fourth prior distinct joint fundamentals update."""
    index = receivables.index
    columns = receivables.columns
    rec_values = receivables.astype(float).to_numpy()
    rev_values = revenue.astype(float).to_numpy()
    n_rows, n_cols = rec_values.shape
    gap = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    for col in range(n_cols):
        updates: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
        previous_rec = np.nan
        previous_rev = np.nan

        for row in range(n_rows):
            current_rec = rec_values[row, col]
            current_rev = rev_values[row, col]

            rec_present = not np.isnan(current_rec)
            rev_present = not np.isnan(current_rev)
            rec_changed = rec_present and (np.isnan(previous_rec) or current_rec != previous_rec)
            rev_changed = rev_present and (np.isnan(previous_rev) or current_rev != previous_rev)

            if (rec_changed or rev_changed) and np.isfinite(current_rec) and np.isfinite(current_rev):
                if current_rec > 0.0 and current_rev > 0.0:
                    updates.append((float(current_rec), float(current_rev)))

            if (
                np.isfinite(current_rec)
                and np.isfinite(current_rev)
                and current_rec > 0.0
                and current_rev > 0.0
                and len(updates) >= 5
            ):
                prior_rec, prior_rev = updates[-5]
                if prior_rec > 0.0 and prior_rev > 0.0:
                    value = (current_rec / prior_rec) - (current_rev / prior_rev)
                    if np.isfinite(value):
                        gap[row, col] = value

            previous_rec = current_rec
            previous_rev = current_rev

    return pd.DataFrame(gap, index=index, columns=columns)


def _industry_percentile_ranks(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Average-tie percentile ranks, retaining industries with at least five names."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns, dtype=float)

    for row in range(len(values.index)):
        row_values = values.iloc[row]
        row_industry = industry.iloc[row]
        row_eligible = eligible.iloc[row]
        mask = row_eligible & row_values.notna() & row_industry.notna()
        if not bool(mask.any()):
            continue

        subset = pd.Series(
            row_values.loc[mask].to_numpy(dtype=float),
            index=row_industry.loc[mask].to_numpy(),
            dtype=float,
        )
        group_size = subset.groupby(level=0).transform("size")
        kept = group_size >= 5
        if not bool(kept.any()):
            continue

        ranked = subset.groupby(level=0).rank(method="average", pct=True)
        result.loc[result.index[row], mask[mask].index[kept.to_numpy()]] = ranked.loc[kept].to_numpy()

    return result


@register_factor
class ReceivablesSurpriseContradictionAftershock(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-normalized earnings-sales contradiction conditioned on receivables growth."""

    factor_id = "receivables_surprise_contradiction_aftershock"
    name = "Standardized Surprise–Receivables Contradiction"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Release-date long/short tercile signal from the contradiction between "
        "industry-ranked standardized EPS and revenue surprises, retained only "
        "when the four-quarter receivables-versus-revenue growth gap confirms it."
    )
    window_length = 1260
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "receivables",
        "revenue",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        receivables = data["receivables"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        revenue = data["revenue"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        anchors, eps_z, rev_z = _event_standardized_surprises(eps_surprise, revenue_surprise)
        growth_gap = _receivables_growth_gap(receivables, revenue)

        base_eligible = anchors & eps_z.notna() & rev_z.notna() & growth_gap.notna()
        eps_rank = _industry_percentile_ranks(eps_z, industry, base_eligible)
        rev_rank = _industry_percentile_ranks(rev_z, industry, base_eligible)
        gap_rank = _industry_percentile_ranks(growth_gap, industry, base_eligible)

        eligible = base_eligible & eps_rank.notna() & rev_rank.notna() & gap_rank.notna()
        contradiction = eps_rank - rev_rank
        quality = gap_rank - 0.5
        confirmation = (contradiction * quality).clip(lower=0.0)
        score = (-contradiction * confirmation).where(eligible, 0.0)

        signal = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for row in range(len(close.index)):
            row_eligible = eligible.iloc[row]
            if int(row_eligible.sum()) < 10:
                continue

            row_score = score.iloc[row]
            nonzero = row_eligible & row_score.notna() & (row_score != 0.0)
            if not bool(nonzero.any()):
                continue

            nonzero_scores = row_score.loc[nonzero]
            score_rank = nonzero_scores.rank(method="average", pct=True)
            long_names = score_rank.index[score_rank >= (2.0 / 3.0)]
            short_names = score_rank.index[score_rank <= (1.0 / 3.0)]

            if len(long_names) > 0:
                signal.loc[signal.index[row], long_names] = 1.0
            if len(short_names) > 0:
                signal.loc[signal.index[row], short_names] = -1.0

        return signal

programs.trading_idea: Quarterly releases can trigger headline-driven order-flow cascades around EPS results, while the relative sales outcome and the working-capital intensity of that sales outcome receive less uniform attention. The signal does not interpret receivables growth as evidence of misconduct; rather, it treats unusually high receivables growth relative to year-over-year sales growth as a cautionary quality condition for an EPS-led beat, and unusually low relative receivables growth as support for a sales-led result despite an EPS miss. programs.description: An event anchor occurs only on a bar where either epsSurprise or revenueSurprise is newly non-null or differs from its value on the immediately preceding bar; both surprises must be non-null on the anchor bar. For each issuer and each anchored release, EPS surprise is divided by the sample standard deviation of its latest up-to-eight prior distinct anchored EPS surprises, excluding the current release; revenue surprise is standardized identically using prior distinct anchored revenue surprises. An issuer requires at least six prior releases and a strictly positive finite standard deviation for both series. On each anchor date, standardized EPS and revenue surprises are separately converted to average-tie percentile ranks within industry, using only anchored eligible issuers in industries with at least five eligible names. Define W = rank(EPS standardized surprise) - rank(revenue standardized surprise). Receivables quality is G = (receivables_t / receivables_t-4) - (revenue_t / revenue_t-4), where t-4 is the fourth prior distinct quarterly availability update for that issuer; all four denominator values and current receivables and revenue must be finite and strictly positive. G is converted to an average-tie industry percentile rank on the same anchor date and centered as Q = rank(G) - 0.5. The causal event score is S = -W * max(0, W*Q): EPS-led beats with excess receivables growth receive negative scores, while revenue-led outcomes with relatively improving receivables receive positive scores; all non-confirmed contradictions receive zero. At each anchor date with at least ten eligible names, rank S cross-sectionally, enter equal-risk long positions in the highest nonzero score tercile and short positions in the lowest nonzero score tercile at the next bar's open, and close each position after the sixth subsequent daily bar. No centered windows, post-event filters, future values, or shifted fundamentals are used.
