"""This is not an identification claim about buyer-initiated flow or informed trading. Instead, it tests whether a stock has persistently greater price sensitivity on up bars than down bars, or vice versa, relative to sector peers, and whether a current modest directional move aligns with that sign-conditioned liquidity asymmetry. The proposed mechanism is slow-moving inventory and participation imbalance: when the historically steeper side of the daily price-volume response is revisited by a non-event-sized move, liquidity replenishment may be incomplete over the following several days, producing continuation; disagreement between the current move and the historical asymmetry is scored negatively."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _historical_directional_impact(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Estimate t-60:t-1 sign-conditional impact using only trailing bars."""
    index = close.index
    columns = close.columns
    n_rows, n_cols = close.shape

    open_values = open_.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    volume_values = volume.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)

    valid_price = (
        np.isfinite(open_values)
        & np.isfinite(close_values)
        & (open_values > 0.0)
        & (close_values > 0.0)
    )
    log_return = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        log_return[valid_price] = np.log(
            close_values[valid_price] / open_values[valid_price]
        )

    directional_difference = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    median_volume = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    eligible = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)

    for t in range(n_rows):
        start = max(0, t - 60)
        if start >= t:
            continue

        hist_volume = volume_values[start:t]
        hist_close = close_values[start:t]
        hist_return = log_return[start:t]
        hist_valid_price = valid_price[start:t]

        for j in range(n_cols):
            positive_volume = hist_volume[:, j]
            positive_volume = positive_volume[
                np.isfinite(positive_volume) & (positive_volume > 0.0)
            ]
            if positive_volume.size == 0:
                continue

            mvol = float(np.median(positive_volume))
            if not np.isfinite(mvol) or mvol <= 0.0:
                continue
            median_volume[t, j] = mvol

            vol_j = hist_volume[:, j]
            ret_j = hist_return[:, j]
            close_j = hist_close[:, j]
            usable = (
                np.isfinite(vol_j)
                & (vol_j > 0.0)
                & (vol_j >= 0.01 * mvol)
                & hist_valid_price[:, j]
                & np.isfinite(ret_j)
            )
            if int(usable.sum()) < 45:
                continue

            positive = usable & (ret_j >= 0.001)
            negative = usable & (ret_j <= -0.001)
            if int(positive.sum()) < 12 or int(negative.sum()) < 12:
                continue

            dollar_volume = close_j[usable] * vol_j[usable]
            dollar_volume = dollar_volume[
                np.isfinite(dollar_volume) & (dollar_volume > 0.0)
            ]
            if dollar_volume.size == 0 or float(np.median(dollar_volume)) < 1000000.0:
                continue

            raw_impact = np.abs(ret_j) / vol_j
            plus_impact = raw_impact[positive]
            minus_impact = raw_impact[negative]
            if not np.all(np.isfinite(plus_impact)) or not np.all(np.isfinite(minus_impact)):
                continue

            e_plus = mvol * float(np.median(plus_impact))
            e_minus = mvol * float(np.median(minus_impact))
            if np.isfinite(e_plus) and np.isfinite(e_minus):
                directional_difference[t, j] = e_plus - e_minus
                eligible[t, j] = True

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(directional_difference, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(median_volume, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(eligible, index=index, columns=columns),
    )


def _sector_residual_and_rank(
    difference: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract same-sector peer medians and average-rank valid residuals."""
    index = difference.index
    columns = difference.columns
    difference_values = difference.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    eligible_values = eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool, copy=False)
    sector_values = sector.reindex(index=index, columns=columns).to_numpy(copy=False)

    n_rows, n_cols = difference.shape
    residuals = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    for t in range(n_rows):
        d_row = difference_values[t]
        valid = eligible_values[t] & np.isfinite(d_row)
        labels = sector_values[t]

        for j in range(n_cols):
            if not valid[j] or pd.isna(labels[j]):
                continue
            peers = valid & (labels == labels[j])
            peers[j] = False
            peer_values = d_row[peers]
            if peer_values.size >= 5:
                residuals[t, j] = d_row[j] - float(np.median(peer_values))

    residual_frame = pd.DataFrame(residuals, index=index, columns=columns)
    return residual_frame.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)


@register_factor
class DirectionalImpactElasticityInformedFlow(BaseFactor):
    """Sign-conditioned impact alignment with sector-relative liquidity asymmetry."""

    factor_id = "directional_impact_elasticity_informed_flow"
    name = "Sign-Conditional Impact Alignment"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Measures trailing up-versus-down daily price-impact asymmetry, "
        "sector-residualizes it, and signs the result by a moderate current "
        "directional impulse aligned with the historically steeper side."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = ["open", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        difference, median_volume, eligible = _historical_directional_impact(
            open_, close, volume
        )
        percentile = _sector_residual_and_rank(difference, eligible, sector)
        alignment = 2.0 * percentile - 1.0

        valid_current_price = (
            open_.notna()
            & close.notna()
            & (open_ > 0.0)
            & (close > 0.0)
        )
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            current_return = np.log(close / open_)
            relative_volume = volume / median_volume

        current_gate = (
            valid_current_price
            & volume.notna()
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & median_volume.notna()
            & (median_volume > 0.0)
            & (volume >= 0.01 * median_volume)
            & (relative_volume >= 0.50)
            & (relative_volume <= 2.00)
            & (current_return.abs() >= 0.001)
            & (current_return.abs() <= 0.05)
        )

        signal = np.sign(current_return) * alignment
        return signal.where(current_gate & signal.notna()).astype(float)
programs.name: Sign-Conditional Impact Alignment
programs.trading_idea: This is not an identification claim about buyer-initiated flow or informed trading. Instead, it tests whether a stock has persistently greater price sensitivity on up bars than down bars, or vice versa, relative to sector peers, and whether a current modest directional move aligns with that sign-conditioned liquidity asymmetry. The proposed mechanism is slow-moving inventory and participation imbalance: when the historically steeper side of the daily price-volume response is revisited by a non-event-sized move, liquidity replenishment may be incomplete over the following several days, producing continuation; disagreement between the current move and the historical asymmetry is scored negatively.
programs.description: At signal date t, use only bars t-60 through t-1 to estimate sign-conditional daily impact. Define r_u = log(close_u/open_u). First compute each stock's trailing median positive volume mV from strictly positive-volume bars in t-60:t-1. Exclude a historical bar from impact estimation if volume is missing, volume <= 0, mV is missing or nonpositive, or volume < 0.01*mV; this treats zero and near-zero volume as unusable rather than as evidence of extreme impact. Define relative volume RV_u = volume_u/mV and impact q_u = abs(r_u)/RV_u. Classify a bar as positive if r_u >= 0.001 and negative if r_u <= -0.001; bars with abs(r_u) < 0.001 are excluded from both groups. Let Eplus be the median q_u across positive bars and Eminus the median q_u across negative bars. A stock is eligible only if it has at least 45 usable historical bars, at least 12 positive and 12 negative classified bars, valid positive open and close prices, and trailing median daily dollar volume median(close_u*volume_u) of at least USD 1,000,000 over usable historical bars. Define D = Eplus - Eminus. At t, sector-residualize D by subtracting the median D of eligible same-sector peers at t; require at least five such peers excluding the stock, otherwise emit NaN. The current impulse uses bar t only: require valid positive open, close, and volume; require volume_t >= 0.01*mV, 0.50 <= RV_t <= 2.00, abs(log(close_t/open_t)) >= 0.001, and abs(log(close_t/open_t)) <= 0.05. These fixed gates define moderate-volume and non-event-sized current moves. For stocks passing all gates, percentile-rank the sector-residual D cross-sectionally among all eligible stocks at t using average ranks, form A = 2*pct_rank(D_residual)-1, and output signal = sign(log(close_t/open_t))*A. All medians, classifications, sector peer sets, and cross-sectional ranks are computed at t using information available no later than that bar's close; no centered windows, future returns, or forward sector normalizations are used. Execute no earlier than the next bar's open, t+1, and evaluate the forecast over the fixed subsequent six daily bars.

programs.code:
"""This revision replaces the ambiguous inventory-unwind reversal mechanism with an information-richness mechanism. A stock-specific volume shock that is unusually large relative both to its own trailing activity and to contemporaneous sector activity, and whose close confirms rather than rejects the intraday displacement, is more consistent with directional information arrival or persistent informed execution than with a completed liquidity-demand episode. Because volume is unsigned, daily price direction and close location are only price-based proxies for directional pressure, not observations of signed order flow."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rolling_mad(values: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Median absolute deviation for a trailing raw rolling-window array."""
    valid = values[np.isfinite(values)]
    if valid.size == 0:
        return np.nan
    median = np.median(valid)
    return float(np.median(np.abs(valid - median)))


def _prior_log_volume_abnormality(volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust log-volume z-score using only observations through t-1."""
    log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))
    history = log_volume.shift(1)

    history_count = history.rolling(60, min_periods=40).count()
    history_median = history.rolling(60, min_periods=40).median()
    history_mad = history.rolling(60, min_periods=40).apply(
        _rolling_mad, raw=True
    )
    scale = (1.4826 * history_mad).where(history_mad > 0.0)

    abnormality = (log_volume - history_median) / scale
    return abnormality.where(history_count >= 40.0)


def _sector_transform(
    values: pd.DataFrame, sector_labels: pd.Series, method: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Apply a same-date cross-sectional transform independently by sector."""
    return values.T.groupby(sector_labels, sort=False).transform(method).T


@register_factor
class IdiosyncraticConfirmedFlowContinuation(BaseFactor):
    """Confirmed idiosyncratic volume shocks signal directional continuation."""

    factor_id = "sector_idiosyncratic_confirmed_flow_continuation"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Confirmed-Flow Continuation"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks endpoint-confirmed up and down intraday displacements only when "
        "current volume is a large robust residual versus both the stock's own "
        "60-session history and its contemporaneous sector."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_price = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]

        # Sector is explicitly static.  Names lacking a label on the first bar
        # cannot be sector-normalized and are therefore excluded.
        sector_labels = sector.iloc[0]

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(
            (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0)
        )
        prior_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.shift(1)
        median_dollar_volume = prior_dollar_volume.rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).median()

        volume_abnormality = _prior_log_volume_abnormality(volume)

        intraday_range = high - low
        valid_bar = (
            (close > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & open_price.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & (intraday_range > 0.0)
        )
        liquid = median_dollar_volume >= 1_000_000.0
        base_eligible = (
            valid_bar
            & liquid
            & volume_abnormality.notna()
            & sector_labels.notna()
        )

        eligible_abnormality = volume_abnormality.where(base_eligible)
        sector_median = _sector_transform(
            eligible_abnormality, sector_labels, "median"
        )
        sector_count = _sector_transform(
            base_eligible.astype(float), sector_labels, "sum"
        )
        sector_eligible = base_eligible & (sector_count >= 5.0)
        idiosyncratic_abnormality = (
            volume_abnormality - sector_median
        ).where(sector_eligible)

        displacement = (close - open_price) / intraday_range
        close_location = (close - low) / intraday_range

        upward = (
            sector_eligible
            & (displacement >= 0.50)
            & (close_location >= 0.80)
            & (idiosyncratic_abnormality >= 1.50)
        )
        downward = (
            sector_eligible
            & (displacement <= -0.50)
            & (close_location <= 0.20)
            & (idiosyncratic_abnormality >= 1.50)
        )

        raw_score = idiosyncratic_abnormality.where(upward, 0.0)
        raw_score = raw_score - idiosyncratic_abnormality.where(downward, 0.0)

        eps_previous = eps_actual.shift(1)
        revenue_previous = revenue_actual.shift(1)
        eps_release = eps_actual.notna() & (
            eps_previous.isna() | eps_actual.ne(eps_previous)
        )
        revenue_release = revenue_actual.notna() & (
            revenue_previous.isna() | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_previous)
        )
        remaining_eligible = sector_eligible & ~(eps_release | revenue_release)

        percentile_rank = raw_score.where(remaining_eligible).rank(
            axis=1, pct=True
        )
        signed_rank = 2.0 * percentile_rank - 1.0
        return signed_rank.where(remaining_eligible, 0.0)

programs.trading_idea: This revision replaces the ambiguous inventory-unwind reversal mechanism with an information-richness mechanism. A stock-specific volume shock that is unusually large relative both to its own trailing activity and to contemporaneous sector activity, and whose close confirms rather than rejects the intraday displacement, is more consistent with directional information arrival or persistent informed execution than with a completed liquidity-demand episode. Because volume is unsigned, daily price direction and close location are only price-based proxies for directional pressure, not observations of signed order flow.
programs.description: At the close of day t, restrict the universe to names with non-missing positive close and volume, a positive intraday range high-low, and trailing 20-session median dollar volume (close*volume, using sessions t-20 through t-1 only) of at least USD 1,000,000. For each eligible stock, compute log-volume abnormality z_t = [log(volume_t) - median(log(volume) over t-60 through t-1)] / [1.4826*MAD(log(volume) over t-60 through t-1)], requiring at least 40 valid trailing observations and strictly positive MAD; otherwise the stock is ineligible. Within each static sector on day t, using only eligible names and requiring at least 5 names, compute the idiosyncratic volume residual a_t = z_t - sector_median(z_t). Define directional displacement d_t=(close_t-open_t)/(high_t-low_t) and close location clv_t=(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t). A confirmed upward-pressure event requires d_t>=0.50, clv_t>=0.80, and a_t>=1.50; a confirmed downward-pressure event requires d_t<=-0.50, clv_t<=0.20, and a_t>=1.50. Set raw score q_t=+a_t for confirmed upward events, q_t=-a_t for confirmed downward events, and 0 otherwise. Exclude a stock on t if either epsActual or revenueActual is newly reported on t, defined deterministically as a non-null value whose prior-day value was null or different; this avoids directly trading the first daily bar carrying an earnings release. Rank q_t cross-sectionally among all remaining eligible names on day t, convert the percentile rank to [-1,1], and use that signed rank as the factor: high values are long candidates and low values are short candidates. All volume-history windows end at t-1; only same-bar OHLCV observed after the day-t close is used for event classification. The signal is formed after the close on t, entered at open on t+1, and evaluated by the six-session executable forward return open(t+7)/open(t+1)-1. The concrete distinction from the prior rejection/exhaustion family is that this factor requires endpoint-confirmed directional displacement and trades continuation, while its volume condition is an explicit residual relative to both a 60-session own-history baseline and the same-day sector median rather than simple high-volume reversal or close-location rejection.

"""A large daily price displacement on volume that is low relative to the stock's own recent volume and range history is treated as a weak-resiliency event rather than a direct observation of displayed order-book depth. Continuation is hypothesized only when the displacement closes decisively in its direction and occurs amid elevated recent instability in this relative depth measure, conditions intended to identify persistent liquidity-supply withdrawal rather than a routine, well-cleared information event. The signal is explicitly a conditional short-horizon continuation hypothesis and must be evaluated after next-bar execution costs and capacity constraints."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _relative_depth_instability_score(close: pd.DataFrame, high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct the causal relative-depth shock score before cross-sectional scaling."""
    previous_close = close.shift(1)
    bar_range = high - low
    normalized_range = bar_range / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    finite_close = np.isfinite(close)
    finite_previous_close = np.isfinite(previous_close)
    finite_high = np.isfinite(high)
    finite_low = np.isfinite(low)
    finite_volume = np.isfinite(volume)
    finite_range = np.isfinite(normalized_range)
    volume_valid = finite_volume & volume.gt(0.0)
    range_valid = finite_previous_close & previous_close.gt(0.0) & finite_high & finite_low & high.gt(low) & finite_range & normalized_range.gt(0.0)
    valid_volume = volume.where(volume_valid)
    valid_range = normalized_range.where(range_valid)
    volume_base = valid_volume.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=1).median()
    range_base = valid_range.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=1).median()
    volume_count = volume_valid.astype(float).shift(1).rolling(22, min_periods=1).sum()
    range_count = range_valid.astype(float).shift(1).rolling(19, min_periods=1).sum()
    eligible = finite_close & finite_previous_close & previous_close.gt(0.0) & volume_valid & range_valid & volume_count.ge(15.0) & range_count.ge(15.0) & np.isfinite(volume_base) & np.isfinite(range_base) & volume_base.gt(0.0) & range_base.gt(0.0)
    relative_depth = volume / volume_base / (normalized_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    depth_valid = eligible & np.isfinite(relative_depth) & relative_depth.gt(0.0)
    log_depth = np.log(relative_depth.where(depth_valid))
    instability = log_depth.rolling(11, min_periods=8).std()
    close_location = 2.0 * (close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    signed_return = np.sign(close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
    directional_alignment = (signed_return * close_location).clip(lower=0.0)
    confirmation = signed_return * directional_alignment
    shock_strength = (-log_depth).clip(lower=0.0)
    raw = shock_strength * instability * confirmation
    raw = raw.where(eligible & np.isfinite(instability) & np.isfinite(raw))
    return raw

@register_factor
class RelativeDepthShockContinuation(BaseFactor):
    """Conditional continuation after unstable relative-depth withdrawal shocks."""
    factor_id = 'depth_proxy_instability_jump_continuation_j'
    name = 'Relative Depth Shock Continuation'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Cross-sectionally winsorized and standardized conditional continuation signal for decisive price moves occurring on unusually low relative depth amid unstable recent liquidity conditions.'
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        raw = _relative_depth_instability_score(close, data['high'], data['low'], data['volume'])
        lower = raw.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
        upper = raw.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
        winsorized = raw.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        cross_mean = winsorized.mean(axis=1)
        cross_std = winsorized.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        standardized = winsorized.sub(cross_mean, axis=0).div(cross_std, axis=0)
        return standardized.where(np.isfinite(standardized))

Continuation is hypothesized only when the displacement closes decisively in its direction and occurs amid elevated recent instability in this relative depth measure, conditions intended to identify persistent liquidity-supply withdrawal rather than a routine, well-cleared information event. programs.description: At the completion of day t, define normalized range r_t = (high_t - low_t) / close_{t-1}. A stock is eligible only when close_{t-1} > 0, high_t > low_t, volume_t > 0, and at least 15 valid observations exist in each of the prior 20 completed daily bars. Let Vbase_t and Rbase_t be the medians of valid volume and normalized range, respectively, over days t-20 through t-1. Define relative depth q_t = (volume_t / Vbase_t) / (r_t / Rbase_t) and log relative depth d_t = log(q_t); observations with nonpositive or nonfinite inputs, including zero range, are missing rather than imputed. Define depth-shock strength D_t = max(0, -d_t), so unusually low volume relative to an unusually large range receives a positive value. Define instability I_t as the sample standard deviation of d over days t-9 through t, requiring at least 8 valid observations. Define close location CLV_t = 2 * (close_t - low_t) / (high_t - low_t) - 1 and signed return sign_t = sign(close_t / close_{t-1} - 1). Define directional-extreme confirmation A_t = sign_t * max(0, sign_t * CLV_t), which is positive for an upward return closing near the high, negative for a downward return closing near the low, and zero when return direction and close location disagree. The raw score is S_t = D_t * I_t * A_t. Each day, winsorize S_t cross-sectionally at the 5th and 95th percentiles among eligible stocks, then standardize it by the same-day cross-sectional mean and standard deviation; this standardized value is the factor. The signal is formed only after all OHLCV information for day t is complete, entered no earlier than the next executable bar/session (for example, day t+1 open), and evaluated over the fixed six-bar horizon measured from that entry.

programs.code:
"""Daily OHLCV cannot identify institutional signed order flow or self-excitation directly. Instead, the signal treats an unusually high-volume, directionally confirmed daily move as an information-rich event whose news may diffuse gradually over subsequent sessions, particularly when its directional intensity is idiosyncratic rather than shared by the stock's sector. The expected effect is continuation, but it should fail when abnormal volume reflects liquidity-demand exhaustion, broad sector repricing, or short-term profit taking."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _signed_arrival_intensity(f: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal asymmetric exponential arrival intensities, reset across gaps."""
    values = f.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    intensity = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    positive_state = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    negative_state = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    active = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=bool)

    for row in range(n_rows):
        current = values[row]
        valid = np.isfinite(current)
        continuing = valid & active
        starting = valid & ~active

        positive = np.maximum(current, 0.0)
        negative = np.maximum(-current, 0.0)

        positive_state[continuing] = (
            0.8 * positive_state[continuing] + 0.2 * positive[continuing]
        )
        negative_state[continuing] = (
            0.8 * negative_state[continuing] + 0.2 * negative[continuing]
        )

        # The first valid observation after the required trailing history
        # initializes the recursion from a zero pre-history state.
        positive_state[starting] = 0.2 * positive[starting]
        negative_state[starting] = 0.2 * negative[starting]

        intensity[row, valid] = (
            positive_state[valid] - negative_state[valid]
        )
        active = valid

    return pd.DataFrame(intensity, index=f.index, columns=f.columns)


def _sector_idiosyncrasy(
    directional_intensity: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract same-day eligible-sector medians, requiring five names."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(
        np.nan,
        index=directional_intensity.index,
        columns=directional_intensity.columns,
        dtype=float,
    )

    for row in range(len(directional_intensity.index)):
        intensity_row = directional_intensity.iloc[row]
        eligible_row = eligible.iloc[row]
        sector_row = sector.iloc[row]

        usable = intensity_row.where(eligible_row & sector_row.notna())
        group_median = usable.groupby(sector_row).transform("median")
        group_count = usable.notna().groupby(sector_row).transform("sum")

        result.iloc[row] = (usable - group_median).where(group_count >= 5)

    return result


def _decile_equal_weights(idiosyncrasy: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Form equal-weighted long and short deciles from cross-sectional ranks."""
    ranks = idiosyncrasy.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    long_mask = ranks >= 0.90
    short_mask = ranks <= 0.10

    long_count = long_mask.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan)
    short_count = short_mask.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan)

    long_weights = long_mask.astype(float).div(long_count, axis=0)
    short_weights = short_mask.astype(float).div(short_count, axis=0)
    return (long_weights - short_weights).where(idiosyncrasy.notna(), 0.0)


@register_factor
class RareSignedVolumeArrivalDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Equal-weighted decile portfolio of sector-idiosyncratic rare volume arrivals."""

    factor_id = "rare_signed_volume_arrival_drift"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Abnormal-Volume Drift"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks sector-idiosyncratic asymmetric exponential intensity from rare, "
        "directionally confirmed abnormal-volume days and forms equal-weighted "
        "long and short deciles."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        prior_median_volume = (
            positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median().shift(1)
        )
        q = volume / prior_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        price_range = high - low
        valid_prices = (
            (close > 0.0)
            & (prior_close > 0.0)
            & (high > 0.0)
            & (low > 0.0)
            & (high > low)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(prior_close)
            & np.isfinite(high)
            & np.isfinite(low)
        )
        valid_bar = (
            valid_prices
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
            & np.isfinite(q)
        )

        close_location = (
            (2.0 * close - high - low) / price_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        direction = np.sign(close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
        confirmation = q.clip(upper=5.0) * direction * close_location.abs()
        confirmation = confirmation.where(valid_bar)

        directional_intensity = _signed_arrival_intensity(confirmation)

        prior_q_95 = q.rolling(60, min_periods=60).quantile(0.95).shift(1)
        eligible = (
            valid_bar
            & (q >= prior_q_95)
            & np.isfinite(directional_intensity)
            & sector.notna()
        )

        idiosyncrasy = _sector_idiosyncrasy(
            directional_intensity, eligible, sector
        )
        return _decile_equal_weights(idiosyncrasy)

"""Reversal after a mature idiosyncratic arrival depletes relative depth.

A prior rare, sector-idiosyncratic signed-volume arrival represents an already
revealed directional-information state.  When a later same-direction bar moves
far on unusually little relative depth, the move is interpreted as terminal
liquidity depletion rather than fresh information and is faded.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _reset_ewma(mark: pd.DataFrame, alpha: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal EWMA that resets after missing observations rather than bridging gaps."""
    values = mark.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    out = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    state = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    active = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=bool)

    for t in range(n_rows):
        x = values[t]
        valid = np.isfinite(x)
        continuing = valid & active
        starting = valid & ~active
        state[continuing] = (1.0 - alpha) * state[continuing] + alpha * x[continuing]
        state[starting] = alpha * x[starting]
        out[t, valid] = state[valid]
        active = valid

    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=mark.index, columns=mark.columns)


def _sector_residual(
    value: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-day sector-median residual, requiring a minimally broad peer set."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=value.index, columns=value.columns, dtype=float)
    for t in range(len(value.index)):
        row = value.iloc[t]
        groups = sector.iloc[t]
        usable = row.where(row.notna() & groups.notna())
        median = usable.groupby(groups).transform("median")
        count = usable.notna().groupby(groups).transform("sum")
        result.iloc[t] = (usable - median).where(count >= 5)
    return result


@register_factor
class MatureArrivalDepthDepletionReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "mature_arrival_depth_depletion_reversal"
    name = "Mature Arrival Depth-Depletion Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fades a decisive low-relative-depth displacement only when it aligns "
        "with a decayed prior rare signed-volume arrival that is idiosyncratic "
        "to the stock's sector."
    )
    window_length = 81
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        bar_range = high - low
        valid_price = (
            np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(prior_close)
            & np.isfinite(high)
            & np.isfinite(low)
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & prior_close.gt(0.0)
            & high.gt(low)
        )
        valid_bar = valid_price & np.isfinite(volume) & volume.gt(0.0)

        positive_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0) & np.isfinite(volume))
        prior_vol_median = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
        q = volume / prior_vol_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        q95 = q.rolling(60, min_periods=45).quantile(0.95).shift(1)

        close_location = (
            (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        direction = np.sign(close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)

        rare = valid_bar & np.isfinite(q) & np.isfinite(q95) & q.ge(q95)
        arrival_mark = (
            direction
            * close_location.abs()
            * np.log(q.clip(lower=1.0, upper=6.0))
        )
        # Valid ordinary bars decay the state; invalid bars reset it.
        arrival_input = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(valid_bar, 0.0, np.nan), index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        )
        arrival_input = arrival_input.where(~rare, arrival_mark)
        prior_arrival_state = _reset_ewma(arrival_input, 0.18).shift(1)
        idio_arrival = _sector_residual(prior_arrival_state, sector)

        normalized_range = bar_range / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        valid_range = valid_bar & np.isfinite(normalized_range) & normalized_range.gt(0.0)
        range_base = normalized_range.where(valid_range).shift(1).rolling(
            20, min_periods=15
        ).median()
        volume_base = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()

        relative_depth = (volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)) / (
            normalized_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        valid_depth = (
            valid_range
            & np.isfinite(relative_depth)
            & relative_depth.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(range_base)
            & range_base.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(volume_base)
            & volume_base.gt(0.0)
        )
        log_depth = np.log(relative_depth.where(valid_depth))
        instability = log_depth.rolling(10, min_periods=8).std()
        depletion = (-log_depth).clip(lower=0.0)

        decisive_alignment = (direction * close_location).clip(lower=0.0)
        same_direction_maturity = (direction * idio_arrival).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        # Negative current direction is deliberately used: mature, aligned thin
        # moves are inventory/depth exhaustion and are expected to mean-revert.
        raw = (
            -direction
            * depletion
            * instability
            * decisive_alignment
            * same_direction_maturity
        )
        eligible = (
            valid_depth
            & np.isfinite(instability)
            & np.isfinite(idio_arrival)
            & sector.notna()
            & np.isfinite(raw)
        )
        raw = raw.where(eligible)

        signal = raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return signal.where(np.isfinite(signal))

"""This is a reduced-form six-day reversal signal, not a claim to observe order flow or dealer inventories. It requires a specific sequence: an earlier, price-signed abnormal-volume arrival, followed two to ten trading days later by a same-direction intraday excursion that has low incremental participation, high range relative to participation, closes back from its directional extreme, and is not accompanied by a material overnight gap. The interpretation is that the second move may represent weak acceptance of the earlier directional pressure rather than fresh information, although informed delayed repricing remains an important failure mode."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile ranks within static sector groups."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    labels = sector.iloc[0]

    for _, tickers in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        columns = list(tickers)
        output.loc[:, columns] = values.loc[:, columns].rank(axis=1, pct=True)

    return output


def _most_recent_arrival_direction(
    direction: pd.DataFrame, qualifying_arrival: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Select the latest qualifying arrival from inclusive lags two through ten."""
    selected = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=direction.index, columns=direction.columns)
    for lag in range(10, 1, -1):
        candidate = direction.shift(lag).where(qualifying_arrival.shift(lag))
        selected = candidate.where(candidate.notna(), selected)
    return selected


@register_factor
class GapFilteredAftershockRejectionReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Fade delayed, low-participation rejections of sector-relative turnover shocks."""

    factor_id = "gap_filtered_aftershock_rejection_reversal"
    name = "Delayed Directional-Turnover Rejection"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks delayed same-direction intraday rejection after a prior "
        "sector-relative directional turnover arrival, requiring low current "
        "participation and a small overnight gap."
    )
    window_length = 31
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        safe_prior_close = prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        daily_return = close / safe_prior_close - 1.0
        arrival_direction = np.sign(daily_return)

        trailing_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        relative_volume = volume / trailing_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        arrival_volume_rank = _sector_rank(relative_volume, sector)
        qualifying_arrival = (
            (relative_volume >= 2.0)
            & (arrival_volume_rank >= 0.80)
            & (arrival_direction != 0.0)
            & arrival_direction.notna()
        )
        direction = _most_recent_arrival_direction(
            arrival_direction, qualifying_arrival
        )
        has_arrival = direction.notna()

        normalized_true_range = (high - low) / safe_prior_close
        atr_scale = normalized_true_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        atr_scale = atr_scale.clip(lower=1.0e-6)

        upside_excursion = (high - prior_close) / safe_prior_close
        downside_excursion = (low - prior_close) / safe_prior_close
        excursion = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(direction > 0.0, upside_excursion, -downside_excursion),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        normalized_range = (high - low) / safe_prior_close
        participation_floor = relative_volume.clip(lower=0.10)
        range_per_participation = normalized_range / participation_floor.replace(
            0.0, np.nan
        )
        xrank = _sector_rank(range_per_participation, sector)

        bar_range = high - low
        upside_rejection = (high - close) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        downside_rejection = (close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rejection = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(direction > 0.0, upside_rejection, downside_rejection),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        ).fillna(0.0)

        overnight_gap = (open_ / safe_prior_close - 1.0).abs()
        gap_baseline = overnight_gap.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        gap_baseline = gap_baseline.clip(lower=1.0e-6)

        qualifies = (
            has_arrival
            & (excursion >= 0.5 * atr_scale)
            & (relative_volume <= 1.0)
            & (rejection >= 0.50)
            & (overnight_gap <= 0.5 * gap_baseline)
            & xrank.notna()
        )

        raw_score = -direction * rejection * xrank
        eligible_score = raw_score.where(qualifies)
        ranked_score = 2.0 * rank(eligible_score) - 1.0

        return ranked_score.where(qualifies, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Delayed Directional-Turnover Rejection
programs.trading_idea: This is a reduced-form six-day reversal signal, not a claim to observe order flow or dealer inventories. It requires a specific sequence: an earlier, price-signed abnormal-volume arrival, followed two to ten trading days later by a same-direction intraday excursion that has low incremental participation, high range relative to participation, closes back from its directional extreme, and is not accompanied by a material overnight gap. The interpretation is that the second move may represent weak acceptance of the earlier directional pressure rather than fresh information, although informed delayed repricing remains an important failure mode.
programs.description: All quantities for evaluation date t are computed after the close of t, using only bars dated t or earlier. Let r_i,u = close_i,u / close_i,u-1 - 1, q_i,u = sign(r_i,u), and vrel_i,u = volume_i,u / median(volume_i,u-20:u-1). The price-based signed-volume proxy is sv_i,u = q_i,u * volume_i,u; it is only a price-signed volume proxy and is not interpreted as signed order flow. For each candidate arrival date a, define its within-sector turnover percentile P_i,a as the cross-sectional percentile rank of vrel_i,a among names with the same sector on date a. A qualifying arrival satisfies vrel_i,a >= 2, P_i,a >= 0.80, and q_i,a is nonzero. Select a_i(t) as the most recent qualifying arrival in the inclusive lag window t-10 through t-2; names without such an arrival receive a missing/zero signal. Let q_i = q_i,a_i(t). Define ATR-like scale A_i,t = median((high-low)/close.shift(1)) over t-20:t-1, with a small positive floor. The current same-direction excursion is E_i,t = q_i * ((high_i,t - close_i,t-1) / close_i,t-1) when q_i=+1, and E_i,t = q_i * ((low_i,t - close_i,t-1) / close_i,t-1) when q_i=-1; equivalently it is positive only when the relevant high or low extends in the arrival direction. Require E_i,t >= 0.5*A_i,t. Define normalized range R_i,t = (high_i,t-low_i,t)/close_i,t-1, incremental participation vrel_i,t, and range-per-participation X_i,t = R_i,t / max(vrel_i,t,0.10). Require vrel_i,t <= 1.0 and let xrank_i,t be X_i,t's cross-sectional percentile rank within sector at t. Directional rejection is J_i,t = (high_i,t-close_i,t)/(high_i,t-low_i,t) for q_i=+1, and J_i,t = (close_i,t-low_i,t)/(high_i,t-low_i,t) for q_i=-1, with zero assigned when high equals low; require J_i,t >= 0.50. The small-gap condition is |open_i,t/close_i,t-1-1| <= 0.5*median(|open_i,u/close_i,u-1-1|, u=t-20:t-1), again with a small positive floor. For qualifying names, raw score is S_i,t = -q_i * J_i,t * xrank_i,t; otherwise S_i,t = 0. Cross-sectionally rank S_i,t over the eligible universe and map the rank to [-1,1], with high values representing prior downside turnover followed by a rejected downside aftershock and low values representing the symmetric upside case. The factor is formed after the close of t; a tradable implementation enters at the next bar's open, t+1, and evaluates the six-bar return from open at t+1 to open at t+7. No later bar is used to identify either the arrival or the aftershock. Unlike generic terminal-auction or single-bar rejection factors, this specification requires the ordered interaction of a prior sector-relative directional turnover arrival, a delayed same-direction excursion, low incremental participation, and a small contemporaneous gap.

"""Industry-anchored reversal after mature liquidity depletion.

A constituent's incomplete response to a large industry shock is traded only when
its current thin directional move is a terminal reversal state after an earlier
idiosyncratic volume arrival.  The industry gap anchors the correction direction,
while the mature low-depth displacement identifies when the local move is likely
inventory-driven rather than fresh information.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    """Build static membership lists from point-in-time industry labels."""
    if industry.empty:
        return {}
    labels = industry.iloc[0]
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    for column in industry.columns:
        label = labels[column]
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column)
    return groups


def _excluded_industry_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    lag_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: dict[object, list[object]],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-one-out cap-weighted industry return with peer-count protection."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for columns in groups.values():
        if len(columns) < 8:
            continue
        r = ret[columns]
        cap = lag_cap[columns]
        valid = r.notna() & cap.notna() & cap.gt(0.0)
        safe_cap = cap.where(valid, 0.0)
        safe_ret = (r * cap).where(valid, 0.0)
        total_cap = safe_cap.sum(axis=1)
        total_ret = safe_ret.sum(axis=1)
        total_count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        peer_cap = total_cap.to_numpy()[:, None] - safe_cap.to_numpy()
        peer_ret = total_ret.to_numpy()[:, None] - safe_ret.to_numpy()
        peer_count = total_count.to_numpy()[:, None] - valid.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        value = peer_ret / np.where(peer_cap > 0.0, peer_cap, np.nan)
        frame = pd.DataFrame(value, index=ret.index, columns=columns)
        output.loc[:, columns] = frame.where(peer_count >= 7.0)
    return output


def _reset_ewma(values: pd.DataFrame, alpha: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal EWMA whose state resets across missing-data gaps."""
    array = values.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_time, n_assets = array.shape
    output = np.full((n_time, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)
    state = np.zeros(n_assets, dtype=float)
    active = np.zeros(n_assets, dtype=bool)
    for t in range(n_time):
        row = array[t]
        valid = np.isfinite(row)
        continuing = valid & active
        starting = valid & ~active
        state[continuing] = (1.0 - alpha) * state[continuing] + alpha * row[continuing]
        state[starting] = alpha * row[starting]
        output[t, valid] = state[valid]
        active = valid
    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)


def _group_residual(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-day industry-median residual, requiring sufficiently broad peers."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for t in range(len(values.index)):
        row = values.iloc[t]
        labels = industry.iloc[t]
        usable = row.where(row.notna() & labels.notna())
        median = usable.groupby(labels).transform("median")
        count = usable.notna().groupby(labels).transform("sum")
        output.iloc[t] = (usable - median).where(count >= 5)
    return output


@register_factor
class IndustryAnchorMatureDepthReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "industry_anchor_mature_depth_reversal"
    name = "Industry-Anchored Mature Depth Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks industry catch-up gaps only when a prior idiosyncratic arrival and "
        "a current low-depth terminal displacement imply a reversal in the same direction."
    )
    window_length = 122
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "marketCap", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        stock_ret = (close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).where(
            close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        groups = _industry_groups(industry)
        lag_cap = market_cap.shift(1).where(market_cap.shift(1).gt(0.0))
        peer_ret = _excluded_industry_return(stock_ret, lag_cap, groups)

        beta_y = stock_ret.shift(1)
        beta_x = peer_ret.shift(1)
        beta = beta_y.rolling(60, min_periods=45).cov(beta_x) / beta_x.rolling(
            60, min_periods=45
        ).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_peer_abs = peer_ret.abs().shift(1)
        peer_threshold = prior_peer_abs.rolling(60, min_periods=45).quantile(0.80)
        large_peer_shock = peer_ret.abs().gt(peer_threshold)
        catchup_gap = (np.sign(peer_ret) * (beta * peer_ret - stock_ret)).where(
            beta.notna() & peer_ret.notna() & stock_ret.notna()
        )

        bar_range = high - low
        valid_price = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & prior_close.gt(0.0)
            & high.gt(low)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(prior_close)
            & np.isfinite(high)
            & np.isfinite(low)
        )
        valid_bar = valid_price & volume.gt(0.0) & np.isfinite(volume)
        positive_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0) & np.isfinite(volume))
        median_vol = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
        volume_ratio = volume / median_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rare_threshold = volume_ratio.rolling(60, min_periods=45).quantile(0.95).shift(1)
        close_location = (
            (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        direction = np.sign(stock_ret)
        rare_arrival = valid_bar & volume_ratio.ge(rare_threshold)
        arrival_mark = direction * close_location.abs() * np.log(
            volume_ratio.clip(lower=1.0, upper=6.0)
        )
        arrival_input = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(valid_bar, 0.0, np.nan), index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        ).where(~rare_arrival, arrival_mark)
        prior_arrival = _reset_ewma(arrival_input, 0.18).shift(1)
        idio_arrival = _group_residual(prior_arrival, industry)

        normalized_range = bar_range / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_base = normalized_range.where(valid_bar).shift(1).rolling(
            20, min_periods=15
        ).median()
        depth_base = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        relative_depth = (volume / depth_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)) / (
            normalized_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        log_depth = np.log(relative_depth.where(relative_depth.gt(0.0)))
        depletion = (-log_depth).clip(lower=0.0)
        instability = log_depth.rolling(10, min_periods=8).std()
        decisive = (direction * close_location).clip(lower=0.0)
        mature_alignment = (direction * idio_arrival).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        terminal_direction = -direction
        agreement = np.sign(catchup_gap).eq(terminal_direction) & catchup_gap.ne(0.0)

        raw = catchup_gap * depletion * instability * decisive * mature_alignment
        eligible = (
            large_peer_shock
            & agreement
            & valid_bar
            & relative_depth.gt(0.0)
            & range_base.gt(0.0)
            & depth_base.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(idio_arrival)
            & np.isfinite(raw)
        )
        signal = raw.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return signal.reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Industry-Anchored Mature Depth Reversal
programs.trading_idea: A large industry move supplies an external price-discovery anchor, identifying constituents whose beta-adjusted response remains incomplete. The child acts only when the stock simultaneously makes a same-direction, low-depth terminal move after a prior idiosyncratic high-volume arrival, and that local exhaustion predicts reversal toward the industry's implied catch-up direction. Neither parent alone distinguishes an ordinary delayed peer adjustment from a mechanically exhausted late adjustment: the interaction selects laggards whose remaining industry gap and inventory-driven snapback point in the same direction.
programs.description: Computes a beta-adjusted leave-one-out industry catch-up gap and gates it on a mature idiosyncratic arrival followed by a thin, decisive bar whose expected reversal agrees with the peer-implied correction. Eligible observations are cross-sectionally ranked by aligned catch-up magnitude and depletion severity.

programs.code:
"""Industry-shock catch-up conditioned on return-volume state completion.

Mechanism: a sparse-participation constituent can lag a large common industry
shock, but the lag is most actionable when its own repeated return-volume state
is at a terminal point whose historically estimated next transition opposes the
current path.  The latter uses the empirically reversed sign of directional
state persistence as a completion, rather than continuation, forecast.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _industry_groups(industry: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[object, list[object]]:
    """Static industry memberships, formed without dynamic relabelling."""
    if industry.empty:
        return {}
    labels = industry.iloc[0]
    groups: dict[object, list[object]] = {}
    for column in industry.columns:
        label = labels[column]
        if pd.notna(label):
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column)
    return groups

def _excluded_industry_return(ret: pd.DataFrame, lag_cap: pd.DataFrame, groups: dict[object, list[object]]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal cap-weighted peer return, excluding the focal constituent."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for columns in groups.values():
        if len(columns) < 9:
            continue
        r = ret[columns]
        cap = lag_cap[columns]
        valid = r.notna() & cap.notna() & (cap > 0.0)
        safe_cap = cap.where(valid, 0.0)
        safe_weighted = (r * cap).where(valid, 0.0)
        total_cap = safe_cap.sum(axis=1)
        total_return = safe_weighted.sum(axis=1)
        total_count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        ex_cap = total_cap.to_numpy()[:, None] - safe_cap.to_numpy()
        ex_return = total_return.to_numpy()[:, None] - safe_weighted.to_numpy()
        ex_count = total_count.to_numpy()[:, None] - valid.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        peer = ex_return / np.where(ex_cap > 0.0, ex_cap, np.nan)
        frame = pd.DataFrame(peer, index=ret.index, columns=columns)
        output.loc[:, columns] = frame.where(ex_count >= 8.0)
    return output

def _markov_completion(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One-step state forecast from trailing return-sign/volume states.

    The transition estimate uses only transitions already completed before the
    current state is scored.  A negative sign converts persistence expectation
    into the empirically motivated completion forecast.
    """
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    vol_pct = volume.rolling(39, min_periods=30).rank(pct=True)
    sign = np.sign(ret.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    q = vol_pct.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    state = np.full(sign.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(sign) & np.isfinite(q) & (volume.to_numpy(dtype=float) > 0.0)
    vbin = np.where(q <= 1.0 / 3.0, 0, np.where(q <= 2.0 / 3.0, 1, 2))
    state[valid] = (sign[valid] + 1.0) * 3.0 + vbin[valid]
    n_time, n_assets = state.shape
    counts = np.zeros((n_assets, 9, 9), dtype=float)
    result = np.full((n_time, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)
    assets = np.arange(n_assets)
    signed_destination = np.repeat(np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0]), 3)
    for t in range(n_time):
        current = state[t]
        current_valid = np.isfinite(current)
        if current_valid.any():
            current_safe = np.where(current_valid, current, 0.0).astype(int)
            row_count = counts[assets, current_safe, :].sum(axis=1)
            total_count = counts.sum(axis=(1, 2))
            eligible = current_valid & (row_count >= 6.0) & (total_count >= 40.0)
            if eligible.any():
                idx = assets[eligible]
                current_state = current_safe[eligible]
                rows = counts[idx, current_state, :]
                probability = (rows + 1.0) / (rows.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + 9.0)
                expected_sign = probability @ signed_destination
                entropy = -np.sum(probability * np.log(probability), axis=1) / np.log(9.0)
                confidence = row_count[eligible] / (row_count[eligible] + 9.0) * (1.0 - entropy)
                result[t, idx] = -expected_sign * confidence
        if t >= 1:
            source = state[t - 1]
            destination = state[t]
            pair_valid = np.isfinite(source) & np.isfinite(destination)
            if pair_valid.any():
                idx = assets[pair_valid]
                src = source[pair_valid].astype(int)
                dst = destination[pair_valid].astype(int)
                np.add.at(counts, (idx, src, dst), 1.0)
        if t >= 81:
            source = state[t - 81]
            destination = state[t - 80]
            pair_valid = np.isfinite(source) & np.isfinite(destination)
            if pair_valid.any():
                idx = assets[pair_valid]
                src = source[pair_valid].astype(int)
                dst = destination[pair_valid].astype(int)
                np.add.at(counts, (idx, src, dst), -1.0)
    return pd.DataFrame(result, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

def _industry_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, groups: dict[object, list[object]]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Industry-relative centered percentile rank with sparse-group protection."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for columns in groups.values():
        if len(columns) < 6:
            continue
        x = values[columns].where(eligible[columns])
        enough = x.notna().sum(axis=1) >= 5
        lower = x.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        upper = x.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        clipped = x.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        ranked = clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        centered = ranked.sub(ranked.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        output.loc[:, columns] = centered.where(enough, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    return output

@register_factor
class IndustryLagMarkovCompletionGate(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'industry_lag_markov_completion_gate_j'
    name = 'Industry Lag Completion Gate'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = 'Industry-relative rank of beta-adjusted laggards after large peer shocks, activated only when a trailing return-volume Markov completion forecast agrees with the catch-up direction.'
    window_length = 102
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume']
        market_cap = data['marketCap']
        groups = _industry_groups(data['industry'])
        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        stock_ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).where((close > 0.0) & (prior_close > 0.0)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        lag_cap = market_cap.shift(1).where(market_cap.shift(1) > 0.0)
        peer_ret = _excluded_industry_return(stock_ret, lag_cap, groups)
        y = stock_ret.shift(1)
        x = peer_ret.shift(1)
        beta = y.rolling(66, min_periods=45).cov(x) / x.rolling(59, min_periods=45).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_abs_peer = peer_ret.abs().shift(1)
        threshold = prior_abs_peer.rolling(56, min_periods=45).quantile(0.8)
        large_shock = peer_ret.abs() > threshold
        signed_gap = (np.sign(peer_ret) * (beta * peer_ret - stock_ret)).where(beta.notna() & peer_ret.notna() & stock_ret.notna())
        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        median_volume = prior_volume.rolling(21, min_periods=15).median()
        low_participation = (volume > 0.0) & (median_volume > 0.0) & (volume / median_volume <= 0.75)
        dollar_volume = (prior_close * prior_volume).where((prior_close > 0.0) & (prior_volume > 0.0))
        liquid = dollar_volume.rolling(19, min_periods=15).median() >= 5000000.0
        completion = _markov_completion(close, volume)
        agreement = completion * np.sign(signed_gap) > 0.0
        eligible = large_shock & low_participation & liquid & agreement & signed_gap.notna()
        return _industry_rank(signed_gap, eligible, groups).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

"""This is a constrained test of whether daily price-volume states exhibit stable, directionally asymmetric persistence over the next six trading days, rather than evidence that identifies hidden informed metaorders. Repetitive states may reflect gradual information incorporation, recurring liquidity-demand conditions, or systematic fund-flow patterns; low conditional transition entropy is used only as a confidence filter for a direction implied by the full six-step transition path. The signal is explicitly residualized against contemporaneous short-term return and volume-surprise exposures, so any result must be incremental to conventional volume-conditioned continuation."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _volume_percentile(volume: pd.DataFrame, lookback: int=60) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal percentile against the preceding lookback positive volumes only."""
    count_le = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=volume.index, columns=volume.columns)
    all_positive = pd.DataFrame(True, index=volume.index, columns=volume.columns)
    for lag in range(1, lookback + 1):
        prior = volume.shift(lag)
        all_positive = all_positive & prior.gt(0.0)
        count_le = count_le + prior.le(volume).astype(float)
    valid = all_positive & volume.gt(0.0)
    return (count_le / float(lookback)).where(valid)

def _state_panel(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Construct nine return-sign/volume-quantile states without forward filling."""
    ret = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
    ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    q = _volume_percentile(volume, 60)
    sign_value = np.sign(ret.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    q_value = q.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    states = np.full(sign_value.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(sign_value) & np.isfinite(q_value)
    volume_state = np.where(q_value <= 1.0 / 3.0, 0, np.where(q_value <= 2.0 / 3.0, 1, 2))
    states[valid] = (sign_value[valid] + 1.0) * 3.0 + volume_state[valid]
    state_frame = pd.DataFrame(states, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    return (state_frame, q, ret)

def _six_day_markov_signal(states: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Estimate trailing smoothed transition matrices and six-step signed paths."""
    state_values = states.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_time, n_assets = state_values.shape
    output = np.full((n_time, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)
    counts = np.zeros((n_assets, 9, 9), dtype=float)
    asset_ids = np.arange(n_assets)
    signed_states = np.repeat(np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0]), 3)
    for t in range(n_time):
        if t >= 1:
            source = state_values[t - 1]
            destination = state_values[t]
            pair_valid = np.isfinite(source) & np.isfinite(destination)
            if pair_valid.any():
                idx = asset_ids[pair_valid]
                src = source[pair_valid].astype(int)
                dst = destination[pair_valid].astype(int)
                np.add.at(counts, (idx, src, dst), 1.0)
        remove_u = t - 127
        if remove_u >= 0:
            source = state_values[remove_u]
            destination = state_values[remove_u + 1]
            pair_valid = np.isfinite(source) & np.isfinite(destination)
            if pair_valid.any():
                idx = asset_ids[pair_valid]
                src = source[pair_valid].astype(int)
                dst = destination[pair_valid].astype(int)
                np.add.at(counts, (idx, src, dst), -1.0)
        current = state_values[t]
        current_valid = np.isfinite(current)
        if not current_valid.any():
            continue
        current_safe = np.where(current_valid, current, 0.0).astype(int)
        total_pairs = counts.sum(axis=(1, 2))
        current_counts = counts[asset_ids, current_safe, :].sum(axis=1)
        eligible = current_valid & (total_pairs >= 63.0) & (current_counts >= 7.0)
        if not eligible.any():
            continue
        idx = asset_ids[eligible]
        current_state = current_safe[eligible]
        selected_counts = counts[idx]
        row_totals = selected_counts.sum(axis=2, keepdims=True)
        transition = (selected_counts + 1.0) / (row_totals + 9.0)
        row_probability = transition[np.arange(len(idx)), current_state, :]
        entropy = -np.sum(row_probability * np.log(row_probability), axis=1) / np.log(9.0)
        confidence = current_counts[eligible] / (current_counts[eligible] + 9.0) * (1.0 - entropy)
        continuation = np.broadcast_to(signed_states, (len(idx), 9)).copy()
        signed_path_expectation = np.zeros(len(idx), dtype=float)
        selected_rows = np.arange(len(idx))
        for _ in range(6):
            continuation = np.einsum('nij,nj->ni', transition, continuation)
            signed_path_expectation += continuation[selected_rows, current_state]
        output[t, idx] = confidence * signed_path_expectation
    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)

def _residualized_cross_section(raw_signal: pd.DataFrame, close: pd.DataFrame, volume_percentile: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove five-day return and current volume-percentile exposures each day."""
    five_day_return = close / close.shift(4) - 1.0
    five_day_return = five_day_return.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    signal_values = raw_signal.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return_values = five_day_return.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    q_values = volume_percentile.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_time, n_assets = signal_values.shape
    output = np.full((n_time, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)
    for t in range(n_time):
        y_all = signal_values[t]
        r_all = return_values[t]
        q_all = q_values[t]
        usable = np.isfinite(y_all) & np.isfinite(r_all) & np.isfinite(q_all)
        if int(usable.sum()) < 40:
            continue
        y = y_all[usable]
        design = np.column_stack((np.ones(y.size), r_all[usable], q_all[usable]))
        if np.linalg.matrix_rank(design) < 3:
            continue
        beta, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(design, y, rcond=None)
        residual = y - design @ beta
        percentile = pd.Series(residual).rank(method='average', pct=True).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        output[t, usable] = 2.0 * percentile - 1.0
    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=raw_signal.index, columns=raw_signal.columns)

@register_factor
class SixDayConditionalStatePersistence(BaseFactor):
    """Conditional signed six-step Markov persistence residualized cross-sectionally."""
    factor_id = 'markov_compressibility_signed_completion_j'
    name = 'Six-Day Conditional State Persistence'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Nine-state return-sign and volume-percentile Markov persistence: long high-confidence positive six-day signed paths and short negative ones after residualizing conventional five-day return and volume exposure.'
    window_length = 187
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume']
        states, volume_percentile, _ = _state_panel(close, volume)
        raw_signal = _six_day_markov_signal(states)
        return _residualized_cross_section(raw_signal, close, volume_percentile)

Repetitive states may reflect gradual information incorporation, recurring liquidity-demand conditions, or systematic fund-flow patterns; low conditional transition entropy is used only as a confidence filter for a direction implied by the full six-step transition path. The signal is explicitly residualized against contemporaneous short-term return and volume-surprise exposures, so any result must be incremental to conventional volume-conditioned continuation.
programs.description: At each close t, define daily return sign rSign_t as -1 if close_t/close_{t-1}-1 < 0, 0 if it equals 0, and +1 otherwise. Define volume percentile q_t as the fraction of the prior 60 valid positive daily volumes, from t-60 through t-1, that are less than or equal to volume_t; require all 60 observations. Assign volume state vState_t=0 when q_t<=1/3, vState_t=1 when 1/3<q_t<=2/3, and vState_t=2 when q_t>2/3. The joint state X_t=(rSign_t,vState_t) has nine possible values. For each stock, estimate a causal 9-by-9 transition matrix at t using only valid state pairs X_u to X_{u+1} for u in [t-126,t-1], so every transition destination is observed no later than t and the t-to-t+1 outcome is excluded. Require at least 63 valid transition pairs overall and at least 7 observed transitions originating from the current state. Add a fixed Dirichlet prior of 1 to every destination count in each row, then row-normalize to obtain P_t. Let g be the vector of return-sign components for the nine states. Compute the six-day conditional signed-path expectation E_t=sum_{h=1}^6 P_t^h g evaluated at the current-state row. Compute normalized current-row entropy H_t=-sum_j p_j log(p_j)/log(9), and confidence C_t=(nCurrent/(nCurrent+9))*(1-H_t), where nCurrent is the unsmoothed number of historical transitions from the current state. The raw signal is S_t=C_t*E_t. To reduce direct overlap with standard short-horizon continuation, each day cross-sectionally regress S_t on an intercept, the stock's contemporaneous five-day return close_t/close_{t-5}-1, and q_t, using only eligible stocks and requiring at least 40 stocks and a full-rank design. Rank the regression residuals cross-sectionally using average ranks for ties and map percentile rank to [-1,1] as 2*percentileRank-1. Positive values are the long side and negative values the short side. The signal is formed after the t close and may only be traded thereafter; invalid or insufficient-history observations are NaN.
