from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _changed(field: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clean = field.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    previous = clean.shift(1)
    return clean.notna() & (previous.isna() | clean.ne(previous))


def _bounded_surprise(
    surprise: pd.DataFrame, estimate: pd.DataFrame, actual: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    denominator = estimate.abs() + actual.abs()
    valid = surprise.notna() & estimate.notna() & actual.notna() & denominator.gt(0.0)
    value = (surprise / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    return value.where(valid)


def _cross_sectional_score(values: pd.DataFrame, active: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    masked = values.where(active).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    ranks = masked.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    enough = masked.notna().sum(axis=1).ge(20)
    return (2.0 * ranks - 1.0).where(enough, axis=0)


@register_factor
class CashNewsAttentionRegimeSwitch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_news_attention_regime_switch"
    name = "Cash-News Attention Regime Switch"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Uses low-participation reaction gaps to trade delayed assimilation after "
        "cash-confirmed releases, but switches to high-attention valuation-dislocation "
        "reversal when no financial information update is recent."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sharesOutstanding",
        "marketCap",
        "earningsYield",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "epsActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueActual",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_release = _changed(data["epsActual"])
        revenue_release = _changed(data["revenueActual"])
        release = eps_release | revenue_release

        eps_signal = _bounded_surprise(
            data["epsSurprise"], data["epsEstimate"], data["epsActual"]
        )
        revenue_signal = _bounded_surprise(
            data["revenueSurprise"], data["revenueEstimate"], data["revenueActual"]
        )
        surprise_count = eps_signal.notna().astype(float) + revenue_signal.notna().astype(float)
        surprise = (eps_signal.fillna(0.0) + revenue_signal.fillna(0.0)) / surprise_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        fcf = data["freeCashFlow"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_confirmed = fcf.gt(0.0) & income_quality.ge(1.0)
        cash_weak = fcf.le(0.0) | income_quality.lt(1.0)
        credibility = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        credibility = credibility.mask(cash_confirmed, 1.0)
        credibility = credibility.mask(cash_weak, -0.5)
        fundamental = surprise * (1.0 + 0.5 * credibility)

        ret5 = close / close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        turnover = volume / shares.where(shares.gt(0.0))
        fast_turnover = turnover.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        slow_turnover = turnover.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean()
        low_participation = (1.0 - fast_turnover / slow_turnover.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.75)

        market_return = ret5.median(axis=1)
        idio_return = ret5.sub(market_return, axis=0)
        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        idio_scale = daily_return.rolling(60, min_periods=40).std() * np.sqrt(5.0)
        standardized_reaction = (idio_return / idio_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        aligned_reaction = np.sign(fundamental) * standardized_reaction
        event_raw = fundamental * (1.0 - 0.5 * low_participation * aligned_reaction)

        liquid = volume.gt(0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().ge(16.0)
        event_active = (
            release
            & fundamental.notna()
            & standardized_reaction.notna()
            & low_participation.notna()
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & data["marketCap"].ge(300_000_000.0)
            & liquid
        )
        event_position = _cross_sectional_score(event_raw, event_active).fillna(0.0)
        held_event = event_position.rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum()

        valuation_yield = data["earningsYield"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        valuation_yield = valuation_yield.where(valuation_yield.notna(), fcf_yield)
        valuation_rank = valuation_yield.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return_rank = ret5.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        prior_median_volume = volume.shift(1).where(volume.shift(1).gt(0.0)).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        abnormal_attention = np.log(volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)) / prior_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
        quiet_raw = abnormal_attention * ((2.0 * valuation_rank - 1.0) - (2.0 * return_rank - 1.0))

        blocked = release.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).max().gt(0.0)
        quiet_active = (
            ~blocked
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & ret5.notna()
            & valuation_yield.notna()
            & abnormal_attention.notna()
            & liquid
        )
        quiet_position = _cross_sectional_score(quiet_raw, quiet_active).fillna(0.0)

        signal = (held_event + quiet_position).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

Immediately after a cash-confirmed earnings or revenue surprise, an unusually muted turnover response identifies incomplete assimilation, so the fundamental surprise should continue to drift; outside a report window, elevated-volume moves away from an earnings or free-cash-flow valuation anchor are more likely attention-driven overshoots and should reverse. Neither parent alone distinguishes whether volume represents slow diffusion of credible news or crowded non-news extrapolation, while the state switch explicitly assigns opposite meanings to participation conditional on public-information arrival.

"""A fresh quarterly increase in short-term debt financed by a shrinking cash buffer, especially alongside deteriorating interest coverage, reveals rollover risk that headline earnings and conventional valuation models often underweight. Equity investors initially treat the change as routine working-capital financing, while credit-sensitive investors and fundamental analysts update more slowly as they assess whether the issuer can refinance on acceptable terms. The falsifiable claim is that firms with the largest newly disclosed deterioration in net short-term funding capacity subsequently underperform over the next six trading days. The inefficiency persists because benchmarked long-only holders and passive investors are slower to reduce exposure, while specialist credit capital may be unable or unwilling to express the view directly in the equity immediately after disclosure."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_mask(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify point-in-time step changes relative to the preceding bar."""
    previous = frame.shift(1)
    tolerance = 1.0e-12 * (1.0 + frame.abs() + previous.abs())
    return (
        frame.notna()
        & previous.notna()
        & ((frame - previous).abs() > tolerance)
    )


def _robust_cross_section(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal row-wise robust standardisation for heterogeneous accounting ratios."""
    row_median = frame.median(axis=1)
    centered = frame.sub(row_median, axis=0)
    mad = centered.abs().median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    scale = (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return centered.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-5.0, 5.0)


def _refinancing_stress(
    short_term_debt: pd.DataFrame,
    cash: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    interest_coverage: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Construct a fresh-disclosure rollover-risk score using only current and lagged filings."""
    prior_debt = short_term_debt.shift(1)
    prior_cash = cash.shift(1)
    prior_coverage = interest_coverage.shift(1)

    safe_market_cap = market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)
    debt_pressure = (short_term_debt - prior_debt).div(safe_market_cap)

    current_cash_buffer = cash.div(short_term_debt.where(short_term_debt > 0.0))
    prior_cash_buffer = prior_cash.div(prior_debt.where(prior_debt > 0.0))
    cash_buffer_erosion = -(current_cash_buffer - prior_cash_buffer)

    coverage_deterioration = -(interest_coverage - prior_coverage)

    debt_z = _robust_cross_section(debt_pressure)
    cash_z = _robust_cross_section(cash_buffer_erosion)
    coverage_z = _robust_cross_section(coverage_deterioration)

    weighted_parts = [
        debt_z * 0.45,
        cash_z * 0.35,
        coverage_z * 0.20,
    ]
    available_parts = [
        debt_z.notna().astype(float) * 0.45,
        cash_z.notna().astype(float) * 0.35,
        coverage_z.notna().astype(float) * 0.20,
    ]
    weighted_score = sum(weighted_parts)
    available_weight = sum(available_parts).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    stress = weighted_score.div(available_weight)

    disclosure_event = (
        _update_mask(short_term_debt)
        | _update_mask(cash)
        | _update_mask(interest_coverage)
    )
    return stress, disclosure_event


@register_factor
class RefinancingRolloverDisclosureDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Short newly disclosed deterioration in near-term refinancing capacity."""

    factor_id = "refinancing_rollover_disclosure_drift"
    name = "Refinancing Rollover Disclosure Drift"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "On fresh quarterly disclosures, ranks deterioration in short-term debt "
        "relative to market value, cash coverage of short-term debt, and interest "
        "coverage; high funding stress is assigned a negative expected-return signal."
    )
    window_length = 2
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "shortTermDebt",
        "cash",
        "marketCap",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        stress, disclosure_event = _refinancing_stress(
            data["shortTermDebt"],
            data["cash"],
            data["marketCap"],
            data["interestCoverage"],
        )

        event_rank = rank(stress.where(disclosure_event))
        signal = -event_rank.fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Refinancing Rollover Disclosure Drift
programs.trading_idea: A fresh quarterly increase in short-term debt financed by a shrinking cash buffer, especially alongside deteriorating interest coverage, reveals rollover risk that headline earnings and conventional valuation models often underweight. Equity investors initially treat the change as routine working-capital financing, while credit-sensitive investors and fundamental analysts update more slowly as they assess whether the issuer can refinance on acceptable terms. The falsifiable claim is that firms with the largest newly disclosed deterioration in net short-term funding capacity subsequently underperform over the next six trading days. The inefficiency persists because benchmarked long-only holders and passive investors are slower to reduce exposure, while specialist credit capital may be unable or unwilling to express the view directly in the equity immediately after disclosure.
programs.description: On newly available quarterly balance-sheet updates, compute a cross-sectional funding-stress score from the increase in shortTermDebt relative to marketCap, the decline in cash relative to shortTermDebt, and worsening interestCoverage. Assign high scores to firms whose near-term refinancing burden has increased most; the expected return relationship is negative.

programs.code:
"""A sector-relative price displacement on below-normal, but still investable, participation can reflect gradual information diffusion rather than a fully incorporated repricing. The signal therefore treats low relative turnover as a constraint on the speed of incorporation: positive idiosyncratic displacements with subdued participation are expected to continue outperforming, while negative displacements are expected to continue underperforming. This replaces the unsupported assumption that liquidity providers can safely fade every low-volume move with a delayed-information mechanism consistent with concentrated informed trading and slow broader investor response."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_sector_return(
    returns_5d: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute causal same-day, leave-one-out equal-weighted sector returns."""
    peer_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=returns_5d.index, columns=returns_5d.columns)

    for timestamp in returns_5d.index:
        ret_row = returns_5d.loc[timestamp]
        eligible_row = eligible.loc[timestamp]
        sector_row = sector.loc[timestamp]
        valid = eligible_row & ret_row.notna() & sector_row.notna()

        if not valid.any():
            continue

        values = ret_row.where(valid)
        groups = sector_row.where(valid)
        group_sum = values.groupby(groups).transform("sum")
        group_count = values.groupby(groups).transform("count")
        loo_count = group_count - 1.0
        loo_return = (group_sum - values) / loo_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        peer_return.loc[timestamp] = loo_return.where(loo_count >= 4.0)

    return peer_return


def _winsorize_cross_sectionally(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    lower_quantile: float,
    upper_quantile: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each date's valid cross section without using future rows."""
    masked = values.where(valid)
    lower = masked.quantile(lower_quantile, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(upper_quantile, axis=1)
    return masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


@register_factor
class LowParticipationRelativeDisplacementFade(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-relative displacement continuation conditioned on subdued turnover."""

    factor_id = "low_participation_relative_displacement_fade"
    name = "Low-Participation Relative Displacement Continuation"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks five-day leave-one-out sector-relative price displacement, "
        "amplified when recent turnover is below the stock's own trailing "
        "60-day participation baseline."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sharesOutstanding", "marketCap", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        close_5d_ago = close.shift(5)
        return_5d = close / close_5d_ago.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        valid_return = close.gt(0.0) & close_5d_ago.gt(0.0)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close.gt(0.0) & volume.notna())
        positive_volume_days = volume.gt(0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
        median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()

        valid_shares = shares.gt(0.0)
        turnover = volume.where(valid_shares & volume.notna()) / shares.where(valid_shares)
        turnover_valid_count_5 = turnover.notna().rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        turnover_valid_count_60 = turnover.notna().rolling(60, min_periods=60).sum()

        fast_turnover = turnover.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        slow_turnover_sum = turnover.fillna(0.0).rolling(60, min_periods=60).sum()
        slow_turnover = slow_turnover_sum / turnover_valid_count_60.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eligible = (
            valid_return
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & valid_shares
            & market_cap.ge(300_000_000.0)
            & positive_volume_days.ge(16.0)
            & median_dollar_volume.ge(1_000_000.0)
            & turnover_valid_count_5.ge(5.0)
            & turnover_valid_count_60.ge(40.0)
        )

        peer_return = _leave_one_out_sector_return(return_5d, eligible, sector)
        displacement = return_5d - peer_return
        valid_displacement = eligible & peer_return.notna()
        winsorized_displacement = _winsorize_cross_sectionally(
            displacement,
            valid_displacement,
            0.01,
            0.99,
        )

        relative_participation = fast_turnover / slow_turnover.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_participation = relative_participation.clip(lower=0.25, upper=4.0)
        multiplier = 1.0 / relative_participation

        score = (winsorized_displacement * multiplier).where(
            valid_displacement & slow_turnover.gt(0.0) & relative_participation.notna()
        )
        return rank(score)

programs.trading_idea: A sector-relative price displacement on below-normal, but still investable, participation can reflect gradual information diffusion rather than a fully incorporated repricing. The signal therefore treats low relative turnover as a constraint on the speed of incorporation: positive idiosyncratic displacements with subdued participation are expected to continue outperforming, while negative displacements are expected to continue underperforming. This replaces the unsupported assumption that liquidity providers can safely fade every low-volume move with a delayed-information mechanism consistent with concentrated informed trading and slow broader investor response.
programs.description: Form the signal after the close of day t using only observations available through t, and trade no earlier than the next bar, t+1. Eligible stocks must have positive close and positive point-in-time sharesOutstanding on the required dates, marketCap at t of at least USD 300 million, at least 16 positive-volume days over t-19 through t, and median daily dollar volume, median(close multiplied by volume), over t-19 through t of at least USD 1 million. Define the close-to-close 5-day return as r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-5 - 1. For each sector on t, compute an equal-weighted leave-one-out peer return b_i,t from eligible same-sector stocks other than i with valid 5-day returns; require at least four such peers, otherwise assign no signal. The relative displacement is d_i,t = r_i,t - b_i,t. Winsorize d_i,t each day at the 1st and 99th percentiles of valid eligible-stock displacements. Define daily turnover tau_i,s = volume_i,s / sharesOutstanding_i,s, with zero volume retained as zero turnover; require at least five valid turnover observations from t-4 through t and at least 40 valid observations from t-59 through t. Let fast_i,t be the arithmetic mean of tau_i,s over t-4 through t and slow_i,t the arithmetic mean over t-59 through t. Define relative participation q_i,t = fast_i,t / slow_i,t, requiring slow_i,t > 0, clip q_i,t to [0.25, 4.0], and define the bounded low-participation multiplier m_i,t = 1 / q_i,t. The raw score is s_i,t = winsorized(d_i,t) multiplied by m_i,t. The delivered cross-sectional factor is the ascending percentile rank of s_i,t among eligible stocks on t, so higher factor values imply higher expected six-bar returns. This differs from high-volume price-pressure and intraday-dislocation reversal families because it uses a five-day close-to-close, leave-one-out sector-relative displacement and predicts continuation conditional on turnover being below the stock's own 60-day participation baseline, rather than fading a high-impact or opening-volume shock.

"""The revised mechanism is post-earnings-announcement drift rather than a slow valuation-surface reversal. Investors can initially extrapolate a reported earnings or revenue surprise without fully distinguishing a cash-supported operating improvement from an accounting-supported or weak-conversion result. Positive surprises with positive free cash flow and adequate cash conversion should exhibit stronger six-bar continuation, while negative surprises accompanied by weak cash generation should exhibit stronger negative continuation."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _new_release_event(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag a newly available or changed reported release value, causally."""
    previous = actual.shift(1)
    return actual.notna() & (previous.isna() | actual.ne(previous))

def _surprise_intensity(surprise: pd.DataFrame, estimate: pd.DataFrame, actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute a bounded surprise only where every required input is valid."""
    denominator = estimate.abs() + actual.abs()
    valid = surprise.notna() & estimate.notna() & actual.notna() & denominator.gt(0.0)
    intensity = (surprise / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    return intensity.where(valid)

def _cashflow_confirmation(free_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame, income_quality: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Assign cash-flow confirmation without imputing a claim for missing data."""
    available = free_cash_flow.notna() & income_quality.notna()
    positive = free_cash_flow.gt(0.0) & income_quality.ge(1.0)
    negative = free_cash_flow.le(0.0) | income_quality.le(0.0)
    confirmation = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=free_cash_flow.index, columns=free_cash_flow.columns)
    confirmation = confirmation.where(~(available & positive), 1.0)
    confirmation = confirmation.where(~(available & negative), -1.0)
    return confirmation

@register_factor
class EarningsSurpriseCashflowConfirmation(BaseFactor):
    """Cash-confirmed earnings-release surprise drift held for six daily bars."""
    factor_id = 'earnings_surprise_cashflow_confirmation_j'
    name = 'Cash-Flow Confirmed Earnings Surprise'
    category = 'momentum'
    description = 'Ranks new earnings-release surprises after amplifying cash-supported results and penalizing weak cash conversion, then holds the release signal for exactly six daily bars.'
    window_length = 6
    inputs = ['close', 'epsActual', 'revenueActual', 'epsSurprise', 'epsEstimate', 'revenueSurprise', 'revenueEstimate', 'freeCashFlow', 'incomeQuality']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        eps_actual = data['epsActual']
        revenue_actual = data['revenueActual']
        release_event = _new_release_event(eps_actual) | _new_release_event(revenue_actual)
        eps_intensity = _surprise_intensity(data['epsSurprise'], data['epsEstimate'], eps_actual)
        revenue_intensity = _surprise_intensity(data['revenueSurprise'], data['revenueEstimate'], revenue_actual)
        component_count = eps_intensity.notna().astype(float) + revenue_intensity.notna().astype(float)
        event_surprise = (eps_intensity.fillna(0.0) + revenue_intensity.fillna(0.0)) / component_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        confirmation = _cashflow_confirmation(data['freeCashFlow'], data['incomeQuality'])
        event_score = event_surprise * (1.0 + 0.5 * confirmation)
        event_score = event_score.where(release_event & event_surprise.notna())
        sufficient_events = event_score.notna().sum(axis=1).ge(30)
        event_score = event_score.where(sufficient_events, axis=0)
        event_position = (2.0 * rank(event_score) - 1.0).where(event_score.notna())
        held_position = event_position.fillna(0.0).rolling(7, min_periods=1).sum()
        return held_position.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Cash-Flow Confirmed Earnings Surprise (jitter)
programs.trading_idea: The revised mechanism is post-earnings-announcement drift rather than a slow valuation-surface reversal. Investors can initially extrapolate a reported earnings or revenue surprise without fully distinguishing a cash-supported operating improvement from an accounting-supported or weak-conversion result. Positive surprises with positive free cash flow and adequate cash conversion should exhibit stronger six-bar continuation, while negative surprises accompanied by weak cash generation should exhibit stronger negative continuation.
programs.description: On a date when either epsActual or revenueActual changes from its prior available value, treat the name as having a new earnings-release event. Compute EPS surprise intensity as epsSurprise divided by abs(epsEstimate) plus abs(epsActual), and revenue surprise intensity as revenueSurprise divided by abs(revenueEstimate) plus abs(revenueActual); discard an intensity if its denominator is zero or either required input is missing. Define the event surprise as the equal-weight average of the available EPS and revenue intensities, requiring at least one valid component and clipping each component to [-1, 1]. Define cash-flow confirmation q as +1 when freeCashFlow is positive and incomeQuality is at least 1, -1 when freeCashFlow is non-positive or incomeQuality is non-positive, and 0 otherwise; missing freeCashFlow or incomeQuality sets q to 0 rather than imputing a quality claim. The final event score is event surprise multiplied by (1 + 0.5 times q). Rank only current release-event scores cross-sectionally, require at least 30 valid event names on a date, go long high positive scores and short low negative scores, and hold each event position for exactly 6 daily bars. There is no valuation regression, operating-margin expectation, industry surface, or unstated estimate-change window; all inputs are the point-in-time fields available on the release date.

programs.code:
"""Capacity-backed refinancing dislocation.

Mechanism: temporary short-term funding stress is not uniformly bad news.  When a
fresh debt-and-cash deterioration coincides with a substantially improved longer-run
debt-service profile, a lagging equity price can reflect an initial rollover-risk
misclassification that is corrected over the following trading week.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _updated(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time filing-update indicator, using only the preceding bar."""
    previous = frame.shift(1)
    tolerance = 1.0e-12 * (1.0 + frame.abs() + previous.abs())
    return frame.notna() & previous.notna() & ((frame - previous).abs() > tolerance)


def _finite(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.DataFrame(
        np.isfinite(frame.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)),
        index=frame.index,
        columns=frame.columns,
    )


def _industry_peer_return(
    firm_return: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-one-out equal-weight industry return, requiring at least six names."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=firm_return.index, columns=firm_return.columns)
    for row in range(len(firm_return.index)):
        values = firm_return.iloc[row]
        groups = industry.iloc[row]
        valid = values.notna() & groups.notna()
        if not bool(valid.any()):
            continue
        grouped_values = values.where(valid)
        grouped_groups = groups.where(valid)
        group_sum = grouped_values.groupby(grouped_groups, sort=False).sum()
        group_count = grouped_values.groupby(grouped_groups, sort=False).count()
        mapped_sum = grouped_groups.map(group_sum)
        mapped_count = grouped_groups.map(group_count)
        peer = (mapped_sum - grouped_values) / (mapped_count - 1.0)
        output.iloc[row] = peer.where(mapped_count >= 6.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return output


def _carry_event_score(score: pd.DataFrame, bars: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally retain a positive filing-event score for the next few bars."""
    carried = score.copy()
    for lag in range(1, bars):
        carried = carried.combine(score.shift(lag), np.maximum)
    return carried.fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class BridgeRefinancingCapacityDislocation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "bridge_refinancing_capacity_dislocation"
    name = "Bridge Refinancing Capacity Dislocation"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Buys fresh short-term funding-stress disclosures when improving debt-service "
        "capacity and an industry-relative price lag indicate bridge-financing "
        "misclassification rather than persistent rollover distress."
    )
    window_length = 64
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "shortTermDebt",
        "cash",
        "marketCap",
        "interestCoverage",
        "totalDebt",
        "ebitda",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        short_debt = data["shortTermDebt"]
        cash = data["cash"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        coverage = data["interestCoverage"]
        total_debt = data["totalDebt"]
        ebitda = data["ebitda"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        prior_short_debt = short_debt.shift(1)
        prior_cash = cash.shift(1)
        debt_pressure = (short_debt - prior_short_debt) / market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)
        cash_buffer = cash / short_debt.where(short_debt > 0.0)
        prior_cash_buffer = prior_cash / prior_short_debt.where(prior_short_debt > 0.0)
        buffer_erosion = prior_cash_buffer - cash_buffer

        funding_event = _updated(short_debt) | _updated(cash) | _updated(coverage)
        stress = 0.60 * rank(debt_pressure) + 0.40 * rank(buffer_erosion)

        lag_coverage = coverage.shift(63)
        lag_net_debt = total_debt.shift(63) - cash.shift(63)
        lag_ebitda = ebitda.shift(63)
        net_debt = total_debt - cash
        nd_ebitda = net_debt / ebitda.where(ebitda > 0.0)
        lag_nd_ebitda = lag_net_debt / lag_ebitda.where(lag_ebitda > 0.0)

        coverage_change = np.log(coverage.where(coverage > 0.0)) - np.log(
            lag_coverage.where(lag_coverage > 0.0)
        )
        deleveraging_change = lag_nd_ebitda - nd_ebitda
        capacity = 0.50 * rank(coverage_change) + 0.50 * rank(deleveraging_change)

        firm_return = close / close.shift(20).where(close.shift(20) > 0.0) - 1.0
        peer_return = _industry_peer_return(firm_return, industry)
        relative_lag = peer_return - firm_return
        lag_rank = rank(relative_lag)

        valid = (
            short_debt.gt(0.0)
            & market_cap.gt(0.0)
            & ebitda.gt(0.0)
            & lag_ebitda.gt(0.0)
            & coverage.gt(0.0)
            & lag_coverage.gt(0.0)
            & net_debt.ge(0.0)
            & lag_net_debt.ge(0.0)
            & _finite(stress)
            & _finite(capacity)
            & _finite(relative_lag)
        )
        qualification = (
            valid
            & funding_event
            & stress.ge(0.60)
            & capacity.ge(0.60)
            & coverage_change.gt(0.0)
            & deleveraging_change.gt(0.0)
            & relative_lag.gt(0.0)
        )

        event_score = (stress * capacity * lag_rank).where(qualification)
        retained_score = _carry_event_score(event_score, 6)
        signal = rank(retained_score.where(retained_score > 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Bridge Refinancing Capacity Dislocation
programs.trading_idea: A fresh rise in short-term debt and decline in the cash buffer is normally a bearish rollover-risk disclosure, but it can be a temporary bridge-financing signal when the same issuer has materially improved interest coverage and reduced net-debt-to-EBITDA since the prior reporting state. The child buys these apparent refinancing-stress events only when the stock is lagging its industry, identifying cases where equity investors extrapolate the short-term funding deterioration while underweighting the stronger medium-term debt-service trajectory. Neither parent alone distinguishes benign, capacity-backed bridge funding from genuine rollover stress, nor does either isolate the resulting short-horizon correction in an industry-relative laggard.
programs.description: On fresh funding disclosures, the factor identifies firms with cross-sectionally high short-term funding stress but simultaneously strong disclosed improvement in debt-service capacity and a negative industry-relative price gap. The event score is carried for six bars to capture delayed reassessment after the filing.

programs.code:
"""The intended incremental mechanism is a valuation-conditioned subset of short-horizon price-volume reversals: a high-activity move is treated as potentially excessive only when it moves a stock further away from its latest public earnings or cash-flow anchor and no newly available financial report or estimate update is observed. Cheap stocks with recent declines and expensive stocks with recent gains are expected to mean revert over the next six trading days when the move occurs on elevated volume but outside an observable information-update window. This does not assert that all high-volume moves are uninformed; it deliberately excludes names with observable contemporaneous earnings, revenue, cash-flow, balance-sheet, or consensus-estimate updates.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _winsorize_cross_section(values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize eligible observations at row-wise 1st and 99th percentiles."""
    masked = values.where(eligible).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0).where(eligible)

def _report_or_estimate_update(fields: list[pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag new reported values or changes in point-in-time field levels."""
    update = pd.DataFrame(False, index=fields[0].index, columns=fields[0].columns)
    for field in fields:
        current = field.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        previous = current.shift(1)
        changed = current.notna() & (previous.isna() | current.ne(previous))
        update = update | changed.fillna(False)
    return update

@register_factor
class AttentionWeightedValuationOvershoot(BaseFactor):
    """High-volume valuation dislocations outside observable information-update windows."""
    factor_id = 'attention_weighted_valuation_overshoot_j'
    name = 'No-Report Valuation-Return Dislocation'
    category = 'mean_reversion'
    description = 'Equal-dollar decile portfolio of high-volume five-day valuation-return dislocations, excluding stocks on financial-report or estimate-update days and the following five trading days.'
    window_length = 26
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'earningsYield', 'freeCashFlowYield', 'epsActual', 'revenueActual', 'epsSurprise', 'revenueSurprise', 'epsEstimate', 'revenueEstimate', 'revenue', 'eps', 'operatingIncome', 'netIncome', 'freeCashFlow', 'totalAssets', 'totalDebt', 'totalEquity']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data['volume'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        earnings_yield = data['earningsYield'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        fcf_yield = data['freeCashFlowYield'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        valuation_yield = earnings_yield.where(earnings_yield.notna(), fcf_yield)
        prior_close_count = close.notna().shift(1).rolling(27, min_periods=25).sum()
        has_history = prior_close_count.eq(25)
        eligible = close.notna() & volume.notna() & valuation_yield.notna() & has_history
        five_day_return = close / close.shift(4).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).where(volume.shift(1) > 0.0).rolling(21, min_periods=20).median()
        safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        abnormal_volume = np.log(safe_volume / prior_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        valuation_winsor = _winsorize_cross_section(valuation_yield, eligible)
        volume_winsor = _winsorize_cross_section(abnormal_volume, eligible)
        valuation_rank = valuation_winsor.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return_rank = five_day_return.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        valuation_signal = 2.0 * valuation_rank - 1.0
        return_signal = 2.0 * return_rank - 1.0
        attention = volume_winsor.clip(lower=0.0)
        score = attention * (valuation_signal - return_signal)
        update_fields = [data['epsActual'], data['revenueActual'], data['epsSurprise'], data['revenueSurprise'], data['epsEstimate'], data['revenueEstimate'], data['revenue'], data['eps'], data['operatingIncome'], data['netIncome'], data['freeCashFlow'], data['totalAssets'], data['totalDebt'], data['totalEquity']]
        update_today = _report_or_estimate_update(update_fields)
        blocked = update_today.astype(float).rolling(5, min_periods=1).max().gt(0.0)
        active = eligible & score.notna() & ~blocked
        active_count = active.sum(axis=1)
        enough_names = active_count.ge(20)
        score_rank = score.where(active).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        long_mask = active & score_rank.ge(0.9) & enough_names
        short_mask = active & score_rank.le(0.1) & enough_names
        long_count = long_mask.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan)
        short_count = short_mask.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan)
        long_weight = long_mask.astype(float).div(long_count, axis=0)
        short_weight = short_mask.astype(float).div(short_count, axis=0)
        signal = (long_weight - short_weight).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
programs.name: No-Report Valuation-Return Dislocation (jitter)
programs.trading_idea: The intended incremental mechanism is a valuation-conditioned subset of short-horizon price-volume reversals: a high-activity move is treated as potentially excessive only when it moves a stock further away from its latest public earnings or cash-flow anchor and no newly available financial report or estimate update is observed. Cheap stocks with recent declines and expensive stocks with recent gains are expected to mean revert over the next six trading days when the move occurs on elevated volume but outside an observable information-update window. This does not assert that all high-volume moves are uninformed; it deliberately excludes names with observable contemporaneous earnings, revenue, cash-flow, balance-sheet, or consensus-estimate updates.
programs.description: At each decision date, form the eligible universe from stocks with non-missing close, volume, a valuation yield, and at least 25 prior daily bars; rank all eligible stocks cross-sectionally. Define 5-day return as close[t] / close[t-5] - 1. Define abnormal-volume intensity as a = log(volume[t] / median(volume[t-20:t-1])); winsorize a cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles and set A = max(a, 0), so below-baseline volume receives zero weight. Use earningsYield as the predetermined valuation metric; where it is missing, substitute freeCashFlowYield. Winsorize the resulting yield cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles, rank it within the eligible universe, and map the rank to V = 2*rank - 1, where high V denotes cheapness. Rank 5-day returns and map that rank to R = 2*rank - 1. The raw alpha score is S = A * (V - R): high-volume cheap recent losers receive high scores, while high-volume expensive recent winners receive low scores. A stock is neutralized if any of epsActual, revenueActual, epsSurprise, revenueSurprise, epsEstimate, revenueEstimate, revenue, eps, operatingIncome, netIncome, freeCashFlow, totalAssets, totalDebt, or totalEquity changes versus the prior available daily value, including a NaN-to-reported-value transition. The stock remains excluded on that update day and the following 5 trading days. These fields operationalize observable earnings, financial-report, and consensus-information updates; explicit management-guidance and corporate-event labels are not available in the supplied data and therefore cannot be separately identified or claimed to be excluded. Among remaining eligible names, hold an equal-dollar long portfolio in the top score decile and an equal-dollar short portfolio in the bottom score decile, rebalanced daily; require at least 20 non-excluded eligible names, otherwise hold no position.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_cash_confirmed_events(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    free_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame,
    income_quality: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Create causal, cash-conditioned paired-surprise events."""
    eps = eps_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    revenue = revenue_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    eps_new = eps.notna() & (eps.shift(1).isna() | eps.ne(eps.shift(1)))
    revenue_new = revenue.notna() & (
        revenue.shift(1).isna() | revenue.ne(revenue.shift(1))
    )
    same_sign = ((eps > 0.0) & (revenue > 0.0)) | ((eps < 0.0) & (revenue < 0.0))
    event = eps_new & revenue_new & same_sign

    event_eps = eps.abs().where(event)
    event_revenue = revenue.abs().where(event)
    magnitude = 0.5 * (
        event_eps.rank(axis=1, pct=True) + event_revenue.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    )
    direction = np.sign(eps).where(event)

    confirmation = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=eps.index, columns=eps.columns)
    strong_cash = free_cash_flow.gt(0.0) & income_quality.ge(1.0)
    weak_cash = free_cash_flow.le(0.0) | income_quality.le(0.0)
    confirmation = confirmation.where(~strong_cash, 1.0)
    confirmation = confirmation.where(~weak_cash, -1.0)

    # Positive news is more credible with strong cash conversion, while
    # negative news is more credible when cash generation is weak.
    weight = 1.0 + 0.5 * direction * confirmation
    return (direction * magnitude * weight).where(event)


def _report_age(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bars elapsed since the target's own latest surprise-field update."""
    eps_update = eps_surprise.notna() & (
        eps_surprise.shift(1).isna() | eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1))
    )
    revenue_update = revenue_surprise.notna() & (
        revenue_surprise.shift(1).isna()
        | revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_surprise.shift(1))
    )
    update = eps_update | revenue_update
    ages = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=update.index, columns=update.columns)
    running = np.full(len(update.columns), np.nan)
    for row_pos in range(len(update.index)):
        known = np.isfinite(running)
        running[known] += 1.0
        arriving = update.iloc[row_pos].to_numpy(dtype=bool)
        running[arriving] = 0.0
        ages.iloc[row_pos] = running
    return ages


def _industry_relay(
    events: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    report_age: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-one-out three-bar industry event relay to stale reporters."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    for row_pos in range(len(close.index)):
        labels = industry.iloc[row_pos]
        valid = labels.notna() & close.iloc[row_pos].gt(0.0)
        ages = report_age.iloc[row_pos]
        recent = events.iloc[max(0, row_pos - 2) : row_pos + 1]

        for label in pd.unique(labels.loc[valid]):
            members = np.flatnonzero(
                (labels.to_numpy() == label) & valid.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
            )
            if len(members) < 5:
                continue
            for target in members:
                age = ages.iat[target]
                if not np.isfinite(age) or age < 15.0 or age > 100.0:
                    continue
                peers = members[members != target]
                peer_events = recent.iloc[:, peers].to_numpy(dtype=float).ravel()
                peer_events = peer_events[np.isfinite(peer_events)]
                if peer_events.size < 2:
                    continue
                output.iat[row_pos, target] = float(np.mean(peer_events))
    return output


@register_factor
class CashConfirmedPeerRelayAttentionGap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_confirmed_peer_relay_attention_gap"
    name = "Cash-Confirmed Peer Relay Attention Gap"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Relays fresh, cash-confirmed paired earnings and revenue surprises from "
        "industry peers to late-reporting firms, with stronger exposure when the "
        "target's current volume is low relative to its own recent activity."
    )
    window_length = 100
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        events = _fresh_cash_confirmed_events(
            data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
            data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
            data["freeCashFlow"].reindex_like(close),
            data["incomeQuality"].reindex_like(close),
        )
        ages = _report_age(
            data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
            data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
        )
        relay = _industry_relay(
            events,
            data["industry"].reindex_like(close),
            ages,
            close,
        )

        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        activity_ratio = volume.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean() / volume.rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        attention_gap = 1.5 - activity_ratio.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        return (relay * attention_gap).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Cash-Confirmed Peer Relay Attention Gap
programs.trading_idea: Cash-confirmed, same-direction EPS and revenue surprises from reporting peers reveal industry demand information that is more credible than an unconditioned peer surprise. That information should diffuse most slowly to firms that have not reported recently and are experiencing unusually weak trading participation, where low attention and limited liquidity-mediated information processing delay repricing. Neither parent alone distinguishes credible peer news from weak-quality peer news while also identifying the low-attention targets most likely to underreact.
programs.description: The signal forms fresh dual-surprise events whose magnitude is amplified when the reporting peer's cash flow and income quality support the surprise, then relays recent industry-peer events to late-reporting targets. Relay exposure is increased for targets with low 3-bar volume relative to their trailing 20-bar volume.

"""Refinancing-conditioned downside earnings catalyst.

Mechanism: a negative earnings surprise is most damaging when a recent filing has
already revealed worsening short-term refinancing capacity.  The earnings miss
then validates a latent credit concern and causes a faster equity repricing than
either disclosure is expected to generate in isolation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _updated(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time filing update mask, using only the preceding bar."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    tolerance = 1e-12 * (1.0 + clean.abs() + prior.abs())
    return clean.notna() & prior.notna() & ((clean - prior).abs() > tolerance)

def _robust_cs(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional MAD standardisation, clipped against ratio outliers."""
    median = frame.median(axis=1)
    centered = frame.sub(median, axis=0)
    mad = centered.abs().median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return centered.div(1.4826 * mad, axis=0).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

def _funding_stress(short_debt: pd.DataFrame, cash: pd.DataFrame, market_cap: pd.DataFrame, interest_coverage: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Fresh funding-capacity deterioration and its filing-date mask."""
    short_debt = short_debt.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    cash = cash.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    market_cap = market_cap.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    interest_coverage = interest_coverage.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior_debt = short_debt.shift(1)
    prior_cash = cash.shift(1)
    prior_coverage = interest_coverage.shift(1)
    debt_pressure = (short_debt - prior_debt).div(market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0))
    current_buffer = cash.div(short_debt.where(short_debt > 0.0))
    prior_buffer = prior_cash.div(prior_debt.where(prior_debt > 0.0))
    buffer_erosion = -(current_buffer - prior_buffer)
    coverage_drop = -(interest_coverage - prior_coverage)
    debt_z = _robust_cs(debt_pressure)
    cash_z = _robust_cs(buffer_erosion)
    coverage_z = _robust_cs(coverage_drop)
    numerator = 0.45 * debt_z + 0.35 * cash_z + 0.2 * coverage_z
    denominator = (0.45 * debt_z.notna().astype(float) + 0.35 * cash_z.notna().astype(float) + 0.2 * coverage_z.notna().astype(float)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    stress = numerator.div(denominator)
    event = _updated(short_debt) | _updated(cash) | _updated(interest_coverage)
    return (stress, event)

@register_factor
class RefinancingConditionedDownsideEarningsCatalyst(BaseFactor):
    """Short downside earnings events that validate recently disclosed funding stress."""
    factor_id = 'refinancing_conditioned_downside_earnings_cataly'
    name = 'Refinancing-Conditioned Earnings Downside'
    category = 'other'
    description = 'Shorts severe fresh negative EPS surprises only when a high recent refinancing-stress filing has exposed debt, cash-buffer, or coverage deterioration.'
    window_length = 7
    inputs = ['close', 'epsSurprise', 'shortTermDebt', 'cash', 'marketCap', 'interestCoverage']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_surprise = data['epsSurprise'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        stress, funding_event = _funding_stress(data['shortTermDebt'], data['cash'], data['marketCap'], data['interestCoverage'])
        stress_impulse = rank(stress.where(funding_event)).fillna(0.0)
        recent_stress = stress_impulse.rolling(6, min_periods=1).max()
        prior_surprise = eps_surprise.shift(1)
        earnings_event = eps_surprise.notna() & (prior_surprise.isna() | eps_surprise.ne(prior_surprise))
        surprise_yield = eps_surprise.div(close.where(close > 0.0))
        downside_severity = (-surprise_yield).where(surprise_yield < 0.0)
        downside_rank = rank(downside_severity.where(earnings_event))
        signal = -(recent_stress * downside_rank.fillna(0.0))
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A negative earnings surprise is substantially more informative when it arrives while a firm has recently disclosed deteriorating rollover capacity: the miss converts a gradual balance-sheet concern into an immediate financing and covenant-risk narrative. Unlike Parent A, the child does not short every funding-stress disclosure; unlike Parent B, it does not assume generic earnings surprises drift symmetrically. The interaction isolates downside earnings news that validates credit fragility, where equity holders are likely to revise refinancing probabilities and reduce exposure over the following week.
programs.description: Ranks the severity of fresh negative EPS-surprise yields and assigns a negative signal only when the issuer has had a high recent cross-sectional refinancing-stress disclosure, based on short-term debt, cash-buffer, and interest-coverage deterioration. Refinancing stress is retained causally for six bars after its disclosure so that same-day and slightly delayed earnings releases can activate it.

"""The signal isolates an event-time expectation failure rather than generic negative-surprise drift. A stock is eligible only when its price remained unusually strong relative to its own industry despite a recent, publicly observable downward EPS-consensus update, and the subsequent reported EPS is materially below the last pre-release consensus. The proposed delayed repricing is attributable to investors treating relative-price strength as a noisy but favorable counter-signal until the earnings release resolves the conflict; the factor enters only after that public resolution, not during the pre-event revision period."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_industry_median(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return causal cross-sectional leave-one-out medians and valid counts.

    Industry is static, while values and validity are evaluated independently at
    each timestamp.  The order-statistic implementation avoids allowing a
    stock's own return to influence its industry benchmark.
    """
    median = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    counts = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    for industry_name in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(industry_name)]
        if len(members) == 0:
            continue

        member_values = values.loc[:, members].to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
        member_valid = valid.loc[:, members].to_numpy(dtype=bool, copy=False)
        member_values[~member_valid] = np.inf

        order = np.argsort(member_values, axis=1)
        sorted_values = np.take_along_axis(member_values, order, axis=1)
        positions = np.argsort(order, axis=1)
        n_valid = member_valid.sum(axis=1)

        # For each member, remove its sorted position and take the median of
        # the remaining observations.  Invalid members remain NaN below.
        peer_n = n_valid - 1
        lower = (peer_n - 1) // 2
        upper = peer_n // 2

        lower_index = lower[:, None] + (lower[:, None] >= positions)
        upper_index = upper[:, None] + (upper[:, None] >= positions)
        lower_index = np.clip(lower_index, 0, len(members) - 1)
        upper_index = np.clip(upper_index, 0, len(members) - 1)

        lower_value = np.take_along_axis(sorted_values, lower_index, axis=1)
        upper_value = np.take_along_axis(sorted_values, upper_index, axis=1)
        leave_one_out = 0.5 * (lower_value + upper_value)
        leave_one_out[(~member_valid) | (n_valid[:, None] < 2)] = np.nan

        median.loc[:, members] = leave_one_out
        counts.loc[:, members] = n_valid[:, None]

    return median, counts


def _row_condition_frame(condition: pd.Series, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a timestamp-level condition over a panel's ticker columns."""
    values = np.broadcast_to(condition.to_numpy(dtype=bool)[:, None], (len(condition), len(columns)))
    return pd.DataFrame(values, index=condition.index, columns=columns)


@register_factor
class ConsensusPriceDivergenceEarningsUnwind(BaseFactor):
    """Short post-release earnings failures following bullish price-consensus divergence."""

    factor_id = "consensus_price_divergence_earnings_unwind"
    name = "Pre-Release Consensus-Price Divergence Unwind"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "At fresh EPS releases, shorts stocks with unusually strong pre-release "
        "industry-relative price performance despite a recent downward consensus "
        "revision, when actual EPS subsequently misses that final consensus."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "epsEstimate", "epsActual", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        actual = data["epsActual"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        # Static metadata is intentionally read from the first available bar;
        # it does not encode a time-varying market observation.
        industry_labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        estimate_pre = estimate.shift(1)
        estimate_21 = estimate.shift(21)
        denominator_21 = estimate_21.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revision = (estimate_pre - estimate_21) / denominator_21

        # A consensus update is a newly finite estimate or a finite changed
        # estimate.  The strict interior window is t-20 through t-2, excluding
        # both t-21 and the immediately preceding pre-release timestamp t-1.
        estimate_previous = estimate.shift(1)
        estimate_update = estimate.notna() & (
            estimate_previous.isna() | estimate.ne(estimate_previous)
        )
        recent_interior_update = (
            estimate_update.shift(2).rolling(19, min_periods=1).max().fillna(0.0).astype(bool)
        )

        pre_release_valid = (
            estimate_pre.notna()
            & estimate_21.notna()
            & estimate_21.abs().ge(0.01)
            & estimate_pre.lt(estimate_21)
            & recent_interior_update
        )

        # This is close[t-1] / close[t-21] - 1, so no report-day close enters.
        pre_release_return = close.shift(1) / close.shift(21).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        return_valid = pre_release_valid & pre_release_return.notna()

        industry_median, industry_count = _leave_one_out_industry_median(
            pre_release_return,
            return_valid,
            industry_labels,
        )
        price_strength = pre_release_return - industry_median
        price_valid = return_valid & industry_count.ge(5.0) & price_strength.notna()

        price_rank = rank(price_strength.where(price_valid))
        revision_rank = rank(revision.where(pre_release_valid))

        # A fresh EPS event includes the initial finite observation as well as
        # a changed finite observation relative to the preceding timestamp.
        eps_event = actual.notna() & actual.ne(actual.shift(1))
        surprise = (actual - estimate_pre) / estimate_pre.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        surprise_valid = eps_event & estimate_pre.notna() & surprise.notna()
        event_count = surprise_valid.sum(axis=1)
        enough_events = _row_condition_frame(event_count.ge(10), close.columns)
        surprise_rank = rank(surprise.where(surprise_valid & enough_events))

        qualifies = (
            eps_event
            & price_rank.ge(0.80)
            & revision_rank.le(0.20)
            & surprise_rank.le(0.20)
        )
        score = -price_rank * (1.0 - revision_rank) * (1.0 - surprise_rank)
        score = score.where(qualifies, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        # The event is public at t, while the position is entered only on the
        # next executable daily bar.
        return score.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Pre-Release Consensus-Price Divergence Unwind
programs.trading_idea: The signal isolates an event-time expectation failure rather than generic negative-surprise drift. A stock is eligible only when its price remained unusually strong relative to its own industry despite a recent, publicly observable downward EPS-consensus update, and the subsequent reported EPS is materially below the last pre-release consensus. The proposed delayed repricing is attributable to investors treating relative-price strength as a noisy but favorable counter-signal until the earnings release resolves the conflict; the factor enters only after that public resolution, not during the pre-event revision period.
programs.description: At a timestamp t, define an earnings event only when epsActual changes from its immediately preceding point-in-time value (including a transition from NaN to finite), with a finite epsActual at t. The signal is computed upon that public availability timestamp and is entered at the next executable daily bar; no report-day close is used. Let E_pre be epsEstimate as of the immediately preceding tradable timestamp, and let E_21 be epsEstimate as of 21 tradable bars before t. Require both values to be finite, abs(E_21) >= 0.01, E_pre < E_21, and at least one point-in-time epsEstimate update strictly between t-21 and t-1; the most recent such update must be no older than 21 bars before t. Define the pre-release EPS revision as Rev=(E_pre-E_21)/max(abs(E_21),0.01), and define the realized standardized surprise as Surp=(epsActual[t]-E_pre)/max(abs(E_pre),0.01). Price strength is the 20-tradable-bar close return from t-21 through t-1, less the median equivalent return of valid members of the stock's static industry; require at least five valid industry members and exclude the stock from its industry median. Rank industry-relative price strength and Rev cross-sectionally among all stocks satisfying the corresponding pre-release data requirements at t. Rank Surp only among fresh EPS-event stocks at t, requiring at least 10 such events. Emit a negative score only when relative-price-strength rank is at least 0.80, revision rank is at most 0.20, and surprise rank is at most 0.20. For qualifying names, score = -1 * price_strength_rank * (1-revision_rank) * (1-surprise_rank); all other names receive zero. This differs from a standing revision-price anti-alignment signal because it requires a fresh, pre-defined consensus update and a subsequent, independently timed earnings realization that is below the last strictly pre-release consensus.

programs.code:
"""Cash-confirmed event drift versus idiosyncratic attention overshoot.

Credible releases with muted participation signal incomplete information
assimilation, whereas high-attention idiosyncratic moves outside report windows
are treated as valuation-anchor overshoots rather than sector news.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _changed(field: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clean = field.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    previous = clean.shift(1)
    return (clean.notna() & (previous.isna() | clean.ne(previous))).fillna(False)


def _bounded_surprise(
    surprise: pd.DataFrame, estimate: pd.DataFrame, actual: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    surprise = surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    estimate = estimate.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    actual = actual.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    denominator = estimate.abs() + actual.abs()
    valid = surprise.notna() & estimate.notna() & actual.notna() & denominator.gt(0.0)
    return (surprise / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0).where(valid)


def _sector_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-day sector mean; sector labels are static metadata."""
    labels = sector.iloc[0].fillna("Unknown").astype(str)
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T


def _cs_score(values: pd.DataFrame, active: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    masked = values.where(active).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    ranks = masked.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    sufficient = masked.notna().sum(axis=1).ge(20)
    return (2.0 * ranks - 1.0).where(sufficient, axis=0)


@register_factor
class CashEventIdiosyncraticAttentionSwitch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_event_idiosyncratic_attention_switch"
    name = "Cash Event Idiosyncratic Attention Switch"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Continues muted-turnover, cash-confirmed earnings surprises after releases, "
        "then switches to reversal of high-volume idiosyncratic valuation dislocations "
        "outside the six-bar report window."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sharesOutstanding",
        "sector",
        "earningsYield",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "epsActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueActual",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_release = _changed(data["epsActual"])
        revenue_release = _changed(data["revenueActual"])
        release = eps_release | revenue_release

        eps_signal = _bounded_surprise(
            data["epsSurprise"], data["epsEstimate"], data["epsActual"]
        )
        revenue_signal = _bounded_surprise(
            data["revenueSurprise"], data["revenueEstimate"], data["revenueActual"]
        )
        surprise_count = eps_signal.notna().astype(float) + revenue_signal.notna().astype(float)
        surprise = (
            eps_signal.fillna(0.0) + revenue_signal.fillna(0.0)
        ) / surprise_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        fcf = data["freeCashFlow"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_confirmed = fcf.gt(0.0) & income_quality.ge(1.0)

        turnover = volume / shares.where(shares.gt(0.0))
        fast_turnover = turnover.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        slow_turnover = turnover.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean()
        muted_participation = (
            1.0 - fast_turnover / slow_turnover.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(0.0, 0.8)

        ret5 = close / close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        sector_ret5 = _sector_mean(ret5, data["sector"])
        idio_ret5 = ret5 - sector_ret5
        daily_idio = close.pct_change() - _sector_mean(close.pct_change(), data["sector"])
        idio_scale = daily_idio.rolling(60, min_periods=40).std() * np.sqrt(5.0)
        standardized_reaction = (idio_ret5 / idio_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        aligned_reaction = np.sign(surprise) * standardized_reaction
        reaction_deficit = (1.0 - aligned_reaction.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        liquid = volume.gt(0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().ge(16.0)
        event_active = (
            release
            & cash_confirmed
            & surprise.notna()
            & muted_participation.notna()
            & reaction_deficit.notna()
            & liquid
        )
        event_raw = surprise * muted_participation * reaction_deficit
        event_position = _cs_score(event_raw, event_active).fillna(0.0)
        held_event = event_position.rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum()

        earnings_yield = data["earningsYield"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        valuation_yield = earnings_yield.where(earnings_yield.notna(), fcf_yield)
        valuation_rank = valuation_yield.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        idio_return_rank = idio_ret5.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        prior_median_volume = volume.shift(1).where(volume.shift(1).gt(0.0)).rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).median()
        attention = np.log(
            volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)) / prior_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

        blocked = release.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).max().gt(0.0)
        quiet_active = (
            ~blocked
            & valuation_yield.notna()
            & idio_ret5.notna()
            & attention.notna()
            & liquid
        )
        quiet_raw = attention * (
            (2.0 * valuation_rank - 1.0) - (2.0 * idio_return_rank - 1.0)
        )
        quiet_position = _cs_score(quiet_raw, quiet_active).fillna(0.0)

        signal = (held_event + quiet_position).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

"""The signal isolates firms for which a newly public, operationally meaningful improvement in debt-service capacity is not yet reflected in their industry-relative equity performance. Rather than assuming that all leverage deterioration drifts slowly, it takes only the positive re-rating side: firms with material initial leverage, simultaneous improvement in interest coverage and net-debt-to-EBITDA, and a trailing relative-price lag may experience a short-horizon catch-up as cross-sectional capital reallocates toward the improved credit-equity profile. EPS-estimate revisions and earnings surprises are deliberately excluded, making the mechanism conditional on disclosed balance-sheet capacity rather than a generic earnings-news effect."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a finite-value mask while preserving panel alignment."""
    return pd.DataFrame(
        np.isfinite(df.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)),
        index=df.index,
        columns=df.columns,
    )


def _winsorized_percentile_rank(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally rank each row after cross-sectional 5/95 winsorisation."""
    masked = values.where(eligible)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    return clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True, method="average")


def _industry_peer_return(
    firm_return: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    valid_peer: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Equal-weight industry return excluding the stock itself, with 5 peers."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=firm_return.index, columns=firm_return.columns)

    for row in range(len(firm_return.index)):
        values = firm_return.iloc[row]
        groups = industry.iloc[row]
        mask = valid_peer.iloc[row] & groups.notna() & values.notna()
        if not bool(mask.any()):
            continue

        member_values = values.where(mask)
        member_groups = groups.where(mask)
        grouped_sum = member_values.groupby(member_groups, sort=False).sum()
        grouped_count = member_values.groupby(member_groups, sort=False).count()

        sum_by_name = member_groups.map(grouped_sum)
        count_by_name = member_groups.map(grouped_count)
        peer_return = (sum_by_name - member_values) / (count_by_name - 1.0)
        peer_return = peer_return.where(count_by_name >= 6.0)
        result.iloc[row] = peer_return.to_numpy(dtype=float)

    return result


def _industry_neutral_book(
    score: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build equal-gross long/short industry sleeves from the specified score."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=score.index, columns=score.columns)

    for row in range(len(score.index)):
        row_score = score.iloc[row]
        row_industry = industry.iloc[row]
        members = eligible.iloc[row] & row_industry.notna() & row_score.notna()
        if not bool(members.any()):
            continue

        active_scores = row_score.loc[members]
        active_industries = row_industry.loc[members]
        for _, sleeve_scores in active_scores.groupby(active_industries, sort=False):
            if len(sleeve_scores) < 10:
                continue

            positive = sleeve_scores[sleeve_scores > 0.0]
            if positive.empty:
                continue

            positive_rank = positive.rank(pct=True, method="average")
            long_names = positive_rank.index[positive_rank >= 0.80]
            if len(long_names) == 0:
                continue

            short_names = sleeve_scores.index.difference(long_names)
            if len(short_names) == 0:
                continue

            output.loc[output.index[row], long_names] = 1.0 / float(len(long_names))
            output.loc[output.index[row], short_names] = -1.0 / float(len(short_names))

    return output


@register_factor
class DebtServiceReratingRelay(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-neutral relay from improved disclosed debt-service capacity."""

    factor_id = "debt_service_rerating_relay"
    name = "Levered Capacity Catch-Up"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral long/short portfolio that buys leveraged non-financial "
        "firms with improving disclosed debt-service capacity and unreconciled "
        "industry-relative price lags, financed by eligible industry peers."
    )
    window_length = 64
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "industry",
        "totalDebt",
        "totalAssets",
        "ebit",
        "interestExpense",
        "cash",
        "ebitda",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        industry = data["industry"]
        total_debt = data["totalDebt"]
        total_assets = data["totalAssets"]
        ebit = data["ebit"]
        interest_expense = data["interestExpense"]
        cash = data["cash"]
        ebitda = data["ebitda"]

        debt_lag = total_debt.shift(63)
        assets_lag = total_assets.shift(63)
        ebit_lag = ebit.shift(63)
        interest_lag = interest_expense.shift(63)
        cash_lag = cash.shift(63)
        ebitda_lag = ebitda.shift(63)

        leverage_lag = debt_lag / assets_lag.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        interest_abs = interest_expense.abs()
        interest_abs_lag = interest_lag.abs()
        interest_coverage = ebit / interest_abs.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        interest_coverage_lag = ebit_lag / interest_abs_lag.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        net_debt = total_debt - cash
        net_debt_lag = debt_lag - cash_lag
        nd_to_ebitda = net_debt / ebitda.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        nd_to_ebitda_lag = net_debt_lag / ebitda_lag.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        non_financial = sector.notna() & sector.ne("Financials")
        leverage_ok = (
            assets_lag.gt(0.0)
            & leverage_lag.ge(0.15)
            & leverage_lag.le(0.80)
            & _finite(leverage_lag)
        )
        coverage_ok = (
            ebit.gt(0.0)
            & ebit_lag.gt(0.0)
            & interest_abs.gt(0.0)
            & interest_abs_lag.gt(0.0)
            & _finite(interest_coverage)
            & _finite(interest_coverage_lag)
        )
        net_debt_ok = (
            net_debt.ge(0.0)
            & net_debt_lag.ge(0.0)
            & ebitda.gt(0.0)
            & ebitda_lag.gt(0.0)
            & _finite(nd_to_ebitda)
            & _finite(nd_to_ebitda_lag)
        )

        firm_return = close / close.shift(20).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        return_ok = close.gt(0.0) & close.shift(20).gt(0.0) & _finite(firm_return)

        base_eligible = (
            non_financial
            & industry.notna()
            & leverage_ok
            & coverage_ok
            & net_debt_ok
            & return_ok
        )

        delta_coverage = np.log(interest_coverage) - np.log(interest_coverage_lag)
        delta_nd = nd_to_ebitda_lag - nd_to_ebitda
        base_eligible = base_eligible & _finite(delta_coverage) & _finite(delta_nd)

        rank_coverage = _winsorized_percentile_rank(delta_coverage, base_eligible)
        rank_nd = _winsorized_percentile_rank(delta_nd, base_eligible)
        capacity = 0.5 * rank_coverage + 0.5 * rank_nd

        industry_return = _industry_peer_return(firm_return, industry, base_eligible)
        gap = industry_return - firm_return
        rank_gap = _winsorized_percentile_rank(gap, base_eligible & gap.notna())

        current_qualification = (
            base_eligible
            & delta_coverage.gt(0.0)
            & delta_nd.gt(0.0)
            & gap.gt(0.0)
            & rank_coverage.notna()
            & rank_nd.notna()
            & rank_gap.notna()
        )
        persistent = current_qualification.shift(1).fillna(False)

        score = (capacity * rank_gap).where(current_qualification & persistent, 0.0)
        score = score.where(_finite(score), 0.0)

        portfolio_eligible = (
            base_eligible
            & gap.notna()
            & rank_coverage.notna()
            & rank_nd.notna()
            & rank_gap.notna()
        )
        return _industry_neutral_book(score, portfolio_eligible, industry)
