"""This is a reduced-form test for persistent, stock-specific trading pressure rather than an identified measure of unfinished metaorder inventory. A large sector-residual move on unusually high volume that produces less residual return per unit of relative volume than the stock's own trailing baseline may indicate temporarily elastic liquidity or offsetting flow; continuation is considered only when the next day's small adverse residual move does not materially undo the original move. Sector residualization and the explicitly delayed acceptance test distinguish the signal from a simple signed-volume continuation rule."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_sector_residual(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap_lagged: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute causal market-cap-weighted leave-one-out sector residuals.

    Sector is specified as static in the feed, so its first row supplies the
    group membership.  Market-cap weights are already lagged by one bar before
    entering this helper.  A sector benchmark is available only when at least
    three other valid, positively weighted peers exist.
    """
    sector_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    labels = sector.iloc[0]

    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        group_cols = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(group_cols) == 0:
            continue

        group_ret = ret.loc[:, group_cols]
        group_cap = market_cap_lagged.loc[:, group_cols]
        valid = group_ret.notna() & group_cap.notna() & (group_cap > 0.0)
        weights = group_cap.where(valid)
        weighted_returns = group_ret * weights

        total_weighted_return = weighted_returns.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        total_weight = weights.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        valid_count = valid.sum(axis=1)

        peer_weighted_return = weighted_returns.fillna(0.0).rsub(
            total_weighted_return, axis=0
        )
        peer_weight = weights.fillna(0.0).rsub(total_weight, axis=0)
        peer_count = valid_count.to_frame().reindex(columns=group_cols, fill_value=0)
        peer_count = peer_count.sub(valid.astype(int), axis=0)

        loo_return = peer_weighted_return / peer_weight.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        loo_return = loo_return.where((peer_count >= 3) & (peer_weight > 0.0))
        sector_return.loc[:, group_cols] = loo_return

    return ret - sector_return


@register_factor
class SectorResidualUnderimpactBacklogDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Accepted low-impact sector-residual pressure with a delayed adverse probe."""

    factor_id = "sector_residual_underimpact_backlog_drift"
    name = "Sector-Residual Underimpact Acceptance"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks accepted sector-residual volume shocks whose residual price impact "
        "is unusually low versus history and whose next-day low-volume adverse "
        "probe fails to reverse most of the original move."
    )
    window_length = 82
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        lagged_cap = market_cap.shift(1)
        residual = _leave_one_out_sector_residual(ret, lagged_cap, sector)

        valid_share_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        vmed = valid_share_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where((close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0))
        dollar_median = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
        residual_sigma = residual.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)

        relative_volume = volume / vmed.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact = residual.abs() / relative_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        baseline_impact = impact.rolling(60, min_periods=40).median().shift(1)
        underimpact = impact / baseline_impact.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        liquid_eligible = (
            (close > 1.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & (lagged_cap >= 100_000_000.0)
            & (dollar_median >= 1_000_000.0)
        )
        event = (
            liquid_eligible
            & (relative_volume >= 1.5)
            & (residual.abs() >= residual_sigma)
            & (baseline_impact > 0.0)
            & (underimpact <= 0.50)
        )

        event_residual = residual.shift(1)
        event_direction = np.sign(event_residual)
        event_underimpact = underimpact.shift(1)
        event_vmed = vmed.shift(1)
        prior_event = event.shift(1).fillna(False)

        adverse_probe = (event_direction * residual) < 0.0
        low_volume_probe = volume <= event_vmed
        accepted_movement = (
            event_direction * (event_residual + residual)
            / event_residual.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        qualifies = (
            prior_event
            & low_volume_probe
            & adverse_probe
            & (accepted_movement >= 0.50)
            & (event_direction != 0.0)
        )

        raw_strength = (
            (1.0 / event_underimpact.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(upper=5.0)
            * accepted_movement.clip(upper=1.5)
        )
        ranked_strength = rank(raw_strength.where(qualifies))
        signal = (event_direction * ranked_strength).where(qualifies, 0.0)

        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: This is a reduced-form test for persistent, stock-specific trading pressure rather than an identified measure of unfinished metaorder inventory. A large sector-residual move on unusually high volume that produces less residual return per unit of relative volume than the stock's own trailing baseline may indicate temporarily elastic liquidity or offsetting flow; continuation is considered only when the next day's small adverse residual move does not materially undo the original move. Sector residualization and the explicitly delayed acceptance test distinguish the signal from a simple signed-volume continuation rule.
programs.description: All quantities are computed using only information available by the relevant daily close. Let r(i,d) = close(i,d) / close(i,d-1) - 1. For stock i on day d, define its leave-one-out sector return Rsec(i,d) as the market-cap-weighted mean of r(j,d) for other stocks j with the same point-in-time sector label, using nonmissing positive marketCap(j,d-1) weights; require at least three such peers. Define residual return e(i,d) = r(i,d) - Rsec(i,d). A stock is liquidity-eligible on event day t only if close(i,t) > 1 USD, volume(i,t) > 0, marketCap(i,t-1) >= 100 million USD, and its median daily dollar volume close*volume over t-20 through t-1 is at least 1 million USD. Let Vmed(i,t) be the median share volume over t-20 through t-1, requiring at least 15 valid observations, and define relative volume q(i,t) = volume(i,t) / Vmed(i,t). Let sigma(i,t) be the sample standard deviation of e(i,d) over t-20 through t-1, requiring at least 15 valid residuals. Define daily residual impact I(i,d) = abs(e(i,d)) / [volume(i,d) / median(volume(i,k), k=d-20,...,d-1)]. The trailing impact baseline B(i,t) is the median of I(i,d) over d=t-60,...,t-1, requiring at least 40 valid observations and B(i,t)>0. An event occurs at t when: (1) q(i,t) >= 1.5; (2) abs(e(i,t)) >= sigma(i,t); and (3) underimpact U(i,t) = I(i,t)/B(i,t) <= 0.50. Its direction is s(i,t) = sign(e(i,t)). The probe is exclusively day t+1 and is evaluated only after that close: require volume(i,t+1) <= Vmed(i,t), s(i,t)*e(i,t+1) < 0, and cumulative accepted residual movement A(i,t) = s(i,t)*[e(i,t)+e(i,t+1)]/abs(e(i,t)) >= 0.50. Thus the probe is low-volume, adverse, and has reversed less than half of the event residual move. On t+1 close, qualifying names receive raw strength W(i,t) = min(5, 1/U(i,t)) * min(1.5, A(i,t)); the factor value is s(i,t) times the cross-sectional percentile rank of W among that day's qualifying names, and is zero for nonqualifiers. The signal is formed only after the t+1 close and may be traded no earlier than t+2 under the execution convention. No return after t+1, including any return in the following six-bar forecast interval, is used for event selection, ranking, or sizing. Events are not accumulated or carried forward: each signal date uses only the immediately preceding event/probe pair, so overlapping daily events replace rather than stack prior signals.

"""Liquidity-risk conditioned reversal of persistent inventory pressure.

Mechanism: persistent price impact identifies shallow effective market depth,
while persistent and dispersing impact identifies a repeated inventory-pressure
state.  In that state, an extreme latest signed impact is treated as temporary
mechanical overextension and is faded rather than extrapolated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ascending within-sector percentile rank, requiring at least five names."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns, dtype=float)
    for i in range(len(values.index)):
        row = values.iloc[i]
        labels = sector.iloc[i]
        valid = row.notna() & labels.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        x = row.loc[valid]
        g = labels.loc[valid]
        counts = g.map(g.value_counts())
        ranked = x.groupby(g, sort=False).rank(pct=True)
        accepted = ranked.loc[counts.ge(5)]
        if not accepted.empty:
            result.iloc[i, result.columns.get_indexer(accepted.index)] = accepted.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return result


def _cross_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank while retaining unavailable observations."""
    return values.rank(axis=1, pct=True, method="average")


@register_factor
class LiquidityRiskMemoryShockReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "liquidity_risk_memory_shock_reversal"
    name = "Liquidity-Risk Memory Shock Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fades an extreme normalized signed impact shock only when persistent "
        "sector-relative illiquidity and a high-memory, rising-dispersion impact "
        "state indicate shallow-depth inventory pressure."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        sector = data["sector"]

        valid_close = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & close.gt(0.0))
        valid_volume = volume.where(np.isfinite(volume) & volume.gt(0.0))
        prior_close = valid_close.shift(1)
        log_return = np.log(valid_close / prior_close)

        dollar_volume = (valid_close * valid_volume).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        daily_impact = (log_return.abs() / dollar_volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        persistent_impact = daily_impact.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        depth_rank = _sector_rank(persistent_impact, sector)

        prior_median_volume = valid_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        relative_volume = valid_volume / prior_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        signed_impact = log_return / np.sqrt(relative_volume)
        signed_impact = signed_impact.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        absolute_impact = signed_impact.abs()

        memory = absolute_impact.rolling(19, min_periods=19).corr(absolute_impact.shift(1))
        recent_var = absolute_impact.rolling(10, min_periods=10).var()
        prior_var = absolute_impact.shift(10).rolling(10, min_periods=10).var()
        total_var = absolute_impact.rolling(20, min_periods=20).var()
        dispersion_change = (recent_var - prior_var) / (total_var + 1.0e-12)

        persistence = 0.5 * _cross_rank(memory) + 0.5 * _cross_rank(dispersion_change)
        state_gate = ((persistence - 0.65) / 0.35).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        impact_scale = signed_impact.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        signed_z = (signed_impact / impact_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=-6.0, upper=6.0)
        shock_rank = _cross_rank(signed_z.abs())
        shock_gate = ((shock_rank - 0.70) / 0.30).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        eligible = depth_rank.notna() & state_gate.notna() & signed_z.notna() & shock_gate.notna()
        raw = (depth_rank * state_gate * (-signed_z) * shock_gate).where(eligible)
        signal = 2.0 * _cross_rank(raw) - 1.0
        return signal.where(eligible).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: Persistent sector-relative price impact identifies stocks with structurally shallow effective depth, where liquidity risk is economically priced. Within that shallow-depth state, a serially persistent and increasingly dispersed impact process indicates recurring mechanical inventory pressure; the realized negative sign of Parent A suggests that an extreme latest signed move is more likely an overextension to fade than continuation. The interaction has edge because persistent illiquidity alone is a slow premium and signed impact alone mixes information with noise, whereas their conjunction isolates temporary inventory shocks occurring where limited depth makes their reversal largest.

"""Late-stage deleveraging exhaustion conditioned on correlation stress.

Mechanism: correlation shocks and abnormal turnover identify likely risk-control
selling, while a declining return response per unit of signed flow identifies the
point at which the marginal forced seller has lost price impact.  Excess downside
displacement in that joint state is expected to repair over the next few bars.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _panel_correlation(y: pd.DataFrame, market: pd.Series, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing stock/market correlation, with a permissive causal warm-up."""
    x = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(market.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], y.shape[1], axis=1), index=y.index, columns=y.columns)
    ym = y.rolling(window, min_periods=6).mean()
    xm = x.rolling(window, min_periods=6).mean()
    cov = (y * x).rolling(window, min_periods=6).mean() - ym * xm
    vy = (y * y).rolling(window, min_periods=6).mean() - ym * ym
    vx = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=6).mean() - xm * xm
    return cov.div(np.sqrt(vy * vx).replace(0.0, np.nan))

def _completed_slope(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing slope of y on x, estimated only through the prior bar."""
    yy = y.shift(1)
    xx = x.shift(1)
    my = yy.rolling(window, min_periods=10).mean()
    mx = xx.rolling(window, min_periods=10).mean()
    cov = (yy * xx).rolling(window, min_periods=10).mean() - my * mx
    var = (xx * xx).rolling(window, min_periods=10).mean() - mx * mx
    return cov.div(var.replace(0.0, np.nan))

@register_factor
class CorrelationConditionedFlowExhaustionRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'correlation_conditioned_flow_exhaustion_repair_j_1'
    name = 'Correlation-Conditioned Flow Exhaustion Repair'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Ranks exhausted downside flow overhangs: excess three-bar sell displacement whose correlation-shock and abnormal-volume state indicates deleveraging, but whose marginal signed-flow impact is fading.'
    window_length = 45
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        ret = close.div(prior_close).sub(1.0)
        ret = ret.where((close > 0.0) & (prior_close > 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
        bar_range = high.sub(low)
        clv = 2.0 * close.sub(low).div(bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)) - 1.0
        clv = clv.where(bar_range > 0.0, 0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        dollar_volume = close.mul(volume).where((close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0))
        dollar_base = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(18, min_periods=5).median()
        volume_ratio = dollar_volume.div(dollar_base.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        volume_ratio = volume_ratio.clip(0.0, 6.0).fillna(1.0)
        abnormal_volume = np.log(volume_ratio.clip(lower=1.0)).clip(0.0, 1.8)
        flow = clv.mul(np.log1p(volume_ratio)).clip(-2.0, 2.0).fillna(0.0)
        market = ret.median(axis=1).fillna(0.0)
        correlation = _panel_correlation(ret, market, 15).clip(-0.98, 0.98)
        corr_rise = np.arctanh(correlation).sub(np.arctanh(correlation.shift(11))).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0).fillna(0.0)
        beta_market = _completed_slope(ret, pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(market.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], close.shape[1], axis=1), index=close.index, columns=close.columns), 30).fillna(0.0)
        market_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(market.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], close.shape[1], axis=1), index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        residual = ret.sub(beta_market.mul(market_panel))
        residual_scale = residual.shift(1).rolling(19, min_periods=5).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        idio_downside = residual.mul(-1.0).div(residual_scale).clip(0.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)
        flow_beta = _completed_slope(ret, flow, 35).clip(-0.15, 0.15).fillna(0.0)
        flow_sum = flow.rolling(4, min_periods=1).sum()
        displacement = ret.rolling(2, min_periods=1).sum()
        excess_displacement = displacement.sub(flow_beta.mul(flow_sum))
        sell_overhang = excess_displacement.mul(-1.0).div(ret.shift(1).rolling(19, min_periods=5).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 6.0).fillna(0.0)
        aligned_impact = ret.mul(np.sign(flow)).div(flow.abs().add(0.25))
        prior_impact = aligned_impact.shift(1).rolling(4, min_periods=1).mean()
        impact_decay = prior_impact.sub(aligned_impact).clip(0.0, 0.25).fillna(0.0)
        coherence = flow_sum.abs().div(flow.abs().rolling(4, min_periods=1).sum().add(0.05))
        coherence = coherence.clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        forced_sale_state = idio_downside.mul(corr_rise).mul(abnormal_volume)
        raw = sell_overhang.mul(forced_sale_state).mul(impact_decay).mul(coherence)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(raw).fillna(0.5)

'''Cadence exhaustion conditioned on a historical reversal impact kernel.

Mechanism: a regular directional participation run that suddenly loses volume is
faded only in names where earlier signed volume shocks have causally been
followed by negative six-bar responses. This combines current inventory-pressure
completion with a stock-specific estimate of liquidity replenishment.
'''

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _reversal_kernel(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    '''Trailing correlation of a signed volume shock with its realised six-bar return.

    At t, the response belongs to the shock at t-6, so both sides of every
    correlation observation are already known. Negative correlation denotes
    shocks that historically unwind rather than propagate.
    '''
    prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=12).median()
    volume_ratio = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    bar_range = high - low
    valid = (
        (close > 0.0)
        & (volume_ratio > 0.0)
        & (bar_range > 0.0)
        & np.isfinite(close)
        & np.isfinite(volume_ratio)
        & np.isfinite(bar_range)
    )
    clv = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).where(valid)
    shock = (clv * np.sqrt(volume_ratio.clip(lower=0.0, upper=9.0))).where(valid)
    response_ratio = close / close.shift(6)
    response = np.log(response_ratio.where((response_ratio > 0.0) & np.isfinite(response_ratio)))
    return shock.shift(6).rolling(90, min_periods=60).corr(response)


@register_factor
class CadenceKernelConditionedExhaustion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'cadence_kernel_conditioned_exhaustion'
    name = 'Kernel-Conditioned Cadence Exhaustion'
    category = 'mean_reversion'
    description = (
        'Fades regular directional close-location runs after a participation '
        'break, but only where a trailing signed-volume impact kernel shows '
        'that comparable shocks historically reverse over six bars.'
    )
    window_length = 105
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        high = data['high']
        low = data['low']
        volume = data['volume']

        bar_range = high - low
        valid_bar = (
            (close > 0.0)
            & (high >= low)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(high)
            & np.isfinite(low)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
        )
        clv = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid_bar)

        base_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=12).median()
        volume_mad = volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=12).apply(
            lambda x: np.median(np.abs(x - np.median(x))), raw=True
        )
        regularity = 1.0 - (volume_mad / base_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        regularity = regularity.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        participation_break = (1.0 - volume / base_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        prior_clv = clv.shift(1)
        pressure = prior_clv.rolling(4, min_periods=4).mean()
        directional = prior_clv.abs().rolling(4, min_periods=4).min().ge(0.20)
        direction = np.sign(pressure)
        endpoint = (
            ((direction > 0.0) & close.ge(close.shift(1).rolling(4, min_periods=4).max() * 0.99))
            | ((direction < 0.0) & close.le(close.shift(1).rolling(4, min_periods=4).min() * 1.01))
        )

        kernel = _reversal_kernel(close, high, low, volume)
        reversal_state = (-kernel).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        candidate = (
            valid_bar
            & directional
            & endpoint
            & (regularity >= 0.55)
            & (participation_break >= 0.35)
            & (reversal_state > 0.0)
        )

        amplitude = regularity * participation_break * pressure.abs() * reversal_state
        ranked_amplitude = rank(amplitude.where(candidate))
        score = (-direction * ranked_amplitude).where(candidate, 0.0)
        enough_names = candidate.sum(axis=1).ge(2).astype(float)
        return score.mul(enough_names, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

The child only fades that episode when the same stock has a causally estimated negative six-bar response kernel to prior signed volume shocks: this identifies names in which liquidity replenishment has historically converted directional pressure into delayed reversal. Parent A supplies the current exhaustion event, while Parent B supplies a stock-specific state variable distinguishing reliably temporary pressure from pressure that tends to persist.

"""An analyst estimate revision and a sharply opposite sector-relative price move are competing public signals rather than evidence that either source is intrinsically superior. The hypothesis is that, over the next six trading days, the conflict resolves toward the estimate revision when the adverse price move is not corroborated by unusually high turnover; high relative turnover is used only as a filter to avoid treating a low-participation price fluctuation as meaningful disagreement. This reframes the signal as conditional analyst-revision drift under incomplete contemporaneous price incorporation, rather than assuming that institutional flow necessarily dominates the revision."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_relative_return(
    close: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute each name's completed daily return less its sector median.

    Sector is documented as static.  Labels are therefore taken from the first
    available panel row and used solely for contemporaneous cross-sectional
    grouping; price returns remain strictly trailing close-to-close returns.
    """
    previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    daily_return = close / previous_close - 1.0

    labels = sector.iloc[0].fillna("Unknown")
    sector_median = daily_return.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("median").T
    return daily_return - sector_median


def _revision_strength(eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale a one-bar public consensus revision by prior estimate magnitude.

    The floor prevents tiny or near-zero EPS estimates from creating unbounded
    percentage revisions while preserving the revision sign.
    """
    prior_estimate = eps_estimate.shift(1)
    revision = eps_estimate - prior_estimate
    denominator = prior_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.05)
    return (revision / denominator).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)


def _relative_turnover(volume: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Current volume divided by a prior-only trailing median volume baseline."""
    prior_baseline = volume.shift(1).rolling(window, min_periods=10).median()
    return volume / prior_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class TurnoverValidatedRevisionAntiAlignment(BaseFactor):
    """Conditional analyst-revision drift after low-turnover price disagreement."""

    factor_id = "turnover_validated_revision_anti_alignment"
    name = "Revision-Price Disagreement Resolution"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks public EPS-estimate revisions only when the completed daily "
        "sector-relative return opposes the revision and current turnover is "
        "not elevated versus the stock's prior 20-day volume baseline."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "epsEstimate", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        revision = _revision_strength(estimate)
        sector_relative_return = _sector_relative_return(close, sector)
        turnover = _relative_turnover(volume, 20)

        # A negative product identifies a price move opposite to the newly
        # available revision.  Elevated turnover is exclusionary rather than a
        # directional confirmation: broad participation makes the adverse move
        # more credible and therefore weakens the intended disagreement setup.
        disagreement = (revision * sector_relative_return) < 0.0
        low_turnover = turnover <= 1.25
        valid_revision = revision.notna() & sector_relative_return.notna()
        eligible = disagreement & low_turnover & valid_revision

        # Rank absolute revision magnitude among eligible names, then restore
        # revision direction so both long and short exposures follow consensus.
        magnitude_rank = rank(revision.abs().where(eligible))
        signal = magnitude_rank * np.sign(revision)
        return signal.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

"""Operating-backed earnings delivery that resolves distributed headline disbelief.

Mechanism: a tax-clean operating surprise can reprice rapidly when investors have
already sold a recently upgraded but unconfirmed narrative.  The factor requires a
completed high-turnover downside episode whose range is cooling, separating an
exhausted sceptical distribution from an ongoing deterioration."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank excluding non-finite observations."""
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _distribution_release(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal score for a past turnover-backed selloff now losing range intensity."""
    prior_close = close.shift(1)
    valid = (prior_close > 0.0) & (close > 0.0) & (high >= low) & (volume >= 0.0)
    ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).where(valid)
    bar_range = ((high - low) / prior_close).where(valid)

    completed_loss = (-ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum().shift(3)).clip(lower=0.0)
    shock_range = bar_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().shift(3)
    base_range = bar_range.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(6)
    current_range = bar_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()

    shock_volume = volume.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().shift(3)
    base_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(6)
    turnover_excess = (
        shock_volume / base_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).clip(lower=0.0)

    range_excess = (
        shock_range / base_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).clip(lower=0.0)
    cooling = (
        1.0 - current_range / base_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(lower=0.0)

    return completed_loss * turnover_excess * range_excess * cooling


@register_factor
class OperatingDeliveryDisbeliefRelease(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "operating_delivery_disbelief_release"
    name = "Operating Delivery Disbelief Release"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks operating-backed and tax-clean EPS surprises when they resolve a "
        "recent unconfirmed upgrade narrative after turnover-backed downside "
        "pressure has cooled."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "epsActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "marketCap",
        "debtToEquity",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        pretax_income = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax_expense = data["incomeTaxExpense"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(21)
        eps_revision = (eps_estimate - eps_lag) / eps_lag.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        revenue_revision = (
            (revenue_estimate - revenue_lag)
            / revenue_lag.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        operating_margin = operating_income / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        margin_change = operating_margin - operating_margin.shift(63)

        estimate_updated = eps_estimate.notna() & eps_estimate.shift(1).notna() & eps_estimate.ne(eps_estimate.shift(1))
        positive_upgrade = estimate_updated & (eps_revision > 0.0)

        financing_deterioration = (
            _cs_rank(data["debtToEquity"] - data["debtToEquity"].shift(63)).fillna(0.5)
            + _cs_rank(-(data["currentRatio"] - data["currentRatio"].shift(63))).fillna(0.5)
            + _cs_rank(-(data["interestCoverage"] - data["interestCoverage"].shift(63))).fillna(0.5)
        ) / 3.0
        confirmation = (
            _cs_rank(revenue_revision.where(positive_upgrade)).fillna(0.5)
            + _cs_rank(margin_change.where(positive_upgrade)).fillna(0.5)
        ) / 2.0
        headline_fragility = (
            _cs_rank(eps_revision.where(positive_upgrade)).fillna(0.0)
            * (1.0 - confirmation).clip(0.0, 1.0)
            * financing_deterioration
        ).where(positive_upgrade)
        active_disbelief = headline_fragility.ffill(limit=15)

        prior_actual = eps_actual.shift(1)
        report_event = eps_actual.notna() & (prior_actual.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_actual))
        annual_operating_income = operating_income.shift(252)
        annual_pretax_income = pretax_income.shift(252)
        annual_tax_expense = tax_expense.shift(252)
        safe_cap = market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)

        current_etr = (tax_expense / pretax_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)
        annual_etr = (
            annual_tax_expense / annual_pretax_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(0.0, 0.50)
        eps_surprise = (eps_actual - eps_estimate) / (eps_estimate.abs() + 0.01)
        operating_support = (operating_income - annual_operating_income) / safe_cap
        tax_support = (
            -pretax_income * (current_etr - annual_etr) / safe_cap
        )

        eligible = (
            report_event
            & (pretax_income > 0.0)
            & (annual_pretax_income > 0.0)
            & eps_estimate.notna()
            & operating_support.notna()
            & tax_support.notna()
            & active_disbelief.notna()
        )
        credible_delivery = (
            _cs_rank(eps_surprise.where(eligible))
            + _cs_rank(operating_support.where(eligible))
            - _cs_rank(tax_support.where(eligible))
            - 0.5
        )

        release = _distribution_release(close, data["high"], data["low"], data["volume"])
        release_gate = _cs_rank(release.where(release > 0.0))
        disbelief_gate = _cs_rank(active_disbelief.where(active_disbelief > 0.0))
        active = eligible & release_gate.notna() & disbelief_gate.notna()

        signal = credible_delivery * disbelief_gate * release_gate
        return (
            signal.where(active, 0.0)
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0)
            .reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
            .fillna(0.0)
            .astype(float)
        )

The scepticism state is identified by an EPS revision lacking revenue or margin corroboration and accompanied by deteriorating financing capacity; a completed high-turnover selloff whose range is now cooling indicates that this disbelief has already been distributed into price. Neither parent mechanism alone distinguishes a genuinely operating-backed report from a fragile headline narrative that is being incorrectly unwound just before confirmation arrives.

"""Tax-fragility conditioned industry-support unwind.

Mechanism: tax-led estimate optimism can keep fragile firms relatively supported
through an industry selloff.  Relative price resilience followed by abnormal
participation during that common shock is interpreted as transient support,
whose unwind should be negative over the next several bars.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date percentile rank with invalid numerical values removed."""
    return values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Replicate causal same-date industry medians, with market fallback."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(members) == 0:
            continue
        median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
        out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    market_median = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return out.T.fillna(market_median).T


def _safe_revision(current: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale-free positive-lag revision, robust to zero denominators."""
    previous = current.shift(lag)
    return (current - previous) / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class TaxFragilityIndustrySupportUnwind(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "tax_fragility_industry_support_unwind"
    name = "Tax-Fragility Industry Support Unwind"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Shorts tax-led, financially fragile upgrades that retain relative price "
        "support and attract abnormal volume during a negative industry impulse."
    )
    window_length = 42
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        stock_return = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        industry_return = _group_median(stock_return, industry_labels)
        industry_three_day = industry_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = (
            industry_three_day.shift(1)
            .rolling(20, min_periods=10)
            .std()
            .clip(lower=0.002)
        )
        downside_impulse = (-industry_three_day / industry_scale).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        downside_impulse = downside_impulse.fillna(0.0)

        stock_three_day = stock_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        relative_resilience = stock_three_day - industry_three_day
        prior_resilience = _cs_rank(relative_resilience.shift(1)).fillna(0.5)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume >= 0.0))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean()
        volume_scale = (
            log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).std().clip(lower=0.05)
        )
        abnormal_participation = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_scale).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        abnormal_participation = abnormal_participation.fillna(0.0)

        eps_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data["epsEstimate"], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        sales_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        tax_rate = data["incomeTaxExpense"] / data["incomeBeforeTax"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = _cs_rank(tax_rate.shift(42) - tax_rate).fillna(0.5)

        # High only when the optimistic EPS change is more tax-led than
        # revenue-confirmed; the continuous construction retains broad coverage.
        tax_led_upgrade = eps_revision * tax_decline * (1.0 - sales_revision)

        debt = _cs_rank(data["debtToAssets"]).fillna(0.5)
        illiquidity = _cs_rank(-data["currentRatio"]).fillna(0.5)
        weak_coverage = _cs_rank(-data["interestCoverage"]).fillna(0.5)
        fragility = (debt + illiquidity + weak_coverage) / 3.0

        support_sequence = prior_resilience * abnormal_participation
        unwind_risk = tax_led_upgrade * fragility * downside_impulse * support_sequence

        # Invert the risk rank: high returned factor values predict higher returns.
        alpha = 0.5 - _cs_rank(unwind_risk).fillna(0.5)
        return alpha.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

Parent A supplies the shock-propagation and price-then-participation timing state, while Parent B identifies the accounting-quality and balance-sheet state in which apparent support is most vulnerable to a short-horizon unwind.

    valid = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0)
    log_range = np.log((high / low).where(valid))

class CalmSupportFailureIndustryBreak(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "calm_support_failure_industry_break"

        "during an industry selloff is failing through a fresh calm-regime downside break."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "close",

        "revenueEstimate",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        log_return = np.log(close.where(close > 0.0)).diff()
        industry_return = _group_median(log_return, industry_labels)

        industry_three_day = industry_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = industry_three_day.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.002)
        industry_downside = (-industry_three_day / industry_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        stock_three_day = log_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        prior_resilience = _cs_rank((stock_three_day - industry_three_day).shift(1)).fillna(0.5)
        stock_two_day = log_return.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        industry_two_day = industry_return.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        relative_break = _cs_rank(-(stock_two_day - industry_two_day)).fillna(0.5)

        log_volume = np.log1p(data["volume"].where(data["volume"] >= 0.0))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).std().clip(lower=0.05)
        participation = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)
        participation_gate = 0.5 + 0.5 * (participation / 3.0)

        eps_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data["epsEstimate"], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        sales_revision = _cs_rank(_safe_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], 42)).fillna(0.5)
        tax_rate = data["incomeTaxExpense"] / data["incomeBeforeTax"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = _cs_rank(tax_rate.shift(42) - tax_rate).fillna(0.5)
        tax_led_upgrade = eps_revision * tax_decline * (1.0 - sales_revision)

        debt = _cs_rank(data["debtToAssets"]).fillna(0.5)
        illiquidity = _cs_rank(-data["currentRatio"]).fillna(0.5)
        weak_coverage = _cs_rank(-data["interestCoverage"]).fillna(0.5)
        weak_cashflow = _cs_rank(-data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"]).fillna(0.5)
        fragility = (debt + illiquidity + weak_coverage + weak_cashflow) / 4.0

        calmness = (1.0 - _cs_rank(_prior_range_volatility(data["high"], data["low"]))).fillna(0.5)
        raw_risk = (
            tax_led_upgrade
            * fragility
            * industry_downside
            * prior_resilience
            * calmness
            * relative_break
            * participation_gate
        )
        return _cs_rank(raw_risk).fillna(0.5).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

"""Stress-gated credibility polarity for idiosyncratic volume arrivals.

Mechanism: following a negative industry impulse, prior relative resilience and a
late idiosyncratic participation burst can be either informed counterflow or
transient support.  Revenue- and margin-supported revisions validate the burst;
tax-led and financially fragile revisions raise the threshold for continuation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date group median with a same-date market-median fallback."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(group)]
        if len(members) > 0:
            median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
            out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    market = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return out.T.fillna(market).T


def _cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust contemporaneous cross-sectional z-score."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lo = clean.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    hi = clean.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = clean.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    scale = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(scale, axis=0)


def _revision(current: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    previous = current.shift(lag)
    return ((current - previous) / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )


@register_factor
class StressGatedRevisionArrivalPolarity(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "stress_gated_revision_arrival_polarity"
    name = "Stress-Gated Credible Arrival Polarity"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks sector-residual rare signed-volume arrivals after relative resilience "
        "in an industry selloff, continuing only arrivals validated by operating "
        "revision credibility and reversing the rest."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        stock_ret = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        industry_ret = _group_median(stock_ret, labels)
        industry_move = industry_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = industry_move.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.002)
        downside = (-industry_move / industry_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        stock_move = stock_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        prior_resilience = (stock_move - industry_move).shift(1).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        stress_state = np.tanh(downside) * prior_resilience

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        positive_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
        volume_base = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=12).median().shift(1)
        volume_ratio = volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rare_cutoff = volume_ratio.rolling(60, min_periods=40).quantile(0.95).shift(1)
        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        direction = np.sign(close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
        valid = close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0) & high.gt(low)
        rare = valid & volume_ratio.ge(rare_cutoff)
        marked_arrival = (
            direction * location.abs() * volume_ratio.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        ).where(rare, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        arrival_memory = marked_arrival.ewm(halflife=3, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
        idio_arrival = arrival_memory - _group_median(arrival_memory, labels)

        eps = data["epsEstimate"]
        sales = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        pretax = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax = data["incomeTaxExpense"]

        eps_rev = _revision(eps, 42)
        sales_rev = _revision(sales, 42)
        margin = operating_income / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        margin_change = margin - margin.shift(42)
        tax_rate = tax / pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = tax_rate.shift(42) - tax_rate

        eps_sign = np.sign(eps_rev)
        sales_support = eps_sign * _cs_zscore(sales_rev).fillna(0.0)
        margin_support = eps_sign * _cs_zscore(margin_change).fillna(0.0)
        tax_penalty = _cs_zscore(tax_decline).fillna(0.0).where(eps_sign.gt(0.0), 0.0)
        update = eps.notna() & eps.shift(1).notna() & eps.ne(eps.shift(1))
        credibility_impulse = (
            eps_sign * (0.55 * sales_support + 0.45 * margin_support - 0.40 * tax_penalty)
        ).clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0).where(update, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        credibility = credibility_impulse.ewm(halflife=10, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

        debt = data["debtToAssets"].rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        liquidity_weakness = (-data["currentRatio"]).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        coverage_weakness = (-data["interestCoverage"]).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        fragility = (debt + liquidity_weakness + coverage_weakness) / 3.0

        arrival_sign = np.sign(idio_arrival)
        alignment = arrival_sign * credibility
        polarity = np.tanh(2.0 * (alignment - 0.30 * fragility) - 0.35)
        signal = stress_state * idio_arrival * polarity
        return signal.rank(axis=1, pct=True).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: An idiosyncratic volume arrival during an industry downside impulse is especially informative only after the stock has first shown relative resilience: this is the common-shock support state identified by Parent A. Parent B supplies the polarity test: revenue- and margin-confirmed estimate revisions make the arrival likely informed counterflow and therefore continuation, whereas tax-led or financially fragile revisions make the same support more likely transient liquidity demand and therefore reversal. The interaction distinguishes genuine information-driven sheltering from mechanically supported resilience, which neither industry stress nor signed-volume arrivals identify alone.
programs.description: The signal isolates sector-residual rare signed-volume arrivals following relative resilience during a negative industry impulse, then flips their direction unless they agree with a decaying revenue/margin-supported and tax-discounted EPS-revision state. Financial fragility raises the credibility threshold required for continuation.

programs.code:
"""A synchronized sector liquidation can temporarily depress high-sector-beta constituents through basket and liquidity flows, but a reversal is only expected where the sector has already begun a broad, completed recovery and there is no contemporaneous negative earnings or revenue-surprise disclosure for the individual stock. The signal therefore targets moderate residual laggards with high pre-event sector loading and demonstrably resilient balance-sheet/profitability characteristics, rather than treating every underperformer as a flow-driven dislocation. The intended mechanism is delayed normalization of constituent prices after common-flow pressure has receded, not prediction of an unobserved future correlation decline."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _compound_return(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Return compounded return per column, requiring every bar to exist."""
    return (1.0 + frame).prod(axis=0, min_count=frame.shape[0]) - 1.0


def _mean_pairwise_correlation(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    """Mean of available off-diagonal Pearson correlations in a trailing panel."""
    if frame.shape[1] < 2:
        return np.nan
    corr = frame.corr(min_periods=2).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    values = corr[np.triu_indices(corr.shape[0], k=1)]
    values = values[np.isfinite(values)]
    if values.size == 0:
        return np.nan
    return float(values.mean())


def _percentile(values: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank while preserving missing observations."""
    return values.rank(pct=True, method="average")


@register_factor
class CorrelationReleaseResilientRepairLag(BaseFactor):
    """Long repaired sectors' resilient, high-beta residual laggards."""

    factor_id = "correlation_release_resilient_repair_lag"
    name = "Correlation-Release Repair"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Selects resilient high-sector-beta stocks that lag a broad sector repair "
        "after a completed correlation-release event, excluding negative surprise news."
    )
    window_length = 65
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "industry",
        "marketCap",
        "roic",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        industry = data["industry"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        roic = data["roic"]
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"]
        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]

        # Explicit lagged arithmetic avoids any implicit interpolation over gaps.
        ret = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
        liquid_days = (volume > 0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum() >= 18

        current_fundamental_data = (
            market_cap.notna()
            & roic.notna()
            & current_ratio.notna()
            & debt_to_equity.notna()
            & eps_surprise.notna()
            & revenue_surprise.notna()
        )
        base_eligible = (
            (market_cap > 1.0e9)
            & (close > 5.0)
            & liquid_days
            & current_fundamental_data
            & sector.notna()
            & industry.notna()
        )

        # A change at date d is observable at d.  The extra leading row permits
        # identifying an update exactly at t-14 without any future information.
        eps_change = eps_surprise - eps_surprise.shift(1)
        rev_change = revenue_surprise - revenue_surprise.shift(1)

        output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        n_rows = len(close.index)

        for t in range(64, n_rows):
            eligible_row = base_eligible.iloc[t].copy()

            # Surprise histories must be observable throughout the event window;
            # otherwise a missing release update is not silently treated as benign.
            surprise_history = slice(t - 15, t + 1)
            surprise_known = (
                eps_surprise.iloc[surprise_history].notna().all(axis=0)
                & revenue_surprise.iloc[surprise_history].notna().all(axis=0)
            )
            negative_update = (
                (eps_change.iloc[t - 14 : t + 1] < 0.0).any(axis=0)
                | (rev_change.iloc[t - 14 : t + 1] < 0.0).any(axis=0)
            )
            eligible_row &= surprise_known & ~negative_update

            if int(eligible_row.sum()) < 8:
                continue

            sector_row = sector.iloc[t]
            industry_row = industry.iloc[t]
            eligible_columns = close.columns[eligible_row.to_numpy()]
            sector_values = pd.unique(sector_row.loc[eligible_columns])

            # The industry threshold is evaluated in the same current eligible
            # universe used to construct peer returns and sector baskets.
            industry_counts = industry_row.loc[eligible_columns].value_counts(dropna=True)
            selected_by_sector: list[list[int]] = []

            for sector_value in sector_values:
                sector_mask = eligible_row & sector_row.eq(sector_value)
                sector_columns = close.columns[sector_mask.to_numpy()]
                if len(sector_columns) < 8:
                    continue

                prior_corr_window = ret.loc[:, sector_columns].iloc[t - 24 : t - 4]
                recent_corr_window = ret.loc[:, sector_columns].iloc[t - 4 : t + 1]
                prior_corr = _mean_pairwise_correlation(prior_corr_window)
                recent_corr = _mean_pairwise_correlation(recent_corr_window)
                if not np.isfinite(prior_corr) or not np.isfinite(recent_corr):
                    continue
                if prior_corr < 0.35 or recent_corr > prior_corr - 0.10:
                    continue

                shock_returns = ret.loc[:, sector_columns].iloc[t - 14 : t - 9]
                repair_returns = ret.loc[:, sector_columns].iloc[t - 4 : t + 1]
                sector_shock_daily = shock_returns.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
                sector_repair_daily = repair_returns.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
                if sector_shock_daily.notna().sum() != 5 or sector_repair_daily.notna().sum() != 5:
                    continue
                sector_shock = float((1.0 + sector_shock_daily).prod() - 1.0)
                sector_repair = float((1.0 + sector_repair_daily).prod() - 1.0)
                stock_repair = _compound_return(repair_returns)
                breadth = float((stock_repair > 0.0).mean())
                if sector_shock > -0.04 or sector_repair < 0.02 or breadth < 0.65:
                    continue

                # Common-mode beta is estimated against a leave-one-out sector
                # basket over t-64 through t-5, preventing own-return leakage.
                beta_values = pd.Series(np.nan, index=sector_columns, dtype=float)
                beta_window = ret.loc[:, sector_columns].iloc[t - 64 : t - 4]
                for ticker in sector_columns:
                    own = beta_window[ticker]
                    peers = beta_window.drop(columns=ticker)
                    loo = peers.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
                    valid = own.notna() & loo.notna()
                    if int(valid.sum()) < 40:
                        continue
                    x = loo.loc[valid].to_numpy(dtype=float)
                    y = own.loc[valid].to_numpy(dtype=float)
                    x_centered = x - x.mean()
                    denominator = float(np.dot(x_centered, x_centered))
                    if denominator <= 0.0 or not np.isfinite(denominator):
                        continue
                    beta_values.loc[ticker] = float(np.dot(x_centered, y - y.mean()) / denominator)

                beta_pct = _percentile(beta_values)

                # Resilience is ranked against the complete eligible sector,
                # before residual-lag filters are applied.
                sector_roic = roic.iloc[t].loc[sector_columns]
                sector_current = current_ratio.iloc[t].loc[sector_columns]
                sector_debt = debt_to_equity.iloc[t].loc[sector_columns]
                resilience = (
                    _percentile(sector_roic)
                    + _percentile(sector_current)
                    + _percentile(-sector_debt)
                ) / 3.0
                resilience_pct = _percentile(resilience)

                residual_values = pd.Series(np.nan, index=sector_columns, dtype=float)
                for ticker in sector_columns:
                    industry_value = industry_row.loc[ticker]
                    if industry_counts.get(industry_value, 0) < 5:
                        continue
                    peer_columns = close.columns[
                        (eligible_row & industry_row.eq(industry_value)).to_numpy()
                    ]
                    peer_columns = peer_columns[peer_columns != ticker]
                    if len(peer_columns) == 0:
                        continue
                    peer_cumulative = _compound_return(ret.loc[:, peer_columns].iloc[t - 4 : t + 1])
                    peer_return = peer_cumulative.mean(skipna=True)
                    own_return = stock_repair.loc[ticker]
                    if np.isfinite(own_return) and np.isfinite(peer_return):
                        residual_values.loc[ticker] = own_return - peer_return

                candidate = (
                    beta_values.notna()
                    & beta_pct.ge(2.0 / 3.0)
                    & residual_values.ge(-0.08)
                    & residual_values.le(-0.01)
                    & resilience.gt(resilience.median(skipna=True))
                )
                candidate_columns = sector_columns[candidate.loc[sector_columns].to_numpy()]
                if len(candidate_columns) == 0:
                    continue

                candidate_residual = residual_values.loc[candidate_columns]
                candidate_beta = beta_values.loc[candidate_columns]
                candidate_resilience = resilience.loc[candidate_columns]
                score = (
                    0.50 * _percentile(-candidate_residual)
                    + 0.25 * _percentile(candidate_beta)
                    + 0.25 * _percentile(candidate_resilience)
                )
                score = score.dropna()
                if score.empty:
                    continue

                n_select = min(5, max(1, int(np.ceil(0.20 * len(score)))))
                chosen = score.sort_values(ascending=False, kind="mergesort").iloc[:n_select].index
                positions = [close.columns.get_loc(ticker) for ticker in chosen]
                if positions:
                    selected_by_sector.append(positions)

            # The factor value is the requested long-only portfolio weight:
            # equal sector capital and equal capital inside each selected sector.
            if selected_by_sector:
                sector_weight = 1.0 / float(len(selected_by_sector))
                for positions in selected_by_sector:
                    stock_weight = sector_weight / float(len(positions))
                    output.iloc[t, positions] = stock_weight

        return output

The signal therefore targets moderate residual laggards with high pre-event sector loading and demonstrably resilient balance-sheet/profitability characteristics, rather than treating every underperformer as a flow-driven dislocation. programs.description: At each rebalance close t, use all tickers with positive marketCap above USD 1 billion, close above USD 5, positive volume on at least 18 of the prior 20 bars, and non-missing sector, industry, marketCap, roic, currentRatio, debtToEquity, epsSurprise, and revenueSurprise data. Use the supplied static sector and industry labels; require at least 8 eligible names in a sector and at least 5 eligible names in an industry. Define daily return as close.pct_change(1). For each sector, form an equal-weight sector return using eligible constituent returns, and compute: (1) a completed downside shock, sector cumulative return from t-14 through t-10 of at most -4%; (2) a correlation peak, the mean of all available pairwise constituent-return correlations over t-24 through t-5 of at least 0.35; (3) a completed correlation release, mean pairwise correlation over t-4 through t at least 0.10 below that prior 20-bar correlation measure; and (4) a completed repair, sector cumulative return over t-4 through t of at least +2% with at least 65% of eligible sector constituents having positive cumulative return over that same five-bar interval. All correlation, return, and breadth inputs end at t. For each stock i in a qualifying sector, estimate its common-mode loading as the OLS beta of its daily return on the leave-one-out equal-weight sector return over t-64 through t-5; require at least 40 valid observations and retain only stocks in the top tercile of beta within their sector. Compute stock i's five-bar residual recovery as its cumulative return from t-4 through t minus the leave-one-out equal-weight cumulative return of its industry peers over the same dates; retain only residuals between -8% and -1%, excluding extreme collapses rather than assuming they are flow dislocations. Exclude a stock if either epsSurprise or revenueSurprise declines on any availability-date update during t-14 through t, where an update is identified by a non-zero one-bar change in the point-in-time field; unchanged quarterly values are not treated as news. Define financial resilience as the equally weighted mean of within-sector percentile ranks of roic, currentRatio, and negative debtToEquity, requiring a score above the sector median. Among remaining stocks, score 50% by the within-sector percentile rank of more-negative residual recovery, 25% by beta percentile rank, and 25% by resilience percentile rank. At close t, rank qualifying names within each qualifying sector and select the top 20%, with a minimum of one and maximum of five names per sector. Form a long-only portfolio with equal sector weights and equal weights within each selected sector; trade at the next bar's open and hold for six daily bars. Missing observations, insufficient peer counts, undefined correlations, undefined beta estimates, or unavailable surprise updates make a stock ineligible rather than imputed.

programs.code:
"""This is a conditional price-pressure continuation hypothesis rather than an identified claim about informed absorption. Repeated high-relative-volume closes near the same end of the daily range may indicate persistent imbalance or constrained liquidity replenishment when the stock has not yet moved materially across days; the opposite pattern indicates persistent downside pressure. The effect is explicitly conditional on no large overnight or same-day repricing event, where daily OHLCV cannot distinguish liquidity pressure from public-information incorporation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _historical_volume_median_and_mad(
    log_volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Trailing t-20 through t-1 robust volume baseline and observation count."""
    history = log_volume.shift(1)
    count = history.notna().rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    median = history.rolling(20, min_periods=1).median()

    def median_absolute_deviation(values: np.ndarray) -> float:
        center = np.nanmedian(values)
        return float(np.nanmedian(np.abs(values - center)))

    mad = history.rolling(20, min_periods=1).apply(
        median_absolute_deviation,
        raw=True,
    )
    return median, mad, count


@register_factor
class NeutralReturnVolumeLocationCoherenceDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks persistent signed range-location pressure during neutral trends."""

    factor_id = "neutral_return_volume_location_coherence_drift"
    name = "Neutral-Return Volume-Location Coherence"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of ten-session coherence between robust abnormal "
        "volume and close location, restricted to non-shock names whose ten-day "
        "close return remains near neutral."
    )
    window_length = 31
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        finite_ohlcv = (
            np.isfinite(open_)
            & np.isfinite(high)
            & np.isfinite(low)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
        )
        bar_valid = (
            finite_ohlcv
            & (open_ > 0.0)
            & (high > 0.0)
            & (low > 0.0)
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (volume >= 0.0)
            & (high >= low)
        )

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        overnight_return = open_ / previous_close - 1.0
        daily_return = close / previous_close - 1.0
        valid_observation = (
            bar_valid
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & (previous_close > 0.0)
            & (overnight_return.abs() <= 0.08)
            & (daily_return.abs() <= 0.12)
        )

        price_range = high - low
        clv = (2.0 * (close - low) / price_range - 1.0).where(
            price_range > 0.0,
            0.0,
        )
        clv = clv.where(bar_valid)

        volume_valid = np.isfinite(volume) & (volume >= 0.0)
        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume_valid))
        baseline_median, baseline_mad, baseline_count = (
            _historical_volume_median_and_mad(log_volume)
        )
        volume_z = (log_volume - baseline_median) / (1.4826 * baseline_mad)
        volume_z = volume_z.where(baseline_mad > 0.0, 0.0).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        signed_location_volume = (clv * volume_z).where(valid_observation)
        coherence_count = valid_observation.astype(float).rolling(
            10,
            min_periods=1,
        ).sum()
        coherence = signed_location_volume.rolling(10, min_periods=1).sum()
        coherence = coherence / coherence_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        coherence = coherence.where(coherence_count >= 7.0)

        return_10 = close / close.shift(10) - 1.0
        neutral_weight = (1.0 - return_10.abs() / 0.10).clip(lower=0.0)
        raw_score = coherence * neutral_weight

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(
            np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (volume >= 0.0)
        )
        median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        liquid_large_cap = (
            np.isfinite(market_cap)
            & (market_cap >= 1_000_000_000.0)
            & (median_dollar_volume >= 10_000_000.0)
        )

        eligible = (
            valid_observation
            & (baseline_count >= 15.0)
            & return_10.notna()
            & liquid_large_cap
        )
        return rank(raw_score.where(eligible))
programs.name: Neutral-Return Volume-Location Coherence
programs.trading_idea: This is a conditional price-pressure continuation hypothesis rather than an identified claim about informed absorption. Repeated high-relative-volume closes near the same end of the daily range may indicate persistent imbalance or constrained liquidity replenishment when the stock has not yet moved materially across days; the opposite pattern indicates persistent downside pressure. The effect is explicitly conditional on no large overnight or same-day repricing event, where daily OHLCV cannot distinguish liquidity pressure from public-information incorporation.
programs.description: For stock i on day t, define close location CLV_t = 2*(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t)-1 when high_t>low_t, and CLV_t=0 when high_t=low_t. Let x_t=log(1+volume_t). Estimate abnormal log volume using only days t-20 through t-1: m_t is the rolling median of x, d_t is the rolling median of |x-m_t|, and z_t=(x_t-m_t)/(1.4826*d_t) when d_t>0; otherwise z_t=0. Clip z_t to [-3,3]. Define a valid non-shock observation as one with valid OHLCV, |open_t/close_{t-1}-1|<=0.08, and |close_t/close_{t-1}-1|<=0.12. The 10-day coherence is C_t=mean(CLV_s*clip(z_s,-3,3)) over valid observations s=t-9,...,t, requiring at least 7 valid observations; invalid observations are omitted from the mean. Define the cumulative close return R10_t=close_t/close_{t-10}-1 and the fixed neutral-trend weight W_t=max(0,1-|R10_t|/0.10). The raw score is S_t=C_t*W_t, set to missing when the current day is invalid, the 20-day volume baseline has fewer than 15 valid observations, or R10_t is unavailable. Each day, rank S_t cross-sectionally among eligible names into a percentile score; higher scores are long candidates and lower scores are short candidates. For implementation, restrict the trading universe ex ante to names with marketCap>=1 billion USD and trailing 20-day median(close*volume)>=10 million USD, both measured using information available by t. This differs from endpoint-price/volume-acceptance signals by requiring a robust relative-volume interaction with range location to persist across ten non-shock sessions while mechanically attenuating stocks that have already moved more than 10% over the same period. Before adoption, conduct a redundancy test against idiosyncratic_volume_arrival_information_score, lagged_signed_volume_price_acceptance, lagged_burst_acceptance_resilience_carry, persistent_downside_pressure_amplification, and volume_time_impact_convexity_exhaustion: report daily cross-sectional correlations and test the six-bar return efficacy of S_t residualized cross-sectionally on those signals; do not treat the factor as distinct unless the residualized version retains economically meaningful net-of-cost performance.
