"""Sequential unwind of an initially endorsed but unvalidated earnings upgrade.

Mechanism: a positive EPS-consensus revision can attract extrapolative demand before
revenue, operating performance, and funding capacity validate it.  When that early
endorsement is followed by a calm-regime distribution break, the reversal identifies
crowded narrative ownership being unwound rather than an ordinary pullback.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _clean_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional rank after excluding undefined observations."""
    return rank(frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))


@register_factor
class EndorsedUpgradeFailureDistribution(BaseFactor):
    """Bearish continuation after an endorsed upgrade loses narrative credibility."""

    factor_id = "endorsed_upgrade_failure_distribution"
    name = "Endorsed Upgrade Failure Distribution"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks calm-regime distribution breaks after initially endorsed positive EPS "
        "revisions that lack revenue and margin confirmation and coincide with "
        "deteriorating financing capacity."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "debtToEquity",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"]
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"]
        interest_coverage = data["interestCoverage"]

        eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(21)
        eps_revision = eps_estimate.sub(eps_lag).div(eps_lag.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        revenue_revision = revenue_estimate.sub(revenue_lag).div(
            revenue_lag.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        operating_margin = operating_income.div(revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        margin_change = operating_margin.sub(operating_margin.shift(63))

        update = (
            eps_estimate.notna()
            & eps_estimate.shift(1).notna()
            & eps_estimate.ne(eps_estimate.shift(1))
        )
        positive_upgrade = update & eps_revision.gt(0.0)

        eps_strength = _clean_rank(eps_revision.where(positive_upgrade))
        revenue_confirmation = _clean_rank(revenue_revision.where(positive_upgrade)).fillna(0.5)
        margin_confirmation = _clean_rank(margin_change.where(positive_upgrade)).fillna(0.5)
        narrative_gap = (1.0 - 0.5 * revenue_confirmation - 0.5 * margin_confirmation).clip(
            lower=0.0, upper=1.0
        )

        leverage_worsening = _clean_rank(debt_to_equity.sub(debt_to_equity.shift(63)))
        liquidity_worsening = _clean_rank(current_ratio.sub(current_ratio.shift(63)).mul(-1.0))
        coverage_worsening = _clean_rank(interest_coverage.sub(interest_coverage.shift(63)).mul(-1.0))
        financing_deterioration = (
            0.40 * leverage_worsening.fillna(0.5)
            + 0.30 * liquidity_worsening.fillna(0.5)
            + 0.30 * coverage_worsening.fillna(0.5)
        )

        event_risk = (
            eps_strength.mul(narrative_gap).mul(financing_deterioration)
        ).where(positive_upgrade)
        recent_event_risk = event_risk.ffill(limit=10)

        # The endorsement is deliberately measured through yesterday, before the
        # current distribution bar, so it represents the narrative's prior acceptance.
        prior_five_bar_return = close.shift(1).div(close.shift(6).replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
        prior_endorsement = _clean_rank(prior_five_bar_return)

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        support = prior_close.rolling(20, min_periods=20).min()
        mean_volume = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        prior_log_range_sq = np.log(high.div(low.replace(0.0, np.nan))).pow(2).shift(1)
        prior_range_vol = np.sqrt(prior_log_range_sq.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean())

        bar_range = high.sub(low)
        break_fraction = support.sub(close).div(support.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0)
        close_near_low = 1.0 - close.sub(low).div(bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        close_near_low = close_near_low.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        turnover = volume.div(mean_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        eligible = (
            high.gt(0.0)
            & low.gt(0.0)
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & bar_range.gt(0.0)
            & recent_event_risk.notna()
            & prior_endorsement.notna()
            & prior_range_vol.notna()
        )

        calmness = 1.0 - _clean_rank(prior_range_vol.where(eligible))
        support_failure = _clean_rank(break_fraction.where(eligible & break_fraction.gt(0.0)))
        turnover_pressure = _clean_rank(turnover.where(eligible))

        distribution = (
            calmness.mul(support_failure).mul(turnover_pressure).mul(close_near_low)
        )
        raw_score = recent_event_risk.mul(prior_endorsement).mul(distribution)
        active = eligible & break_fraction.gt(0.0) & raw_score.notna()

        signal = _clean_rank(raw_score.where(active)).sub(0.5)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(close).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: The signal targets a sequential narrative-unwind state: investors initially endorse a positive EPS upgrade through relative price strength, but the upgrade lacks revenue or margin confirmation and is attached to a financially deteriorating issuer. A subsequent calm-regime support failure with high turnover and a close near the low indicates that the earlier endorsement is being reversed by informed distribution rather than a routine pullback. Parent A detects fragile technical ignition and Parent B detects weak upgrade quality, but the explicit prior-endorsement condition isolates the more crowded, over-extrapolated narratives whose reversal can persist over the next six sessions.

Higher values identify likely six-day downside continuation.

"""A sudden sector-relative consensus-rank jump is treated as a salient reclassification event rather than as ordinary revision momentum. Over the next six trading days, investors may extrapolate an abrupt peer-ranking change too far, especially when the revision is not corroborated by contemporaneously available cash-generation, working-capital, and leverage trends; the expected return is therefore opposite the rank jump. This differs from conventional revision drift because it trades the discontinuity in relative consensus status and its accounting-credibility interaction, not the level of revisions or the price response to a revision."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _global_rescaled_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ascending average-tie ranks rescaled to [-1, 1] independently by date."""
    counts = values.notna().sum(axis=1)
    raw_rank = values.rank(axis=1, method="average", ascending=True)
    denominator = counts.sub(1).replace(0, np.nan)
    percentile = raw_rank.sub(1).div(denominator, axis=0)
    result = 2.0 * percentile - 1.0
    singleton_rows = counts.eq(1)
    if singleton_rows.any():
        result.loc[singleton_rows] = result.loc[singleton_rows].where(
            result.loc[singleton_rows].isna(), 0.0
        )
    return result


def _sector_rescaled_rank(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    sectors: pd.DataFrame,
    min_count: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-date sector ranks, emitting NaN where a sector is too small."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns, dtype=float)

    for timestamp in values.index:
        row = values.loc[timestamp]
        sector_row = sectors.loc[timestamp]
        valid = row.notna() & sector_row.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        valid_sectors = sector_row.loc[valid]
        for sector_name, members in valid_sectors.groupby(valid_sectors).groups.items():
            member_index = pd.Index(members)
            count = len(member_index)
            if count < min_count:
                continue

            member_values = row.loc[member_index]
            ranks = member_values.rank(method="average", ascending=True)
            if count == 1:
                scaled = pd.Series(0.0, index=member_index)
            else:
                scaled = 2.0 * (ranks - 1.0) / float(count - 1) - 1.0
            output.loc[timestamp, member_index] = scaled

    return output


def _common_sector_eligibility(
    valid_now: pd.DataFrame,
    valid_previous: pd.DataFrame,
    sectors: pd.DataFrame,
    min_count: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Marks names in sectors having enough names valid on both adjacent dates."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(False, index=valid_now.index, columns=valid_now.columns)

    for row_number, timestamp in enumerate(valid_now.index):
        if row_number == 0:
            continue

        sector_row = sectors.loc[timestamp]
        common = valid_now.loc[timestamp] & valid_previous.loc[timestamp] & sector_row.notna()
        if not common.any():
            continue

        common_sectors = sector_row.loc[common]
        for sector_name, members in common_sectors.groupby(common_sectors).groups.items():
            member_index = pd.Index(members)
            if len(member_index) >= min_count:
                output.loc[timestamp, member_index] = True

    return output


def _sector_neutral_event_book(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sectors: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build equal-gross, sector-neutral daily entry weights from event scores."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=scores.index, columns=scores.columns)

    for timestamp in scores.index:
        score_row = scores.loc[timestamp]
        sector_row = sectors.loc[timestamp]
        valid = eligible.loc[timestamp] & score_row.notna() & sector_row.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        sector_books: list[tuple[pd.Index, pd.Index]] = []
        valid_sectors = sector_row.loc[valid]
        for sector_name, members in valid_sectors.groupby(valid_sectors).groups.items():
            member_index = pd.Index(members)
            sector_scores = score_row.loc[member_index]
            positive = sector_scores[sector_scores > 0.0]
            negative = sector_scores[sector_scores < 0.0]
            if positive.empty or negative.empty:
                continue

            selection_count = int(math.ceil(0.20 * len(member_index)))
            long_names = pd.Index(positive.nlargest(selection_count).index)
            short_names = pd.Index(negative.nsmallest(selection_count).index)
            if len(long_names) and len(short_names):
                sector_books.append((long_names, short_names))

        active_sectors = len(sector_books)
        if active_sectors == 0:
            continue

        sector_gross_side = 0.5 / float(active_sectors)
        for long_names, short_names in sector_books:
            output.loc[timestamp, long_names] = sector_gross_side / float(len(long_names))
            output.loc[timestamp, short_names] = -sector_gross_side / float(len(short_names))

    return output


@register_factor
class SectorRevisionRankCredibilityReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Fade abrupt sector-relative coherent-consensus rank reclassifications."""

    factor_id = "sector_revision_rank_credibility_reversal"
    name = "Sector Revision-Rank Credibility Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral six-bar reversal portfolio that fades fresh, abrupt "
        "changes in sector-relative coherent EPS and revenue consensus ranks, "
        "scaled by point-in-time accounting credibility."
    )
    window_length = 64
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "revenue",
        "receivables",
        "inventory",
        "debtToEquity",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        sectors = data["sector"].reindex_like(close).ffill()

        eps_lag_1 = eps_estimate.shift(1)
        revenue_lag_1 = revenue_estimate.shift(1)
        eps_lag_21 = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_lag_21 = revenue_estimate.shift(21)

        estimate_valid = (
            eps_estimate.notna()
            & eps_lag_1.notna()
            & eps_lag_21.notna()
            & revenue_estimate.notna()
            & revenue_lag_1.notna()
            & revenue_lag_21.notna()
        )

        eps_revision = (eps_estimate - eps_lag_21) / eps_lag_21.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revenue_revision = (revenue_estimate - revenue_lag_21) / revenue_lag_21.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        eps_revision = eps_revision.where(estimate_valid)
        revenue_revision = revenue_revision.where(estimate_valid)

        eps_rank = _global_rescaled_rank(eps_revision)
        revenue_rank = _global_rescaled_rank(revenue_revision)
        coherent = (eps_revision * revenue_revision) > 0.0
        coherent_score = ((eps_rank + revenue_rank) / 2.0).where(coherent, 0.0)
        coherent_score = coherent_score.where(estimate_valid)

        fresh_event = estimate_valid & (
            eps_estimate.ne(eps_lag_1) | revenue_estimate.ne(revenue_lag_1)
        )

        rank_now = _sector_rescaled_rank(coherent_score, sectors, 1)
        rank_previous = rank_now.shift(1)
        common_valid = _common_sector_eligibility(
            coherent_score.notna(),
            coherent_score.shift(1).notna(),
            sectors,
            10,
        )
        discontinuity = (rank_now - rank_previous).where(common_valid)
        event_eligible = fresh_event & discontinuity.abs().ge(0.30) & discontinuity.notna()

        free_cash_flow = data["freeCashFlow"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue = data["revenue"].reindex_like(close)
        receivables = data["receivables"].reindex_like(close)
        inventory = data["inventory"].reindex_like(close)
        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"].reindex_like(close)

        safe_revenue = revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        fcf_margin_change = free_cash_flow.div(safe_revenue) - free_cash_flow.div(safe_revenue).shift(63)
        receivables_ratio = receivables.div(safe_revenue)
        inventory_ratio = inventory.div(safe_revenue)
        receivables_improvement = -(receivables_ratio - receivables_ratio.shift(63))
        inventory_improvement = -(inventory_ratio - inventory_ratio.shift(63))
        leverage_improvement = -(debt_to_equity - debt_to_equity.shift(63))

        credibility_components = [
            _sector_rescaled_rank(fcf_margin_change, sectors, 10),
            _sector_rescaled_rank(receivables_improvement, sectors, 10),
            _sector_rescaled_rank(inventory_improvement, sectors, 10),
            _sector_rescaled_rank(leverage_improvement, sectors, 10),
        ]
        credibility = sum(component.fillna(0.0) for component in credibility_components) / 4.0

        raw_score = -discontinuity * (1.0 - 0.5 * credibility)
        raw_score = raw_score.where(event_eligible)
        return _sector_neutral_event_book(raw_score, event_eligible, sectors).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Sector Revision-Rank Credibility Reversal
programs.trading_idea: A sudden sector-relative consensus-rank jump is treated as a salient reclassification event rather than as ordinary revision momentum. Over the next six trading days, investors may extrapolate an abrupt peer-ranking change too far, especially when the revision is not corroborated by contemporaneously available cash-generation, working-capital, and leverage trends; the expected return is therefore opposite the rank jump. This differs from conventional revision drift because it trades the discontinuity in relative consensus status and its accounting-credibility interaction, not the level of revisions or the price response to a revision.
programs.description: At each daily close t, use the latest-quarter point-in-time epsEstimate and revenueEstimate values, requiring both estimates to be non-missing at t, t-1, and t-21. Define 21-bar proportional revisions rEPS=(epsEstimate_t-epsEstimate_t-21)/max(abs(epsEstimate_t-21),0.01) and rREV=(revenueEstimate_t-revenueEstimate_t-21)/max(abs(revenueEstimate_t-21),1000000). Convert each revision into an all-universe ascending percentile rank among valid names at t, rescaled to [-1,1]. The coherent revision score C is the average of the two rescaled ranks when rEPS and rREV have the same strict sign; otherwise C=0. A fresh event requires that at least one of epsEstimate or revenueEstimate changed between t-1 and t. Within each static sector, provided at least 10 names have valid C values at both t and t-1, compute ascending percentile ranks R_t(C) and R_t-1(C), using average ranks for ties and (rank-1)/(peer_count-1) scaling. The rank discontinuity is D=R_t(C)-R_t-1(C); only fresh coherent events with abs(D)>=0.30 are eligible. Accounting credibility Q is a sector-relative average of four 63-bar point-in-time changes: delta(freeCashFlow/revenue), -delta(receivables/revenue), -delta(inventory/revenue), and -delta(debtToEquity). Each available component is converted to a sector percentile rank rescaled to [-1,1], with at least 10 valid sector observations required for that component; unavailable components contribute 0, so Q is the sum divided by four. These quarterly fields are used as supplied at their availability dates, with no shifts. The tradable score is S=-D*(1-0.5*Q): a positive revision-rank jump receives a negative expected-return score, with stronger reversal when accounting credibility is weak, while a negative rank jump receives a positive expected-return score, with stronger reversal when credibility is strong. This is materially distinct from revision_response_elasticity_calibration: it does not trade revision magnitude/level or calibrate on contemporaneous price response; its non-overlapping construction is the one-day change in sector-relative coherent-revision rank. Rebalance daily after the close and enter at the next bar open. In every active sector with both sides available, select up to ceil(20% of eligible names) with the highest positive S as longs and the lowest negative S as shorts, equal-weighting names on each side and assigning equal long and short dollar exposure within sector. Allocate equal gross exposure across active sectors, making the book sector-neutral; no beta neutralization is claimed because beta is not in scope. Each daily entry is held for six bars with linear remaining weights of 1, 5/6, 4/6, 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, then exits after the sixth bar.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _new_release(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    prior = actual.shift(1)
    return actual.notna() & (prior.isna() | actual.ne(prior))


def _bounded_surprise(
    surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    actual: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    denom = estimate.abs() + actual.abs()
    valid = surprise.notna() & estimate.notna() & actual.notna() & denom.gt(0.0)
    result = surprise / denom.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return result.clip(-1.0, 1.0).where(valid)


def _prior_range_volatility(high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    valid = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0)
    squared_range = np.log((high / low).where(valid)).pow(2.0)
    return np.sqrt(squared_range.rolling(20, min_periods=12).mean().shift(1))


@register_factor
class CashTaxCredibilityMomentumSwitch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_tax_credibility_momentum_switch"
    name = "Cash-Tax Credibility Momentum Switch"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks release surprises by whether cash conversion validates the news, "
        "while reversing nominally positive surprises that are tax-led, fragile, "
        "calm, and already under downside price pressure."
    )
    window_length = 26
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "epsActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueActual",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "incomeQuality",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]

        eps_signal = _bounded_surprise(
            data["epsSurprise"], data["epsEstimate"], eps_actual
        )
        revenue_signal = _bounded_surprise(
            data["revenueSurprise"], data["revenueEstimate"], revenue_actual
        )
        n_components = eps_signal.notna().astype(float) + revenue_signal.notna().astype(float)
        surprise = (eps_signal.fillna(0.0) + revenue_signal.fillna(0.0)) / n_components.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        release = _new_release(eps_actual) | _new_release(revenue_actual)

        free_cash_flow = data["freeCashFlow"]
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"]
        cash_available = free_cash_flow.notna() & income_quality.notna()
        cash_confirmed = free_cash_flow.gt(0.0) & income_quality.ge(1.0)
        cash_weak = free_cash_flow.le(0.0) | income_quality.lt(1.0)
        cash_state = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        cash_state = cash_state.where(~(cash_available & cash_confirmed), 1.0)
        cash_state = cash_state.where(~(cash_available & cash_weak), -1.0)

        pretax = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax = data["incomeTaxExpense"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        prior_pretax = pretax.shift(1)
        prior_tax = tax.shift(1)
        prior_operating_income = operating_income.shift(1)
        prior_revenue = revenue.shift(1)

        tax_decline = (
            prior_tax / prior_pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            - tax / pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_change = (
            (revenue - prior_revenue) / prior_revenue.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        margin_change = (
            operating_income / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            - prior_operating_income / prior_revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        tax_led = (
            _cs_rank(tax_decline)
            - 0.5 * (_cs_rank(revenue_change) + _cs_rank(margin_change))
        ).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        fragility_parts = (
            _cs_rank(data["debtToAssets"])
            + _cs_rank(-data["currentRatio"])
            + _cs_rank(-data["interestCoverage"])
        )
        fragility_count = (
            data["debtToAssets"].notna().astype(float)
            + data["currentRatio"].notna().astype(float)
            + data["interestCoverage"].notna().astype(float)
        )
        fragility = (fragility_parts / fragility_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).fillna(0.5)

        calmness = (1.0 - _cs_rank(_prior_range_volatility(data["high"], data["low"]))).fillna(0.5)
        five_day_return = close / close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        downside_break = _cs_rank((-five_day_return).clip(lower=0.0)).fillna(0.5)
        break_state = tax_led * fragility * calmness * downside_break

        positive_surprise = surprise.clip(lower=0.0)
        negative_surprise = (-surprise).clip(lower=0.0)
        confirmed_upside = positive_surprise * (0.5 + 0.5 * cash_state)
        tax_fragility_break = positive_surprise * break_state
        weak_cash_downside = negative_surprise * (0.5 - 0.5 * cash_state)
        event_score = confirmed_upside - tax_fragility_break - weak_cash_downside
        event_score = event_score.where(release & surprise.notna())

        event_position = (2.0 * _cs_rank(event_score) - 1.0).where(event_score.notna())
        held_position = event_position.fillna(0.0).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum()
        signal = _cs_rank(held_position).fillna(0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: Post-earnings drift depends on whether a reported surprise is economically credible: cash-supported surprises should continue because investors gradually update toward durable operating improvement. Conversely, a positive surprise that is tax-led, financially fragile, calm before the release, and already beginning to break down is vulnerable to delayed skepticism and should reverse downward; negative surprises with weak cash conversion likewise continue lower. The interaction creates edge because cash-flow confirmation distinguishes genuine surprise drift from Parent A's fragile tax-attribution break regime, while tax attribution and fragility identify the subset of nominally positive surprises for which Parent B's generic confirmation logic is insufficient.
programs.description: On new earnings or revenue releases, the factor combines normalized surprise direction with cash-flow confirmation, then switches positive-surprise exposure toward a short when the result is tax-led and occurs in a calm, fragile downside-break state. Release scores are cross-sectionally ranked and retained for six trading days.

"""This is a reduced-form downside-continuation signal, not an identification claim about withdrawn bids or an outstanding sell program. A recent downside-volatility shock that coincides with a large negative return per unit of below-normal participation, a close near the session low, and weak balance-sheet buffers may indicate that adverse-risk repricing is not yet fully absorbed by natural risk-bearing capital. The defining prediction is conditional: the joint state, rather than downside return, volume, close location, or financial fragility alone, predicts lower six-day returns."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_winsorize(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each date's valid cross-section at empirical 1% and 99% tails."""
    lower = df.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = df.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return df.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _cross_sectional_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Percentile rank by date, using average ranks for ties."""
    return df.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)


@register_factor
class FragileUnabsorbedDownsideImpactState(BaseFactor):
    """Joint downside-impact, close-pressure, and balance-sheet fragility state."""

    factor_id = "fragile_unabsorbed_downside_impact_state"
    name = "Fragile Downside Impact Interaction"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Conditional downside-continuation state combining a strictly-prior "
        "downside-variance innovation, return per unit of abnormal volume, "
        "close-near-low pressure, and point-in-time financial fragility. "
        "High scores indicate potentially unabsorbed adverse repricing and "
        "forecast lower six-day returns."
    )
    window_length = 65
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        debt_to_assets = data["debtToAssets"]
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"]

        positive_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        log_return = np.log(positive_close / positive_close.shift(1))
        valid_return = pd.DataFrame(
            np.isfinite(log_return.to_numpy()),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        valid_return_history = valid_return.rolling(65, min_periods=65).sum().eq(65)

        downside_component = log_return.clip(upper=0.0).pow(2)
        downside_variance = downside_component.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        downside_baseline = downside_variance.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=60).mean()
        volatility_innovation = np.log(downside_variance / downside_baseline)

        positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        prior_volume = positive_volume.shift(1)
        prior_volume_mean = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        prior_volume_count = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).count()
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume_mean
        signed_downside_impact = -log_return / abnormal_volume

        bar_range = high - low
        close_near_low = 1.0 - (close - low) / bar_range

        debt_valid = debt_to_assets.where(
            np.isfinite(debt_to_assets) & (debt_to_assets >= 0.0)
        )
        current_valid = current_ratio.where(
            np.isfinite(current_ratio) & (current_ratio > 0.0)
        )

        finite_volatility = pd.DataFrame(
            np.isfinite(volatility_innovation.to_numpy()),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        finite_impact = pd.DataFrame(
            np.isfinite(signed_downside_impact.to_numpy()),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        finite_location = pd.DataFrame(
            np.isfinite(close_near_low.to_numpy()),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        eligible = (
            valid_return_history
            & (downside_variance > 0.0)
            & (downside_baseline > 0.0)
            & finite_volatility
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & prior_volume_count.eq(20)
            & (abnormal_volume > 0.0)
            & finite_impact
            & (high > low)
            & finite_location
            & debt_valid.notna()
            & current_valid.notna()
        )

        volatility_innovation = _cross_sectional_winsorize(
            volatility_innovation.where(eligible)
        )
        signed_downside_impact = _cross_sectional_winsorize(
            signed_downside_impact.where(eligible)
        )
        debt_winsorized = _cross_sectional_winsorize(debt_valid.where(eligible))
        current_winsorized = _cross_sectional_winsorize(current_valid.where(eligible))
        close_near_low = close_near_low.where(eligible)

        fragility = 0.5 * _cross_sectional_rank(debt_winsorized) + 0.5 * (
            1.0 - _cross_sectional_rank(current_winsorized)
        )

        score = (
            _cross_sectional_rank(volatility_innovation)
            * _cross_sectional_rank(signed_downside_impact)
            * _cross_sectional_rank(close_near_low)
            * _cross_sectional_rank(fragility)
        ).where(eligible)

        sufficient_universe = eligible.sum(axis=1).ge(20)
        return score.where(sufficient_universe, np.nan)

programs.trading_idea: This is a reduced-form downside-continuation signal, not an identification claim about withdrawn bids or an outstanding sell program. A recent downside-volatility shock that coincides with a large negative return per unit of below-normal participation, a close near the session low, and weak balance-sheet buffers may indicate that adverse-risk repricing is not yet fully absorbed by natural risk-bearing capital. The defining prediction is conditional: the joint state, rather than downside return, volume, close location, or financial fragility alone, predicts lower six-day returns.
programs.description: Signal is computed after the close of day t and may be traded no earlier than day t+1. Let r_t = ln(close_t / close_{t-1}). For each stock, define five-day downside variance D_t = mean_{j=t-4,...,t}[min(r_j,0)^2]. Define its strictly prior baseline B_t = mean_{u=t-60,...,t-1}[D_u], and downside-variance innovation V_t = ln(D_t / B_t). This requires valid positive closes for returns t-64 through t, D_t > 0, and B_t > 0; otherwise the stock is ineligible. Define abnormal-volume ratio AVol_t = volume_t / mean_{j=t-20,...,t-1}[volume_j], requiring 20 prior strictly positive volume observations, current volume_t > 0, and AVol_t > 0. Define signed downside impact I_t = (-r_t) / AVol_t, so larger positive values represent a more negative current return per unit of abnormal participation. Define close-near-low pressure L_t = 1 - (close_t - low_t) / (high_t - low_t), requiring high_t > low_t; L_t = 1 at the low and 0 at the high. Financial fragility uses only point-in-time fields available at t: F_t = 0.5 × Rank(debtToAssets_t) + 0.5 × [1 - Rank(currentRatio_t)]. debtToAssets must be finite and nonnegative, and currentRatio must be finite and strictly positive; missing values are not imputed and make the stock ineligible. On each date, use the common eligible universe containing all required price, volume, and fundamental inputs. Winsorize V_t, I_t, debtToAssets_t, and currentRatio_t cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th empirical percentiles; L_t is already bounded and is not winsorized. Convert each of V_t, I_t, L_t, and F_t to cross-sectional percentile ranks in [0,1], with average ranks for ties. The final raw state score is S_t = Rank(V_t) × Rank(I_t) × Rank(L_t) × Rank(F_t). Require at least 20 eligible stocks on a date; otherwise output NaN for all stocks that date. High S_t forecasts underperformance, so implementation is short high-score names and long low-score names subject to normal liquidity, borrow, and risk controls. No centered windows, forward shifts, future realized volatility, t+1-or-later bars, or non-listed fields may be used.

"""This is a conditional short-horizon reversal signal, not an identification of order-flow branching, dealer inventory, or forced liquidation. A stock that experiences an unusually large sector-residual downside displacement on high participation, then shows materially lower volume and intraday downside range without a meaningful new low on the following day, may have an overextended price response relative to the immediately observable continuation of stress. The confirmation is deliberately observed only after the follow-on close; its economic interpretation is limited to a measurable shock-and-cooling pattern whose return value must be evaluated net of trading costs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_equal_weighted_return(
    stock_returns: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct causal daily equal-weighted sector returns for each ticker."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stock_returns.index, columns=stock_returns.columns)

    # Sector is static metadata. Forward filling only propagates labels already
    # available at or before each date; the final row supplies stable column labels.
    labels = sector.ffill().iloc[-1].reindex(stock_returns.columns)
    valid_labels = labels.dropna()

    for sector_name in pd.unique(valid_labels):
        members = valid_labels.index[valid_labels == sector_name]
        if len(members) == 0:
            continue
        sector_return = stock_returns.loc[:, members].mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
        output.loc[:, members] = np.broadcast_to(
            sector_return.to_numpy()[:, None],
            (len(stock_returns.index), len(members)),
        )

    return output


@register_factor
class IdioBranchingDeficitInventoryRepair(BaseFactor):
    """Confirmed idiosyncratic downside-exhaustion reversal after stress cools."""

    factor_id = "idio_branching_deficit_inventory_repair"
    name = "Confirmed Idiosyncratic Downside-Exhaustion Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Ranks stocks with a prior-day sector-residual downside shock on elevated "
        "range and participation when the following bar confirms stress cooling, "
        "no material new low, persistent residual displacement, and sector weakness."
    )
    window_length = 22
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        stock_return = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        sector_return = _sector_equal_weighted_return(stock_return, sector)
        residual_return = stock_return - sector_return

        true_range = (high - low) / previous_close
        true_range = true_range.where(true_range > 0.0)

        prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()
        relative_volume = volume / prior_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume = relative_volume.where(relative_volume > 0.0)

        # At the current close, the putative shock belongs to the prior bar and
        # the current bar is its fully observed confirmation bar.
        shock_residual = residual_return.shift(1)
        shock_range = true_range.shift(1)
        shock_relative_volume = relative_volume.shift(1)
        shock_sector_return = sector_return.shift(1)

        residual_rank = rank(shock_residual)
        range_rank = rank(shock_range)
        volume_rank = rank(shock_relative_volume)

        downside_shock = (
            (residual_rank <= 0.10)
            & (range_rank >= 0.80)
            & (volume_rank >= 0.80)
            & (shock_residual < 0.0)
            & (shock_range > 0.0)
            & (shock_relative_volume > 0.0)
        )

        volume_cooling = (volume / volume.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)) <= 0.60
        range_cooling = (true_range / shock_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)) <= 0.60
        no_material_new_low = low >= 0.99 * low.shift(1)

        two_bar_stock_return = close / close.shift(2).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        remains_depressed = two_bar_stock_return <= 0.5 * shock_residual
        sector_weakness = sector_return <= 0.0

        confirmed = (
            downside_shock
            & volume_cooling
            & range_cooling
            & no_material_new_low
            & remains_depressed
            & sector_weakness
        )

        remaining_residual_displacement = -(
            two_bar_stock_return - (shock_sector_return + sector_return)
        )
        displacement_rank = rank(remaining_residual_displacement)

        raw_score = displacement_rank * volume_rank * range_rank
        confirmed_score = raw_score.where(confirmed)

        # Rank only confirmed names, preserving exact zero exposure elsewhere.
        final_score = rank(confirmed_score).where(confirmed, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        return final_score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: This is a conditional short-horizon reversal signal, not an identification of order-flow branching, dealer inventory, or forced liquidation. A stock that experiences an unusually large sector-residual downside displacement on high participation, then shows materially lower volume and intraday downside range without a meaningful new low on the following day, may have an overextended price response relative to the immediately observable continuation of stress. The confirmation is deliberately observed only after the follow-on close; its economic interpretation is limited to a measurable shock-and-cooling pattern whose return value must be evaluated net of trading costs.
programs.description: Let t be the shock bar and t+1 the confirmation bar. At the close of t+1, compute stock return r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1 and sector return r_s,t as the equal-weighted return of valid names sharing sector_i; define residual return e_i,t = r_i,t - r_s,t. Define true range proxy TR_i,t = (high_i,t - low_i,t) / close_i,t-1 and relative volume RV_i,t = volume_i,t / median(volume_i,t-20:t-1), requiring at least 10 valid prior observations. A downside shock requires e_i,t to be in the bottom 10% of the cross-section, TR_i,t to be in the top 20%, and RV_i,t to be in the top 20%, with e_i,t < 0. On confirmation bar t+1, require volume cooling volume_i,t+1 / volume_i,t <= 0.60, range cooling TR_i,t+1 / TR_i,t <= 0.60, and no material new low: low_i,t+1 >= 0.99 * low_i,t. Require the stock to remain depressed, close_i,t+1 / close_i,t-1 - 1 <= 0.5 * e_i,t, so that at least half of the sector-residual shock displacement remains unrepaired. Apply a modest sector-weakness filter, r_s,t+1 <= 0, to avoid treating a broad sector rebound as idiosyncratic repair. Among confirmed names, score positively by the cross-sectional rank of remaining residual displacement, -(close_i,t+1 / close_i,t-1 - 1 - (r_s,t + r_s,t+1)), multiplied by the ranks of initial relative volume and initial true range; set non-confirmed names to zero. Cross-sectionally winsorize component ranks through percentile ranking and normalize the final nonzero score to ranks. The signal is timestamped after the t+1 close; any portfolio is formed no earlier than t+2 open, and the six-bar forward return begins after this formation timestamp.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _numeric(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return frame.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _downside_stress(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal downside liquidity-withdrawal measure from price, range, and volume."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close.div(safe_close.shift(1)).sub(1.0)
    sigma = ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    base_volume = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
    relative_volume = positive_volume.div(base_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))

    bar_range = high.sub(low)
    close_location = close.sub(low).mul(2.0).div(bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
    downside = ret.div(sigma).mul(-1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0)
    lower_close = close_location.mul(-1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    activity = np.log(relative_volume).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

    daily = downside.mul(lower_close).mul(activity)
    valid = sigma.notna() & base_volume.notna() & close_location.notna() & ret.notna()
    return daily.where(valid).ewm(halflife=2.0, adjust=False, min_periods=3).mean()


def _information_update(fields: list[pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time arrival flag for reports and consensus changes."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(False, index=fields[0].index, columns=fields[0].columns)
    for field in fields:
        clean = _numeric(field)
        previous = clean.shift(1)
        arrived = clean.notna() & (previous.isna() | clean.ne(previous))
        result = result | arrived.fillna(False)
    return result


def _cs_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


@register_factor
class CredibilitySplitCapitulationPolarity(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "credibility_split_capitulation_polarity"
    name = "Credibility-Split Capitulation Polarity"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Routes downside volume stress toward reversal for valuation-anchored, "
        "cash-resilient issuers and toward continuation for recently disclosed "
        "tax-supported, weakly confirmed EPS revisions."
    )
    window_length = 41
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "earningsYield",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "totalDebt",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "eps",
        "netIncome",
        "freeCashFlow",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _numeric(data["close"])
        high = _numeric(data["high"])
        low = _numeric(data["low"])
        volume = _numeric(data["volume"])
        stress = _downside_stress(close, high, low, volume)

        earnings_yield = _numeric(data["earningsYield"])
        fcf_yield = _numeric(data["freeCashFlowYield"])
        valuation_yield = earnings_yield.where(earnings_yield.notna(), fcf_yield)
        five_day_return = close.where(close > 0.0).div(close.shift(5).where(close.shift(5) > 0.0)).sub(1.0)

        operating_income = _numeric(data["operatingIncome"])
        revenue = _numeric(data["revenue"])
        pretax = _numeric(data["incomeBeforeTax"])
        tax = _numeric(data["incomeTaxExpense"])
        operating_cash_flow = _numeric(data["operatingCashFlow"])
        total_debt = _numeric(data["totalDebt"])
        eps_estimate = _numeric(data["epsEstimate"])
        revenue_estimate = _numeric(data["revenueEstimate"])

        cash_debt = operating_cash_flow.div(total_debt.where(total_debt > 0.0))
        resilience = _cs_rank(cash_debt.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=2.0))

        eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(21)
        eps_revision = eps_estimate.sub(eps_lag).div(eps_lag.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        revenue_revision = revenue_estimate.sub(revenue_lag).div(revenue_lag.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        margin = operating_income.div(revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        margin_change = margin.sub(margin.shift(1))
        tax_rate = tax.div(pretax.where(pretax > 0.0))
        tax_rate_decline = tax_rate.shift(1).sub(tax_rate)

        report_change = (
            operating_income.ne(operating_income.shift(1))
            | revenue.ne(revenue.shift(1))
            | pretax.ne(pretax.shift(1))
            | tax.ne(tax.shift(1))
        )
        revision_event = (
            eps_estimate.ne(eps_estimate.shift(1))
            & eps_revision.gt(0.0)
            & pretax.gt(0.0)
            & tax_rate_decline.notna()
            & revenue_revision.notna()
            & margin_change.notna()
            & report_change
        )

        weak_operating = 1.0 - 0.5 * (
            _cs_rank(revenue_revision.where(revision_event))
            + _cs_rank(margin_change.where(revision_event))
        )
        tax_supported = _cs_rank(tax_rate_decline.where(revision_event))
        weak_cash_cover = 1.0 - resilience
        event_risk = (
            _cs_rank(eps_revision.where(revision_event))
            .mul(tax_supported)
            .mul(weak_operating)
            .mul(weak_cash_cover)
            .where(revision_event)
        )

        latent_credibility_risk = event_risk.shift(4).rolling(12, min_periods=1).max().fillna(0.0)

        update_fields = [
            data["epsActual"],
            data["revenueActual"],
            data["epsSurprise"],
            data["revenueSurprise"],
            data["epsEstimate"],
            data["revenueEstimate"],
            data["revenue"],
            data["eps"],
            data["operatingIncome"],
            data["netIncome"],
            data["freeCashFlow"],
        ]
        update_today = _information_update(update_fields)
        recently_updated = update_today.astype(float).rolling(4, min_periods=1).max().gt(0.0)

        valuation_rank = _cs_rank(valuation_yield)
        return_rank = _cs_rank(five_day_return)
        anchor_gap = valuation_rank.sub(return_rank).clip(lower=0.0)

        recovery_leg = stress.mul(anchor_gap).mul(resilience)
        credibility_failure_leg = stress.mul(latent_credibility_risk)
        raw_score = recovery_leg.sub(credibility_failure_leg)

        history = close.shift(1).notna().rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().eq(20)
        eligible = (
            history
            & stress.notna()
            & valuation_yield.notna()
            & five_day_return.notna()
            & resilience.notna()
            & ~recently_updated
        )
        raw_score = raw_score.where(eligible)
        count = raw_score.notna().sum(axis=1)
        score = _cs_rank(raw_score).sub(0.5)
        return score.where(count.ge(20)).reindex_like(close).astype(float)
programs.name: Credibility-Split Capitulation Polarity
programs.trading_idea: Downside volume stress has two economically distinct meanings: cheap stocks with strong cash-debt coverage are more likely experiencing forced-liquidation overshoot and liquidity replenishment, while the same stress following a tax-supported positive revision with weak operating confirmation is more likely a delayed credibility unwind. The factor therefore routes identical-looking capitulation through a fundamental-credibility state variable rather than treating all sell pressure as either continuation or reversal. This interaction carries edge because valuation alone cannot identify value traps created by weak earnings quality, while revision fragility alone cannot identify when a price decline has become a tradable liquidity overshoot.
programs.description: Ranks a polarity score that rewards valuation-anchored downside stress in cash-resilient firms and penalizes the same stress when a recently disclosed, weakly supported positive EPS revision leaves a latent credibility-risk state. Report and estimate-update days are excluded so the signal targets post-information liquidity dynamics.

"""Solvency-gated polarity of post-shock liquidity cooling.

Mechanism: cooling after an idiosyncratic high-participation downside shock is
an inventory-overhang completion signal when balance-sheet liquidity permits
market makers and fundamental buyers to reload.  Weak cash and operating-cash-
flow coverage instead turns the same pause into a fragile aftershock state in
which bad-news amplification can restart selling.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _numeric(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Coerce a feed panel to a numeric panel without changing its alignment."""
    return frame.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")


def _sector_mean_return(ret: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-day equal-weighted sector return, using only static sector labels."""
    labels = sector.reindex(index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns).ffill()
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns, dtype=float)
    for i in range(len(ret.index)):
        row_labels = labels.iloc[i].astype(object).where(
            labels.iloc[i].notna(), "__MISSING_SECTOR__"
        )
        output.iloc[i] = ret.iloc[i].groupby(row_labels, sort=False).transform("mean")
    return output


def _compound_lagged_three_day_return(ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compounded return over t-4 through t-2, entirely observable at t."""
    return (1.0 + ret.shift(4)) * (1.0 + ret.shift(3)) * (1.0 + ret.shift(2)) - 1.0


@register_factor
class BalanceSheetGatedCoolingReversalPolarity(BaseFactor):
    """Completed liquidity-shock reversals whose sign is set by debt coverage."""

    factor_id = "balance_sheet_gated_cooling_reversal_polarity"
    name = "Solvency-Gated Cooling Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Scores completed idiosyncratic downside-shock cooling, then assigns "
        "positive polarity to high cash/OCF debt coverage and negative polarity "
        "to financing-fragile names."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "cash",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "totalDebt",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _numeric(data["close"])
        open_price = _numeric(data["open"])
        low = _numeric(data["low"])
        volume = _numeric(data["volume"])
        cash = _numeric(data["cash"])
        operating_cash_flow = _numeric(data["operatingCashFlow"])
        total_debt = _numeric(data["totalDebt"])

        positive_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        positive_open = open_price.where(open_price > 0.0)
        ret = positive_close / positive_close.shift(1) - 1.0
        downside_range = ((positive_open - low) / positive_open).clip(lower=0.0)

        volume_base = volume.shift(5).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        range_base = downside_range.shift(5).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        shock_volume = volume.shift(2).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        shock_range = downside_range.shift(2).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        volume_shock = shock_volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_shock = shock_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        shock_return = _compound_lagged_three_day_return(ret)
        sector_return = _sector_mean_return(ret, data["sector"])
        idio_shock_return = shock_return - _compound_lagged_three_day_return(sector_return)
        negative_days = (
            ret.lt(0.0).astype(float).where(ret.notna()).shift(2).rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        )

        cooling_volume = volume.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean() / shock_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cooling_range = downside_range.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean() / shock_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        current_range_max = downside_range.rolling(2, min_periods=2).max()
        cooling_return = (1.0 + ret.shift(1)) * (1.0 + ret) - 1.0

        eps = _numeric(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue = _numeric(data["revenueSurprise"])
        eps_update = eps.notna() & eps.ne(eps.shift(1))
        revenue_update = revenue.notna() & revenue.ne(revenue.shift(1))
        no_recent_announcement = ~(
            eps_update.astype(float).rolling(5, min_periods=1).max().eq(1.0)
            | revenue_update.astype(float).rolling(5, min_periods=1).max().eq(1.0)
        )

        cash_coverage = cash / total_debt.where(total_debt > 0.0)
        ocf_coverage = operating_cash_flow / total_debt.where(total_debt > 0.0)
        fundamental_valid = cash_coverage.notna() & ocf_coverage.notna()

        eligible = (
            fundamental_valid
            & (volume_shock >= 1.4)
            & (range_shock >= 1.4)
            & (shock_return <= -0.045)
            & (idio_shock_return <= -0.025)
            & (negative_days >= 2.0)
            & (cooling_volume <= 0.70)
            & (cooling_range <= 0.70)
            & (current_range_max <= shock_range)
            & (cooling_return > -0.025)
            & no_recent_announcement
        )

        completion = (
            rank((-idio_shock_return).where(eligible))
            + rank(volume_shock.where(eligible))
            + rank((-cooling_volume).where(eligible))
            + rank((-cooling_range).where(eligible))
        ) / 4.0

        resilience = (
            rank(cash_coverage.where(eligible))
            + rank(ocf_coverage.where(eligible))
            - 1.0
        )
        score = completion * resilience
        return score.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Solvency-Gated Cooling Reversal
programs.trading_idea: A completed idiosyncratic downside-volume shock followed by contraction in range and participation is evidence that the initial sell program has exhausted, but only when the issuer has sufficient cash and operating-cash-flow coverage of debt for liquidity providers to reload inventory. In financing-fragile names, the same apparent cooling can instead be a temporary pause in risk-bearing capacity, leaving bad-news reflexivity and renewed selling over the six-day horizon. The interaction therefore separates genuine forced-flow completion from fragile-balance-sheet aftershock continuation, a polarity distinction neither the mechanical cooling state nor financing fragility identifies alone.
programs.description: Detects a non-announcement idiosyncratic downside shock with abnormal volume and downside range, then measures its two-day cooling. The completed-shock score is multiplied by a cross-sectional cash- and operating-cash-flow-to-debt resilience state, producing positive signals for resilient recoveries and negative signals for fragile cooling episodes.

"""Credible earnings news whose skeptical opening auction is completed intraday.

A fundamentally supported earnings surprise is most actionable when an opening gap in
the opposite direction is rejected on unusual participation, identifying temporary
auction pressure rather than a durable disagreement with the report."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _auction_reversal_direction(
    open_price: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Signed direction of an abnormal opening displacement rejected by the close.

    Positive values denote a gap-down followed by recovery; negative values denote a
    gap-up followed by rejection. All reference quantities use prior or current bars.
    """
    prior_close = close.shift(1)
    prior_median_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(12, min_periods=8).median()
    valid = (
        open_price.gt(0.0)
        & close.gt(0.0)
        & prior_close.gt(0.0)
        & volume.gt(0.0)
        & prior_median_volume.gt(0.0)
    )

    gap = np.log(open_price.where(valid) / prior_close.where(valid)).clip(-0.20, 0.20)
    intraday = np.log(close.where(valid) / open_price.where(valid)).clip(-0.20, 0.20)
    rejection = (-np.sign(gap) * intraday).clip(lower=0.0)

    participation = np.log(
        volume.where(valid) / prior_median_volume.where(valid).clip(lower=1.0)
    ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.5)
    return (-np.sign(gap) * rejection * participation).where(valid)


@register_factor
class CredibleAuctionSkepticismCompletion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "credible_auction_skepticism_completion"
    name = "Credible Surprise Auction Completion"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks operating-supported rather than tax-supported EPS surprises, retaining "
        "them when an abnormal opening gap opposite to the credible news is rejected "
        "during the same daily auction session."
    )
    window_length = 258
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "marketCap",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        pretax_income = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax_expense = data["incomeTaxExpense"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        prior_eps = eps_actual.shift(1)
        report_event = eps_actual.notna() & (
            prior_eps.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_eps)
        )

        annual_operating = operating_income.shift(252)
        annual_pretax = pretax_income.shift(252)
        annual_tax = tax_expense.shift(252)
        safe_cap = market_cap.where(market_cap.gt(0.0))

        current_etr = (
            tax_expense / pretax_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.50)
        annual_etr = (
            annual_tax / annual_pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.50)
        eps_surprise = (eps_actual - eps_estimate) / (eps_estimate.abs() + 0.01)
        operating_support = (operating_income - annual_operating) / safe_cap
        tax_support = (-pretax_income * (current_etr - annual_etr)) / safe_cap

        eligible = (
            report_event
            & eps_estimate.notna()
            & pretax_income.gt(0.0)
            & annual_pretax.gt(0.0)
            & eps_surprise.notna()
            & operating_support.notna()
            & tax_support.notna()
        )

        credible_news = (
            rank(eps_surprise.where(eligible))
            + rank(operating_support.where(eligible))
            - rank(tax_support.where(eligible))
            - 0.5
        )

        auction_direction = _auction_reversal_direction(
            data["open"], close, data["volume"]
        )
        aligned_skepticism = (credible_news * auction_direction).clip(lower=0.0)
        completion_weight = 0.25 + rank(aligned_skepticism.where(eligible))

        signal = credible_news * completion_weight
        signal = signal.where(
            eligible & aligned_skepticism.gt(0.0) & completion_weight.notna(),
            0.0,
        )
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Credible Surprise Auction Completion
programs.trading_idea: A credible earnings surprise has more six-day drift when the opening auction initially moves against its fundamental implication but that displacement is rejected intraday on abnormal participation. A positive operating-supported surprise paired with a gap-down-and-recovery indicates pessimistic liquidity supply was absorbed, while a tax-supported or unsupported surprise is less likely to sustain; symmetrically, a credible negative surprise paired with a rejected gap-up indicates failed optimistic demand. Neither parent alone distinguishes a temporary auction disagreement from an informed fundamental repricing, whereas their interaction identifies a completed transfer of inventory from skeptical opening traders to investors reacting to credible information.
programs.description: On fresh earnings reports, the factor ranks EPS surprises supported by year-over-year operating-income improvement rather than tax-rate changes. It retains and amplifies those signals only when a high-participation opening gap opposite to the credible surprise is rejected during the same session.
