"""Stress-gated credibility polarity for idiosyncratic volume arrivals.

Mechanism: following a negative industry impulse, prior relative resilience and a
late idiosyncratic participation burst can be either informed counterflow or
transient support.  Revenue- and margin-supported revisions validate the burst;
tax-led and financially fragile revisions raise the threshold for continuation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _group_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date group median with a same-date market-median fallback."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(group)]
        if len(members) > 0:
            median = values.loc[:, members].median(axis=1, skipna=True)
            out.loc[:, members] = np.tile(median.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, len(members)))
    market = values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return out.T.fillna(market).T


def _cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust contemporaneous cross-sectional z-score."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lo = clean.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    hi = clean.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = clean.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    scale = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(scale, axis=0)


def _revision(current: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    previous = current.shift(lag)
    return ((current - previous) / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )


@register_factor
class StressGatedRevisionArrivalPolarity(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "stress_gated_revision_arrival_polarity"
    name = "Stress-Gated Credible Arrival Polarity"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks sector-residual rare signed-volume arrivals after relative resilience "
        "in an industry selloff, continuing only arrivals validated by operating "
        "revision credibility and reversing the rest."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingIncome",
        "revenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "debtToAssets",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        stock_ret = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        industry_ret = _group_median(stock_ret, labels)
        industry_move = industry_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        industry_scale = industry_move.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().clip(lower=0.002)
        downside = (-industry_move / industry_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

        stock_move = stock_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        prior_resilience = (stock_move - industry_move).shift(1).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        stress_state = np.tanh(downside) * prior_resilience

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        positive_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
        volume_base = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=12).median().shift(1)
        volume_ratio = volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rare_cutoff = volume_ratio.rolling(60, min_periods=40).quantile(0.95).shift(1)
        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        direction = np.sign(close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
        valid = close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0) & high.gt(low)
        rare = valid & volume_ratio.ge(rare_cutoff)
        marked_arrival = (
            direction * location.abs() * volume_ratio.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        ).where(rare, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        arrival_memory = marked_arrival.ewm(halflife=3, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
        idio_arrival = arrival_memory - _group_median(arrival_memory, labels)

        eps = data["epsEstimate"]
        sales = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_income = data["operatingIncome"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        pretax = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax = data["incomeTaxExpense"]

        eps_rev = _revision(eps, 42)
        sales_rev = _revision(sales, 42)
        margin = operating_income / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        margin_change = margin - margin.shift(42)
        tax_rate = tax / pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tax_decline = tax_rate.shift(42) - tax_rate

        eps_sign = np.sign(eps_rev)
        sales_support = eps_sign * _cs_zscore(sales_rev).fillna(0.0)
        margin_support = eps_sign * _cs_zscore(margin_change).fillna(0.0)
        tax_penalty = _cs_zscore(tax_decline).fillna(0.0).where(eps_sign.gt(0.0), 0.0)
        update = eps.notna() & eps.shift(1).notna() & eps.ne(eps.shift(1))
        credibility_impulse = (
            eps_sign * (0.55 * sales_support + 0.45 * margin_support - 0.40 * tax_penalty)
        ).clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0).where(update, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        credibility = credibility_impulse.ewm(halflife=10, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

        debt = data["debtToAssets"].rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        liquidity_weakness = (-data["currentRatio"]).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        coverage_weakness = (-data["interestCoverage"]).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
        fragility = (debt + liquidity_weakness + coverage_weakness) / 3.0

        arrival_sign = np.sign(idio_arrival)
        alignment = arrival_sign * credibility
        polarity = np.tanh(2.0 * (alignment - 0.30 * fragility) - 0.35)
        signal = stress_state * idio_arrival * polarity
        return signal.rank(axis=1, pct=True).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Stress-Gated Credible Arrival Polarity
programs.trading_idea: An idiosyncratic volume arrival during an industry downside impulse is especially informative only after the stock has first shown relative resilience: this is the common-shock support state identified by Parent A. Parent B supplies the polarity test: revenue- and margin-confirmed estimate revisions make the arrival likely informed counterflow and therefore continuation, whereas tax-led or financially fragile revisions make the same support more likely transient liquidity demand and therefore reversal. The interaction distinguishes genuine information-driven sheltering from mechanically supported resilience, which neither industry stress nor signed-volume arrivals identify alone.
programs.description: The signal isolates sector-residual rare signed-volume arrivals following relative resilience during a negative industry impulse, then flips their direction unless they agree with a decaying revenue/margin-supported and tax-discounted EPS-revision state. Financial fragility raises the credibility threshold required for continuation.

programs.code:
"""Peer-confirmed disclosure direction conditioned on adverse endpoint pressure.

Mechanism: a peer cluster of revenue/collection disclosures establishes whether an
issuer's earlier collection signal is economically credible.  When the issuer has
not caught up but a fresh, high-participation endpoint bar moves in the opposite
direction after a quiet state, the move is treated as transient inventory pressure
and is expected to repair toward the validated disclosure direction.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_transform(
    values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, operation: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-industry row-wise transform using static, point-in-time labels."""
    valid_labels = labels.reindex(values.columns)
    result = values.T.groupby(valid_labels, sort=False).transform(operation).T
    return result.reindex(index=values.index, columns=values.columns)


def _leave_one_out_industry_median(
    values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal leave-one-out industry median; looping only over static groups."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    labelled = labels.dropna()
    for _, group in labelled.groupby(labelled, sort=False):
        members = list(group.index)
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        block = values.loc[:, members]
        for member in members:
            result.loc[:, member] = block.drop(columns=member).median(axis=1)
    return result


def _peer_echo_endpoint_score(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_actual: pd.DataFrame,
    dso: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build a causal disclosure-confirmed adverse-flow repair score."""
    if close.empty or industry.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
    labelled = labels.notna()
    group_size = labels.map(labels.value_counts()).reindex(close.columns)
    enough_peers = group_size.ge(4.0) & labelled

    safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
    safe_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))

    # A filing pulse requires simultaneous newly available revenue and DSO data.
    report_event = (
        revenue_actual.notna()
        & dso.notna()
        & revenue_actual.shift(1).notna()
        & dso.shift(1).notna()
        & revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1))
        & dso.ne(dso.shift(1))
    )

    # Collection improvement is measured against the prior annual disclosure,
    # then made relative to contemporaneous industry collection behaviour.
    old_dso = dso.shift(252)
    dso_change = (dso / old_dso.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).where(
        dso.gt(0.0) & old_dso.gt(0.0)
    )
    industry_dso = _industry_transform(dso_change, labels, "median")
    collection_quality = (-(dso_change - industry_dso)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

    surprise_ratio = (
        revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    issuer_event = report_event & collection_quality.notna() & labelled
    peer_event = issuer_event & surprise_ratio.notna() & enough_peers

    # A marked five-day peer disclosure cluster, excluding the issuer itself.
    disclosure_mark = (0.5 * (surprise_ratio + collection_quality)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    marked_events = disclosure_mark.where(peer_event, 0.0)
    rolling_mark = marked_events.rolling(5, min_periods=1).sum()
    rolling_count = peer_event.astype(float).rolling(5, min_periods=1).sum()
    industry_mark = _industry_transform(rolling_mark, labels, "sum")
    industry_count = _industry_transform(rolling_count, labels, "sum")
    peer_mark = industry_mark - rolling_mark
    peer_count = industry_count - rolling_count
    peer_impulse = peer_mark / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    # Keep the most recent issuer event and measure its elapsed, observable age.
    rows = np.arange(len(close.index), dtype=float)[:, None]
    stamps = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(rows, close.shape).copy(),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    ).where(issuer_event)
    latest_stamp = stamps.ffill()
    event_age = pd.DataFrame(
        rows - latest_stamp.to_numpy(), index=close.index, columns=close.columns
    )
    latest_quality = collection_quality.where(issuer_event).ffill()

    # Relative response is measured over exactly the event-to-score interval.
    response = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    for age in range(1, 11):
        issuer_return = safe_close / safe_close.shift(age).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        peer_return = _leave_one_out_industry_median(issuer_return, labels)
        response = response.where(~event_age.eq(float(age)), issuer_return - peer_return)

    fundamental_direction = np.sign(peer_impulse)
    confirmation = (peer_impulse * latest_quality).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    directed_response = response * fundamental_direction
    muted_weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp((directed_response * 20.0).clip(-20.0, 20.0)))

    # Parent-A-style endpoint pressure, with a continuous refractory/quiet gate.
    log_volume = np.log1p(safe_volume)
    volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean()
    volume_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).std()
    volume_z = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
    bar_range = high - low
    endpoint = (
        (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    endpoint = endpoint.where(bar_range.gt(0.0), 0.0)
    endpoint_pressure = volume_z.clip(lower=0.0) * endpoint

    recent_abnormal = volume_z.shift(1).ge(0.5).astype(float).rolling(8, min_periods=1).sum()
    refractory = 1.0 / (1.0 + recent_abnormal)
    prior_displacement = (
        safe_close.shift(1) / safe_close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).abs().clip(0.0, 0.20)
    quietness = (1.0 - prior_displacement / 0.08).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    # Only endpoint pressure contrary to the peer-confirmed economic direction
    # is faded.  Its signed repair target is the validated disclosure direction.
    adverse_pressure = (-endpoint_pressure * fundamental_direction).clip(lower=0.0)
    raw = (
        fundamental_direction
        * adverse_pressure
        * np.sqrt(confirmation)
        * muted_weight
        * refractory
        * quietness
    )
    valid = (
        enough_peers
        & event_age.ge(1.0)
        & event_age.le(10.0)
        & response.notna()
        & confirmation.gt(0.0)
        & fundamental_direction.ne(0.0)
        & adverse_pressure.gt(0.0)
    )
    active = raw.where(valid)
    cross_mean = active.mean(axis=1)
    cross_std = active.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    standardized = active.sub(cross_mean, axis=0).div(cross_std, axis=0)
    return standardized.where(valid & standardized.notna(), 0.0).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0
    )

"""Sector-flow-conditioned impact exhaustion with an earnings-information switch.

A decaying return-per-participation response after an accelerating directional
run is usually an attention and inventory endpoint.  Broad, non-directional
sector volume synchrony identifies the common-flow state in which that repair
is most credible, while a confirmed earnings surprise switches aligned cases
to information-diffusion continuation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _sector_flow_state(ret: pd.DataFrame, volume_z: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Broadcast causal same-bar sector return, shock breadth, and dispersion."""
    sector_ret = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    dispersion = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for i in range(len(ret.index)):
        labels = sector.iloc[i]
        valid = labels.notna() & ret.iloc[i].notna() & volume_z.iloc[i].notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        for label in pd.unique(labels.loc[valid].dropna()):
            members = labels.index[((labels == label) & valid).to_numpy()]
            values = ret.iloc[i].loc[members].dropna()
            if len(values) < 5:
                continue
            mean_ret = values.mean()
            std_ret = values.std(ddof=1)
            shock_share = (volume_z.iloc[i].loc[members] >= 1.0).mean()
            if np.isfinite(mean_ret) and np.isfinite(std_ret) and np.isfinite(shock_share):
                sector_ret.loc[ret.index[i], members] = mean_ret
                breadth.loc[ret.index[i], members] = shock_share
                dispersion.loc[ret.index[i], members] = std_ret
    return (sector_ret, breadth, dispersion)

def _sector_mean(state: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast same-date sector average without using future observations."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=state.index, columns=state.columns)
    for i in range(len(state.index)):
        labels = sector.iloc[i]
        valid = labels.notna() & state.iloc[i].notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        for label in pd.unique(labels.loc[valid].dropna()):
            members = labels.index[((labels == label) & valid).to_numpy()]
            values = state.iloc[i].loc[members]
            if len(values) >= 2:
                result.loc[state.index[i], members] = values.mean()
    return result

def _sector_demean(score: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove same-bar sector common mode while retaining the full panel shape."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=score.index, columns=score.columns)
    for i in range(len(score.index)):
        labels = sector.iloc[i]
        valid = labels.notna() & score.iloc[i].notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        for label in pd.unique(labels.loc[valid].dropna()):
            members = labels.index[((labels == label) & valid).to_numpy()]
            values = score.iloc[i].loc[members]
            if len(values) >= 2:
                result.loc[score.index[i], members] = values - values.mean()
    return result

def _three_leg_exhaustion(ret: pd.DataFrame, participation: pd.DataFrame, sigma: pd.DataFrame, direction: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal three-leg impact acceleration followed by response decay."""
    old_ret = ret.shift(6).rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    mid_ret = ret.shift(3).rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    new_ret = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    old_part = participation.shift(6).rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    mid_part = participation.shift(3).rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    new_part = participation.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    safe_sigma = sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    d_old = direction * old_ret / safe_sigma
    d_mid = direction * mid_ret / safe_sigma
    d_new = direction * new_ret / safe_sigma
    q_old = direction * old_part
    q_mid = direction * mid_part
    q_new = direction * new_part
    valid = (d_old > 0.0) & (d_mid > 0.0) & (d_new > 0.0)
    valid &= (q_old > 0.0) & (q_mid > 0.0) & (q_new > 0.0)
    impact_old = (d_old / q_old.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)
    impact_mid = (d_mid / q_mid.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)
    impact_new = (d_new / q_new.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)
    acceleration = ((impact_mid - impact_old) / (impact_old + 0.25)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
    decay = ((impact_mid - impact_new) / (impact_mid + 0.25)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
    exhaustion = np.sqrt(acceleration * decay).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    return exhaustion.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

@register_factor
class SynchronousFlowImpactExhaustionInformationSwitch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'synchronous_flow_impact_exhaustion_information_s'
    name = 'Synchronous Flow Impact Information Switch'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = 'Fades mature return-volume impact exhaustion during broad, non-directional sector flow shocks, but switches to continuation for runs aligned with a fresh volume-confirmed earnings-surprise information state.'
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'sector', 'epsActual', 'epsSurprise']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].where(data['close'] > 0.0)
        volume = data['volume'].where(data['volume'] >= 0.0)
        sector = data['sector'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        eps_actual = data['epsActual'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        eps_surprise = data['epsSurprise'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        ret = np.log(close / close.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        log_volume = np.log1p(volume)
        vol_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).mean()
        vol_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).std(ddof=1)
        volume_z = ((log_volume - vol_mean) / vol_std.where(vol_std > 0.0)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector_ret, shock_breadth, dispersion = _sector_flow_state(ret, volume_z, sector)
        dispersion_base = dispersion.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=20).median()
        dispersion_ratio = dispersion / dispersion_base.where(dispersion_base > 0.0)
        broadness = ((shock_breadth - 0.2) / 0.6).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        dispersed = ((dispersion_ratio - 0.8) / 0.8).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        muted_direction = (1.0 - sector_ret.abs() / dispersion.where(dispersion > 0.0)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        sector_flow = (broadness * dispersed * muted_direction).fillna(0.0)
        sigma = np.sqrt(ret.pow(2).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean())
        relative_volume = volume / volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        participation = np.sign(ret) * relative_volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mature_z = ret.rolling(12, min_periods=9).sum() / (np.sqrt(12.0) * sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        direction = np.sign(mature_z).fillna(0.0)
        maturity = ((mature_z.abs() - 0.5) / 2.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
        exhaustion = _three_leg_exhaustion(ret, participation, sigma, direction)
        prior_actual = eps_actual.shift(1)
        fresh_report = eps_actual.notna() & (prior_actual.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_actual))
        surprise_rank = eps_surprise.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        reported_state = (2.0 * surprise_rank - 1.0).where(fresh_report, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        delayed_state = reported_state.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
        confirmed = (delayed_state * ret > 0.0) & (volume_z >= 0.0) & ret.notna()
        impulse = delayed_state.where(confirmed, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        own_state = impulse.ewm(halflife=10.0, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
        peer_state = _sector_mean(own_state, sector)
        own_scale = impulse.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=8).mean().fillna(0.05).clip(lower=0.05)
        peer_scale = peer_state.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=8).mean().fillna(0.05).clip(lower=0.05)
        information_state = np.tanh(own_state / own_scale + 0.5 * peer_state / peer_scale)
        alignment = (direction * information_state).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        regime_multiplier = -1.0 + 2.0 * alignment
        raw_score = sector_flow * maturity * exhaustion * direction * regime_multiplier
        output = _sector_demean(raw_score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan), sector)
        return output.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The factor identifies a mature directional run whose price response per unit of signed relative volume first accelerates and then decays, a pattern consistent with late-stage attention-driven impact exhaustion. It only trades this endpoint during broad, non-directional sector volume synchrony, where common basket activity makes temporary inventory pressure more plausible. A fresh, volume-confirmed earnings-surprise state reverses the fade when it agrees with the run direction: an exhausted-looking move backed by disclosed information can still be under-assimilated and drift, whereas the same impact pattern without information should repair. This interaction distinguishes mechanical sector-flow overshoots from informational repricing, which neither parent can isolate alone.

"""Sector-relative return polarity selected by price-volume hysteresis.

Mechanism: sector-mode residuals are followed when close-location pressure leads
abnormal participation, but faded when participation leads pressure and the move
is more likely execution-driven liquidity displacement.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_pc_residual(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal rolling sector-PC residual and leading-mode variance share."""
    index = close.index
    columns = close.columns
    prices = close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    labels_matrix = sector.to_numpy(dtype=object, copy=False)
    n_dates, n_assets = prices.shape

    ret = np.full((n_dates, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)
    if n_dates > 1:
        prior = prices[:-1]
        current = prices[1:]
        valid = np.isfinite(prior) & np.isfinite(current) & (prior > 0.0)
        ret[1:] = np.where(valid, current / prior - 1.0, np.nan)

    residual = np.full((n_dates, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)
    synchronization = np.full((n_dates, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)

    for t in range(lookback - 1, n_dates):
        sample_window = ret[t - lookback + 1:t + 1]
        labels = labels_matrix[t]
        valid_labels = pd.notna(labels)
        complete = np.isfinite(sample_window).all(axis=0)

        for label in pd.unique(labels[valid_labels]):
            members = np.flatnonzero((labels == label) & complete)
            if members.size < 4:
                continue

            sample = sample_window[:, members]
            mean = sample.mean(axis=0)
            scale = sample.std(axis=0, ddof=1)
            usable = np.isfinite(scale) & (scale > 0.0)
            members = members[usable]
            if members.size < 4:
                continue

            sample = sample_window[:, members]
            mean = sample.mean(axis=0)
            scale = sample.std(axis=0, ddof=1)
            standardized = (sample - mean) / scale
            corr = standardized.T @ standardized / float(lookback - 1)
            corr = 0.5 * (corr + corr.T)

            try:
                eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eigh(corr)
            except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
                continue

            lead = int(np.argmax(eigenvalues))
            loading = eigenvectors[:, lead]
            current_z = standardized[-1]
            mode_score = float(np.dot(loading, current_z))
            residual[t, members] = current_z - loading * mode_score
            synchronization[t, members] = float(eigenvalues[lead]) / float(members.size)

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(residual, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(synchronization, index=index, columns=columns),
    )


def _abnormal_log_volume(volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing robust abnormal log-volume using observations available before t."""
    clean = volume.where(volume >= 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    log_volume = np.log1p(clean)
    history = log_volume.shift(1)
    median = history.rolling(20, min_periods=12).median()
    mad = history.rolling(20, min_periods=12).apply(
        lambda values: np.median(np.abs(values - np.median(values))), raw=True
    )
    scale = (1.4826 * mad).where(mad > 0.0)
    return ((log_volume - median) / scale).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)


def _oriented_area(x: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.DataFrame, length: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing closed shoelace area; positive orientation is price-led rotation."""
    area = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)
    for older_lag in range(length - 1, 0, -1):
        newer_lag = older_lag - 1
        area = area + (
            x.shift(older_lag) * y.shift(newer_lag)
            - x.shift(newer_lag) * y.shift(older_lag)
        )
    area = area + (x * y.shift(length - 1) - x.shift(length - 1) * y)
    return 0.5 * area


@register_factor
class SectorModeHysteresisPolaritySwitch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_mode_hysteresis_polarity_switch"
    name = "Sector-Mode Hysteresis Polarity Switch"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-PC residual momentum is retained for price-led volume loops and "
        "reversed for participation-led loops, weighted by sector synchronization."
    )
    window_length = 30
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        low = data["low"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        residual, synchronization = _sector_pc_residual(close, sector, 30)

        bar_range = high - low
        valid_bar = (
            close.notna() & high.notna() & low.notna() & (bar_range > 0.0)
        )
        location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).where(valid_bar)
        abnormal_volume = _abnormal_log_volume(volume)
        path_valid = location.notna() & abnormal_volume.notna()
        complete_path = path_valid.rolling(10, min_periods=10).sum() == 10.0

        area = _oriented_area(location, abnormal_volume, 10)
        area_scale = area.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).std()
        phase = np.tanh(area / area_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        endpoint_gap = (
            (location - location.shift(9)) ** 2
            + (abnormal_volume - abnormal_volume.shift(9)) ** 2
        )
        closure = np.exp(-0.5 * endpoint_gap)
        mode_weight = ((synchronization - 0.20) / 0.35).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        raw = residual * phase * closure * mode_weight
        raw = raw.where(complete_path & np.isfinite(raw), 0.0)
        return raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True, method="average").fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Sector-Mode Hysteresis Polarity Switch
programs.trading_idea: A sector-relative displacement has different implications depending on whether price pressure leads participation or participation arrives before price pressure. When the close-location/volume loop indicates price-led participation, the residual move is treated as gradual information diffusion and followed; when volume leads price, the same residual move is treated as execution-led liquidity pressure and faded. The sector-mode residual removes broad basket repricing, while the hysteresis sign identifies whether the remaining idiosyncratic displacement is informational or transient, an interaction neither a residual-only reversal nor a loop-only signal can isolate.
programs.description: Computes a trailing sector principal-component residual and conditions its direction on the normalized oriented area of a close-location versus abnormal-volume path. Positive price-led loop orientation preserves residual momentum; negative participation-led orientation reverses it, with stronger sector synchronization receiving greater weight.

"""This revision replaces the ambiguous inventory-unwind reversal mechanism with an information-richness mechanism. A stock-specific volume shock that is unusually large relative both to its own trailing activity and to contemporaneous sector activity, and whose close confirms rather than rejects the intraday displacement, is more consistent with directional information arrival or persistent informed execution than with a completed liquidity-demand episode. Because volume is unsigned, daily price direction and close location are only price-based proxies for directional pressure, not observations of signed order flow."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rolling_mad(values: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Median absolute deviation for a trailing raw rolling-window array."""
    valid = values[np.isfinite(values)]
    if valid.size == 0:
        return np.nan
    median = np.median(valid)
    return float(np.median(np.abs(valid - median)))


def _prior_log_volume_abnormality(volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust log-volume z-score using only observations through t-1."""
    log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))
    history = log_volume.shift(1)

    history_count = history.rolling(60, min_periods=40).count()
    history_median = history.rolling(60, min_periods=40).median()
    history_mad = history.rolling(60, min_periods=40).apply(
        _rolling_mad, raw=True
    )
    scale = (1.4826 * history_mad).where(history_mad > 0.0)

    abnormality = (log_volume - history_median) / scale
    return abnormality.where(history_count >= 40.0)


def _sector_transform(
    values: pd.DataFrame, sector_labels: pd.Series, method: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Apply a same-date cross-sectional transform independently by sector."""
    return values.T.groupby(sector_labels, sort=False).transform(method).T


@register_factor
class IdiosyncraticConfirmedFlowContinuation(BaseFactor):
    """Confirmed idiosyncratic volume shocks signal directional continuation."""

    factor_id = "sector_idiosyncratic_confirmed_flow_continuation"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Confirmed-Flow Continuation"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks endpoint-confirmed up and down intraday displacements only when "
        "current volume is a large robust residual versus both the stock's own "
        "60-session history and its contemporaneous sector."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_price = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]

        # Sector is explicitly static.  Names lacking a label on the first bar
        # cannot be sector-normalized and are therefore excluded.
        sector_labels = sector.iloc[0]

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(
            (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0)
        )
        prior_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.shift(1)
        median_dollar_volume = prior_dollar_volume.rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).median()

        volume_abnormality = _prior_log_volume_abnormality(volume)

        intraday_range = high - low
        valid_bar = (
            (close > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & open_price.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & (intraday_range > 0.0)
        )
        liquid = median_dollar_volume >= 1_000_000.0
        base_eligible = (
            valid_bar
            & liquid
            & volume_abnormality.notna()
            & sector_labels.notna()
        )

        eligible_abnormality = volume_abnormality.where(base_eligible)
        sector_median = _sector_transform(
            eligible_abnormality, sector_labels, "median"
        )
        sector_count = _sector_transform(
            base_eligible.astype(float), sector_labels, "sum"
        )
        sector_eligible = base_eligible & (sector_count >= 5.0)
        idiosyncratic_abnormality = (
            volume_abnormality - sector_median
        ).where(sector_eligible)

        displacement = (close - open_price) / intraday_range
        close_location = (close - low) / intraday_range

        upward = (
            sector_eligible
            & (displacement >= 0.50)
            & (close_location >= 0.80)
            & (idiosyncratic_abnormality >= 1.50)
        )
        downward = (
            sector_eligible
            & (displacement <= -0.50)
            & (close_location <= 0.20)
            & (idiosyncratic_abnormality >= 1.50)
        )

        raw_score = idiosyncratic_abnormality.where(upward, 0.0)
        raw_score = raw_score - idiosyncratic_abnormality.where(downward, 0.0)

        eps_previous = eps_actual.shift(1)
        revenue_previous = revenue_actual.shift(1)
        eps_release = eps_actual.notna() & (
            eps_previous.isna() | eps_actual.ne(eps_previous)
        )
        revenue_release = revenue_actual.notna() & (
            revenue_previous.isna() | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_previous)
        )
        remaining_eligible = sector_eligible & ~(eps_release | revenue_release)

        percentile_rank = raw_score.where(remaining_eligible).rank(
            axis=1, pct=True
        )
        signed_rank = 2.0 * percentile_rank - 1.0
        return signed_rank.where(remaining_eligible, 0.0)
programs.name: Idiosyncratic Confirmed-Flow Continuation
programs.trading_idea: This revision replaces the ambiguous inventory-unwind reversal mechanism with an information-richness mechanism. A stock-specific volume shock that is unusually large relative both to its own trailing activity and to contemporaneous sector activity, and whose close confirms rather than rejects the intraday displacement, is more consistent with directional information arrival or persistent informed execution than with a completed liquidity-demand episode. Because volume is unsigned, daily price direction and close location are only price-based proxies for directional pressure, not observations of signed order flow.
programs.description: At the close of day t, restrict the universe to names with non-missing positive close and volume, a positive intraday range high-low, and trailing 20-session median dollar volume (close*volume, using sessions t-20 through t-1 only) of at least USD 1,000,000. For each eligible stock, compute log-volume abnormality z_t = [log(volume_t) - median(log(volume) over t-60 through t-1)] / [1.4826*MAD(log(volume) over t-60 through t-1)], requiring at least 40 valid trailing observations and strictly positive MAD; otherwise the stock is ineligible. Within each static sector on day t, using only eligible names and requiring at least 5 names, compute the idiosyncratic volume residual a_t = z_t - sector_median(z_t). Define directional displacement d_t=(close_t-open_t)/(high_t-low_t) and close location clv_t=(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t). A confirmed upward-pressure event requires d_t>=0.50, clv_t>=0.80, and a_t>=1.50; a confirmed downward-pressure event requires d_t<=-0.50, clv_t<=0.20, and a_t>=1.50. Set raw score q_t=+a_t for confirmed upward events, q_t=-a_t for confirmed downward events, and 0 otherwise. Exclude a stock on t if either epsActual or revenueActual is newly reported on t, defined deterministically as a non-null value whose prior-day value was null or different; this avoids directly trading the first daily bar carrying an earnings release. Rank q_t cross-sectionally among all remaining eligible names on day t, convert the percentile rank to [-1,1], and use that signed rank as the factor: high values are long candidates and low values are short candidates. All volume-history windows end at t-1; only same-bar OHLCV observed after the day-t close is used for event classification. The signal is formed after the close on t, entered at open on t+1, and evaluated by the six-session executable forward return open(t+7)/open(t+1)-1. The concrete distinction from the prior rejection/exhaustion family is that this factor requires endpoint-confirmed directional displacement and trades continuation, while its volume condition is an explicit residual relative to both a 60-session own-history baseline and the same-day sector median rather than simple high-volume reversal or close-location rejection.

programs.code:
"""Industry-wide synchronization in abnormal intrabar ranges identifies a common liquidity-stress episode rather than a stock-specific earnings-information event. Within such episodes, a constituent that closes near one extreme of an unusually large range despite below-normal own participation is more likely to have been displaced through a temporarily thin book than repriced by informed demand; the factor therefore takes the opposite side of that signed endpoint displacement, with positive factor values expected to earn positive subsequent returns. The inefficiency persists because urgent hedgers, benchmark rebalancers, and liquidity-constrained traders must execute during the stress episode, while liquidity providers and slower arbitrage capital replenish only after the transient volatility shock has passed."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_synchronized_breadth(
    abnormal_range: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame, threshold: float
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing-information industry breadth of contemporaneous range shocks."""
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=abnormal_range.index, columns=abnormal_range.columns)
    labels = industry.ffill().bfill()

    for timestamp in abnormal_range.index:
        row = abnormal_range.loc[timestamp]
        group_row = labels.loc[timestamp]
        valid = row.notna() & group_row.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        shocked = (row > threshold).where(valid)
        counts = valid.groupby(group_row).sum()
        shock_counts = shocked.groupby(group_row).sum(min_count=1)
        group_breadth = shock_counts / counts.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        breadth.loc[timestamp] = group_row.map(group_breadth)

    return breadth


@register_factor
class SynchronizedRangeThinParticipationSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Contrarian extreme-close signal conditional on synchronized industry range stress."""

    factor_id = "synchronized_range_thin_participation_snapback"
    name = "Synchronized Thin-Range Displacement Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Computes industry-level breadth of abnormal high-low ranges, then identifies "
        "stocks with unusually large own ranges, low relative volume, and a close near "
        "the signed bar extreme. It assigns a contrarian score to those thin-participation "
        "extreme closes only when range expansion is broadly synchronized among industry peers."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        industry = data["industry"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        price_scale = prior_close.where(prior_close > 0.0, close.where(close > 0.0))
        bar_range = ((high - low).clip(lower=0.0) / price_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        range_mean = bar_range.rolling(60, min_periods=20).mean()
        range_std = bar_range.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std()
        abnormal_range = (bar_range - range_mean) / range_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        industry_breadth = _industry_synchronized_breadth(abnormal_range, industry, 1.0)
        synchronized_stress = ((industry_breadth - 0.30) / 0.70).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        volume_base = volume.rolling(60, min_periods=20).mean()
        relative_volume = volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        thin_participation = (1.0 - relative_volume).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        midpoint = (high + low) / 2.0
        half_range = (high - low) / 2.0
        endpoint = ((close - midpoint) / half_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        extreme_close = endpoint.abs()

        range_intensity = ((abnormal_range - 1.0) / 2.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        raw_signal = -endpoint * extreme_close * range_intensity * thin_participation * synchronized_stress
        raw_signal = raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        return rank(raw_signal)

"""The revised mechanism is post-earnings-announcement drift rather than a slow valuation-surface reversal. Investors can initially extrapolate a reported earnings or revenue surprise without fully distinguishing a cash-supported operating improvement from an accounting-supported or weak-conversion result. Positive surprises with positive free cash flow and adequate cash conversion should exhibit stronger six-bar continuation, while negative surprises accompanied by weak cash generation should exhibit stronger negative continuation."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _new_release_event(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag a newly available or changed reported release value, causally."""
    previous = actual.shift(1)
    return actual.notna() & (previous.isna() | actual.ne(previous))

def _surprise_intensity(surprise: pd.DataFrame, estimate: pd.DataFrame, actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute a bounded surprise only where every required input is valid."""
    denominator = estimate.abs() + actual.abs()
    valid = surprise.notna() & estimate.notna() & actual.notna() & denominator.gt(0.0)
    intensity = (surprise / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    return intensity.where(valid)

def _cashflow_confirmation(free_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame, income_quality: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Assign cash-flow confirmation without imputing a claim for missing data."""
    available = free_cash_flow.notna() & income_quality.notna()
    positive = free_cash_flow.gt(0.0) & income_quality.ge(1.0)
    negative = free_cash_flow.le(0.0) | income_quality.le(0.0)
    confirmation = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=free_cash_flow.index, columns=free_cash_flow.columns)
    confirmation = confirmation.where(~(available & positive), 1.0)
    confirmation = confirmation.where(~(available & negative), -1.0)
    return confirmation

@register_factor
class EarningsSurpriseCashflowConfirmation(BaseFactor):
    """Cash-confirmed earnings-release surprise drift held for six daily bars."""
    factor_id = 'earnings_surprise_cashflow_confirmation_j'
    name = 'Cash-Flow Confirmed Earnings Surprise'
    category = 'momentum'
    description = 'Ranks new earnings-release surprises after amplifying cash-supported results and penalizing weak cash conversion, then holds the release signal for exactly six daily bars.'
    window_length = 6
    inputs = ['close', 'epsActual', 'revenueActual', 'epsSurprise', 'epsEstimate', 'revenueSurprise', 'revenueEstimate', 'freeCashFlow', 'incomeQuality']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        eps_actual = data['epsActual']
        revenue_actual = data['revenueActual']
        release_event = _new_release_event(eps_actual) | _new_release_event(revenue_actual)
        eps_intensity = _surprise_intensity(data['epsSurprise'], data['epsEstimate'], eps_actual)
        revenue_intensity = _surprise_intensity(data['revenueSurprise'], data['revenueEstimate'], revenue_actual)
        component_count = eps_intensity.notna().astype(float) + revenue_intensity.notna().astype(float)
        event_surprise = (eps_intensity.fillna(0.0) + revenue_intensity.fillna(0.0)) / component_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        confirmation = _cashflow_confirmation(data['freeCashFlow'], data['incomeQuality'])
        event_score = event_surprise * (1.0 + 0.5 * confirmation)
        event_score = event_score.where(release_event & event_surprise.notna())
        sufficient_events = event_score.notna().sum(axis=1).ge(30)
        event_score = event_score.where(sufficient_events, axis=0)
        event_position = (2.0 * rank(event_score) - 1.0).where(event_score.notna())
        held_position = event_position.fillna(0.0).rolling(7, min_periods=1).sum()
        return held_position.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The revised mechanism is post-earnings-announcement drift rather than a slow valuation-surface reversal. Investors can initially extrapolate a reported earnings or revenue surprise without fully distinguishing a cash-supported operating improvement from an accounting-supported or weak-conversion result. Positive surprises with positive free cash flow and adequate cash conversion should exhibit stronger six-bar continuation, while negative surprises accompanied by weak cash generation should exhibit stronger negative continuation.
programs.description: On a date when either epsActual or revenueActual changes from its prior available value, treat the name as having a new earnings-release event. Compute EPS surprise intensity as epsSurprise divided by abs(epsEstimate) plus abs(epsActual), and revenue surprise intensity as revenueSurprise divided by abs(revenueEstimate) plus abs(revenueActual); discard an intensity if its denominator is zero or either required input is missing. Define the event surprise as the equal-weight average of the available EPS and revenue intensities, requiring at least one valid component and clipping each component to [-1, 1]. Define cash-flow confirmation q as +1 when freeCashFlow is positive and incomeQuality is at least 1, -1 when freeCashFlow is non-positive or incomeQuality is non-positive, and 0 otherwise; missing freeCashFlow or incomeQuality sets q to 0 rather than imputing a quality claim. The final event score is event surprise multiplied by (1 + 0.5 times q). Rank only current release-event scores cross-sectionally, require at least 30 valid event names on a date, go long high positive scores and short low negative scores, and hold each event position for exactly 6 daily bars. There is no valuation regression, operating-margin expectation, industry surface, or unstated estimate-change window; all inputs are the point-in-time fields available on the release date.

programs.code:
"""Fresh earnings surprises whose quiet relative price response reveals assimilation gaps.

Mechanism: a disclosed EPS surprise identifies the direction of a fundamental
innovation.  When its sector-relative price response is muted or contrary on
subdued turnover, the observed move is more likely incomplete price discovery
than a fully assimilated repricing, creating post-announcement drift.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_surprise_score(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally identify newly available surprise observations and rank them."""
    prior = eps_surprise.shift(1)
    event = eps_surprise.notna() & (
        prior.isna() | (eps_surprise.sub(prior).abs() > 1e-12)
    )
    denominator = eps_estimate.abs().where(eps_estimate.abs() >= 0.01, 0.01)
    standardized = eps_surprise.div(denominator)
    eligible = event & standardized.notna()

    count = eligible.sum(axis=1)
    percentile = standardized.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    score = (2.0 * percentile - 1.0).where(eligible, 0.0)
    return score.where(count.ge(10), 0.0).fillna(0.0)


def _leave_one_out_sector_return(
    stock_return: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date leave-one-out sector return requiring at least four peers."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stock_return.index, columns=stock_return.columns)
    for timestamp in stock_return.index:
        values = stock_return.loc[timestamp]
        groups = sector.loc[timestamp]
        valid = values.notna() & groups.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        masked_values = values.where(valid)
        masked_groups = groups.where(valid)
        group_sum = masked_values.groupby(masked_groups).transform("sum")
        group_count = masked_values.groupby(masked_groups).transform("count")
        peer_count = group_count - 1.0
        peer = (group_sum - masked_values).div(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        output.loc[timestamp] = peer.where(peer_count.ge(4.0))
    return output


@register_factor
class FreshSurpriseQuietRelativeResponseGap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "fresh_surprise_quiet_relative_response_gap"
    name = "Quiet Earnings Response Gap"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks fresh standardized EPS surprises, amplified when a three-day "
        "sector-relative price response is muted or opposite and turnover is "
        "below its trailing participation baseline."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sharesOutstanding", "sector", "epsSurprise", "epsEstimate"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close)
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"].reindex_like(close)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close)

        surprise = _fresh_surprise_score(eps_surprise, eps_estimate)

        lag_close = close.shift(3)
        return_3d = close.div(lag_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
        return_3d = return_3d.where(close.gt(0.0) & lag_close.gt(0.0))
        peer_return = _leave_one_out_sector_return(return_3d, sector)
        displacement = return_3d.sub(peer_return)
        response_rank = displacement.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        response = (2.0 * response_rank - 1.0).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)

        turnover = volume.where(shares.gt(0.0)).div(shares.where(shares.gt(0.0)))
        fast_turnover = turnover.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        slow_turnover = turnover.rolling(40, min_periods=30).mean()
        relative_turnover = fast_turnover.div(slow_turnover.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        quietness = (1.0 / relative_turnover).clip(lower=0.5, upper=2.0)

        surprise_direction = np.sign(surprise)
        response_gap = surprise.mul(1.0 - surprise_direction.mul(response))
        valid = (
            surprise.ne(0.0)
            & peer_return.notna()
            & quietness.notna()
            & close.gt(0.0)
        )
        score = response_gap.mul(quietness).where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(score).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Quiet Earnings Response Gap
programs.trading_idea: A fresh EPS surprise supplies the directional fundamental innovation, while a muted or opposite sector-relative price response identifies names for which that innovation has not yet been incorporated. Low turnover is used as a state variable rather than a directional continuation signal: Parent B's reversed realized sign suggests quiet relative moves are often stale or insufficiently informative price discovery, so an earnings surprise that contradicts such a move is especially likely to correct over the next week. Neither parent alone distinguishes a genuine fundamental shock from a quiet price displacement; their interaction isolates delayed assimilation of a disclosed earnings shock.
programs.description: On fresh EPS-surprise dates, the factor ranks standardized surprises and amplifies them when the contemporaneous three-day sector-relative return is muted or opposite in sign, with greater weight when turnover is below its own 40-day baseline. It is zero for non-events, illiquid turnover histories, or sectors without enough peers.

programs.code:
"""During a predeclared same-sector earnings cluster, investors may initially trade the aggregate sector earnings narrative and allocate limited attention to firm-specific accounting quality. A signed earnings surprise supported by positive free cash flow and stronger income quality should therefore continue to be incorporated when its first observable sector-relative response is unusually small in the same direction as the disclosure. Congestion is not assumed to delay all news: it is a conditioning state in which a weak, sign-consistent initial response identifies issuer-specific information that was plausibly dominated by the contemporaneously available sector news flow."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_sector_labels(sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Recover the static taxonomy without changing the panel shape."""
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
    return labels.reindex(sector.columns)


def _sector_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Percentile rank each date within the fixed sector taxonomy."""
    return frame.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True).T.reindex_like(frame)


def _sector_sum(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast each date's sector sum back to every constituent."""
    return frame.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T.reindex_like(frame)


def _disclosure_score(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    free_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame,
    free_cash_flow_yield: pd.DataFrame,
    income_quality: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Sector-relative signed disclosure score with availability-weight rescaling."""
    eps_component = 2.0 * _sector_rank(eps_surprise, labels) - 1.0
    revenue_component = 2.0 * _sector_rank(revenue_surprise, labels) - 1.0

    cash_signal = np.sign(free_cash_flow) * free_cash_flow_yield.abs()
    cash_signal = cash_signal.where(
        free_cash_flow.notna() & free_cash_flow_yield.notna()
    )
    cash_component = 2.0 * _sector_rank(cash_signal, labels) - 1.0
    quality_component = 2.0 * _sector_rank(income_quality, labels) - 1.0

    components = (
        (eps_component, 0.50),
        (revenue_component, 0.25),
        (cash_component, 0.15),
        (quality_component, 0.10),
    )
    numerator = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=eps_surprise.index, columns=eps_surprise.columns)
    denominator = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=eps_surprise.index, columns=eps_surprise.columns)
    for component, weight in components:
        numerator = numerator + component.fillna(0.0) * weight
        denominator = denominator + component.notna().astype(float) * abs(weight)

    return numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class CashConfirmedDisclosureCongestionGap(BaseFactor):
    """Cash-confirmed underreaction to issuer disclosures during sector congestion."""

    factor_id = "cash_confirmed_disclosure_congestion_gap"
    name = "Cash-Confirmed Congested-Disclosure Drift"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks event disclosures whose cash-confirmed, sector-relative surprise "
        "received an unusually weak initial sector-relative response during a "
        "dense and dispersed same-sector disclosure window."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "marketCap",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        free_cash_flow = data["freeCashFlow"]
        free_cash_flow_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"]
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        labels = _static_sector_labels(data["sector"])

        # A disclosure is a newly available reported surprise, not the initial
        # unavailable-to-available observation before a prior report exists.
        eps_event = eps_surprise.notna() & eps_surprise.shift(1).notna() & eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1))
        revenue_event = (
            revenue_surprise.notna()
            & revenue_surprise.shift(1).notna()
            & revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_surprise.shift(1))
        )
        event = eps_event | revenue_event

        score = _disclosure_score(
            eps_surprise,
            revenue_surprise,
            free_cash_flow,
            free_cash_flow_yield,
            income_quality,
            labels,
        )

        # At cutoff tau=t+1, the issuer's event occurred at t.  The return
        # below is therefore entirely observed at tau and uses no post-cutoff bar.
        valid_return = close.notna() & close.shift(1).notna() & close.shift(1).ne(0.0)
        one_bar_return = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).where(valid_return)
        sector_return_sum = _sector_sum(one_bar_return, labels)
        sector_return_count = _sector_sum(valid_return.astype(float), labels)
        peer_return_count = sector_return_count - valid_return.astype(float)
        peer_return = (sector_return_sum - one_bar_return.fillna(0.0)) / peer_return_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_return = (one_bar_return - peer_return).where(peer_return_count.gt(0.0))

        event_at_cutoff = event.shift(1).fillna(False)
        event_score = score.shift(1)
        signed_initial_gap = (event_score * relative_return).where(event_at_cutoff)
        underreaction = -rank(signed_initial_gap)

        # The trailing six cutoff bars are exactly event dates t-4 through t+1.
        # A rolling maximum counts each issuer once even if a feed correction
        # causes more than one surprise update in the same short window.
        window_member = event.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).max()
        sector_window_members = _sector_sum(window_member, labels)
        peer_event_count = sector_window_members - window_member

        sector_members = _sector_sum(market_cap.notna().astype(float), labels)
        congestion = peer_event_count / sector_members.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # In normal quarterly data there is at most one event per issuer in six
        # bars.  Summing event-tagged scores gives the event score while retaining
        # strict trailing causality and permits exact issuer exclusion below.
        tagged_score = score.where(event)
        rolling_score = tagged_score.fillna(0.0).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum()
        rolling_score_sq = (tagged_score * tagged_score).fillna(0.0).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum()
        rolling_score_count = tagged_score.notna().astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum()

        sector_score_sum = _sector_sum(rolling_score, labels)
        sector_score_sq_sum = _sector_sum(rolling_score_sq, labels)
        sector_score_count = _sector_sum(rolling_score_count, labels)

        peer_score_sum = sector_score_sum - rolling_score
        peer_score_sq_sum = sector_score_sq_sum - rolling_score_sq
        peer_score_count = sector_score_count - rolling_score_count
        peer_variance = (
            peer_score_sq_sum - peer_score_sum.pow(2) / peer_score_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ) / (peer_score_count - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        dispersion = np.sqrt(peer_variance.clip(lower=0.0)).where(peer_score_count.ge(3.0))

        usable = (
            event_at_cutoff
            & event_score.notna()
            & relative_return.notna()
            & congestion.notna()
            & dispersion.notna()
        )

        final_raw = (
            rank(event_score.where(usable))
            * rank(underreaction.where(usable))
            * rank(congestion.where(usable))
            * rank(dispersion.where(usable))
        )
        return rank(final_raw.where(usable)).where(usable, 0.0).reindex_like(close)
programs.name: Cash-Confirmed Congested-Disclosure Drift
programs.trading_idea: During a predeclared same-sector earnings cluster, investors may initially trade the aggregate sector earnings narrative and allocate limited attention to firm-specific accounting quality. A signed earnings surprise supported by positive free cash flow and stronger income quality should therefore continue to be incorporated when its first observable sector-relative response is unusually small in the same direction as the disclosure. Congestion is not assumed to delay all news: it is a conditioning state in which a weak, sign-consistent initial response identifies issuer-specific information that was plausibly dominated by the contemporaneously available sector news flow.
programs.description: Define an issuer event date t as a daily bar on which either epsSurprise or revenueSurprise changes from its prior available point-in-time value; use the new values available at the close of t as the disclosure cutoff. Compute a cross-sectional, sector-neutral signed disclosure score S at t from percentile ranks: S = 0.5*rank_within_sector(epsSurprise) + 0.25*rank_within_sector(revenueSurprise) + 0.15*rank_within_sector(sign(freeCashFlow)*abs(freeCashFlowYield)) + 0.10*rank_within_sector(incomeQuality), with each component set to zero where unavailable and the weighted sum rescaled by the sum of available absolute weights. Observe the initial response only through the close of t+1: R = close[t+1]/close[t] - 1 minus the equal-weighted return of all same-sector peers with valid closes over t to t+1. Define underreaction U as -rank_cross_section(S*R) among names with an event at t, so high U means the realized sector-relative response was low or adverse relative to the signed disclosure; no return after t+1 enters the signal. Using the static sector field as the fixed taxonomy, define the peer event window as bars t-4 through t+1 inclusive, and, at the t+1 cutoff, count only peers whose epsSurprise or revenueSurprise changed on or before t+1. Congestion C is the within-sector event count excluding the issuer, divided by the number of sector members with nonmissing marketCap at t+1; peer dispersion D is the cross-sectional standard deviation of those peers' signed disclosure scores S, requiring at least three peer events. Form the final score at the t+1 close as rank_cross_section(S) * rank_cross_section(U) * rank_cross_section(C) * rank_cross_section(D), with missing C or D producing no position. Enter at t+2 open, long high scores and short low scores after daily cross-sectional ranking, and hold each event position for exactly six daily bars, exiting at the close of t+7. All fundamentals are read as supplied point-in-time fields; peer events and peer scores are restricted to disclosures public by the t+1 entry cutoff.

programs.code:
"""The signal treats a negative idiosyncratic opening gap that is substantially retraced by the regular-session close as an observable price-path pattern, not as proof of forced selling or uninformed trading. A bounded intraday range and non-exceptional volume condition select gap closures that occur without a broad volatility or turnover expansion, where short-run downside-risk amplification may be more likely to have completed than to remain unresolved. The expected positive six-bar return is therefore a conditional mean-reversion hypothesis that must be tested incrementally after controlling for existing opening-auction reversal factors."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_sector_median(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    sectors: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_peers: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal cross-sectional leave-one-out medians for each date and sector."""
    value_array = values.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    sector_array = sectors.to_numpy(dtype=object)
    eligible_array = eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    output = np.full(value_array.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for row in range(value_array.shape[0]):
        groups: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
        for col in range(value_array.shape[1]):
            value = value_array[row, col]
            sector = sector_array[row, col]
            if not eligible_array[row, col] or not np.isfinite(value) or pd.isna(sector):
                continue
            key = str(sector)
            groups.setdefault(key, []).append(col)

        for members in groups.values():
            count = len(members)
            if count - 1 < minimum_peers:
                continue

            member_array = np.asarray(members, dtype=int)
            group_values = value_array[row, member_array]
            order = np.argsort(group_values, kind="mergesort")
            sorted_values = group_values[order]
            sorted_member_columns = member_array[order]
            remaining_count = count - 1

            if remaining_count % 2 == 1:
                middle = remaining_count // 2
                for position, col in enumerate(sorted_member_columns):
                    source_position = middle + 1 if position <= middle else middle
                    output[row, col] = sorted_values[source_position]
            else:
                lower_middle = remaining_count // 2 - 1
                upper_middle = remaining_count // 2
                for position, col in enumerate(sorted_member_columns):
                    lower_source = (
                        lower_middle + 1 if position <= lower_middle else lower_middle
                    )
                    upper_source = (
                        upper_middle + 1 if position <= upper_middle else upper_middle
                    )
                    output[row, col] = 0.5 * (
                        sorted_values[lower_source] + sorted_values[upper_source]
                    )

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)


def _trailing_gap_regression(
    gap: pd.DataFrame,
    sector_gap: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    minimum_observations: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Fit per-name trailing OLS on prior sessions and return alpha, beta, sigma."""
    y = gap.shift(1)
    x = sector_gap.shift(1)
    valid = x.notna() & y.notna()

    x0 = x.where(valid, 0.0)
    y0 = y.where(valid, 0.0)
    count = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_x = x0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_y = y0.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xx = (x0 * x0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_yy = (y0 * y0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xy = (x0 * y0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    safe_count = count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    centered_xx = sum_xx - sum_x * sum_x / safe_count
    centered_yy = sum_yy - sum_y * sum_y / safe_count
    centered_xy = sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y / safe_count

    raw_beta = centered_xy / centered_xx.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    alpha = sum_y / safe_count - raw_beta * sum_x / safe_count
    residual_ss = (centered_yy - raw_beta * centered_xy).clip(lower=0.0)
    sigma = np.sqrt(residual_ss / (count - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan))

    valid_model = (count >= float(minimum_observations)) & sigma.gt(0.0)
    alpha = alpha.where(valid_model)
    beta = raw_beta.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0).where(valid_model)
    sigma = sigma.where(valid_model)
    return alpha, beta, sigma


def _cross_sectional_winsorize(values: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize masked observations at each day's one and ninety-nine percentiles."""
    masked = values.where(mask)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    return clipped.where(mask)


def _sector_decile_weights(
    gap_strength: pd.DataFrame,
    retracement: pd.DataFrame,
    sectors: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct equal-sector, equal-name weights for sector-local top deciles."""
    strength_array = gap_strength.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    retracement_array = retracement.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    sector_array = sectors.to_numpy(dtype=object)
    eligible_array = eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    result = np.zeros(strength_array.shape, dtype=float)

    for row in range(result.shape[0]):
        groups: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
        for col in range(result.shape[1]):
            sector = sector_array[row, col]
            if (
                not eligible_array[row, col]
                or not np.isfinite(strength_array[row, col])
                or not np.isfinite(retracement_array[row, col])
                or pd.isna(sector)
            ):
                continue
            groups.setdefault(str(sector), []).append(col)

        selected_groups: list[np.ndarray] = []
        for members in groups.values():
            if len(members) < 10:
                continue
            member_array = np.asarray(members, dtype=int)
            strength_series = pd.Series(strength_array[row, member_array])
            retracement_series = pd.Series(retracement_array[row, member_array])
            composite = 0.5 * strength_series.rank(pct=True) + 0.5 * retracement_series.rank(pct=True)
            composite_rank = composite.rank(pct=True)
            selected = member_array[composite_rank.to_numpy() >= 0.90]
            if len(selected) > 0:
                selected_groups.append(selected)

        if selected_groups:
            sector_weight = 1.0 / float(len(selected_groups))
            for selected in selected_groups:
                result[row, selected] = sector_weight / float(len(selected))

    return pd.DataFrame(result, index=gap_strength.index, columns=gap_strength.columns)


@register_factor
class GapRecoveryVarianceBudgetReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-residual gap closure with restrained range and volume."""

    factor_id = "gap_recovery_variance_budget_reversal"
    name = "Sector-Residual Gap Closure"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Equal-sector portfolio of stocks with a large negative sector-residual "
        "opening gap that closes substantially on ordinary range and volume."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_price = data["open"].reindex_like(close)
        high = data["high"].reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex_like(close)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex_like(close)

        positive_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        positive_open = open_price.where(open_price.gt(0.0))
        prior_close = positive_close.shift(1)
        gap = np.log(positive_open / prior_close)

        dollar_volume = (positive_close * volume.where(volume.ge(0.0))).where(volume.ge(0.0))
        prior_median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        base_eligible = (
            sector.notna()
            & market_cap.ge(200_000_000.0)
            & positive_close.ge(5.0)
            & prior_median_dollar_volume.ge(1_000_000.0)
        )

        sector_gap = _leave_one_out_sector_median(gap, sector, base_eligible, 5)
        alpha, beta, sigma = _trailing_gap_regression(gap, sector_gap, 60, 45)
        residual_gap = gap - alpha - beta * sector_gap
        standardized_gap = residual_gap / sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        recovery = np.log(positive_close / positive_open)
        retracement_denominator = (-residual_gap).clip(lower=0.005)
        retracement = recovery / retracement_denominator

        positive_high = high.where(high.gt(0.0))
        positive_low = low.where(low.gt(0.0))
        log_range = np.log(positive_high / positive_low)
        prior_median_range = log_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        normalized_range = log_range / prior_median_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_median_volume = volume.where(volume.ge(0.0)).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        relative_volume = volume / prior_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eligible = (
            base_eligible
            & sigma.gt(0.0)
            & standardized_gap.le(-1.5)
            & residual_gap.le(-0.01)
            & recovery.gt(0.0)
            & retracement.ge(0.50)
            & retracement.le(1.50)
            & normalized_range.ge(0.75)
            & normalized_range.le(1.25)
            & relative_volume.le(1.50)
        )

        winsorized_gap = _cross_sectional_winsorize(standardized_gap, eligible)
        winsorized_retracement = _cross_sectional_winsorize(retracement, eligible)
        _ = _cross_sectional_winsorize(normalized_range, eligible)
        _ = _cross_sectional_winsorize(relative_volume, eligible)

        weights = _sector_decile_weights(
            -winsorized_gap,
            winsorized_retracement,
            sector,
            eligible,
        )
        return weights.reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
